memories.description: I woke with a start because my aunt was shouting outside my door. Great way to wake up.
memories.source_text: "Up! Get up! Now!"

memories.description: That dream with the flying motorcycle has happened to me before. It's important to me, I can't just shrug it off.
memories.source_text: "He rolled onto his back and tried to remember the dream he had been having. It had been a good one. There had been a flying motorcycle in it. He had a funny feeling he’d had the same dream before."

memories.description: Aunt told me to get up and mind the bacon. So I'm in charge of breakfast whether I like it or not.
memories.source_text: "Well, get a move on, I want you to look after the bacon."

memories.description: It's from Hogwarts. There's a purple wax seal with the four animals and a big H. This is a Hogwarts letter.
memories.source_text: "Turning the envelope over, his hand trembling, Harry saw a purple wax seal bearing a coat of arms; a lion, an eagle, a badger, and a snake surrounding a large letter H."

memories.description: Uncle Vernon is not interested in what I might have. He rushes me, mocks me, and treats the letter like something to be laughed at or feared. I need to be careful with him.
memories.source_text: "Hurry up, boy! What are you doing, checking for letter bombs?"

memories.description: No one has ever written to me. I can't believe there's actually a letter with my name on it.
memories.source_text: No one, ever, in his whole life, had written to him.

memories.description: The letter is addressed to me, plain as day, to the cupboard under the stairs at 4 Privet Drive. It's meant for me and only me.
memories.source_text: Mr. H. Potter The Cupboard under the Stairs 4 Privet Drive Little Whinging Surrey

memories.description: The envelope isn't normal paper. It's thick yellow parchment and the address is written in emerald green. This isn't any ordinary letter.
memories.source_text: The envelope was thick and heavy, made of yellowish parchment, and the address was written in emerald-green ink.

memories.description: My heart's racing and I actually feel like something important is happening. This could change everything.
memories.source_text: Harry picked it up and stared at it, his heart twanging like a giant elastic band.

memories.description: That's my letter. I'm not going to let them keep it from me.
memories.source_text: "I want to read it," said Harry furiously, "as it’s mine."

memories.description: What the hell? I just jumped because something alive was under my foot on the doormat.
memories.source_text: "AAAAARRRGH!" Harry leapt into the air; he’d trodden on something big and squashy on the doormat — something alive!

memories.description: He's a scrawny kid with a rat face and he's the sort who pins people down while Dudley does the hitting. I don't trust him one bit.
memories.source_text: [Piers was a scrawny boy with a face like a rat. He was usually the one who held people’s arms behind their backs while Dudley hit them.]

memories.description: Dudley isn't just a spoilt brat putting on an act. He's nasty when he wants to be, and Piers helps him. That's worrying.
memories.source_text: [He was usually the one who held people’s arms behind their backs while Dudley hit them. Dudley stopped pretending to cry at once.]

memories.description: I'm actually going to the zoo. I can't believe it, I'm sitting in the car with Dudley and that awful Piers and I'm finally going to see animals.
memories.source_text: [Harry, who couldn’t believe his luck, was sitting in the back of the Dursleys’ car with Piers and Dudley, on the way to the zoo for the first time in his life.]

memories.description: So they're making my school uniform out of Dudley’s old clothes and dyeing them gray for me.
memories.source_text: "Your new school uniform," she said. "I’m dyeing some of Dudley’s old things gray for you."

memories.description: They boss me about and try to make me fetch things. I'm being ordered around like I'm nothing.
memories.source_text: "Get the mail, Dudley," said Uncle Vernon... "Make Harry get it." "Get the mail, Harry." "Make Dudley get it."

memories.description: There is a letter addressed to me on the doormat.
memories.source_text: Three things lay on the doormat... and — a letter for Harry.

memories.description: That's my name and my cupboard. It's meant for me. I couldn't believe it when I saw my own address written so plainly.
memories.source_text: Mr H. Potter The Cupboard under the Stairs 4 Privet Drive Little Whinging Surrey

memories.description: The letter isn't ordinary. Thick yellowish parchment and green ink, and there's no stamp. This isn't the sort of post we get.
memories.source_text: The envelope was thick and heavy, made of yellowish parchment, and the address was written in emerald-green ink. There was no stamp.

memories.description: There's a purple wax seal with a coat of arms and a big H. That seal means something important and not Muggle.
memories.source_text: Turning the envelope over, his hand trembling, Harry saw a purple wax seal bearing a coat of arms; a lion, an eagle, a badger, and a snake surrounding a large letter H.

memories.description: Vernon is mocking me and doesn't take this seriously. He's impatient and makes crude jokes instead of caring about what the letter might mean.
memories.source_text: “Hurry up, boy!” shouted Uncle Vernon from the kitchen. “What are you doing, checking for letter bombs?” He chuckled at his own joke.

memories.description: He was right there at the foot of the front door in a sleeping bag, his face all squashy. He was staying put to stop me getting out. What the hell, he actually sat up to block me.
memories.source_text: [Lights clicked on upstairs and to his horror Harry realized that the big, squashy something had been his uncle’s face. Uncle Vernon had been lying at the foot of the front door in a sleeping bag, clearly making sure that Harry didn’t do exactly what he’d been trying to do.]

memories.description: Vernon will go to ridiculous lengths to keep me under his control. Of course he would lie there like that to make sure I could not leave.
memories.source_text: [Lights clicked on upstairs and to his horror Harry realized that the big, squashy something had been his uncle’s face. Uncle Vernon had been lying at the foot of the front door in a sleeping bag, clearly making sure that Harry didn’t do exactly what he’d been trying to do.]

memories.description: Vernon shoved his face right up to mine and warned me that if I do anything he calls 'funny' I'll be locked in the cupboard until Christmas. He's treating me like a menace and I won't let him bully me into hiding.
memories.source_text: "I'm warning you now, boy, any funny business, anything at all, and you'll be in that cupboard from now until Christmas."

memories.description: It must be a dream. Hagrid told me I'm going to a school for wizards, but I'm telling myself it's only a dream until I actually open my eyes.
memories.source_text: "It was a dream," he told himself firmly. "I dreamed a giant called Hagrid came to tell me I was going to a school for wizards. When I open my eyes I’ll be at home in my cupboard."

memories.description: There's someone at the door. Aunt Petunia's knocking and my stomach just drops when I think about her being there.
memories.source_text: There was suddenly a loud tapping noise. And there’s Aunt Petunia knocking on the door, Harry thought, his heart sinking.

memories.description: Hagrid was actually here. I sat up and his huge coat fell off me, so it wasn't just a dream anymore.
memories.source_text: He sat up and Hagrid’s heavy coat fell off him.

memories.description: Fine, I'm getting up. No point pretending any longer.
memories.source_text: Tap. Tap. Tap. "All right," Harry mumbled, "I’m getting up."

memories.description: Mrs Figg has broken her leg and she can't take Dudley on his birthday. That means I'm not stuck with her today.
memories.source_text: "Mrs. Figg’s broken her leg. She can’t take him."

memories.description: I couldn't help grinning on the inside. The idea of not having to spend the day with Mrs Figg and her awful cats for a whole year actually made me feel proper relieved.
memories.source_text: "Dudley’s mouth fell open in horror, but Harry’s heart gave a leap."

memories.description: They treat me like I'm disgusting, like I'm not even there. Petunia and Vernon talk about me as if I'm a slug and Marge hates me, so I can't expect them to be decent.
memories.source_text: "The Dursleys often spoke about Harry like this, as though he wasn’t there — or rather, as though he was something very nasty that couldn’t understand them, like a slug."

memories.description: They seriously considered phoning Marge to take Dudley but Petunia says Marge hates me, so I'm not an option for them.
memories.source_text: "We could phone Marge," Uncle Vernon suggested. "Don’t be silly, Vernon, she hates the boy."

memories.description: I actually dared to say I could be left at home, imagining I might watch what I want on TV and maybe use Dudley's computer, which felt like a small win.
memories.source_text: "You could just leave me here," Harry put in hopefully

memories.description: He can shout at me for ages and then act like I'm nothing more than a servant. I won't pretend I'm unbothered by that.
memories.source_text: He shouted at Harry for about half an hour and then told him to go and make a cup of tea.

memories.description: I'm the one who gets sent off to make a cup of tea whenever he wants to show who's in charge. Fine, I made the tea.
memories.source_text: He told him to go and make a cup of tea.

memories.description: The post always turns up at the exact worst moment for me. I come back and there's the mail, dumped straight into Vernon's lap like it matters to him more than me.
memories.source_text: By the time he got back, the mail had arrived, right into Uncle Vernon’s lap.

memories.description: He ripped my letters up right in front of me. He actually tore them to pieces so I couldn't read them.
memories.source_text: "Uncle Vernon was tearing the letters into pieces before his eyes."

memories.description: He nailed the mail slot shut so letters can't get through. He's trying to stop any more from coming.
memories.source_text: "He stayed at home and nailed up the mail slot."

memories.description: He thinks blocking the mail will make whoever is sending the letters give up. That's ridiculous but that's what he's doing.
memories.source_text: "See," he explained to Aunt Petunia through a mouthful of nails, "if they can’t deliver them they’ll just give up."

memories.description: Uncle Vernon is actively against me getting those letters. I can't count on him to let me have them or to listen to me.
memories.source_text: "I want —" he began, but Uncle Vernon was tearing the letters into pieces before his eyes.

memories.description: So Voldemort tried to kill my parents and destroy our house and the curse failed on me. That is why people know my name.
memories.source_text: "That’s what yeh get when a powerful, evil curse touches yeh — took care of yer mum an’ dad an’ yer house, even — but it didn’t work on you, an’ that’s why yer famous, Harry."

memories.description: Dumbledore sent Hagrid to rescue me from the ruined house and hand me over to the Dursleys.
memories.source_text: "Took yeh from the ruined house myself, on Dumbledore’s orders. Brought yeh ter this lot . . ."

memories.description: Voldemort disappeared the same night he attacked us. Nobody knows exactly what happened to him.
memories.source_text: "Good question, Harry. Disappeared. Vanished. Same night he tried ter kill you."

memories.description: I thought I couldn't be a wizard, but all those weird things that happened when I was upset suddenly make sense. Maybe I am magical after all.
memories.source_text: "Not a wizard, eh? Never made things happen when you was scared or angry?"

memories.description: Hagrid cares about me and went out of his way to make sure I got my Hogwarts letters. He looks out for me.
memories.source_text: "I was allowed ter do a bit ter follow yeh an’ get yer letters to yeh an’ stuff — one o’ the reasons I was so keen ter take on the job —"

memories.description: Hagrid thinks the world of Dumbledore. Hogwarts and Dumbledore are very important and respected in the wizarding world.
memories.source_text: "NEVER — INSULT — ALBUS — DUMBLEDORE — IN — FRONT — OF — ME!"

memories.description: Hagrid tried to turn Dudley into a pig and actually made a pig's tail appear. Magic can happen right in front of the Dursleys.
memories.source_text: "Meant ter turn him into a pig, but I suppose he was so much like a pig anyway there wasn’t much left ter do."

memories.description: Vernon's keeping the letter away from me. He won't let me read it and he holds things up like that on purpose.
memories.source_text: Dudley tried to grab the letter to read it, but Uncle Vernon held it high out of his reach.

memories.description: Petunia actually read the letter. She looked shocked and I can tell whatever it said matters to them.
memories.source_text: Aunt Petunia took it curiously and read the first line.

memories.description: Something in that letter terrifies them. If Petunia reacts like that, this is not just ordinary post. I can't ignore this.
memories.source_text: For a moment it looked as though she might faint. She clutched her throat and made a choking noise. "Vernon! Oh my goodness Vernon!"

memories.description: A Muggle means nonmagic people. So the Dursleys are Muggles.
memories.source_text: "A Muggle," said Hagrid, "it’s what we call nonmagic folk like them."

memories.description: My mum was a witch and she went to that school. They all knew she was different.
memories.source_text: "Knew! Of course we knew! ... she got a letter just like that and disappeared off to that — that school — and came home every vacation with her pockets full of frog spawn, turning teacups into rats."

memories.description: They didn't die in a car crash. My parents were not killed by an accident.
memories.source_text: "CAR CRASH!" roared Hagrid ... "How could a car crash kill Lily an’ James Potter?"

memories.description: You-Know-Who came for my family and murdered Mum and Dad, and he tried to kill me as well.
memories.source_text: "You-Know-Who killed ’em. An’ then — an’ this is the real myst’ry of the thing — he tried to kill you, too."

memories.description: The wizard who did it is Voldemort. People are terrified to say his name.
memories.source_text: "All right — Voldemort."

memories.description: That lightning scar isn't an ordinary cut. It came from Voldemort's attack when he tried to kill me.
memories.source_text: "Never wondered how you got that mark on yer forehead? That was no ordinary cut."

memories.description: My parents were respected and talented witches and wizards. They were close to Dumbledore and well-regarded in the magical world.
memories.source_text: "Yer mum an’ dad were as good a witch an’ wizard as I ever knew."

memories.description: Owls expect payment for deliveries. I had to give the owl coins for dropping the newspaper.
memories.source_text: "Pay him," Hagrid grunted into the sofa. "He wants payin' fer deliverin' the paper. Look in the pockets."

memories.description: Hagrid's coat is full of pockets with all sorts of rubbish and odd coins. That's where I found the little bronze Knuts.
memories.source_text: Hagrid's coat seemed to be made of nothing but pockets — bunches of keys, slug pellets, balls of string, peppermint humbugs, teabags . . . finally, Harry pulled out a handful of strange-looking coins.

memories.description: I'm over the moon; I'm so happy I could burst. Everything feels brilliant right now.
memories.source_text: "The hut was full of sunlight, the storm was over... he felt as though a large balloon was swelling inside him."

memories.description: Five Knuts is the right payment for the paper. I counted out five little bronze coins and paid the owl.
memories.source_text: "Give him five Knuts," said Hagrid sleepily. "Knuts?" "The little bronze ones."

memories.description: Owls can be stubborn and a bit fierce when they're doing their job. This one snapped at me until I paid it.
memories.source_text: "There’s an owl —"

memories.description: Hagrid introduced himself as Rubeus Hagrid and said he works at Hogwarts. I know someone from that place actually came for me.
memories.source_text: Rubeus Hagrid, Keeper of Keys and Grounds at Hogwarts.

memories.description: Hagrid told me I'm a wizard. Me. I couldn't believe it at first, but that means my life isn't the same as the Dursleys'.
memories.source_text: Harry, yer a wizard.

memories.description: I have a letter saying I've been accepted to Hogwarts. School starts September 1 and they expect my owl by July 31.
memories.source_text: We are pleased to inform you that you have been accepted at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry.

memories.description: Hagrid said I look like my dad and have my mum's eyes. That made me feel like my parents were real people, not just names.
memories.source_text: Yeh look a lot like yer dad, but yeh've got yer mum's eyes.

memories.description: Hagrid exploded at the Dursleys for hiding Dumbledore's letter from me. I now know the Dursleys kept important things from me on purpose.
memories.source_text: You never told him? Never told him what was in the letter Dumbledore left fer him? I was there! I saw Dumbledore leave it, Dursley!

memories.description: Before today I thought my life would always be locked in that hut. Now I know there's a whole different world waiting for me and I actually get to go.
memories.source_text: They await your owl by no later than July 31.

memories.description: Hagrid wrote a note to Dumbledore saying he gave me the letter. Someone important knows I'm coming.
memories.source_text: Given Harry his letter.

memories.description: Hagrid gave me a squashed chocolate cake for my birthday. He tried to be kind in his own rough way and I was starving, so it meant a lot.
memories.source_text: I mighta sat on it at some point, but it'll taste all right.

memories.description: I'm right-handed. That's the arm to use when finding a wand.
memories.source_text: "Which is your wand arm?" "Er — well, I’m right-handed," said Harry.

memories.description: Wands have cores like unicorn hair, phoenix feather, or dragon heartstring and no two wands are the same.
memories.source_text: "Every Ollivander wand has a core of a powerful magical substance, Mr Potter. We use unicorn hairs, phoenix tail feathers, and the heartstrings of dragons."

memories.description: Using someone else's wand won't work properly. A wand needs to match its owner.
memories.source_text: "And of course, you will never get such good results with another wizard’s wand."

memories.description: When a wand fits me, I can feel warmth in my fingers and it will respond spectacularly, like shooting sparks.
memories.source_text: "He felt a sudden warmth in his fingers. He raised the wand above his head, brought it swishing down through the dusty air and a stream of red and gold sparks shot from the end like a firework"

memories.description: Magic sometimes happens on its own. Things around me can act without anyone touching them.
memories.source_text: "That will do," he said, and the tape measure crumpled into a heap on the floor.

memories.description: I don't know, sir. Snape thinks I should have every bit of book-learning memorized and he enjoys throwing that at me. He expects me to remember stuff from One Thousand Magical Herbs and Fungi and uses it to needle me.
memories.source_text: "I don't know, sir." "Thought you wouldn't open a book before coming, eh, Potter?"

memories.description: I can't let Malfoy and his goons get under my skin. They're laughing to wind me up, so I force myself to keep my eyes on Snape and not give them the satisfaction.
memories.source_text: He tried not to look at Malfoy, Crabbe, and Goyle, who were shaking with laughter.

memories.description: I thought I was completely skint and Vernon would never pay, but that isn’t true anymore. I’m not ruined.
memories.source_text: I haven’t got any money and you heard Uncle Vernon last night he won’t pay for me to go and learn magic

memories.description: My parents didn’t keep their money at home. Their gold’s at Gringotts, so there’s something for me there.
memories.source_text: They didn’ keep their gold in the house, boy! Nah, first stop fer us is Gringotts

memories.description: My mum had a ten and a quarter inch willow wand, swishy and good for charm work. And people still say I have her eyes.
memories.source_text: "You have your mother's eyes. It seems only yesterday she was in here herself, buying her first wand. Ten and a quarter inches long, swishy, made of willow. Nice wand for charm work."

memories.description: Dad's wand was mahogany, eleven inches, pliable and better for transfiguration. It sounds like it suited him.
memories.source_text: "Your father, on the other hand, favored a mahogany wand. Eleven inches. Pliable. A little more power and excellent for transfiguration."

memories.description: Wands don't just belong to people, they choose them. It's the wand that chooses the wizard, not the other way around.
memories.source_text: "Well, I say your father favored it — it’s really the wand that chooses the wizard, of course."

memories.description: Ollivander sold the wand that caused my scar. It was thirteen and a half inches, made of yew, and he says it was very powerful and dangerous in the wrong hands.
memories.source_text: "I’m sorry to say I sold the wand that did it," "Thirteen-and-a-half inches. Yew. Powerful wand, very powerful, and in the wrong hands ..."

memories.description: Hagrid's wand was oak, sixteen inches and bendy. They snapped it when he was expelled, though Hagrid keeps the pieces and doesn't use them.
memories.source_text: "Oak, sixteen inches, rather bendy, wasn’t it?" "It was, sir, yes," "Good wand, that one. But I suppose they snapped it in half when you got expelled?"

memories.description: Ollivander knew who I was before I even said much. He treats me like someone important and seems to remember my parents, especially my mum.
memories.source_text: "Yes, yes. I thought I’d be seeing you soon. Harry Potter."

memories.description: Right, the train leaves from platform nine and three quarters at eleven. I have to find that weird platform.
memories.source_text: "I just take the train from platform nine and three-quarters at eleven o'clock," he read.

memories.description: I do not actually know where Hogwarts is on a map. I just follow the train.
memories.source_text: "I don't know," said Harry, realizing this for the first time.

memories.description: The Dursleys are sneering at me and left me at the station. They are not on my side.
memories.source_text: "Have a good term," said Uncle Vernon with an even nastier smile. He left without another word.

memories.description: Hedwig is safe in her cage and coming with me. She's the reason I'm getting weird looks here.
memories.source_text: "He checked his Hogwarts list yet again to make sure he had everything he needed, saw that Hedwig was shut safely in her cage,"

memories.description: Okay, I have to walk straight at the barrier between nine and ten and not hesitate. If I run at it, I'll get through.
memories.source_text: "Don't stop and don't be scared you’ll crash into it, that's very important. Best do it at a bit of a run if you're nervous."

memories.description: We're at King’s Cross with plenty of time. I will change on the train, not here in front of everyone.
memories.source_text: "They reached King’s Cross at half past ten."

memories.description: I found out there's a fortune in my vault that the Dursleys never told me about. I couldn't believe it!
memories.source_text: All Harry’s — it was incredible. The Dursleys couldn’t have known about this or they’d have had it from him faster than blinking. How often had they complained how much Harry cost them to keep? And all the time there had been a small fortune belonging to him, buried deep under London.

memories.description: Galleons are the gold coins. Seventeen Sickles make a Galleon and twenty-nine Knuts make a Sickle. That's how the money works.
memories.source_text: “The gold ones are Galleons,” he explained. “Seventeen silver Sickles to a Galleon and twenty-nine Knuts to a Sickle, it’s easy enough.

memories.description: My vault is number seven hundred and thirteen. The goblins only do one speed when they go through Gringotts.
memories.source_text: “Vault seven hundred and thirteen now, please, and can we go more slowly?” “One speed only,” said Griphook.

memories.description: There's a shop called Flourish and Blotts that sells all sorts of weird wizarding books. I could have spent ages there.
memories.source_text: They bought Harry’s school books in a shop called Flourish and Blotts where the shelves were stacked to the ceiling with books as large as paving stones bound in leather; books the size of postage stamps in covers of silk; books full of peculiar symbols and a few books with nothing in them at all.

memories.description: I wanted to curse Dudley, but Hagrid reminded me I can't use magic in the Muggle world unless it's really necessary and I couldn't do those curses yet anyway. Fine, I'll wait and learn properly.
memories.source_text: “I was trying to find out how to curse Dudley.” “I’m not sayin’ that’s not a good idea, but yer not ter use magic in the Muggle world except in very special circumstances,” said Hagrid. “An’ anyway, yeh couldn’ work any of them curses yet, yeh’ll need a lot more study before yeh get ter that level.”

memories.description: I can't just buy a solid gold cauldron because my list says pewter. I did get scales and a collapsible telescope though.
memories.source_text: Hagrid wouldn’t let Harry buy a solid gold cauldron, either (“It says pewter on yer list”), but they got a nice set of scales for weighing potion ingredients and a collapsible brass telescope.

memories.description: The Apothecary smells awful but it's full of strange potion ingredients. Unicorn horns cost twenty-one Galleons each and beetle eyes are five Knuts a scoop.
memories.source_text: Then they visited the Apothecary, which was fascinating enough to make up for its horrible smell, a mixture of bad eggs and rotted cabbages.

memories.description: Hagrid's going to get me an owl for a birthday present, and Ollivanders is the only place for wands. I have to get the best wand there.
memories.source_text: “Don’ mention it,” said Hagrid gruffly. “Don’ expect you’ve had a lotta presents from them Dursleys. Just Ollivanders left now — only place fer wands, Ollivanders, and yeh gotta have the best wand.”

memories.description: Ollivanders is this tiny, ancient shop that makes wands. Getting a wand is what I've been waiting for.
memories.source_text: A magic wand . . . this was what Harry had been really looking forward to. The last shop was narrow and shabby. Peeling gold letters over the door read Ollivanders: Makers of Fine Wands since 382 B.C. A single wand lay on a faded purple cushion in the dusty window.

memories.description: I didn't know the difference between monkshood and wolfsbane, but I was sure Hermione did and I pushed Snape to ask her.
memories.source_text: "I don't know," said Harry quietly. "I think Hermione does, though, why don't you try her?"

memories.description: Snape is hostile toward Hermione. He ignored her and snapped at her in front of the class, and I noticed that.
memories.source_text: "Sit down," he snapped at Hermione.

memories.description: Dumbledore stands out in a crowd; his silver hair shines like the ghosts. I spotted him straight away.
memories.source_text: Dumbledore’s silver hair was the only thing in the whole hall that shone as brightly as the ghosts.

memories.description: Quirrell is that nervous bloke from the Leaky Cauldron and he wears a big purple turban. That looks odd.
memories.source_text: Harry spotted Professor Quirrell, too, the nervous young man from the Leaky Cauldron. He was looking very peculiar in a large purple turban.

memories.description: The Sorting Hat put me in Gryffindor. That's where I belong.
memories.source_text: a second later the hat had shouted, “GRYFFINDOR!”

memories.description: Ron got sorted into Gryffindor with me. I was relieved and clapped my head off when it happened.
memories.source_text: He was pale green by now. Harry crossed his fingers under the table and a second later the hat had shouted, “GRYFFINDOR!” Harry clapped loudly with the rest as Ron collapsed into the chair next to him.

memories.description: The feast is mental; there's more food than I ever imagined and everything tastes brilliant. I'm not used to being able to eat as much as I want.
memories.source_text: I had never seen so many things I liked to eat on one table: roast beef, roast chicken, pork chops and lamb chops, sausages, bacon and steak, boiled potatoes, roast potatoes, fries, Yorkshire pudding, peas, carrots, gravy, ketchup, and, for some strange reason, peppermint humbugs.

memories.description: The Gryffindor ghost is Sir Nicholas de Mimsy-Porpington, though everyone calls him Nearly Headless Nick.
memories.source_text: “Sir Nicholas de Mimsy-Porpington at your service. Resident ghost of Gryffindor Tower.”

memories.description: The awful ghost over at Slytherin is called the Bloody Baron. He's horribly covered in silver blood and sits with the Slytherins.
memories.source_text: The Bloody Baron’s becoming almost unbearable — he’s the Slytherin ghost.

memories.description: Nearly Headless Nick was badly beheaded; his head swings off on a hinge. It's gruesome and weird.
memories.source_text: Someone had obviously tried to behead him, but not done it properly.

memories.description: A bezoar? I haven't got the faintest idea what a bezoar is.
memories.source_text: "Let’s try again. Potter, where would you look if I told you to find me a bezoar?"

memories.description: I got sorted into Gryffindor. I was desperate not to go to Slytherin and I said it straight to myself: not Slytherin. The hat argued with me but then shouted GRYFFINDOR and everyone went mental.
memories.source_text: ["Not Slytherin, eh?" said the small voice. "Are you sure? You could be great, you know, it’s all here in your head, and Slytherin will help you on the way to greatness, no doubt about that—no? Well, if you’re sure—better be GRYFFINDOR!"]

memories.description: Everyone knows who I am. I walked up and the whole hall started whispering like I was some kind of spectacle. That made everything feel twice as scary.
memories.source_text: ["Potter, Harry!" As Harry stepped forward, whispers suddenly broke out like little hissing fires all over the hall. "Potter, did she say?" "The Harry Potter?"]

memories.description: Percy acted proper and shook my hand like he mattered, and Fred and George went nuts shouting that they'd got me. I felt oddly welcome with the Weasleys right away.
memories.source_text: ["Percy the Prefect got up and shook his hand vigorously, while the Weasley twins yelled, "We got Potter! We got Potter!" ]

memories.description: I sat opposite that ghost in the ruff and when he patted my arm it felt like I'd plunged my hand into freezing water. That was creepy as anything.
memories.source_text: ["The ghost patted his arm, giving Harry the sudden, horrible feeling he'd just plunged it into a bucket of ice-cold water."]

memories.description: Hagrid caught my eye and gave me a thumbs up. That sort of made me grin; he's good to have on your side.
memories.source_text: ["Hagrid, who caught his eye and gave him the thumbs up."]

memories.description: My wand has a phoenix feather and that same phoenix gave another feather to another wand. That other wand is the one that gave me my scar.
memories.source_text: “I remember every wand I’ve ever sold, Mr Potter. Every single wand. It so happens that the phoenix whose tail feather is in your wand, gave another feather — just one other. It is very curious indeed that you should be destined for this wand when its brother — why, its brother gave you that scar.”

memories.description: People expect big things from me just because the wand chose me. I don’t feel like I deserve that and it scares me.
memories.source_text: “The wand chooses the wizard, remember. . . . I think we must expect great things from you, Mr Potter. . . . After all, He-Who-Must-Not-Be-Named did great things — terrible, yes, but great.”

memories.description: My wand is thirteen and a half inches long and made of yew.
memories.source_text: “Yes, thirteen-and-a-half inches. Yew. Curious indeed how these things happen.”

memories.description: I’m famous for something I can’t remember and I don’t know magic yet. Being famous feels worthless when I don’t even know why people care.
memories.source_text: “Everyone thinks I’m special,” he said at last. “All those people in the Leaky Cauldron, Professor Quirrell, Mr Ollivander . . . but I don’t know anything about magic at all. How can they expect great things? I’m famous and I can’t even remember what I’m famous for. I don’t know what happened when Vol-, sorry — I mean, the night my parents died.”

memories.description: Hagrid’s on my side. He’ll help me get to Hogwarts and gave me the ticket. If the Dursleys give me trouble I can write to him and he’ll find me.
memories.source_text: “Don’ you worry, Harry. You’ll learn fast enough. Everyone starts at the beginning at Hogwarts, you’ll be just fine. Just be yerself. I know it’s hard. Yeh’ve been singled out, an’ that’s always hard. But yeh’ll have a great time at Hogwarts — I did — still do, ’smatter of fact.” Hagrid helped Harry on to the train that would take him back to the Dursleys, then handed him an envelope. “Yer ticket fer Hogwarts,” he said. “First o’ September — King’s Cross — it’s all on yer ticket. Any problems with the Dursleys, send me a letter with yer owl, she’ll know where to find me. . . . See yeh soon, Harry.”

memories.description: That look from the hook-nosed teacher made my scar burn. It hurt, plain and simple, and whatever he felt about me was bad news.
memories.source_text: "Ouch!"

memories.description: I don’t trust that bloke talking to Quirrell. He makes me feel like he hates me, and he did something to my scar. I’ll keep an eye on him.
memories.source_text: "Who’s that teacher talking to Professor Quirrell?"

memories.description: When Dumbledore said the third-floor corridor is out of bounds if you don’t want to die a very painful death, I laughed because it sounded mad, but it could be serious. Still, it sounded like the sort of thing Dumbledore might be playing at.
memories.source_text: "He’s not serious?"

memories.description: I like treacle tart. Also, while we were eating I was watching the teachers and paying attention to how people acted, especially that greasy-haired teacher.
memories.source_text: As Harry helped himself to a treacle tart, the talk turned to their families.

memories.description: They know who I am. I can feel everyone staring at my scar and I’m not sure I like it.
memories.source_text: “Harry Potter,” chorused the twins.

memories.description: There’s proper wizard sweet stuff on the train. I’ve got pockets full of galleons and I’m going to try as much as I can.
memories.source_text: What she did have were Bertie Bott’s Every Flavor Beans, Drooble’s Best Blowing Gum, Chocolate Frogs, Pumpkin Pasties, Cauldron Cakes, Licorice Wands, and a number of other strange things Harry had never seen in his life.

memories.description: I shared my food with Ron. It felt... good. Like I’m not on my own for once.
memories.source_text: “Go on, have a pasty,” said Harry, who had never had anything to share before or, indeed, anyone to share it with.

memories.description: Chocolate Frogs have cards inside them with famous witches and wizards. I just opened one and the card shows some old wizard with silver hair.
memories.source_text: “I’m missing Agrippa.”

memories.description: He just told me he'd take a point from Gryffindor for my cheek. Great — one more reason to watch Snape like a hawk.
memories.source_text: “And a point will be taken from Gryffindor House for your cheek, Potter.”

memories.description: Snape's always on at everyone, but he clearly gives Malfoy special treatment. He likes him more than he pretends to.
memories.source_text: criticizing almost everyone except Malfoy, whom he seemed to like.

memories.description: Potions can go horribly wrong fast — that green smoke and hissing showed how dangerous a simple lesson can become.
memories.source_text: clouds of acid green smoke and a loud hissing filled the dungeon.

memories.description: I'm the new Seeker. I'm probably the youngest House player in about a century.
memories.source_text: “Seeker?” he said. “But first years never — you must be the youngest House player in about —” “— a century,” said Harry, shoveling pie into his mouth.

memories.description: Wood told me he picked me. That means he trusts my ability.
memories.source_text: “Wood told me.”

memories.description: I start training next week and Wood wants it kept quiet for now. I won't blab.
memories.source_text: “I start training next week,” said Harry. “Only don’t tell anyone, Wood wants to keep it a secret.”

memories.description: Fred and George know and they're pleased. They've got my back on the team as Beaters.
memories.source_text: Fred and George Weasley now came into the hall, spotted Harry, and hurried over. “Well done,” said George in a low voice. “Wood told us. We’re on the team too — Beaters.”

memories.description: I won't be intimidated by Malfoy. I can handle his taunts without losing my cool.
memories.source_text: “You’re a lot braver now that you’re back on the ground and you’ve got your little friends with you,” said Harry coolly.

memories.description: I am furious and embarrassed. The last thing I wanted was to make a fool of myself on a broom in front of Malfoy.
memories.source_text: "Typical," said Harry darkly. "Just what I always wanted. To make a fool of myself on a broomstick in front of Malfoy."

memories.description: I was really eager to learn to fly. I wanted it more than anything.
memories.source_text: "He had been looking forward to learning to fly more than anything else."

memories.description: Neville's never flown a broom. His gran never let him near one and I think he is awful clumsy on dry land.
memories.source_text: "Neville had never been on a broomstick in his life, because his grandmother had never let him near one."

memories.description: Hermione is surprisingly nervous about flying. You can't learn it from a book, and even she knows that.
memories.source_text: "Hermione Granger was almost as nervous about flying as Neville was."

memories.description: Malfoy gets constant letters and treats from home and he loves showing off them at the table. It winds me up.
memories.source_text: "Malfoy’s eagle owl was always bringing him packages of sweets from home, which he opened gloatingly at the Slytherin table."

memories.description: Malfoy will grab stuff from people just to be nasty. He nicked Neville's Remembrall right out of his hand.
memories.source_text: "Malfoy’s got my Remembrall, Professor."

memories.description: My broom listens to me and actually obeys. That one behaved straight away when I said Up.
memories.source_text: "Harry’s broom jumped into his hand at once, but it was one of the few that did."

memories.description: Neville panics on a broom. He's terrified of flying and that fear can make things go badly wrong.
memories.source_text: "Neville was rising straight up like a cork shot out of a bottle — twelve feet — twenty feet."

memories.description: McGonagall spots trouble fast and steps in before things get out of hand. I know she'll act when needed.
memories.source_text: "Well, what are you all waiting for?" she barked. "Everyone stand by a broomstick. Come on, hurry up."

memories.description: I'm not going to blow up the house. I said it straight and meant it, even if nobody's listening.
memories.source_text: "I won't blow up the house"

memories.description: They panic the moment company arrives and will put Dudley first every time, no matter what I say.
memories.source_text: "Oh, good Lord, they're here!" said Aunt Petunia frantically

memories.description: Dudley fakes tears to get what he wants. He'll put on that show and Mum will fall for it every time.
memories.source_text: Dudley began to cry loudly

memories.description: The Bludgers are nasty, jet black balls that rocket about trying to knock players off their brooms.
memories.source_text: "These two are the Bludgers."

memories.description: Beaters' job is to hit the Bludgers away from our team and send them at the other side. The Weasley twins are our Beaters.
memories.source_text: "That’s why you have two Beaters on each team — the Weasley twins are ours — it’s their job to protect their side from the Bludgers and try and knock them toward the other team."

memories.description: I'm the Seeker. My main job is to catch the Golden Snitch, not bother with the Quaffle or the Bludgers most of the time.
memories.source_text: "Now, the last member of the team is the Seeker. That’s you."

memories.description: Okay, fine, the Bludgers can actually be dangerous to me too. I could get seriously hurt if one hits me.
memories.source_text: "— unless they crack my head open."

memories.description: They move fast and unpredictably; when one charged me I had to swing the club to stop it from smashing my face in.
memories.source_text: "I’m going to show you what the Bludgers do."

memories.description: Bludgers have caused broken jaws at Hogwarts, but nobody's ever been killed by them here.
memories.source_text: "Never at Hogwarts. We’ve had a couple of broken jaws but nothing worse than that."

memories.description: The Snitch is tiny, gold with little silver wings, about the size of a walnut, and it's ridiculously fast and hard to spot. Catching it is the key to winning.
memories.source_text: "This is the Golden Snitch... It’s very hard to catch because it’s so fast and difficult to see."

memories.description: The Weasley twins are tough and fearless on the pitch; I can count on them to deal with the Bludgers for our side.
memories.source_text: "The Weasleys are more than a match for the Bludgers — I mean, they’re like a pair of human Bludgers themselves."

memories.description: It's my choice to go or not. I don't need anyone policing me about what I do at night.
memories.source_text: "And it's really none of your business,"

memories.description: Wood told me to hang back until I can actually see the Snitch. Stay out of trouble until the moment I need to act.
memories.source_text: "Keep out of the way until you catch sight of the Snitch," Wood had said.

memories.description: A Bludger came flying at me like a cannonball and I had to dodge it. I can handle that kind of thing and Fred will chase after the Bludger.
memories.source_text: Once a Bludger decided to come pelting his way, more like a cannonball than anything, but Harry dodged it and Fred Weasley came chasing after it.

memories.description: There was a flash of gold by Pucey's ear and I actually saw the Snitch. That's the moment I had to go for it.
memories.source_text: A murmur ran through the crowd as Adrian Pucey dropped the Quaffle, too busy looking over his shoulder at the flash of gold that had passed his left ear. Harry saw it.

memories.description: I’m going out onto the field in an hour. Right now I need to get ready and keep my strength.
memories.source_text: "In an hour’s time he’d be walking onto the field."

memories.description: Seamus thinks Seekers take a lot of hits. Fine, then I’ll be careful and keep myself geared up. I don’t want to get flattened out there.
memories.source_text: "Harry, you need your strength," said Seamus Finnigan. "Seekers are always the ones who get clobbered by the other team."

memories.description: Everyone’s already up and flying. The match has started and Angelina’s on it right away with the Quaffle.
memories.source_text: "Mount your brooms, please." "And the Quaffle is taken immediately by Angelina Johnson of Gryffindor — what an excellent Chaser that"

memories.description: Seamus looks out for me in his blunt way. I appreciate it, even if he’s more interested in his sausages than the game.
memories.source_text: "Thanks, Seamus," said Harry, watching Seamus pile ketchup on his sausages.

memories.description: Dumbledore is the Headmaster and people reckon he's the greatest wizard of modern times. Of course he'd be on a Chocolate Frog card.
memories.source_text: ALBUS DUMBLEDORE CURRENTLY HEADMASTER OF HOGWARTS Considered by many the greatest wizard of modern times

memories.description: Photos in the wizarding world move. That is mental. Muggle pictures do not do that at all.
memories.source_text: But in, you know, the Muggle world, people just stay put in photos.

memories.description: These Chocolate Frog cards are collectible and people swap duplicates. I can start a proper collection.
memories.source_text: He’ll be back. No, I’ve got Morgana again and I’ve got about six of her

memories.description: Bertie Bott's really does make every flavour. You can get proper disgusting ones like spinach and liver. Watch out.
memories.source_text: When they say every flavor, they mean every flavor

memories.description: People still panic when You-Know-Who might be involved. Saying his name makes me nervous now.
memories.source_text: ’Course, everyone gets scared when something like this happens in case You-Know-Who’s behind it.

memories.description: After Hogwarts people go off and do proper wizarding jobs. Charlie studies dragons. Bill works for Gringotts overseas.
memories.source_text: Charlie’s in Romania studying dragons, and Bill’s in Africa doing something for Gringotts

memories.description: I don't follow any Quidditch teams yet. I don't know which side I'd support.
memories.source_text: What’s your Quidditch team? "Er — I don’t know any," Harry confessed.

memories.description: Flint nearly took me out with that Bludger. Spinnet took the penalty for Gryffindor so we kept the Quaffle, but that was way too close for comfort.
memories.source_text: "Flint nearly kills the Gryffindor Seeker, which could happen to anyone, I’m sure, so a penalty to Gryffindor, taken by Spinnet, who puts it away, no trouble, and we continue play, Gryffindor still in possession."

memories.description: My broom acted like it wanted me off it, not normal at all. It felt like someone was messing with it, trying to throw me. I held on tight because I was not falling off that thing.
memories.source_text: His broom gave a sudden, frightening lurch. For a split second, he thought he was going to fall. He gripped the broom tightly with both his hands and knees. He’d never felt anything like that. It happened again. It was as though the broom was trying to buck him off.

memories.description: Give it here! I'm not letting him keep it. I'm going after Malfoy and I won't back down.
memories.source_text: "Give it here!" Harry yelled, but Malfoy had leapt onto his broomstick and taken off.

memories.description: If he doesn't hand it over I'm going to take him off that broom. I'm not messing about.
memories.source_text: "Give it here," Harry called, "or I'll knock you off that broom!"

memories.description: Flying is brilliant. I can do this without lessons. It's natural to me and it feels amazing.
memories.source_text: He mounted the broom and kicked hard against the ground and up, up he soared; air rushed through his hair, and his robes whipped out behind him — and in a rush of fierce joy he realized he’d found something he could do without being taught — this was easy, this was wonderful.

memories.description: I can take Malfoy on. He might be smart on the ground, but up here I've got the advantage.
memories.source_text: He turned his broomstick sharply to face Malfoy in midair. Malfoy looked stunned.

memories.description: I wasn't looking at its feet — I was too busy with its heads.
memories.source_text: "The floor?" Harry suggested. "I wasn’t looking at its feet, I was too busy with its heads."

memories.description: Mind your own business. I'm not having this argued about when there's something else going on.
memories.source_text: "And it’s really none of your business," said Harry.

memories.description: Keep quiet and pay attention. I heard something and we need to move now.
memories.source_text: "Shut up, both of you!" said Harry sharply. "I heard something."

memories.description: The Fat Lady's away and the usual password won't get us in. We're locked out unless she comes back.
memories.source_text: "Keep your voice down, Neville. The password’s ‘Pig snout’ but it won’t help you now, the Fat Lady’s gone off somewhere."

memories.description: Move quietly and stick together. I tried to lead them away when Filch was nearby.
memories.source_text: "This way!" Harry mouthed to the others and, petrified, they began to creep down a long gallery full of suits of armor.

memories.description: Filch is searching the area and thinks we might be hiding nearby. We’re in serious danger of being caught.
memories.source_text: "They’re in here somewhere," Filch muttered.

memories.description: The key is in the lock and I can grab it and lock the door. Do that and we can trap the troll.
memories.source_text: "The key's in the lock," Harry muttered.

memories.description: The scream came from the girls' bathroom and Hermione must be in there. I have to get back in, even if it's the last thing I want to do.
memories.source_text: "It's the girls' bathroom!" Harry gasped.

memories.description: If you throw something loud at the troll it will stop and give Hermione a chance. I can act fast and use whatever's to hand to distract it.
memories.source_text: "Confuse it!" Harry said desperately to Ron, and, seizing a tap, he threw it as hard as he could against the wall.

memories.description: It's a Nimbus Two Thousand. That's the real deal, not some cheap broom.
memories.source_text: "It’s not any old broomstick," he said, "it’s a Nimbus Two Thousand."

memories.description: I said it was thanks to Malfoy. I told people that to wind him up and because McGonagall sorted it all out for me.
memories.source_text: "And it’s really thanks to Malfoy here that I’ve got it," he added.

memories.description: Quidditch rules: seven players per side, three Chasers who use the Quaffle to score through the hoops.
memories.source_text: "Now, Quidditch is easy enough to understand, even if it’s not too easy to play. There are seven players on each side. Three of them are called Chasers."

memories.description: I'm the Keeper for Gryffindor. I have to fly around our hoops and stop the other team from scoring.
memories.source_text: "Now, there’s another player on each side who’s called the Keeper — I’m Keeper for Gryffindor."

memories.description: I couldn't focus on lessons because all I could think about was my new broom and learning to play Quidditch.
memories.source_text: "Harry had a lot of trouble keeping his mind on his lessons that day. It kept wandering up to the dormitory where his new broomstick was lying under his bed..."

memories.description: A troll is in the castle, down in the dungeons. A proper alarm, we need to act fast.
memories.source_text: Troll — in the dungeons — thought you ought to know.

memories.description: Hermione has no idea there's a troll loose. I have to tell her, now.
memories.source_text: She doesn't know about the troll.

memories.description: What the hell, a troll somehow got inside Hogwarts. This is worse than I thought.
memories.source_text: How could a troll get in?

memories.description: I put out Seamus's flaming feather with my hat. Honestly, I did what needed doing without fuss.
memories.source_text: Seamus got so impatient that he prodded it with his wand and set fire to it — Harry had to put it out with his hat.

memories.description: Hermione can do the charm properly. She made the feather float like it was nothing.
memories.source_text: Hermione rolled up the sleeves of her gown, flicked her wand, and said, “Wingardium Leviosa!” Their feather rose off the desk and hovered about four feet above their heads.

memories.description: I saw Hermione in tears in the corridor. That hit me — she isn't all right and she's on her own.
memories.source_text: Harry caught a glimpse of her face — and was startled to see that she was in tears.

memories.description: I had to act fast and throw something to distract the troll. Quick, direct action can work when there's no time to think.
memories.source_text: "Confuse it!"

memories.description: When someone freezes with fear, shouting and pulling can be the only way to get them moving. I won't leave people behind if I can help it.
memories.source_text: "Come on, run, run!"

memories.description: The troll wasn't dead, just knocked out. Dangerous things can look finished but still be a threat.
memories.source_text: "I don't think so," said Harry

memories.description: I can do something that looks stupid and it might still work. Bravery and a bit of luck go a long way.
memories.source_text: Harry's wand had still been in his hand when he'd jumped — it had gone straight up one of the troll's nostrils.

memories.description: Getting close to a troll is disgusting. Troll snot is the worst.
memories.source_text: "Urgh – troll boogers."

memories.description: My broom has gone completely out of control. I can't steer it and it keeps throwing me around. This is dangerous and I need to get it under control now.
memories.source_text: He couldn’t turn it. He couldn’t direct it at all. It was zigzagging through the air, and every now and then making violent swishing movements that almost unseated him.

memories.description: Nobody else seems to see how badly my broom is acting. I'm on my own with this mess.
memories.source_text: No one seemed to have noticed that Harry’s broom was behaving strangely.

memories.description: Slytherin managed to score while I'm struggling. The other team and the commentators are focused on the play, not on what's happening to me.
memories.source_text: Slytherin in possession, Flint with the Quaffle, passes Spinnet, passes Bell, hit hard in the face by a Bludger, hope it broke his nose, only joking, Professor, Slytherins score, oh no

memories.description: Flint shoved me on purpose! My broom spun out and I was hanging on for dear life.
memories.source_text: Marcus Flint had blocked Harry on purpose, and Harry’s broom spun off course, Harry holding on for dear life.

memories.description: Higgs saw the Snitch too and was neck and neck with me. I was faster but he was right on my tail.
memories.source_text: In a great rush of excitement he dived downward after the streak of gold. Slytherin Seeker Terence Higgs had seen it, too. Neck and neck they hurtled toward the Snitch — all the Chasers seemed to have forgotten what they were supposed to be doing as they hung in midair to watch.

memories.description: Hooch saw Flint's foul and called it. She gave us a free shot at the goalposts.
memories.source_text: Madam Hooch spoke angrily to Flint and then ordered a free shot at the goalposts for Gryffindor.

memories.description: Everyone down below thought it was a foul. I know I was cheated and I want a proper chance to catch that Snitch.
memories.source_text: "Foul!" screamed the Gryffindors.

memories.description: He tried to get past that three-headed dog at Halloween. He's after whatever the dog is guarding and I reckon he even let that troll in to make a diversion. I wouldn't put anything past him.
memories.source_text: "You know what this means?" he finished breathlessly. "He tried to get past that three-headed dog at Halloween! That’s where he was going when we saw him — he’s after whatever it’s guarding! And I’d bet my broomstick he let that troll in, to make a diversion!"

memories.description: I couldn't eat. I felt awful and had no appetite.
memories.source_text: "I don't want anything."

memories.description: I managed to clamber back onto my broom mid-air. Right then I just got back to it, no messing about.
memories.source_text: Up in the air, Harry was suddenly able to clamber back on to his broom.

memories.description: I caught the Snitch. I nearly swallowed it and I landed rough, but I’ve got it and Gryffindor won.
memories.source_text: "I've got the Snitch!"

memories.description: He's jinxing my broom. I'm fighting to stay on and it's getting worse — I can barely hang on, and everyone's watching me like I'm about to fall.
memories.source_text: "He’s doing something — jinxing the broom," said Hermione.

memories.description: I found the Mirror of Erised. It shows me what I want most, not facts or truth.
memories.source_text: "you, like hundreds before you, have discovered the delights of the Mirror of Erised."

memories.description: The mirror reflects the deepest desire of your heart. It can trick you into thinking those visions are real.
memories.source_text: "It shows us nothing more or less than the deepest, most desperate desire of our hearts."

memories.description: I can't let myself get lost in what the mirror shows. Dwelling on dreams can ruin you.
memories.source_text: "However, this mirror will give us neither knowledge or truth. Men have wasted away before it, entranced by what they have seen, or been driven mad"

memories.description: They're moving the mirror tomorrow and I must not go searching for it again.
memories.source_text: "The Mirror will be moved to a new home tomorrow, Harry, and I ask you not to go looking for it again."

memories.description: Dumbledore knew I was there even when I thought I was hidden. He sees things I can't hide from him.
memories.source_text: "I don't need a cloak to become invisible," said Dumbledore gently.

memories.description: Fluffy belongs to Hagrid. He bought the three-headed dog from a Greek bloke in a pub and lent him to Dumbledore to guard something.
memories.source_text: “Fluffy?” “Yeah — he’s mine — bought him off a Greek chappie I met in the pub las’ year — I lent him to Dumbledore to guard the —”

memories.description: Snape might be after whatever Fluffy is guarding. I’m worried he’s involved and might be dangerous.
memories.source_text: “But Snape’s trying to steal it.”

memories.description: Neville matters to me. I gave him my last Chocolate Frog to show him he’s worth more than Malfoy and I’ll back him up. The Sorting Hat put him in Gryffindor, not some cowardly Slytherin.
memories.source_text: “You’re worth twelve of Malfoy,” Harry said. “The Sorting Hat chose you for Gryffindor, didn’t it? And where’s Malfoy? In stinking Slytherin.”

memories.description: Malfoy attacked Neville outside the library and was looking for someone to pick on. He’s the sort of bloke who goes after people.
memories.source_text: “Malfoy,” said Neville shakily. “I met him outside the library. He said he’d been looking for someone to practice that on.”

memories.description: I'm onto this Nicolas Flamel thing and I'm trying to find out who he is. We've been through loads of books looking for him.
memories.source_text: "Oh, we’re not working," Harry told him brightly. "Ever since you mentioned Nicolas Flamel we’ve been trying to find out who he is."

memories.description: Someone sent me this cloak and a note saying Merry Christmas. I feel weird about it. It might have belonged to my dad, and I can't stop thinking who gave it to me.
memories.source_text: A Very Merry Christmas to you There was no signature. Harry stared at the note. Ron was admiring the Cloak.

memories.description: So Nicolas Flamel made the Sorcerer's Stone. Of course Hermione would know that.
memories.source_text: "Nicolas Flamel," she whispered dramatically, "is the only known maker of the Sorcerer’s Stone!"

memories.description: Snape thinks students must not know about the Stone. That means it's important and secret.
memories.source_text: "Students aren't supposed to know about the Sorcerer’s Stone, after all."

memories.description: Snape is openly threatening Quirrell and trying to intimidate him. He and Quirrell are at odds.
memories.source_text: "You don’t want me as your enemy, Quirrell," said Snape, taking a step toward him.

memories.description: There's something guarding the Stone from Hagrid and people are trying to get past it.
memories.source_text: "Have you found out how to get past that beast of Hagrid’s yet?"

memories.description: Snape is testing loyalties and playing politics. I can't just assume people are on our side.
memories.source_text: "We’ll have another little chat soon, when you’ve had time to think things over and decided where your loyalties lie."

memories.description: I saw Mum and Dad grinning at me in the mirror. I couldn't believe it. It felt like they were really there.
memories.source_text: "There they were. His mother and father beamed at the sight of him."

memories.description: That mirror isn't the same for everyone. When Ron stood in front of it I couldn't see my family anymore. The way it shows you depends on who's looking.
memories.source_text: "I can only see you." "Look in it properly, go on, stand where I am."

memories.description: My family are gone. Seeing them in the mirror hit me hard but I know they're not alive anymore.
memories.source_text: "All my family are dead — let me have another look —"

memories.description: Ron is nosy but excited about the mirror too. I don't want to be selfish about it but I also want my turn.
memories.source_text: "You had it to yourself all last night, give me a bit more time."

memories.description: The Invisibility Cloak might not be safe on its own. If a cat can see something odd it's risky to hang around under it.
memories.source_text: "Quick!" Ron threw the Cloak back over them as the luminous eyes of Mrs. Norris came round the door.

memories.description: My broom's gone mad and I can barely hold on. If that thing keeps vibrating like this I'm going to fall.
memories.source_text: His broom was vibrating so hard, it was almost impossible for him to hang on much longer.

memories.description: I can see the Weasleys trying to catch me. I can't rely on the broom to do its job right now; I need to stay focused and keep my grip.
memories.source_text: They dropped lower and circled beneath him, obviously hoping to catch him if he fell.

memories.description: No more fooling about. We've done enough poking around. We're not taking any more risks by sneaking about on our own.
memories.source_text: "No," said Harry flatly, "we've done enough poking around."

memories.description: We have no proof and people will believe the teachers over us. If Snape lies and Quirrell won't back us, we're done for.
memories.source_text: "But we've got no proof!" said Harry.

memories.description: If Hagrid's involved, it's not so hopeless. Working with him makes this feel less terrible.
memories.source_text: Harry's heart rose; if they were going to be working with Hagrid it wouldn't be so bad.

memories.description: The unicorn is dead. It's awful and beautiful at the same time and I can't just walk past it.
memories.source_text: It was the unicorn all right, and it was dead.

memories.description: Someone in a hooded cloak is drinking the unicorn's blood. That is horrible and wrong and it's happening right in front of me.
memories.source_text: The cloaked figure reached the unicorn, lowered its head over the wound in the animal’s side, and began to drink its

memories.description: I shouldn't have expected anything friendly out here. Whatever's in those shadows is dangerous and creeping toward us.
memories.source_text: A bush on the edge of the clearing quivered. . . . Then, out of the shadows, a hooded figure came crawling across the ground like some stalking beast.

memories.description: We were right, it's the Sorcerer's Stone. Snape's trying to force Quirrell to help him get it. Quirrell knows something about getting past Fluffy because of his hocus-pocus.
memories.source_text: "So we were right, it is the Sorcerer’s Stone, and Snape’s trying to force Quirrell to help him get it. He asked if he knew how to get past Fluffy — and he said something about Quirrell’s ‘hocus-pocus’— I reckon there are"

memories.description: I thought maybe we were imagining things, but no, this is real and dangerous. Snape's mixed up in it and Quirrell is involved.
memories.source_text: "So we were right, it is the Sorcerer’s Stone, and Snape’s trying to force Quirrell to help him get it."

memories.description: If Snape helped guard the Stone, then he probably knows how the teachers set up the protections. He can't be the one trying to nick it.
memories.source_text: Look, Snape helped protect the Stone, he’s not about ter steal it.

memories.description: Only Hagrid and Dumbledore know how to get past Fluffy. That means the secret isn't common knowledge among the teachers.
memories.source_text: “You’re the only one who knows how to get past Fluffy, aren’t you, Hagrid?” said Harry anxiously.

memories.description: There is a huge black egg burning in Hagrid's fire. It's not normal and it worries me.
memories.source_text: “Hagrid — what’s that?”

memories.description: Hedwig brought a letter from Charlie saying he might take the Norwegian Ridgeback but that getting it here will be tricky because people must not be seen carrying an illegal dragon.
memories.source_text: “It’s Hedwig!” said Harry, hurrying to let her in.

memories.description: Snape wants to referee Quidditch and it feels wrong, like he's up to something sinister. I told them quietly because this isn't something to shout about.
memories.source_text: [Speaking quietly so that no one else would hear, Harry told the other two about Snape’s sudden, sinister desire to be a Quidditch referee.]

memories.description: I can't pull out of the match. There is no reserve Seeker, so if I back out Gryffindor won't be able to play.
memories.source_text: [I can’t, said Harry. There isn’t a reserve Seeker. If I back out, Gryffindor can’t play at all.]

memories.description: There’s unicorn blood on the ground — a unicorn’s been badly hurt in the forest and we’ve got to find it.
memories.source_text: "see that stuff shinin’ on the ground? Silvery stuff? That’s unicorn blood."

memories.description: Hagrid’s planning to go looking for the injured unicorn and might have to kill it to stop it suffering.
memories.source_text: "We’re gonna try an’ find the poor thing. We might have ter put it out of its misery."

memories.description: Hagrid says nothing in the forest will attack us if we stick with him or Fang, so staying together should keep us safer.
memories.source_text: "There’s nothin’ that lives in the forest that’ll hurt yeh if yer with me or Fang."

memories.description: A werewolf probably wouldn’t be quick enough to do this — whatever’s doing it is something different and more dangerous.
memories.source_text: "Could a werewolf be killing the unicorns?" "Not fast enough," said Hagrid.

memories.description: They're making us go into the forest at night as punishment, and Filch is enjoying the idea of it.
memories.source_text: "It's into the forest you are going"

memories.description: People think the forest is dangerous, even Malfoy is scared of it because of things like werewolves.
memories.source_text: "We can't go in there at night — there's all sorts of things in there — werewolves, I heard"

memories.description: Honestly, I felt pleased to see Malfoy panicking; he likes to act superior but he crumbles when it matters.
memories.source_text: "Malfoy didn't move." and "he didn't sound quite as cool as usual"

memories.description: Something had been drinking unicorn blood. That hooded figure was bleeding unicorn blood down its front. What the hell was it doing to a unicorn?
memories.source_text: unicorn blood was dribbling down its front

memories.description: My scar exploded with pain. It felt like it was on fire and I could hardly think.
memories.source_text: Then a pain like he’d never felt before pierced his head; it was as though his scar were on fire

memories.description: Hooves came thundering up behind me and something leapt over me to charge the hooded thing. I was saved by whatever that was.
memories.source_text: He heard hooves behind him, galloping, and something jumped clean over Harry, charging at the figure

memories.description: When I could see again the hooded figure had gone. A centaur was standing over me. He wasn't Ronan or Bane, same as I thought, he was younger with white blond hair and a palomino coat.
memories.source_text: When he looked up, the figure had gone. A centaur was standing over him, not Ronan or Bane; this one looked younger; he had white-blond hair and a palomino

memories.description: I froze with fear when that thing came at me. I can't just stand there next time; I need to do something instead of being stuck.
memories.source_text: It got to its feet and came swiftly toward Harry — he couldn’t move for fear

memories.description: He's spotted me straight away. The centaur knows who I am.
memories.source_text: “You are the Potter boy,”

memories.description: This forest is dangerous right now and I'm especially at risk. I need to get out of here fast.
memories.source_text: “The forest is not safe at this time — especially for you.”

memories.description: He expects me to ride him to get away faster. I can ride if I have to.
memories.source_text: “Can you ride? It will be quicker this way.”

memories.description: There was a unicorn nearby and its death matters. Something bad is lurking here that kills unicorns.
memories.source_text: “Do you not see that unicorn?”

memories.description: The other centaurs follow omens and the stars. They think their duty is to whatever the heavens say, not to mess about with humans.
memories.source_text: “Remember, Firenze, we are sworn not to set ourselves against the heavens. Have we not read what is to come in the movements of the planets?”

memories.description: Firenze is willing to go against his kind and help me. Not all centaurs agree about humans; there's clear conflict between Firenze and Bane.
memories.source_text: “I set myself against what is lurking in this forest, Bane, yes, with humans alongside me if I must.”

memories.description: Fluffy is guarding the Sorcerer’s Stone. That dog isn’t just any pet, it’s the Stone’s guard.
memories.source_text: We know what that dog’s guarding, it’s a Sorcerer’s St —

memories.description: There’s more protecting the Stone than Fluffy. I’m determined to find out who else is involved.
memories.source_text: We were wondering if you could tell us what’s guarding the Sorcerer’s Stone apart from Fluffy.

memories.description: Dumbledore and a bunch of teachers helped set up protections. Fluffy was borrowed from Hagrid, and Professors Sprout, Flitwick, McGonagall and others have put enchantments on the Stone.
memories.source_text: Well, I don’ s’pose it could hurt ter tell yeh that . . . let’s see . . . he borrowed Fluffy from me . . . then some o’ the teachers did enchantments . . . Professor Sprout — Professor Flitwick — Professor McGonagall —

memories.description: If Snape gets the Stone, Voldemort will come back. That would be catastrophic.
memories.source_text: "If Snape gets hold of the Stone, Voldemort's coming back! Haven't you heard what it was like when he was trying to take over?"

memories.description: House points and school rules are meaningless compared to stopping Voldemort. I'm willing to risk expulsion or worse.
memories.source_text: "Losing points doesn't matter anymore, can't you see? D'you think he'll leave you and your families alone if Gryffindor wins the House Cup?"

memories.description: If I'm caught now I go back to the Dursleys and put myself and others at risk later. I have to act tonight.
memories.source_text: "If I get caught before I can get to the Stone, well, I'll have to go back to the Dursleys and wait for Voldemort to find me there"

memories.description: I must go after the Stone myself tonight. I won't let friends stop me from doing what needs to be done.
memories.source_text: "I'm going through that trapdoor tonight and nothing you two say is going to stop me!"

memories.description: Unicorn blood can keep you alive when you're right on the edge, but it's a terrible bargain. If you drink it you kill something pure and you end up with a cursed half-life. That's monstrous.
memories.source_text: "Do you know what unicorn blood is used for?" "No," said Harry, startled by the odd question. "We’ve only used the horn and tail hair in Potions." "That is because it is a monstrous thing, to slay a unicorn," said Firenze. "Only one who has nothing to lose, and everything to gain, would commit such a crime. The blood of a unicorn will keep you alive, even if you are an inch from death, but at a terrible price. You have slain something pure and defenseless to save yourself, and you will have but a half-life, a cursed life, from the moment the blood touches your lips."

memories.description: So the Sorcerer’s Stone makes the Elixir of Life. Someone could use unicorn blood to cling on just long enough to get the Stone and become immortal. That's why anyone desperate would do it.
memories.source_text: "It is," Firenze agreed, "unless all you need is to stay alive long enough to drink something else — something that will bring you back to full strength and power — something that will mean you can never die. Mr. Potter, do you know what is hidden in the school at this very moment?" "The Sorcerer’s Stone! Of course — the Elixir of Life!"

memories.description: I felt cold when Firenze asked that. Of course it must be Voldemort trying to come back. It all fits with what Hagrid said about him maybe not being dead.
memories.source_text: "Can you think of nobody who has waited many years to return to power, who has clung to life, awaiting their chance?"

memories.description: Firenze saved me even though the centaurs like Bane are furious and think I should have been left. I owe Firenze for saving me, but it looks like some of them want events to follow what the stars say, even if that means letting Voldemort finish me.
memories.source_text: "Firenze saved me, but he shouldn’t have done so. . . . Bane was furious . . . he was talking about interfering with what the planets say is going to happen. . . . They must show that Voldemort’s coming back. . . . Bane thinks Firenze should have let Voldemort kill me. . . . I suppose that’s written in the stars as well."

memories.description: I've had enough of their rudeness. Dudley's spoiled and greedy, Vernon will always back him, and I snapped at them — tell him to say please.
memories.source_text: "You’ve forgotten the magic word," said Harry irritably.

memories.description: Of course it's my birthday. Dudley knows the date and he's using it to gloat at me.
memories.source_text: "Today's your birthday," sneered Dudley.

memories.description: I can't take his little victories seriously. Him learning the days of the week is not something to be impressed by and he's only bringing it up to be spiteful.
memories.source_text: "Well done," said Harry. "So you've finally learned the days of the week."

memories.description: He's willing to make fun of me on my birthday. Dudley is openly sneering and hostile, which just proves how miserable he wants me to feel.
memories.source_text: "How come you haven't got any cards?"

memories.description: A werewolf? That was my first thought, but then Hagrid said it wasn’t a werewolf or a unicorn. So whatever did this isn’t either of those.
memories.source_text: "A werewolf?"

memories.description: That thing in the clearing was a centaur. I couldn’t believe it at first, half man and half horse, and Hagrid already knew him.
memories.source_text: "Oh, it’s you, Ronan," said Hagrid in relief.

memories.description: He panics and runs straight to his mum when he's scared. Make a bit of noise and Dudley bolts for home.
memories.source_text: "MUUUUUUM!" howled Dudley, tripping over his feet as he dashed back toward the house.

memories.description: My messing about with a few words is enough to terrify him. I can get a total reaction from Dudley when I act like I'm doing magic.
memories.source_text: "Jiggery pokery! Hocus pocus — squiggly wiggly —" said Harry in a fierce voice.

memories.description: Do you think that was a centaur we heard earlier? I asked. It didn't sound like hooves to me.
memories.source_text: D’you think that was a centaur we heard earlier? said Harry.

memories.description: That noise wasn't hooves. Whatever made it, I reckon it's what has been killing the unicorns.
memories.source_text: Did that sound like hooves to you? Nah, if yeh ask me, that was what’s bin killin’ the unicorns — never heard anythin’ like it before.

memories.description: I stepped closer and saw the unicorn was dead. I couldn't believe how beautiful and sad it looked.
memories.source_text: It was the unicorn all right, and it was dead. Harry had never seen anything so beautiful and sad.

memories.description: People out there call Hogwarts a 'freak place' and think my mates are weird. They'll try to wind me up with that.
memories.source_text: "Haven’t you even got friends at that freak place?”

memories.description: Don't you dare talk about my school like that. I will shut that down and defend Hogwarts and the people in it.
memories.source_text: "Better not let your mum hear you talking about my school," said Harry coolly.

memories.description: I was thinking about which spell would best set that hedge on fire. I'm serious about using magic if I have to.
memories.source_text: "I’m trying to decide what would be the best spell to set it on fire," said Harry.

memories.description: I meant 'please' — I'm trying to be careful and polite here, but it doesn't stop things from getting out of hand.
memories.source_text: "I meant 'please'!"

memories.description: I can't say the 'M' word in their house or Uncle Vernon loses it, shouting and even spraying spit across the table.
memories.source_text: "WHAT HAVE I TOLD YOU ABOUT SAYING THE 'M' WORD IN OUR HOUSE?"

memories.description: If I even try to threaten or stand up to Dudley Uncle Vernon will explode, pound the table and make a huge scene.
memories.source_text: "HOW DARE YOU THREATEN DUDLEY!"

memories.description: Uncle Vernon means business when he's angry; I need to watch what I say or he'll make a brutal fuss.
memories.source_text: "I warned you!"

memories.description: We have to get to Hagrid right away. This is urgent and I am not wasting time.
memories.source_text: "We’ve got to go and see Hagrid, now."

memories.description: It all lines up too neatly: Hagrid wanting a dragon and some stranger showing up with a dragon egg. That is not a coincidence.
memories.source_text: "Don’t you think it’s a bit odd that what Hagrid wants more than anything else is a dragon, and a stranger turns up who just happens to have an egg in his pocket?"

memories.description: I missed it before and I am angry at myself for not seeing how suspicious it was sooner.
memories.source_text: "Why didn’t I see it before?"

memories.description: Hagrid told that stranger about the creatures he looks after and that he always wanted a dragon. The stranger used that to get Hagrid involved.
