memories.source_text: "He asked a bit about the sorta creatures I look after . . . so I told him . . . an’ I said what I’d always really wanted was a dragon . . . an’ then . . . I can’ remember too well, ’cause he kept buyin’ me drinks."

memories.description: The stranger gambled a dragon egg for a card game with Hagrid. That is how Hagrid ended up with Norbert.
memories.source_text: "He said he had the dragon egg an’ we could play cards fer it if I wanted"

memories.description: Someone is going to try to steal the Sorcerer’s Stone and I am convinced it may be tonight. I do not trust leaving it alone.
memories.source_text: "I think — I know — that Sn — that someone’s going to try and steal the Stone."

memories.description: Dumbledore left for London on urgent business. He is not here to protect the school right now.
memories.source_text: "Professor Dumbledore left ten minutes ago"

memories.description: I believe Snape is the one attempting to get the Stone and that he will try to go through the trapdoor tonight now that Dumbledore is away.
memories.source_text: "Snape’s going through the trapdoor tonight."

memories.description: Snape openly threatens me. He plays the role of an enemy and will use his position to try to punish me.
memories.source_text: "Be warned, Potter — any more nighttime wanderings and I will personally make sure you are expelled."

memories.description: We can do this. The Invisibility Cloak will hide two of us and Norbert, so getting him up the tower is doable if we’re careful.
memories.source_text: "We’ve got the Invisibility Cloak," said Harry. "It shouldn’t be too difficult — I think the cloak’s big enough to cover two of us and Norbert."

memories.description: We made it to the tower corridor and were close to getting Norbert where he needed to be.
memories.source_text: "Nearly there!" Harry panted as they reached the corridor beneath the tallest tower.

memories.description: Malfoy’s been caught and got detention. That’s a proper bit of luck for us.
memories.source_text: "Malfoy’s got detention! I could sing!"

memories.description: Filch found us at the stairs. We’re in a right mess now and need to think fast.
memories.source_text: "Well, well, well," he whispered, "we are in trouble."

memories.description: Charlie’s mates helped out properly. I can trust them to take Norbert away safely.
memories.source_text: "Charlie’s friends were a cheery lot. They showed Harry and Hermione the harness they’d rigged up, so they could suspend Norbert between them."

memories.description: I shouldn't have spoken up. I thought I could help, but as soon as I said something, it all went wrong.
memories.source_text: "Can’t anyone help you? Can’t I?"

memories.description: Dobby reacts to my words with overwhelming gratitude and noise, and I have to beg him to calm down because it's making things worse.
memories.source_text: "Please," Harry whispered frantically, "please be quiet."

memories.description: He's furious about me being different and he will lash out if I push it. I can't make them accept me here so I have to keep my head down.
memories.source_text: I WILL NOT TOLERATE MENTION OF YOUR ABNORMALITY UNDER THIS ROOF!

memories.description: Fine. I'm not going to argue right now. I'll back off and try to calm things before it gets worse.
memories.source_text: All right, said Harry, "all right"

memories.description: Dudley is gleeful and looking for trouble. He enjoys winding me up and he's not on my side.
memories.source_text: I know what day it is, sang Dudley, waddling toward him.

memories.description: I'll use the Invisibility Cloak. It's lucky I got it back and I can use it to keep us hidden.
memories.source_text: "I'll use the Invisibility Cloak," said Harry. "It's just lucky I got it back."

memories.description: Voldemort did that to my parents, and that makes this personal. I won't back down.
memories.source_text: "Voldemort killed my parents, remember?" He glared at them.

memories.description: He's still out there. He isn't gone. He'll try other ways to come back and he can't be killed like a normal person.
memories.source_text: No, Harry, he has not. He is still out there somewhere, perhaps looking for another body to share . . . not being truly alive, he cannot be killed.

memories.description: My mum's love left me a real protection in my skin. That's why Quirrell couldn't touch me. It hurts to even think about, but that's the reason.
memories.source_text: Your mother died to save you. If there is one thing Voldemort cannot understand, it is love.

memories.description: The Invisibility Cloak is my dad's. Dumbledore had it and sent it to me.
memories.source_text: Ah -- your father happened to leave it in my possession, and I thought you might like it.

memories.description: Snape and my dad had history. Dad once saved Snape's life. That explains a lot about Snape's feelings and why he might be acting the way he does around me.
memories.source_text: He saved his life.

memories.description: The mirror only gives the Stone to someone who wants to find it but not use it. That's how I could get it.
memories.source_text: only one who wanted to find the Stone -- find it, but not use it -- would be able to get it

memories.description: I don't think Dumbledore just stopped us. I think he let me have a shot at facing Voldemort if I could. He knows more than he tells and maybe he wanted me to try.
memories.source_text: I think he sort of wanted to give me a chance. I think he knows more or less everything that goes on here, you know.

memories.description: If something goes wrong, send Hedwig to Dumbledore straight away. Don't follow me.
memories.source_text: If anything happens to me, don’t follow. Go straight to the owlery and send Hedwig to Dumbledore, right?

memories.description: That plant hates light and warmth. Light is how you get free from it.
memories.source_text: Devil’s Snare, Devil’s Snare . . . what did Professor Sprout say? — it likes the dark and the damp —

memories.description: Hermione's Herbology knowledge actually saved us. She knows what to do with dangerous plants.
memories.source_text: Lucky you pay attention in Herbology, Hermione

memories.description: Sometimes stuff in this place is there to help us, even if it looks weird. Go on, keep moving.
memories.source_text: I suppose it’s here to break the fall. Come on, Hermione!

memories.description: I can spot things in the air other people miss. My Seeker instincts really do help in weird situations.
memories.source_text: Not for nothing, though, was Harry the youngest Seeker in a century. He had a knack for spotting things other people didn’t.

memories.description: If something is enchanted to be a problem, you might have to be clever and grab the enchanted thing yourself.
memories.source_text: We’ve got to catch the key to the door!

memories.description: Sometimes winning means doing exactly what needs doing as quickly as you can. No dawdling, no second guessing.
memories.source_text: The white king took off his crown and threw it at Harry’s feet. They had won.

memories.description: What did you lot do to Neville? He’s bound by a full Body-Bind and I feel awful about it.
memories.source_text: What’ve you done to him?

memories.description: We had to act, even if it meant hurting Neville for a bit. There was no time to hang about explaining.
memories.source_text: We had to, Neville, no time to explain

memories.description: If I play that flute like Hagrid’s, the beast drops off to sleep. I can keep it calm by playing.
memories.source_text: He put Hagrid’s flute to his lips and blew.

memories.description: I said sorry. I know lots of people don't like that name.
memories.source_text: "Sorry," said Harry quickly. "I know lots of people don’t like it."

memories.description: Dobby's come all this way to look out for me and warn me. He'll even put himself through daft things to keep me safe.
memories.source_text: He has braved so many dangers already! But Dobby has come to protect Harry Potter, to warn him, even if he does have to shut his ears in the oven door later.

memories.description: I can't just write Dobby off as a nuisance. He's on my side, proper loyal, even if it gets him into trouble.
memories.source_text: He has braved so many dangers already! But Dobby has come to protect Harry Potter, to warn him, even if he does have to shut his ears in the oven door later.

memories.description: He's a house-elf, bound to serve one wizarding family for life. That's why he acts so scared about being here.
memories.source_text: "Dobby is a house-elf — bound to serve one house and one family forever."

memories.description: He punishes himself for even speaking about his masters. He says he'll shut his ears in the oven door and do terrible things to himself if they find out he came to see me.
memories.source_text: "Dobby will have to punish himself most grievously for coming to see you, sir. Dobby will have to shut his ears in the oven door for this."

memories.description: I couldn't believe he'd actually start hurting himself because he's worried about what his family would think. He's seriously terrified of them.
memories.source_text: "Dobby had to punish himself, sir,"

memories.description: I couldn't believe it! He punishes himself and they make him do extra punishments. That's cruel.
memories.source_text: ["Dobby is always having to punish himself for something, sir. They lets Dobby get on with it, sir. Sometimes they reminds me to do extra punishments."]

memories.description: So house-elves can only be freed if their family frees them. He thinks he'll serve them for life and never be free. That's mental.
memories.source_text: ["A house-elf must be set free, sir. And the family will never set Dobby free. Dobby will serve the family until he dies, sir."]

memories.description: We're trapped between two kinds of magical fire, purple behind us and black ahead of us. We cannot go back or forward without the right potion.
memories.source_text: At the instant we stepped over the threshold, a fire sprang up behind us in the doorway. It wasn't ordinary fire either; it was purple. At the same instant, black flames shot up in the doorway leading onward.

memories.description: The tiny bottle is the one that will get me through the black flames toward the Stone. There's only enough for one swallow.
memories.source_text: The smallest bottle will get us through the black fire - toward the Stone.

memories.description: The rounded bottle at the right end will send someone back through the purple fire.
memories.source_text: Which one will get you back through the purple flames? Hermione pointed at a rounded bottle at the right end of the line.

memories.description: I'm willing to try to face whatever is ahead alone if it gives Hermione and Ron the chance to get Dumbledore. I might get lucky again, even though I know I'm not the best at everything.
memories.source_text: I might be able to hold Snape off for a while, but I'm no match for him, really. - Well - I was lucky once, wasn't I? I might get lucky again.

memories.description: Hermione cares about me more than she lets on. She thinks I'm a great wizard and is willing to risk things for me.
memories.source_text: Hermione dashed at Harry and threw her arms around him. - Harry - you're a great wizard, you know.

memories.description: Someone says I'm in mortal danger if I go back to Hogwarts. That's serious and I can't ignore it.
memories.source_text: "He is too great, too good, to lose. If Harry Potter goes back to Hogwarts, he will be in mortal danger."

memories.description: There's a plot to make terrible things happen at Hogwarts this year. Hogwarts isn't safe and something big is being planned.
memories.source_text: "There is a plot, Harry Potter. A plot to make most terrible things happen at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry this year," whispered Dobby,

memories.description: I can't just accept this without answers. I'm surprised and I need to know why they'd target me and Hogwarts.
memories.source_text: "Why?" said Harry in surprise.

memories.description: Thinking about Ron hurts. It is painful to even bring him up.
memories.source_text: He stopped again. Thinking about Ron was painful, too.

memories.description: I met the Dark Lord again weeks ago and I got away again. People are talking about it.
memories.source_text: “Dobby heard tell,” he said hoarsely, “that Harry Potter met the Dark Lord for a second time, just weeks ago , . . . that Harry Potter escaped yet again.”

memories.description: I tried to apologise and calm him down because Dobby is clearly terrified of upsetting wizards
memories.source_text: "I'm sorry, I didn't mean to offend you or anything"

memories.description: Dobby is proud and sensitive about being insulted or treated badly
memories.source_text: "Offend Dobby!"

memories.description: I told him he must not have met many decent wizards because he looks at me like he already trusts and adores me
memories.source_text: "You can't have met many decent wizards"

memories.description: They just told me I must not go back to Hogwarts. Me. Harry Potter. I can't believe they're saying that.
memories.source_text: “Harry Potter must not go back to Hogwarts.”

memories.description: What the hell? I have to go back. Term starts on September first. I'm supposed to be back at school, not kept away.
memories.source_text: “W-what?” Harry stammered. “But I’ve got to go back - term starts on September first.”

memories.description: I found out there was someone else inside Quirrell talking, not just him.
memories.source_text: "Let me speak to him . . . face-to-face. . . ." "He lies . . . He lies . . ."

memories.description: Quirrell was drinking unicorn blood to help whoever was living inside him.
memories.source_text: "Unicorn blood has strengthened me, these past weeks . . . you saw faithful Quirrell drinking it for me in the forest . . ."

memories.description: That face knew about the Stone in my pocket and wanted it badly.
memories.source_text: "Now . . . why don't you give me that Stone in your pocket?"

memories.description: Quirrell could not touch my bare skin without getting burned and in pain.
memories.source_text: "Quirrell couldn't touch his bare skin, not without suffering terrible pain"

memories.description: Dumbledore came and pulled Quirrell off me before Quirrell could take the Stone.
memories.source_text: "I arrived in time to prevent that, although you were doing very well on your own, I must say."

memories.description: The Stone is gone. It has been destroyed and nobody can use it anymore.
memories.source_text: "As for the Stone, it has been destroyed."

memories.description: Flamel and his wife will die soon because the Stone is destroyed but they have enough Elixir to settle things first.
memories.source_text: "They have enough Elixir stored to set their affairs in order and then, yes, they will die."

memories.description: I know for sure that whoever was with Quirrell hates me and wanted to kill me.
memories.source_text: "Seize him! SEIZE HIM!" "KILL HIM! KILL HIM!"

memories.description: I was told to call him Voldemort and not to be terrified of saying his name.
memories.source_text: "Call him Voldemort, Harry. Always use the proper name for things."

memories.description: So Quirrell's been here looking for me. He's the one I walked into.
memories.source_text: "Me," he said calmly. "I wondered whether I’d be meeting you here, Potter."

memories.description: Snape isn't the mastermind; I was wrong to think he was behind everything. That idea's gone.
memories.source_text: "Severus?" Quirrell laughed... "Yes, Severus does seem the type, doesn’t he?... Next to him, who would suspect p-p-poor, st-stuttering P-Professor Quirrell?"

memories.description: Quirrell tried to make me fall off my broom and kill me at the Quidditch match. Hermione almost stopped him by accident.
memories.source_text: "No, no, no. I tried to kill you. Your friend Miss Granger accidentally knocked me over as she rushed to set fire to Snape at that Quidditch match."

memories.description: Snape actually wanted to protect me at the match. He was trying to stop Quirrell, not hurt me.
memories.source_text: "Of course," said Quirrell coolly. "Why do you think he wanted to referee your next match? He was trying to make sure I didn’t do it again."

memories.description: Quirrell let the troll into Hogwarts on purpose to create chaos and distract people while he searched for the Stone.
memories.source_text: "You let the troll in?" "Certainly. I have a special gift with trolls — you must have seen what I did to the one in the chamber back there?"

memories.description: The Mirror of Erised is the way to find the Stone. It's how Quirrell has been trying to get it.
memories.source_text: "This mirror is the key to finding the Stone," Quirrell murmured, tapping his way around the frame.

memories.description: Quirrell met Voldemort while traveling and he serves him now. Voldemort changed what Quirrell believes about power and right and wrong.
memories.source_text: "I met him when I traveled around the world. A foolish young man I was then, full of ridiculous ideas about good and evil. Lord Voldemort showed me how wrong I was."

memories.description: Something or someone told Quirrell to use me to get the Stone. He was being ordered to take advantage of me.
memories.source_text: "Use the boy . . . Use the boy . . ."

memories.description: Quirrell can control magical ropes and he set me free when he wanted me to look in the mirror.
memories.source_text: "He clapped his hands once, and the ropes binding Harry fell off."

memories.description: When I looked in the Mirror of Erised, I somehow got the Stone in my pocket. The mirror gave it to me.
memories.source_text: "He saw his reflection... the reflection put its hand into its pocket and pulled out a blood-red stone... Harry felt something heavy drop into his real pocket."

memories.description: Dobby can just vanish into thin air. I was stunned when he disappeared like that.
memories.source_text: With a crack like a whip, Dobby vanished.

memories.description: Uncle Vernon will cover things up for appearances and then take it out on me. He says he will flay me and then makes me clean up. I can't count on him to protect me or be honest.
memories.source_text: he shooed the shocked Masons back into the dining room, promised Harry he would flay him to within an inch of his life when the Masons had left, and handed him a mop.

memories.description: I ended up soaked in Aunt Petunia's pudding and shaking, and then they made me scrub the kitchen clean. Great.
memories.source_text: covered from head to foot in Aunt Petunia’s pudding.

memories.description: Someone is warning me that I'm in danger and that I'm too important to risk going back to school. I can't just ignore that.
memories.source_text: "Harry Potter must not put himself in peril. He is too important, sir!"

memories.description: This warning is not about You-Know-Who. Whatever's going on, it isn't Voldemort.
memories.source_text: "Not — not He-Who-Must-Not-Be-Named, sir —"

memories.description: Someone wants me to say I will not return to school, and Dobby thinks it is for my own good. I don't like being pushed into that, but I can see they're desperate.
memories.source_text: "Harry Potter must say he’s not going back to school —"

memories.description: Dobby is willing to take extreme steps on my behalf. He clearly cares about me enough to try and protect me, even if it gets messy.
memories.source_text: "Then Dobby must do it, sir, for Harry Potter’s own good."

memories.description: That Malfoys are dodgy and probably tied up with dark people. Malfoy would very likely have servants and plenty of money. I can't help thinking he sent someone to stop me going back to Hogwarts.
memories.source_text: "Load of dung — Dad reckons he was right in You-Know-Who’s inner circle."

memories.description: If a family has a house-elf it means they're old and rich. Makes perfect sense why Malfoy always has the best of everything.
memories.source_text: "I don’t know whether the Malfoys own a house-elf. . . ."

memories.description: I appreciate Ron. He really worried when I didn't answer his letters and they went out of their way to fetch me. I like being here. This is the best house I've ever been in.
memories.source_text: "I’m glad we came to get you, anyway," said Ron.

memories.description: People think I'm great, but that's rubbish. I'm not even top of my year. Hermione is.
memories.source_text: "Whatever you’ve heard about my greatness is a load of rubbish. I’m not even top of my year at Hogwarts; that’s Hermione, she —"

memories.description: Hermione's ahead of me at school and thinking about her is painful.
memories.source_text: "I’m not even top of my year at Hogwarts; that’s Hermione, she —"

memories.description: Oh — you mean Voldemort. That's who they're talking about.
memories.source_text: "Harry Potter speaks not of his triumph over He-Who-Must-Not-Be-Named —" "Voldemort?"

memories.description: Draco Malfoy hates me. He's the sort of person who would hold a grudge.
memories.source_text: "Draco Malfoy," Harry explained. "He hates me."

memories.description: So the Malfoys have ties to You-Know-Who's supporters. That makes Draco even more dangerous around school.
memories.source_text: "I've heard Dad talking about him," said George. "He was a big supporter of You-Know-Who."

memories.description: We haven't been expelled. That's the important thing, okay
memories.source_text: "Well, we haven’t been expelled," Harry assured her.

memories.description: The road's clear and no one is watching. Let's go
memories.source_text: "Okay," he said.

memories.description: Why can’t we get through? The barrier's sealed and nothing I do is getting us on that train.
memories.source_text: "Why can’t we get through?"

memories.description: The gateway has sealed itself for some reason and it's stopped us from getting on the train.
memories.source_text: "I don’t understand why the gateway’s sealed itself —"

memories.description: I pushed as hard as I could and the barrier stayed solid, and then the train left. We're actually stuck here, we've missed it.
memories.source_text: He wheeled his trolley forward cautiously until it was right against the barrier and pushed with all his might. The metal remained solid. "It’s gone," said Ron, sounding stunned.

memories.description: I haven't had any pocket money from the Dursleys for ages. Great, so I'm skint and can't help with Muggle cash.
memories.source_text: "The Dursleys haven’t given me pocket money for about six years."

memories.description: I laughed hollowly because this is ridiculous. I'm stuck here with no money and no easy way to fix it.
memories.source_text: "The Dursleys haven’t given me pocket money for about six years."

memories.description: I saw Malfoy and his father in Borgin and Burkes. That means Lucius was selling, not buying.
memories.source_text: "Guess who I saw in Borgin and Burkes?"

memories.description: Lucius Malfoy was selling things, not buying. Good. He's worried about something.
memories.source_text: "No, he was selling —"

memories.description: Molly Weasley fusses over me like I’m her own. They all care, which is comforting.
memories.source_text: "Oh, Harry — oh, my dear — you could have been anywhere —"

memories.description: Hagrid nearly lost me in Knockturn Alley. He rescued me, then took off for Hogwarts.
memories.source_text: "Well, gotta be off," said Hagrid, who was having his hand wrung by Mrs Weasley ("Knockturn Alley! If you hadn't found him, Hagrid!").

memories.description: He says we are safe while he's here. I don't trust him but for now he's making everyone feel safer.
memories.source_text: "Know only that no harm can befall you whilst I am here."

memories.description: They're pixies. Small, supposedly a joke, but everyone's watching them like they might do something. I leaned in to get a better look because I wanted to see what they actually were.
memories.source_text: "Freshly caught Cornish pixies."

memories.description: Lockhart is all show and drama. He tells us not to scream like he's running a play. I think he's more about the performance than the danger.
memories.source_text: "I must ask you not to scream," said Lockhart in a low voice. "It might provoke them."

memories.description: What the hell? Ron is actually in a flying car outside my window.
memories.source_text: Ron was leaning out of the back window of an old turquoise car, which was parked in midair.

memories.description: Fred and George are with Ron. Of course they are grinning like idiots.
memories.source_text: Grinning at Harry from the front seats were Fred and George, Ron’s elder twin brothers.

memories.description: The Dursleys have locked me in and are keeping me from going back to Hogwarts.
memories.source_text: look, can you tell them at Hogwarts that the Dursleys have locked me up and won’t let me come back

memories.description: I can't magic myself out without getting in even more trouble with the Ministry.
memories.source_text: obviously I can’t magic myself out, because the Ministry’ll think that’s the second spell I’ve done in three days

memories.description: I have to get out by tying a rope to the bars and being pulled out by them.
memories.source_text: Tie that around the bars," said Fred, throwing the end of a rope to Harry.

memories.description: My trunk, wand and broom are locked in the cupboard under the stairs and I can't reach them by myself.
memories.source_text: All my Hogwarts stuff — my wand — my broomstick — "Locked in the cupboard under the stairs, and I can’t get out of this room

memories.description: Hedwig is with me and I nearly left her behind. I wasn't going to abandon her.
memories.source_text: I’ve forgotten Hedwig!" Harry tore back across the room as the landing light clicked on — he snatched up Hedwig’s cage, dashed to the window, and passed it out to Ron.

memories.description: The bars were off the window and dangling a few feet above the ground. I could climb out.
memories.source_text: "Harry ran back to the window to see the bars dangling a few feet above the ground."

memories.description: Ron got the bars into the car for me so we could get out fast.
memories.source_text: "Panting, Ron hoisted them up into the car."

memories.description: My wand and everything are locked in the cupboard under the stairs. I can't get them right now.
memories.source_text: "But all my Hogwarts stuff — my wand — my broomstick —"

memories.description: Fred and George can pick a lock. They opened my door with a hairpin.
memories.source_text: "There was a small click and the door swung open."

memories.description: The bottom stair creaks. We had to be careful sneaking past it.
memories.source_text: "Watch out for the bottom stair — it creaks," Harry whispered back as the twins disappeared onto the dark landing.

memories.description: I almost left Hedwig behind. I had to grab her cage and throw it out the window.
memories.source_text: "I've forgotten Hedwig!"

memories.description: Uncle Vernon tried to stop me and grabbed my ankle. He will do anything to keep me here.
memories.source_text: "For a split second, Uncle Vernon stood framed in the doorway; then he let out a bellow like an angry bull and dived at Harry, grabbing him by the ankle."

memories.description: We actually got away. I thought we might be caught, but the Weasleys pulled me free and we flew off. I can't believe it, we left!
memories.source_text: "But the Weasleys gave a gigantic tug and Harry’s leg slid out of Uncle Vernon’s grasp — Harry was in the car — he’d slammed the door shut — 'Put your foot down, Fred!' yelled Ron, and the car shot suddenly toward the moon."

memories.description: I shouted 'See you next summer' as we left. I'm going back to the Burrow, at least for now.
memories.source_text: "'See you next summer!' Harry yelled."

memories.description: Dobby tried to warn me, but he couldn't say who was behind it because every time he came close to spilling anything he started banging his head against the wall.
memories.source_text: I don't think he could," said Harry. "I told you, every time he got close to letting something slip, he started banging his head against the wall.

memories.description: Hedwig's coming with us; I want her free to fly alongside the car so she can stretch her wings.
memories.source_text: "Let Hedwig out," he told Ron. "She can fly behind us. She hasn’t had a chance to stretch her wings for ages."

memories.description: Alright, house-elves can do powerful magic, but they probably can't just act on their own without their master's say-so.
memories.source_text: "Well," said Fred, "put it this way — house-elves have got powerful magic of their own, but they can’t usually use it without their master’s permission."

memories.description: This isn't nearly as bad as Floo powder. I can do this, no problem.
memories.source_text: [He felt perfectly confident; this wasn’t nearly as uncomfortable as using Floo powder.]

memories.description: I couldn't believe it! We smashed into the barrier, I got knocked flat and Hedwig went rolling. That went wrong fast.
memories.source_text: [Both trolleys hit the barrier and bounced backward; Ron’s trunk fell off with a loud thump, Harry was knocked off his feet, and Hedwig’s cage bounced onto the shiny floor, and she rolled away, shrieking indignantly; people all around them stared and a guard nearby yelled, “What in blazes d’you think you’re doing?”]

memories.description: Lost control of the trolley. That's exactly what happened, and it hurt.
memories.source_text: ["Lost control of the trolley," Harry gasped, clutching his ribs as he got up.]

memories.description: I’ve never used Floo powder. I’m nervous about it and I don’t know what I’m doing.
memories.source_text: "He’s never traveled by Floo powder," said Ron suddenly.

memories.description: I have to say the destination properly when I step into the fire or I might end up somewhere else.
memories.source_text: "You must speak clearly, dear," Mrs. Weasley told Harry as George dipped his hand into the flowerpot.

memories.description: There are loads of wizard fireplaces, so I need to get out at the right grate or I’ll be lost.
memories.source_text: "And be sure to get out at the right grate."

memories.description: They think I’ll manage it if I follow directions. I have to trust them and do what they say.
memories.source_text: "He’ll be fine, Molly, don’t fuss," said Mr. Weasley, helping himself to Floo powder, too.

memories.description: I mustn’t jump out too soon. I should wait until I see Fred and George so I know I’m at the right place.
memories.source_text: "But don’t panic and get out too early; wait until you see Fred and George."

memories.description: Of course I agree that being properly beheaded would have been better for him. I feel sorry for Nick and I can see how awful that must have been.
memories.source_text: "Oh — yes," said Harry, who was obviously supposed to agree. "I mean, nobody wishes more than I do that it had all been quick and clean, and my head had come off properly, I mean, it would have saved me a great deal of pain and ridicule."

memories.description: So Nick's having his five hundredth Deathday this Halloween. He's throwing a party in a roomy dungeon and inviting guests from all over the country.
memories.source_text: "Well, this Halloween will be my five hundredth deathday," said Nearly Headless Nick, drawing himself up and looking dignified.

memories.description: I'll go to Nick's Deathday party. I don't want to leave him hanging and I said I'd come even though the school feast is on.
memories.source_text: "No," said Harry quickly, "I’ll come —"

memories.description: So Malfoy is hiding embarrassing stuff at home and is worried about Ministry raids. He's the sort who'd sell to keep himself safe.
memories.source_text: "I have a few — ah — items at home that might embarrass me, if the Ministry were to call. . . ."

memories.description: Malfoy thinks his name still means something and he looks down on the Ministry. He blames people like Arthur Weasley for making things difficult.
memories.source_text: "The name Malfoy still commands a certain respect, yet the Ministry grows ever more meddlesome."

memories.description: Draco likes dangerous, flashy junk. He picked the Hand of Glory without a second thought.
memories.source_text: "Insert a candle and it gives light only to the holder! Best friend of thieves and plunderers! Your son has fine taste, sir."

memories.description: Lucius acts like he wants Draco to be better than a common thief, but he also insults him if his grades slip. He cares about status more than his son's feelings.
memories.source_text: "I hope my son will amount to more than a thief or a plunderer, Borgin,"

memories.description: Draco blames Hermione when he does badly. He can't handle being beaten by someone he sees as beneath him.
memories.source_text: "It’s not my fault," retorted Draco. "The teachers all have favorites, that Hermione Granger —"

memories.description: Malfoy is openly contemptuous of anyone without pure wizarding pedigree, and he uses that to needle Draco. He thinks blood status matters above all.
memories.source_text: "I would have thought you’d be ashamed that a girl of no wizard family beat you in every exam," snapped Mr Malfoy.

memories.description: Borgin feeds Malfoy's ego and agrees that wizard blood is important. He's sycophantic and willing to flatter for business.
memories.source_text: "It’s the same all over," said Mr Borgin, in his oily voice. "Wizard blood is counting for less everywhere —"

memories.description: I felt pleased to see Draco thrown off balance. Seeing him embarrassed by Hermione's success makes me quietly smug.
memories.source_text: "Ha!" said Harry under his breath, pleased to see Draco looking both abashed and angry.

memories.description: I was hiding nearby and worried when Draco came close. He's nosy and his curiosity is dangerous when I'm trying to stay unseen.
memories.source_text: Harry watched nervously as Draco drew nearer and nearer to his hiding place, examining the objects for sale.

memories.description: I lied and said I didn't know who that was. I wanted away from Colin and his camera, fast.
memories.source_text: "No idea,"

memories.description: I blurted that the photographer was a Gryffindor to calm things down. Quick, direct, keep it simple.
memories.source_text: "He's in Gryffindor," said Harry quickly.

memories.description: When Malfoy called Hermione that, I knew immediately he'd crossed a line. The whole place erupted.
memories.source_text: "No one asked your opinion, you filthy little Mudblood," he spat.

memories.description: Trouble doesn't have to be punishments from teachers to be awful. Having slugs poured all over you is right up there as proper awful. That's the kind of thing I'd call real trouble.
memories.source_text: Harry would have pointed out that trouble didn’t come much worse than having slugs pouring

memories.description: I felt like he was X-raying me with that twinkling look. I know he can see straight through people and he was judging the whole situation, not just me.
memories.source_text: ["Innocent until proven guilty, Severus,"]

memories.description: We're allowed to leave. Get out while we can and keep our heads down.
memories.source_text: ["You may go,"]

memories.description: What's a Howler? I stared at the red envelope and at everyone looking terrified, and I had no idea what it was.
memories.source_text: “What's a Howler?”

memories.description: We should get Ron to Hagrid's, it's the nearest place to take him.
memories.source_text: "We'd better get him to Hagrid's, it's nearest," said Harry to Hermione

memories.description: I couldn't believe Hagrid was slagging off a teacher. If Hagrid's saying Lockhart's stories are rubbish, then Lockhart's full of it.
memories.source_text: "Givin' me advice on gettin' kelpies out of a well," growled Hagrid ... "If one word of it was true, I'll eat my kettle."

memories.description: Should I have told them about that voice I heard? I kept asking that. I know it’s weird. The whole thing’s weird.
memories.source_text: "D’you think I should have told them about that voice I heard?"

memories.description: You do believe me, don’t you? I needed Ron to say he believed me, and he did.
memories.source_text: "You do believe me, don’t you?"

memories.description: Someone's been petrified. That's serious and everyone's treating it like a big deal.
memories.source_text: “She has been Petrified,” said Dumbledore

memories.description: I didn't touch Mrs Norris. I'm saying it straight out because people think I did.
memories.source_text: “I never touched Mrs Norris!” Harry said loudly

memories.description: Filch thinks I saw his Kwikspell letter in his office and that's why he's accusing me.
memories.source_text: “He saw my Kwikspell letter!” Filch

memories.description: Filch thinks I'm connected to him being a Squib, like he blurted out this terrible idea about me.
memories.source_text: “He knows I’m a Squib!” Filch

memories.description: I don't even know what a Squib is, so I can't be that or at least I don't understand what Filch's accusation means.
memories.source_text: “And I don’t even know what a Squib is.” Harry said

memories.description: People are treating me like a suspect just for being in the corridor. I'm starting to think being in the wrong place is going to get me blamed for everything.
memories.source_text: “Potter and his friends may have simply been in the wrong place at the wrong time,” said Snape

memories.description: Everyone's questioning why I was in the upstairs corridor. That question is being used against me, whether I like it or not.
memories.source_text: “Why was he in the upstairs corridor at all?” Snape

memories.description: Remember all that water on the floor? I'm trying to get us off the subject by bringing it up.
memories.source_text: "Remember all that water on the floor?"

memories.description: Of course I'll tell Sir Patrick how frightening and impressive you find me.
memories.source_text: “Of — of course,” said Harry.

memories.description: I asked if ghosts can taste food when they walk straight through it.
memories.source_text: “Can you taste it if you walk through it?” Harry asked him.

memories.description: I couldn't believe a ghost could walk right through the food like that and act like it mattered.
memories.source_text: Harry watched, amazed, as a portly ghost approached the table, crouched low, and walked through it, his mouth held wide so that it passed through one of the stinking salmon.

memories.description: I have not been giving out signed photos. I'm furious about being blamed and I'm quick to deny it.
memories.source_text: "I have not been giving out signed photos,"

memories.description: If Lockhart is spreading rumors about me giving out signed photos then he's the one causing trouble. I don't trust him on this.
memories.source_text: "If Lockhart’s still spreading that around —"

memories.description: He's terrified of spiders. He was hanging back, like he wanted to bolt.
memories.source_text: ["Ron was standing well back and seemed to be fighting the impulse to run."]

memories.description: No. Have you, Ron? Ron? I can't believe spiders are behaving like that, trying to get out like that.
memories.source_text: “No,” said Harry, “have you, Ron? Ron?”

memories.description: Something's up with Ron and that envelope. I asked what's wrong because it looked serious.
memories.source_text: "What's the matter?" said Harry.

memories.description: Something made me pull my hand away like I'd been burned. That told me there was still something weird or unpleasant about that doorknob area.
memories.source_text: "What’s the matter?"

memories.description: I asked Myrtle straight out if she saw anyone on Halloween because the cat was attacked right outside her door. I wanted a straight answer.
memories.source_text: "Did you see anyone near here that night?"

memories.description: Myrtle is way too wrapped up in her own drama and not a reliable witness for what happened that night. I can't count on her to have noticed anything useful.
memories.source_text: "I wasn’t paying attention," said Myrtle dramatically. "Peeves upset me so much I came in here and tried to kill myself. Then, of course, I remembered that I’m — that I’m —" "Already dead," said Ron helpfully.

memories.description: That's the same voice I heard in Lockhart's office. It's cold and murderous, saying rip tear kill and saying it's been hungry for so long. I shut everyone up because we had to listen and work out what that meant.
memories.source_text: ". . . rip . . . tear . . . kill . . ." It was the same voice, the same cold, murderous voice he had heard in Lockhart’s office.

memories.description: I couldn't believe it! She actually dived headfirst into the loo and disappeared down the U-bend. That's mental.
memories.source_text: Myrtle gave a tragic sob, rose up in the air, turned over, and dived headfirst into the toilet, splashing water all over them and vanishing from sight

memories.description: Something hit the door or the magic nearby. I jerked my hand out of instinct. That's not normal quiet hospital stuff.
memories.source_text: [There was a loud crack, and Harry’s fist was suddenly clenched on thin air.]

memories.description: Someone's coming for me and I need to be ready. I won't panic but I won't let my guard down either.
memories.source_text: [He slumped back into bed, his eyes on the dark doorway to the hospital wing as the footsteps drew nearer.]

memories.description: That Bludger is after me. I swear it's following me and no one else's getting this much trouble. The Slytherins have to have done something to it.
memories.source_text: "Someone's fixed it — it won't leave Harry alone. It hasn't gone for anyone else all game. The Slytherins must have done something to it."

memories.description: If Fred and George keep circling me I'm not going to have a chance to catch the Snitch. I need them off me so I can deal with the rogue Bludger myself.
memories.source_text: "Listen, with you two flying around me all the time the only way I'm going to catch the Snitch is if it flies up my sleeve. Go back to the rest of the team and let me deal with the rogue one."

memories.description: We can't just stop and hand them the match. I'm not letting Slytherin win because of some mad Bludger. We're carrying on.
memories.source_text: "If we stop now, we'll have to forfeit the match! And we're not losing to Slytherin just because of a crazy Bludger!"

memories.description: He's got a Slytherin pedigree. Malfoy and his family are proper Slytherins and could be the sort to pass down something like the Chamber's key.
memories.source_text: "Look at his family," said Harry, closing his books, too. "The whole lot of them have been in Slytherin; he’s always boasting about it. They could easily be Slytherin’s descendants. His father’s definitely evil enough."

memories.description: If the Malfoys are Slytherin through and through, then yeah, it's likely the key has been kept in the family for generations.
memories.source_text: "They could’ve had the key to the Chamber of Secrets for centuries! Handing it down, father to son," said Ron.

memories.description: I asked Lockhart to show me the blocking move again because I want to actually learn how to defend myself properly.
memories.source_text: "Professor, could you show me that blocking thing again?"

memories.description: I won't let Malfoy get under my skin. If he thinks I'm scared he can forget it.
memories.source_text: "Scared?" muttered Malfoy... "You wish," said Harry out of the corner of his mouth.

memories.description: I'm going to find Justin and set the record straight about the snake. I need him to know the truth, not the rumours.
memories.source_text: "Hello," said Harry. "I'm looking for Justin Finch-Fletchley." ... "I wanted to tell him what really happened with that snake at the Dueling Club," said Harry.

memories.description: We're going to have to steal some proper dangerous stuff. Breaking into Snape's private stores might be on the table and I don't think that's a good idea.
memories.source_text: "D'you realize how much we’re going to have to steal, Hermione? Shredded skin of a boomslang, that’s definitely not in the students’ cupboard. What're we going to do, break into Snape's private stores? I don't know if this is a good idea."

memories.description: This potion is far more complicated than I expected. If Hermione's calling it the most complicated she's seen then it's serious and not something we can just mess about with.
memories.source_text: "Here it is," said Hermione excitedly as she found the page headed The Polyjuice Potion. ... "This is the most complicated potion I’ve ever seen," said Hermione as they scanned the recipe.

memories.description: What on earth is a Squib. I asked it straight out because I needed to know what people meant.
memories.source_text: "And what on earth’s a Squib?"

memories.description: People are calling me Slytherin's heir. That stings and makes me worry everyone will be afraid of me.
memories.source_text: "That I’m Slytherin’s heir, I expect,"

memories.description: I decided to search the corridor myself. I got down on my hands and knees to look for clues.
memories.source_text: "Can’t hurt to have a poke around,"

memories.description: There are scorch marks near the message on the wall. Something powerful or dangerous was here.
memories.source_text: "Scorch marks!"

memories.description: Colin called out to me and squeaked bye. He still looks up to me a bit, even with all this panic.
memories.source_text: "Hullo, Colin,"

memories.description: The Hat still thinks I'd fit in Slytherin. I pulled the stupid thing off and felt sick. I don't want that to be true.
memories.source_text: "you would have done well in Slytherin"

memories.description: Dumbledore's bird suddenly burst into flames right in front of me. For a terrifying second I thought the bird was going to die while I was alone with it.
memories.source_text: the bird burst into flames

memories.description: You stopped the barrier from letting us through. Dobby tells me he hid and sealed the gateway so I couldn't get to platform nine and three quarters.
memories.source_text: "Dobby hid and watched for Harry Potter and sealed the gateway and Dobby had to iron his hands afterward"

memories.description: Dobby admits his Bludger was made to hurt me enough to send me home. He didn't want to kill me, just to get me out of school.
memories.source_text: "Dobby only wanted Harry Potter hurt enough to be sent home!"

memories.description: Dobby wears a pillowcase because house-elves stay enslaved until their masters give them clothes. That's why he hasn't been freed.
memories.source_text: "'Tis a mark of the house-elf's enslavement, sir. Dobby can only be freed if his masters present him with clothes"

memories.description: Dobby says the Chamber of Secrets has been opened again at Hogwarts and that terrible things are happening or are about to happen there.
memories.source_text: "the Chamber of Secrets is open once more"

memories.description: Dobby says house-elves suffered badly when Voldemort was powerful, and that people like me were a beacon of hope back then.
memories.source_text: "Dobby remembers how it was when He-Who-Must-Not-Be-Named was at the height of his powers"

memories.description: I know I'll put myself in danger to protect my friends. Dobby even praises me for risking my life for them, and I accept that about myself.
memories.source_text: "Harry Potter risks his own life for his friends!"

memories.description: Dobby refuses to say who opened the Chamber last time or who opened it now. He's terrified to name names.
memories.source_text: "Dobby can't, sir, Dobby can't, Dobby mustn't tell!"

memories.description: Someone I care about at school is Muggle-born and would be in serious danger if the Chamber targets Muggle-born students.
memories.source_text: "One of my best friends is Muggle-born; she’ll be first in line if the Chamber really has been opened"

memories.description: My feelings toward Dobby are conflicted. I get angry with him for what he did but I also see how miserable and abused he is, so I don't hate him.
memories.source_text: "Dobby is used to death threats, sir. Dobby gets them five times a day at home."

memories.description: She said a silly little word and the gargoyle sprang to life. Say the password and the entrance opens.
memories.source_text: "Lemon drop!"

memories.description: A gargoyle guards the door and it actually moves when you give the right password. It's not just a statue.
memories.source_text: "the gargoyle sprang suddenly to life and hopped aside as the wall behind him split in two."

memories.description: There's a moving spiral staircase hidden behind the wall. It goes up like an escalator to where McGonagall's office must be.
memories.source_text: "Behind the wall was a spiral staircase that was moving smoothly upward, like an escalator."

memories.description: The staircase takes you up to a gleaming oak door with a griffin-shaped knocker. That's where we're heading.
memories.source_text: "They rose upward in circles, higher and higher, until at last, slightly dizzy, Harry saw a gleaming oak door ahead, with a brass knocker in the shape of a griffin."

memories.description: I was terrified about what would happen, but I couldn't help being amazed by the place. Hogwarts still manages to surprise me.
memories.source_text: "Even full of dread for what was coming, Harry couldn’t fail to be amazed."

memories.description: Once you step on that staircase the wall closes behind you. It's private and a bit claustrophobic.
memories.source_text: "As he and Professor McGonagall stepped onto it, Harry heard the wall thud closed behind them."

memories.description: I earned fifty points for that flying. Gryffindor's in the lead now. Well, that's something.
memories.source_text: "Oh, hello, Harry," he said. "Excellent flying yesterday, really excellent. Gryffindor has just taken the lead for the House Cup — you earned fifty points!"

memories.description: I was desperate to tell Ron and Hermione about Colin and Dobby, but they weren't even there. It stung that they didn't seem interested in whether I had my bones back or not.
memories.source_text: "desperate to tell Ron and Hermione about Colin and Dobby, but they weren’t there."

memories.description: I blasted Malfoy with Rictusempra and it actually tickled him sick. That spell hits hard enough to drop someone laughing, not just a bit of show-off magic.
memories.source_text: "Rictusempra!" A jet of silver light hit Malfoy in the stomach and he doubled up, wheezing.

memories.description: I told myself not to take advantage and hang back. That was daft. Being decent in the middle of a duel left me open and I got Tarantallegra right in the knees. Never assume mercy from Malfoy again.
memories.source_text: "I hung back, with a vague feeling it would be unsporting to bewitch Malfoy while he was on the floor, but this was a mistake; gasping for breath, Malfoy pointed his wand at Harry’s knees, choked, "Tarantallegra!" and the next second Harry’s legs began to jerk around out of his control in a kind of quickstep."

memories.description: Snape set me up with Malfoy on purpose. He was smirking and pulling strings, so I don't trust that he has my best interests at heart when he volunteers pairings.
memories.source_text: "How about Malfoy and Potter?" said Snape with a twisted smile.

memories.description: Lockhart tries to look confident but he's useless when it comes to real teaching. Snape will step in every time to make things worse or manipulate the situation.
memories.source_text: "Let's have a volunteer pair — Longbottom and Finch-Fletchley, how about you —" "A bad idea, Professor Lockhart," said Snape, gliding over like a large and malevolent bat. "Longbottom causes devastation with the simplest spells. We'll be sending what's left of Finch-Fletchley up to the hospital wing in a matchbox."

memories.description: A month to brew it. Right, that gives us time but not loads.
memories.source_text: “Well, since the fluxweed has got to be picked at the full moon and the lacewings have got to be stewed for twenty-one days . . . I’d say it’d be ready in about a month, if we can get all the ingredients.”

memories.description: That's mental. The Bludger is fixating on me, which is not normal. Someone or something is making it target me.
memories.source_text: “Close one, Harry!” said George, streaking past him with his club in his hand, ready to knock the Bludger back toward a Slytherin. ... the Bludger changed direction in midair and shot straight for Harry again. ... Once again, the Bludger swerved like a boomerang and shot at Harry’s head. ... He could hear the Bludger whistling along behind him. What was going on? Bludgers never concentrated on one player like this; it was their job to try and unseat as many people as possible.

memories.description: I know people expect me to go for the Snitch no matter what. They shout stuff like "get the Snitch or die trying" and it puts pressure on me to do something reckless.
memories.source_text: "Get the Snitch or die trying," what a stupid thing to tell him —"

memories.description: The Bludger really was gunning for me. I let it get the better of me for one second and my arm got smashed. It's broken and it hurts like mad.
memories.source_text: He had stayed still a second too long. The Bludger had hit him at last, smashed into his elbow, and Harry felt his arm break.

memories.description: I saw the Snitch sitting right above Malfoy's head while he was laughing at me. If I could have managed it, I would have grabbed it off him in a heartbeat.
memories.source_text: he saw it — the Golden Snitch. It was hovering inches above Malfoy’s left ear — and Malfoy, busy laughing at Harry, hadn’t seen it.

memories.description: Madam Pomfrey can mend bones and she'll be able to grow mine back, but it's going to hurt and I'll have to stay in the hospital wing overnight.
memories.source_text: "You will be able to, won’t you?" said Harry desperately. "I’ll be able to, certainly, but it will be painful," said Madam Pomfrey grimly, throwing Harry a pair of pajamas. "You’ll have to stay the night. . . ."

memories.description: Pomfrey said I've got thirty-three bones to regrow. She makes it clear she wants me left alone so I can rest.
memories.source_text: "This boy needs rest, he’s got thirty-three bones to regrow! Out! OUT!"

memories.description: Fred and George back me up more than they tease when it matters. They argue but they step in on my side when things get serious.
memories.source_text: "Fred, George, you heard Harry — leave him alone and let him deal with the Bludger on his own."

memories.description: Even after I got hit, people noticed I was flying well. Marcus Flint was yelling at Malfoy about the Snitch on his head. Malfoy was furious, which proves I messed him up enough to scare him.
memories.source_text: "Unbelievable flying, Harry," said George. "I’ve just seen Marcus Flint yelling at Malfoy. Something about having the Snitch on top of his head and not noticing. Malfoy didn’t seem too happy."

memories.description: The crowd laughed at me while I dodged that rogue Bludger. I looked ridiculous but I kept going because I had to keep control and try to get the Snitch.
memories.source_text: He could hear laughter from the crowd; he knew he must look very stupid, but the rogue Bludger was heavy and couldn’t change direction as quickly as Harry could; he began a kind of roller-coaster ride around the edges of the stadium

memories.description: They saw me speaking Parseltongue and reckon I chased a snake toward Justin.
memories.source_text: All I saw," said Ernie stubbornly, though he was trembling as he spoke, "was you speaking Parseltongue and chasing the snake toward Justin."

memories.description: I didn't chase it at him! It didn't even touch him, but people are already convinced otherwise.
memories.source_text: "I didn’t chase it at him!" Harry said, his voice shaking with anger. "It didn’t even touch him!"

memories.description: McGonagall says it's out of her hands, so this is being taken up to the headmistress and I'm not in control of what happens next.
memories.source_text: "This is out of my hands, Potter," said Professor McGonagall curtly.

memories.description: They're bringing blood status into it and using that to justify suspicion; people are assuming my abilities tie me to dark things because of blood.
memories.source_text: "And in case you’re getting ideas," he added hastily, "I might tell you that you can trace my family back through nine generations of witches and warlocks and my blood’s as pure as anyone’s, so —"

memories.description: That Bludger is after me. It keeps coming for my head no matter how many times others try to hit it away.
memories.source_text: "Close one, Harry!" said George, streaking past him with his club in his hand, ready to knock the Bludger back toward a Slytherin.

memories.description: Someone's messed with the Bludger. This isn't normal Quidditch business. It's deliberately targeting me.
memories.source_text: "Someone's — tampered — with — this — Bludger —" Fred grunted, swinging his bat with all his might at it as it launched a new attack on Harry.

memories.description: I can hear it right behind me. I need to get away fast or it'll smash me out of the sky.
memories.source_text: He could hear the Bludger whistling along behind him.

memories.description: Slytherin are way ahead. The rest of the game is going badly while I'm being chased by that blasted Bludger.
memories.source_text: He didn’t have a clue what was going on in the rest of the game until he heard Lee Jordan, who was commentating, say, "Slytherin lead, sixty points to zero —"

memories.description: They're totally blank. Not a single thing written in it.
memories.source_text: They were completely blank. There wasn’t the faintest trace of writing on any of them

memories.description: I saw a shop name from Vauxhall Road on the back. It's a Muggle shop.
memories.source_text: Harry turned to the back cover of the book and saw the printed name of a variety store on Vauxhall Road, London.

memories.description: He must have been Muggle-born if he'd bought a diary from Vauxhall Road.
memories.source_text: “He must’ve been Muggle-born,” said Harry thoughtfully.

memories.description: I kept the diary. I'm holding onto it.
memories.source_text: Harry, however, pocketed it.

memories.description: Hagrid was expelled. Of course he was kicked out, and the attacks seem to have stopped once he was gone. That's what everyone thinks now.
memories.source_text: "We always knew Hagrid had been expelled," said Harry miserably. "And the attacks must’ve stopped after Hagrid was kicked out."

memories.description: So phoenixes literally burst into flame when it's their time and then are reborn from the ashes. He really did come back from being just a pile of ash.
memories.source_text: Fawkes is a phoenix, Harry. Phoenixes burst into flame when it is time for them to die and are reborn from the ashes. Watch him

memories.description: I thought there was nothing I could do to save Fawkes and felt useless, but seeing him reborn made me stop panicking so hard — it wasn't the end.
memories.source_text: Your bird, I couldn't do anything, he just caught fire

memories.description: Dumbledore wasn't angry or upset about Fawkes dying, he was oddly amused and calm. He treats Fawkes like family and expects this to happen, which made me feel less guilty and more confused.
memories.source_text: About time, too, He's been looking dreadful for days, I've been telling him to get a move on

memories.description: It's ready. I woke up and wanted to know for certain, because if we're doing this tonight I need it to work.
memories.source_text: "It’s ready." Harry sat up, suddenly wide awake. "Are you sure?"

memories.description: Of course I want to investigate Malfoy. I agreed to go along even though it sounds risky.
memories.source_text: "You do want to investigate Malfoy, don’t you?"

memories.description: We only get an hour in someone else's body after drinking the Polyjuice. We have to be quick.
memories.source_text: "Once we’ve drunk it, we’ll have exactly an hour before we change back into ourselves."

memories.description: It's a diary and it's fifty years old. The name T. M. Riddle is on the first page.
memories.source_text: The little book lay on the floor, nondescript and soggy. Harry saw at once that it was a diary, and the faded year on the cover told him it was fifty years old.

memories.description: Right, we're not going to just stand here. If we want answers, I have to check the thing myself.
memories.source_text: Well, we won’t find out unless we look at it," he said, and he ducked around Ron and picked it up off the floor.

memories.description: That's Riddle's diary. I can tell it's not just any book.
memories.source_text: Leering, he showed it to Crabbe and Goyle, and Harry realized that he’d got Riddle’s diary.

memories.description: Ginny looked terrified when she saw that diary. Whatever's going on with her is serious.
memories.source_text: Ginny was staring from the diary to Harry, looking terrified.

memories.description: Malfoy getting one over on me matters. Beating him feels like winning for all of us.
memories.source_text: But Harry didn’t care, he was one-up on Malfoy, and that was worth five points from Gryffindor any day.

memories.description: If Malfoy has something that could hurt Ginny or mess things up, I will use magic to stop him even if I'll get in trouble.
memories.source_text: Percy said, "As a school prefect —" but Harry had lost his temper. He pulled out his wand and shouted, "Expelliarmus!"

memories.description: He apologized and offered his hand. I shook it. We're not enemies anymore.
memories.source_text: “I just want to say, Harry, that I’m sorry I ever suspected you. I know you’d never attack Hermione Granger, and I apologize for all the stuff I said. We’re all in the same boat now, and, well —”

memories.description: Ernie admits he was wrong to suspect me. I can count on him not to accuse me again.
memories.source_text: “I just want to say, Harry, that I’m sorry I ever suspected you. I know you’d never attack Hermione Granger, and I apologize for all the stuff I said. We’re all in the same boat now, and, well —”

memories.description: We have to add other people's hair to the Polyjuice Potion to take their form.
memories.source_text: Add yours, then,

memories.description: We can't all change into Crabbe and Goyle in the same tiny bathroom stall or we'll not fit.
memories.source_text: We'd better not all drink them in here.

memories.description: The password to that passage was 'pure-blood' and Malfoy used it to open the door.
memories.source_text: pure-blood!

memories.description: Malfoy acted like he might know who's behind the Chamber nonsense, but I don't trust him; he sounded smug not helpful.
memories.source_text: I could help them.

memories.description: Someone who opened the Chamber before was expelled and they might be in Azkaban.
memories.source_text: Azkaban?

memories.description: What does she understand? I need her to tell me straight away.
memories.source_text: [What does she understand?]

memories.description: I thought Hagrid had opened the Chamber and released the monster, but that was wrong. Hagrid didn’t set it free.
memories.source_text: "And you . . . you didn’t come from the Chamber of Secrets?" said Harry, who could feel cold sweat on his forehead.

memories.description: No way is this over. I don't buy that the danger has passed just because someone's saying so.
memories.source_text: Don't you people realize," said Lockhart, speaking slowly, as though they were all a bit dim, "the danger has passed! The culprit has been taken away —

memories.description: I can't trust Lockhart's smug confidence. He talks like he knows everything and he doesn't.
memories.source_text: "My dear young man, the Minister of Magic wouldn't have taken Hagrid if he hadn't been one hundred percent sure that he was guilty," said Lockhart

memories.description: We're going tonight. I'm not waiting around while Hagrid gets blamed.
memories.source_text: Let’s do it tonight.

memories.description: Fang comes with me. He's eager and I'll use him to get into the forest.
memories.source_text: "C'mon, Fang, we're going for a walk," said Harry, patting his leg, and Fang bounded happily out of the house behind them

memories.description: A little wand light is perfect for watching the path. I use Lumos to look for spiders without drawing too much attention.
memories.source_text: Harry took out his wand, murmured, "Lumos!" and a tiny light appeared at the end of it, just enough to let them watch the path for signs of spiders.

memories.description: Ron and I are in this together. He cares about Hagrid and I shut him up because we need to act, not argue.
memories.source_text: Ron started to say that he didn't think so, somehow, but stopped in midsentence when Harry kicked him hard under the desk. "We weren't there, remember?" Harry muttered.

memories.description: I want to drop Potions, I'm fed up with it and would happily give it up if I could.
memories.source_text: I just want to give up Potions

memories.description: I heard that terrifying voice again. I'm certain something odd is happening and it might be dangerous.
memories.source_text: The voice! I just heard it again didn't you?

memories.description: I don't blame him for wanting to stay here. If I had the choice between going back to a Muggle orphanage or staying at Hogwarts, I'd stay too.
memories.source_text: "And Riddle was going to go back to some Muggle orphanage if they closed Hogwarts," said Harry.

memories.description: I met Hagrid down Knockturn Alley and he was buying a Flesh-Eating Slug Repellent. That's what I told them, quick and simple.
memories.source_text: "He was buying a Flesh-Eating Slug Repellent," said Harry quickly.

memories.description: No. I'm certain it's not Malfoy. I just won't buy that for a second.
memories.source_text: "No," said Harry, so firmly that Ernie and Hannah stared.

memories.description: Those spiders are moving in a straight line like they're being sent somewhere. If they keep that course, we'll know exactly where they're going.
memories.source_text: Several large spiders were scuttling over the ground on the other side of the glass, moving in an unnaturally straight line as though taking the shortest route to a prearranged meeting.

memories.description: Hagrid, did you hear about Hermione?
memories.source_text: "Hagrid?" said Harry. "Did you hear about Hermione?"

memories.description: I'm one of Hagrid's friends and I'm standing up for him.
memories.source_text: "We're friends of Hagrid's," Harry shouted.

memories.description: The Ministry has taken Hagrid to Azkaban.
memories.source_text: "They've taken him to Azkaban."

memories.description: If Hagrid had men go into the spiders' hollow, something serious must be wrong with him.
memories.source_text: "Hagrid has never sent men into our hollow before," he said slowly.

memories.description: So Aragog wasn't born in the castle. He was brought here as an egg and given to Hagrid.
memories.source_text: “I was not born in the castle. I come from a distant land. A traveler gave me to Hagrid when I was an egg.”

memories.description: Hagrid looked after Aragog when he was a baby, hiding him in a cupboard and feeding him. That explains why Aragog is loyal to him.
memories.source_text: “Hagrid was only a boy, but he cared for me, hidden in a cupboard in the castle, feeding me on scraps from the table.”

memories.description: Hagrid protected Aragog and even found him a mate. Aragog sees Hagrid as a true friend and a good man.
memories.source_text: “Hagrid is my good friend, and a good man.”

memories.description: I can't believe people blamed Aragog for the Chamber attacks. He wasn't the monster from the Chamber.
memories.source_text: “They believed that I was the monster that dwells in what they call the Chamber of Secrets. They thought that Hagrid had opened the Chamber and set me free.”

memories.description: Aragog says he never attacked anyone and avoided hurting humans out of respect for Hagrid.
memories.source_text: “Never,” croaked the old spider. “It would have been my instinct, but out of respect for Hagrid, I never harmed a human.”

memories.description: There is another, ancient creature living in the castle that even the spiders fear. That's the real threat.
memories.source_text: “The thing that lives in the castle,” said Aragog, “is an ancient creature we spiders fear above all others.”

memories.description: We're lucky to be alive
memories.source_text: "We’re lucky to be alive."

memories.description: He probably thought Aragog wouldn't hurt his friends
memories.source_text: "I bet he thought Aragog wouldn’t hurt friends of his," said Harry.

memories.description: Hagrid never opened the Chamber of Secrets
memories.source_text: "That Hagrid never opened the Chamber of Secrets," said Harry, throwing the

memories.description: It's a basilisk, a huge snake. Of course it explains the voice I keep hearing. I can talk Parseltongue so I hear it and they don't.
memories.source_text: The monster in the Chamber's a basilisk, a giant serpent! That's why I've been hearing that voice all over the place, and nobody else has heard it. It's because I understand Parseltongue.

memories.description: The thing kills by eye contact. Nobody's been killed because nobody looked it straight in the eye. That's why people only end up petrified.
memories.source_text: The basilisk kills people by looking at them. But no one's died because no one looked it straight in the eye.

memories.description: Colin saw it on camera but the film was ruined. He got petrified, not killed, which fits with the eye thing.
memories.source_text: Colin saw it through his camera. The basilisk burned up all the film inside it, but Colin just got Petrified.

memories.description: Justin's petrified too. That's another victim who didn't look straight at it but still got turned to stone.
memories.source_text: Justin . . .

memories.description: I'm going down there. I can't not go now we've found the entrance to the Chamber. If there's even the faintest chance Ginny might be alive I have to try.
memories.source_text: "I’m going down there," he said.

memories.description: She died in this very toilet stall. The place where Myrtle haunts is where she died.
memories.source_text: "I died in this very stall."

memories.description: Myrtle says she saw huge yellow eyes right before she died. Whatever did it had huge yellow eyes.
memories.source_text: "I just remember seeing a pair of great, big, yellow eyes."

memories.description: Someone spoke in a strange language in the bathroom when she died. It wasn't normal talk.
memories.source_text: "They said something funny. A different language, I think it must have been."

memories.description: The person who came in and spoke was a boy. So a boy was involved the night she died.
memories.source_text: "Anyway, what really got me was that it was a boy speaking."

memories.description: Myrtle was hiding in the stall because Olive Hornby was teasing her about her glasses. She was upset and crying when it happened.
memories.source_text: "I'd hidden because Olive Hornby was teasing me about my glasses."

memories.description: It could be in Moaning Myrtle's bathroom. That's where the thing's been hiding.
memories.source_text: "What if it’s in —" "— Moaning Myrtle’s bathroom," said Harry.

memories.description: I can't be the only Parselmouth here. The Heir of Slytherin can speak to the basilisk, and that's how it's been controlled.
memories.source_text: "This means," said Harry, "I can’t be the only Parselmouth in the school. The Heir of Slytherin’s one, too. That’s how he’s been controlling the basilisk."

memories.description: We're going straight to the staffroom to find Professor McGonagall right away. She'll be there soon.
memories.source_text: "Let’s go to the staffroom," said Harry, jumping up. "She’ll be there in ten minutes. It’s nearly break."

memories.description: Lockhart thinks he can get away with a Memory Charm to stop us telling anyone. He means to wipe our memories.
memories.source_text: "Awfully sorry, boys, but I’ll have to put a Memory Charm on you now. Can’t have you blabbing my secrets all over the place."

memories.description: She says she saw eyes at the sink. She actually pointed at it, so I treated the sink as suspect.
memories.source_text: "Where exactly did you see the eyes?" said Harry. "Somewhere there," said Myrtle, pointing vaguely toward the sink in front of her toilet.

memories.description: I rushed to the sink and checked it properly. It looked normal, but we went over every inch, even the pipes.
memories.source_text: Harry and Ron hurried over to it. Lockhart was standing well back, a look of utter terror on his face. It looked like an ordinary sink. They examined every inch of it, inside and out, including the pipes below.

memories.description: There is some ancient creature living in the castle that even the spiders are terrified of.
memories.source_text: “The thing that lives in the castle,” said Aragog, “is an ancient creature we spiders fear above all others.”

memories.description: Aragog never told Hagrid the name of that dread creature even though Hagrid asked him again and again.
memories.source_text: “I never even told Hagrid the name of that dread creature, though he asked me, many times.”

memories.description: I stopped pushing for details once Aragog snarled that they will not speak of or name it and the spiders closed in on me.
memories.source_text: “We do not speak of it!” said Aragog fiercely. “We do not name it!”

memories.description: We're miles under the school. We're well below Hogwarts.
memories.source_text: "We must be miles under the school," said Harry, his voice echoing in the black tunnel.

memories.description: We're probably under the lake. That's where we are.
memories.source_text: "Under the lake, probably," said Ron, squinting around at the dark, slimy walls.

memories.description: My wand lights the tunnel. I can light the way when it's pitch black.
memories.source_text: "Lumos!" Harry muttered to his wand and it lit again.

memories.description: I had to push Lockhart into the pipe to get things moving. He's useless without being shoved.
memories.source_text: Harry jabbed him in the back with his wand. Lockhart slid his legs into the pipe.

memories.description: I went over to Myrtle because she was clearly upset. I asked what was wrong and who had been bothering her.
memories.source_text: "What’s up, Myrtle?" said Harry.

memories.description: There was a small shabby black book under the sink that had been washed out of Myrtle's stall.
memories.source_text: "It’s over there, it got washed out."

memories.description: I thought being a ghost would mean thrown things just go through her and can't hurt her. Apparently I was wrong to be flippant about it.
memories.source_text: "But it can’t hurt you if someone throws something at you," said Harry.

memories.description: I decided not to let fear stop me. If there's a mystery, I'm going to check it out myself.
memories.source_text: "Well, we won’t find out unless we look at it," he said, and he ducked around Ron and picked it up off the floor.

memories.description: She's alive but barely. I need to act fast or she'll die.
memories.source_text: "She’s still alive," said Riddle. "But only just."

memories.description: That boy is not a ghost, he's a memory trapped in a diary. The diary holds him.
memories.source_text: "Are you a ghost?" "A memory," said Riddle quietly. "Preserved in a diary for fifty years."

memories.description: The basilisk won't attack randomly. Someone has to call it first.
memories.source_text: "It won’t come until it is called," said Riddle calmly.

memories.description: My wand has been taken. I don't have it and Riddle's holding it, so I'm at a real disadvantage.
memories.source_text: "Thanks," said Harry, stretching out his hand for it. A smile curled the corners of Riddle’s mouth. He continued to stare at Harry, twirling the wand idly."

memories.description: Riddle isn't just some leftover memory; he's been waiting to meet me. This is personal and dangerous.
memories.source_text: "I’ve waited a long time for this, Harry Potter," said Riddle. "For the chance to see you. To speak to you."

memories.description: The diary I found in Myrtle's bathroom is here in the Chamber and it's connected to what's happened to Ginny.
memories.source_text: "Lying open there was the little black diary Harry had found in Moaning Myrtle’s bathroom."

memories.description: I said "Open up" and it came out as a hiss in Parseltongue, and the tap actually opened. I can force Parseltongue to work even when there is only an engraving if I really believe it.
memories.source_text: "Open up," he said. Except that the words weren’t what he heard; a strange hissing had escaped him, and at once the tap glowed with a brilliant white light and began to spin.

memories.description: When the tap opened, the sink sank and revealed a big pipe I could go down. There is a passage hidden beneath the sink.
memories.source_text: Next second, the sink began to move; the sink, in fact, sank, right out of sight, leaving a large pipe exposed, a pipe wide enough for a man to slide into.

memories.description: I used to think I could only speak Parseltongue to real snakes, but I forced it here, so I know I can trigger it by convincing myself the mark is alive.
memories.source_text: "But —" Harry thought hard. The only times he’d ever managed to speak Parseltongue were when he’d been faced with a real snake.

memories.description: I have to go on alone. I'm telling Ron to stay with Lockhart and I'm setting an hour as a cutoff. I need to get on despite being scared, so I'm pushing myself to sound confident.
memories.source_text: "Wait there," he called to Ron. "Wait with Lockhart. I'll go on, If I'm not back in an hour"

memories.description: This is it. The thing in the Chamber is a basilisk, a giant serpent, and I can hear it because I speak Parseltongue. Of course the others couldn't hear it.
memories.source_text: This is it. This is the answer.

memories.description: The basilisk kills by eye contact. No one died because no one looked it straight in the eye. They got petrified instead from indirect viewing like through a camera, Nearly Headless Nick, or a mirror.
memories.source_text: The basilisk kills people by looking at them.

memories.description: Hermione was clutching a scrunched bit of paper in her hand. She must have worked something out and tried to warn people.
memories.source_text: Harry looked up at the beds around him.

memories.description: The Basilisk is terrified of roosters. If a rooster crows it drives the thing off.
memories.source_text: 'The Basilisk flees only from the crowing of the rooster, which is fatal to it'!

memories.description: Spiders run from the Basilisk. That explains why they're bolting and why Hagrid's creatures were connected to this.
memories.source_text: 'Spiders flee before the Basilisk'!
