memories.description: It's been getting around through the plumbing. I kept hearing that voice inside the walls and now it makes sense.
memories.source_text: Pipes

memories.description: I can't be the only Parselmouth at Hogwarts. The Heir of Slytherin must be a Parselmouth too, and that's how he's been controlling the basilisk.
memories.source_text: - Moaning Myrtle’s bathroom,

memories.description: Let's go to the staffroom. McGonagall'll be there in ten minutes and we need to tell her.
memories.source_text: Let’s go to the staffroom,

memories.description: Ginny's been in the Chamber for hours. There's no time to faff about.
memories.source_text: "Ginny had already been in the Chamber of Secrets for hours."

memories.description: I'm going on alone. You stay with Lockhart and wait for me. If I'm not back in an hour, well, I'll have to deal with it.
memories.source_text: "Wait there," he called to Ron. "Wait with Lockhart. I'll go on. If I'm not back in an hour..."

memories.description: If anything moves down here, shut your eyes straight away. No dawdling, it could be dangerous.
memories.source_text: Remember, any sign of movement, close your eyes right away.

memories.description: Those cracks in the tunnel mean it could cave in. I can't risk blasting the rocks with magic or the whole place might fall.
memories.source_text: Huge cracks had appeared in it.

memories.description: She poured her heart into a diary and it was feeding whatever's in there. Ginny's been writing to it about everything, even about me. That's why she's like this.
memories.source_text: "My diary. Little Ginny’s been writing in it for months and months, telling me all her pitiful worries and woes — how her brothers tease her, how she had to come to school with secondhand robes and books, how ... how she didn’t think famous, good, great Harry Potter would ever like her."

memories.description: Riddle claims Dumbledore was forced out by him. I don't believe that, but Riddle wants me to think he's powerful enough to scare Dumbledore off.
memories.source_text: "Dumbledore’s been driven out of this castle by the mere memory of me!"

memories.description: A phoenix showed up, sat on my shoulder and dropped the Sorting Hat at my feet. It's Fawkes and he came for me.
memories.source_text: "A crimson bird the size of a swan... A second later, the bird was flying straight at Harry. It dropped the ragged thing it was carrying at his feet, then landed heavily on his shoulder."

memories.description: The bird is Fawkes. He's on my side right now and he came exactly when I needed him.
memories.source_text: "That’s a phoenix... Fawkes?"

memories.description: The thing Fawkes dropped is the Sorting Hat. It just appeared in the Chamber and it's with me now.
memories.source_text: "that’s the old school Sorting Hat"

memories.description: The Slytherin statue is moving and something is coming out of its mouth. Whatever's in the Chamber is waking up and it's coming for me.
memories.source_text: "Speak to me, Slytherin, greatest of the Hogwarts Four."

memories.description: I felt terrified and alone for a second. Even with Fawkes here I worried we're up against something huge and dangerous.
memories.source_text: "Harry wanted to shout, 'Don’t leave me!' but what chance did a phoenix have against the king of serpents?"

memories.description: I couldn't believe it when Dumbledore said Voldemort put part of himself inside me. That's mental and it explains why I can do things like Parseltongue.
memories.source_text: Voldemort put a bit of himself in me?

memories.description: For a second I thought I must belong in Slytherin because of what the Sorting Hat saw and because of those Slytherin traits in me, but I asked not to go there and that choice matters. Choosing Gryffindor proves something about who I am.
memories.source_text: So I should be in Slytherin

memories.description: When Dumbledore handed me the sword of Godric Gryffindor and showed the name engraved on it I knew that I really am a Gryffindor. Pulling that sword out wasn't luck.
memories.source_text: Only a true Gryffindor could have pulled that out of the hat, Harry

memories.description: Dumbledore made it clear I'm not like Tom Riddle. It's my choices, not the stuff I'm capable of, that define me. I actually feel more certain about who I want to be.
memories.source_text: Which makes you very different from Tom Riddle. It is our choices, Harry, that show what we truly are, far more than our abilities.

memories.description: I want that Firebolt more than anything. I can't stop thinking about it.
memories.source_text: He had never wanted anything as much in his whole life

memories.description: I won't empty my Gringotts vault for the Firebolt. My Nimbus Two Thousand is a very good broom, and blowing all my money on a new one isn't worth it.
memories.source_text: what was the point in emptying his Gringotts vault for the Firebolt, when he had a very good broom already?

memories.description: Even though I'm not buying it, I keep going back to look at the Firebolt every day. I can't help it.
memories.source_text: he returned, almost every day after that, just to look at the Firebolt

memories.description: You gave Ginny that diary by slipping it into her old Transfiguration book in Flourish and Blotts. I know you did it.
memories.source_text: [Because you gave it to her, said Harry. In Flourish and Blotts. You picked up her old Transfiguration book and slipped the diary inside it, didn’t you?]

memories.description: Riddle's memories were wiped from the diary, otherwise who knows how badly things would have turned out.
memories.source_text: [Very fortunate the diary was discovered, and Riddle’s memories wiped from it. Who knows what the consequences might have been otherwise. . . .]

memories.description: Dobby tried to help and actually did something for me, but I told him to never try to save my life again.
memories.source_text: [Least I could do, Dobby, said Harry, grinning. Just promise never to try and save my life again.]

memories.description: When Dobby kept pointing at the diary and Malfoy and hitting himself, it all clicked for me. Of course, Dobby was trying to tell us Lucius was involved.
memories.source_text: [The elf was doing something very odd. His great eyes fixed meaningfully on Harry, he kept pointing at the diary, then at Mr Malfoy, and then hitting himself hard on the head with his fist.]

memories.description: Dobby's loyalty to Malfoy is complicated, but he helped me anyway. I trust Dobby more after this, even if he belongs to Lucius.
memories.source_text: [We’re going, Dobby! said Lucius Malfoy. ... The elf’s ugly brown face split suddenly into a wide, toothy smile.]

memories.description: They ignore me most of the time. I can't expect any kindness from them on my birthday or any other day.
memories.source_text: Far from wishing Harry a happy birthday, none of the Dursleys made any sign that they had noticed Harry enter the room

memories.description: Vernon hates my hair and uses it as an excuse to pick on me whenever he can.
memories.source_text: He shot a nasty look sideways at Harry, whose untidy hair had always been a source of great annoyance to Uncle Vernon

memories.description: Aunt Marge is coming to stay for a week. Fantastic. That's the worst 'present' I could imagine.
memories.source_text: Marge'll be here for a week

memories.description: Vernon's lied to his sister about me. He's told Aunt Marge I go to some horrible place called St. Brutus's and I have to stick to that story.
memories.source_text: we've told Marge you attend St. Brutus's Secure Center for Incurably Criminal Boys

memories.description: Dudley enjoys seeing me humiliated. He sits there and laughs when Vernon picks on me.
memories.source_text: Watching Harry being bullied by Uncle Vernon was Dudley's favorite form of entertainment

memories.description: Petunia is nosey and will love having something to gossip about. She'd jump at the chance to call any hotline or tell tales to anyone who'll listen.
memories.source_text: Aunt Petunia ... was the nosiest woman in the world and spent most of her life spying on the boring, law-abiding neighbors

memories.description: If Vernon beats me into silence, that won't stop me from telling the truth to Aunt Marge. I won't be cowed into hiding what I know.
memories.source_text: Knocking the stuffing out of me won't make Aunt Marge forget what I could tell her

memories.description: I need Vernon to sign a permission form so I can visit the village with my year. He's the obstacle I have to get past.
memories.source_text: I need you to sign the permission form

memories.description: I must have shown real loyalty down in the Chamber because that is what called Fawkes to me.
memories.source_text: "Nothing but that could have called Fawkes to you."

memories.description: The Sorting Hat put the sword in my hands. That is how I got the sword.
memories.source_text: "the Sorting Hat giving him the sword."

memories.description: Riddle's diary caused what happened to Ginny. The diary did the messing with her.
memories.source_text: "It was this diary," said Harry quickly, picking it up and showing it to Dumbledore.

memories.description: Tom Riddle and Lord Voldemort are the same person. Dumbledore taught him here years ago.
memories.source_text: "Very few people know that Lord Voldemort was once called Tom Riddle. I taught him myself, fifty years ago, at Hogwarts."

memories.description: Dumbledore thanked me and thinks I was loyal enough to call Fawkes. He knows what I did was brave.
memories.source_text: "I want to thank you," said Dumbledore, "You must have shown me real loyalty down in the Chamber."

memories.description: Riddle tried to tell me I'm like him. I don't think I'm like him. I am in Gryffindor and I won't be Slytherin.
memories.source_text: "Riddle said I’m like him. Strange likenesses, he said."

memories.description: I can speak Parseltongue because Voldemort can. That is why people thought I might be his heir.
memories.source_text: "You can speak Parseltongue, Harry," said Dumbledore calmly, "because Lord Voldemort ... can speak Parseltongue."

memories.description: Ginny is shaken and upset. I feel terrible for her and worried she might get into trouble.
memories.source_text: "She was standing with her head against Mrs. Weasley’s shoulder, and tears were still coursing silently down her cheeks."

memories.description: Yeah, I get beaten a lot. Loads of times. It's normal for them and they treat it like nothing.
memories.source_text: "Have you been beaten often?" "Oh, yeah," said Harry, "loads of times."

memories.description: Aunt Marge and the others think it's fine to use extreme force on me. They actually approve that kind of treatment.
memories.source_text: "If you can speak of your beatings in that casual way, they clearly aren't hitting you hard enough. Petunia, I'd write if I were you. Make it clear that you approve the use of extreme force in this boy's case."

memories.description: I don't want Vernon near me anymore. I mean it — keep away.
memories.source_text: "You keep away from me."

memories.description: I can't let them slander my parents like that. I'm not going to sit there and let them lie about how Mum and Dad died.
memories.source_text: "They didn't die in a car crash!" said Harry.

memories.description: Aunt Marge went completely mad and then started inflating like a huge balloon. It was mental, like something straight out of magic.
memories.source_text: "You are an insolent, ungrateful little —" But Aunt Marge suddenly stopped speaking. ... she was inflating like a monstrous balloon"

memories.description: I felt a reckless rage and I genuinely think she deserved what happened. I wasn't sad about it; I was furious at her.
memories.source_text: "She deserved it," Harry said, breathing very fast. "She deserved what she got."

memories.description: That's it — I'm done. I can't stand living with them anymore. I'm leaving; I've had enough of being treated like dirt.
memories.source_text: "I'm going," Harry said. "I've had enough."

memories.description: Ripper went berserk when Aunt Marge started floating and shouting; the dog reacted like it was all chaos.
memories.source_text: "Ripper came skidding into the room, barking madly."

memories.description: Right now I have to pretend to be a proper Muggle if I want that form signed. I will act normal, keep to the story, and play their game so I can go to Hogsmeade with Ron and Hermione.
memories.source_text: ["But if you sign my permission form," Harry went on quickly, "I swear I’ll remember where I’m supposed to go to school, and I’ll act like a Mug — like I’m normal and everything."]

memories.description: If I toe the line for Marge's visit and keep to the story, Vernon says he'll sign the permission form. That's my one shot to convince them.
memories.source_text: ["I’ll sign your ruddy form." he wheeled around, pulled open the front door, and slammed it so hard that one of the little panes of glass at the top fell out.]

memories.description: Hedwig and Errol are going to stay with Ron for a week. I need to write Ron a note and trust him to look after her while I keep up appearances here.
memories.source_text: ["Hedwig," he said gloomily, "you’re going to have to clear off for a week. Go with Errol. Ron’ll look after you. I’ll write him a note, explaining."]

memories.description: Dudley only tolerates Marge's affections because he gets paid for them. It's all for show and money, nothing genuine.
memories.source_text: [Aunt Marge thrust the suitcase into Harry’s stomach, knocking the wind out of him, seized Dudley in a tight one-armed hug, and planted a large kiss on his cheek. Harry knew perfectly well that Dudley only put up with Aunt Marge’s hugs because he was well paid for it, and sure enough, when they broke apart, Dudley had a crisp twenty-pound note clutched in his fat fist.]

memories.description: Marge loves the idea of punishment and cane culture. Trying to argue with her won't work. I need to avoid provoking her at all costs while I'm stuck here.
memories.source_text: ["I won’t have this namby-pamby, wishy-washy nonsense about not hitting people who deserve it. A good thrashing is what’s needed in ninety-nine cases out of a hundred."]

memories.description: There was something huge and black in that alleyway. It looked like a dog but much bigger. I pointed it out because it freaked me out.
memories.source_text: "There was a big black thing," said Harry, pointing uncertainly into the gap. "Like a dog . . . but massive . . ."

memories.description: The Knight Bus goes anywhere on land. It cannot go underwater. That means it can get me to London if I need to be somewhere fast.
memories.source_text: "Yep," said Stan proudly, "anywhere you like, long's it's on land. Can't do nuffink underwater."

memories.description: I covered my scar and lied because I do not want anyone, especially the Ministry, to spot me. If they are looking for me I must not make it easy for them.
memories.source_text: "Woss that on your 'ead?" said Stan abruptly. "Nothing," said Harry quickly, flattening his hair over his scar.

memories.description: I told Stan my name was Neville Longbottom to keep my real identity secret. I do not trust strangers with the truth right now.
memories.source_text: "Woss your name?" Stan persisted. "Neville Longbottom," said Harry, saying the first name that came into his head.

memories.description: What the hell? They sound like they're letting me off easy for breaking the Decree. That doesn't fit with the way the Ministry treated me before.
memories.source_text: "Oh, my dear boy, we’re not going to punish you for a little thing like that!"

memories.description: I got an official warning last year for magic at the Dursleys. The rules can be enforced harshly against me.
memories.source_text: "Last year, I got an official warning just because a house-elf smashed a pudding in my uncle’s house!"

memories.description: They're suddenly pretended to be worried about my expulsion to justify letting me off. Something odd is going on.
memories.source_text: "Circumstances change, Harry. . . . We have to take into account . . . in the present climate . . . Surely you don’t want to be expelled?"

memories.description: Fudge wants me watched and kept in Diagon Alley and back at the Leaky Cauldron before dark. He's putting someone on me.
memories.source_text: "I don’t want you wandering off into Muggle London, all right? Keep to Diagon Alley. And you’re to be back here before dark each night. Tom will be keeping an eye on you for me."

memories.description: Fudge is acting like he needs to keep an eye on me. He's being oddly possessive about knowing where I am.
memories.source_text: "Don’t want to lose you again, do we?"

memories.description: Fudge is after Sirius Black. The guards are on the case and they're furious, so they think they'll catch him soon.
memories.source_text: "Have you had any luck with Black yet?" "What’s that? Oh, you’ve heard — well, no, not yet, but it’s only a matter of time. The Azkaban guards have never yet failed . . . and they are angrier than I’ve ever seen them."

memories.description: Fudge says he cannot sign my Hogsmeade permission because he's not my guardian. So I can't go even though he's the Minister.
memories.source_text: "No, no, I’m very sorry, Harry, but as I’m not your parent or guardian —"

memories.description: So this is the Firebolt. It rockets to 150 miles an hour in ten seconds and even has an unbreakable Braking Charm. The whole thing is built like a dream, ash handle, tuned birch tail, balance and precision. That's exactly the kind of broom any player would kill for.
memories.source_text: "THE FIREBOLT This state-of-the-art racing broom sports a streamlined, superfine handle of ash, treated with a diamond-hard polish and hand-numbered with its own registration number. Each individually selected birch twig in the broomtail has been honed to aerodynamic perfection, giving the Firebolt unsurpassable balance and pinpoint precision. The Firebolt has an acceleration of 150 miles an hour in ten seconds and incorporates an unbreakable Braking Charm. Price on request."

memories.description: That's the most magnificent broom I've ever seen. I want one so badly I can hardly breathe. If I had that on the pitch nothing could stop me.
memories.source_text: "the most magnificent broom he had ever seen in his life"

memories.description: He's Stan Shunpike. He's the Knight Bus conductor.
memories.source_text: "My name is Stan Shunpike, and I will be your conductor this eve —"

memories.description: I was sitting on the ground and scrabbled to my feet fast. I snatched my wand up the second I saw him.
memories.source_text: He had just caught sight of Harry, who was still sitting on the ground.

memories.description: Up close Stan looks about my age, maybe eighteen or nineteen. Big ears and loads of pimples.
memories.source_text: "The conductor stopped abruptly. He had just caught sight of Harry"

memories.description: He tried to laugh at me. He was mocking me instead of helping.
memories.source_text: "'Choo fall over for?' sniggered Stan."

memories.description: My knee's ripped and my hand is bleeding from when I fell. It hurts.
memories.source_text: "One of the knees in his jeans was torn, and the hand he had thrown out to break his fall was bleeding."

memories.description: He's not exactly sympathetic. I don't trust him to be polite or professional.
memories.source_text: "'Choo fall over for?' sniggered Stan."

memories.description: I didn't fall on purpose. I was annoyed that he kept making light of it.
memories.source_text: "Fell over," said Harry. "'Choo fall over for?" sniggered Stan."

memories.description: The Monster Book of Monsters is actually the set text for Care of Magical Creatures. Great. Of all the books, that one is on the list.
memories.source_text: The Monster Book of Monsters was listed as the required book for Care of Magical Creatures.

memories.description: There were a hundred copies of that book locked in an iron cage in the shop window. That's mental.
memories.source_text: Instead of the usual display of gold-embossed spellbooks the size of paving slabs, there was a large iron cage behind the glass that held about a hundred copies of The Monster Book of Monsters.

memories.description: Those books were vicious. Pages flying everywhere, books biting and wrestling one another. I couldn't believe my eyes.
memories.source_text: Torn pages were flying everywhere as the books grappled with each other, locked together in furious wrestling matches and snapping aggressively.

memories.description: I needed to stock up on potion ingredients and get new robes because mine were too short. So I went to the apothecary and Madam Malkin's.
memories.source_text: He went to the Apothecary to replenish his store of potions ingredients, and as his school robes were now several inches too short in the arm and leg, he visited Madam Malkin’s Robes for All Occasions and bought new ones.

memories.description: That cover was terrifying and that dog felt familiar to me. I kept staring because something about it was wrong and it stuck in my gut
memories.source_text: "It showed a black dog large as a bear, with gleaming eyes. It looked oddly familiar."

memories.description: The bloke behind the counter shoved Unfogging the Future at me and asked if I wanted anything else, so I ended up buying it
memories.source_text: "The manager pressed Unfogging the Future into Harry’s hands. 'Anything else?' he said."

memories.description: I want to know why someone tried to throw the diary away and how Riddle got that special award. The diary might be the key to both.
memories.source_text: “I wish I knew why someone did try to chuck it,” said Harry. “I wouldn’t mind knowing how Riddle got an award for special services to Hogwarts either.”

memories.description: The Chamber was opened fifty years ago. If the diary is the same age, it could be connected.
memories.source_text: “Well, the Chamber of Secrets was opened fifty years ago, wasn’t it?” he said. “That’s what Malfoy said.”

memories.description: That's Sirius Black on the front page. He was on the Muggle news. I saw him there.
memories.source_text: "That man!" Harry said, forgetting his troubles for a moment. "He was on the Muggle news!"

memories.description: Black is still at large. The Ministry says they have not recaptured him.
memories.source_text: "BLACK STILL AT LARGE Sirius Black, possibly the most infamous prisoner ever to be held in Azkaban fortress, is still eluding capture, the Ministry of Magic confirmed today."

memories.description: He killed thirteen people with one curse. That is terrifying.
memories.source_text: "While Muggles have been told that Black is carrying a gun (a kind of metal wand that Muggles use to kill each other), the magical community lives in fear of a massacre like that of twelve years ago, when Black murdered thirteen people with a single curse."

memories.description: Black was a supporter of You-Know-Who. I didn't expect that connection but it explains why he's so dangerous.
memories.source_text: "Black woz a big supporter of You-Know-’Oo," he said. "What, Voldemort?" said Harry, without thinking.

memories.description: After the massacre he laughed. He stood there laughing even as they took him away. That makes him sound completely mad.
memories.source_text: "An' when reinforcements from the Ministry of Magic got there, 'e went wiv 'em quiet as anyfink, still laughing 'is 'ead off."

memories.description: He escaped from Azkaban. No one knows how he managed it.
memories.source_text: "And now 'e's out," said Stan, examining the newspaper picture of Black's gaunt face again. "Never been a breakout from Azkaban before, 'as there, Ern? Beats me 'ow 'e did it."

memories.description: He looks dead or like a vampire. Those shadowed eyes are the only part that seems alive and it makes him look horrible.
memories.source_text: Harry looked into the shadowed eyes of Sirius Black, the only part of the sunken face that seemed alive. Harry had never met a vampire, but he had seen pictures of them in his Defense Against the Dark Arts classes, and Black, with his waxy white skin, looked just like one.

memories.description: Black was close to You-Know-Who and expected to be high up once You-Know-Who won. He didn't back down like the others did.
memories.source_text: "— all You-Know-’Oo’s supporters was tracked down, wasn't they, Ern? Most of 'em knew it was all over, wiv You-Know-’Oo gone, and they came quiet. But not Sirius Black. I 'eard he thought 'e'd be second-in-command once You-Know-’Oo 'ad taken over."

memories.description: Being in Azkaban would have driven him mad if he wasn't already. He is even more dangerous now.
memories.source_text: "If he weren't when he went to Azkaban, he will be now," said Ern in his slow voice.

memories.description: I already have one of those Monster Books. Great, I do not need another one.
memories.source_text: "Hang on," said Harry quickly, "I’ve already got one of those."

memories.description: Of course! That's why Hagrid said it would come in useful. It was meant to be handy, not a new pet to look after.
memories.source_text: Now Harry understood why Hagrid had said it would come in useful.

memories.description: Those Monster Books are proper trouble. The shopkeeper's been bitten loads and he's fed up. He's not stocking them anymore.
memories.source_text: "Thank heavens for that. I’ve been bitten five times already this morning —" "I’m never stocking them again, never!"

memories.description: The Knight Bus really throws you around. One second I'm sitting, next I'm flattened on my bed because it slams off at crazy speed. That's the kind of travel this is.
memories.source_text: There was another tremendous BANG, and the next moment Harry found himself flat on his bed, thrown backward by the speed of the Knight Bus.

memories.description: We can appear on a totally different street in a blink. You don't stay where you expect. That's mental.
memories.source_text: Pulling himself up, Harry stared out of the dark window and saw that they were now bowling along a completely different street.

memories.description: The drivers don't bother much with where we actually were. They move about and joke like it's normal. It doesn't feel safe or organized, more like chaos with a map.
memories.source_text: “This is where we was before you flagged us down,” he said. “Where are we, Ern? Somewhere in Wales?”

memories.description: The bus is hidden from Muggles. They genuinely don't notice us, even though you'd think they'd hear a bus crashing through the night. They just don't see or hear it.
memories.source_text: “How come the Muggles don’t hear the bus?” said Harry.

memories.description: Stan and Ernie treat Muggles like they never look or listen properly. The drivers are casual about it. It's obvious they expect Muggles to miss everything magical.
memories.source_text: “Don’ listen properly, do they? Don’ look properly either. Never notice nuffink, they don’.”

memories.description: We're heading to Abergavenny soon. The bus will drop people off at odd points and expects you to be ready to hop off fast.
memories.source_text: “Best go wake up Madam Marsh, Stan,” said Ern. “We’ll be in Abergavenny in a minute.”

memories.description: The beds slide when they brake. Everything on this bus moves around without warning. You have to hang on or you get shoved about.
memories.source_text: ‘Ere you go, Madam Marsh,” said Stan happily as Ern stamped on the brake and the beds slid a foot or so toward the front of the bus.

memories.description: They fling people off and slam the doors like it's perfectly normal. The bus shoots down narrow lanes with trees apparently getting out of the way. It's frightening and ridiculous at the same time.
memories.source_text: Madam Marsh clamped a handkerchief to her mouth and tottered down the steps. Stan threw her bag out after her and rammed the doors shut; there was another loud BANG, and they were thundering down a narrow country lane, trees leaping out of the way.

memories.description: I can't relax on this thing. It's so noisy and jerky I felt sick and kept thinking about the Dursleys and Aunt Marge. I don't know what's happened back at Privet Drive and I keep worrying about it. I need to know if they're okay and whether Marge's tantrum left her stuck on the ceiling.
memories.source_text: Harry wouldn’t have been able to sleep even if he had been traveling on a bus that didn’t keep banging loudly and jumping a hundred miles at a time. His stomach churned as he fell back to wondering what was going to happen to him, and whether the Dursleys had managed to get Aunt Marge off the ceiling yet.

memories.description: Stan reads the Daily Prophet like it's a time filler while he drives. They don't take this trip very seriously, treating it like a lark while I feel everything's on edge.
memories.source_text: Stan had unfurled a copy of the Daily Prophet and was now reading with his tongue between his teeth.

memories.description: I need Unfogging the Future by Cassandra Vablatsky. That's the book I'm after for Divination.
memories.source_text: “I need Unfogging the Future by Cassandra Vablatsky.”

memories.description: Unfogging the Future is a basic guide to fortune-telling methods like palmistry, crystal balls and reading bird entrails.
memories.source_text: “Unfogging the Future. Very good guide to all your basic fortune-telling methods — palmistry, crystal balls, bird entrails —”

memories.description: There’s a book called Death Omens: What to Do When You Know the Worst Is Coming and the manager warned me not to read it.
memories.source_text: “Oh, I wouldn’t read that if I were you,”

memories.description: If I read that Death Omens book they reckon I'll start seeing death omens everywhere. I probably shouldn't waste my time on it.
memories.source_text: “You’ll start seeing death omens everywhere.”

memories.description: What's going on? Percy's badge is missing and Ron's saying Scabbers's rat tonic is gone. I'm going to sort it. I'll grab Scabbers's stuff, I'm already packed.
memories.source_text: "What's up?" said Harry.

memories.description: Right now I need to help Ron and calm things down. I'm not sticking around for more arguing, I'm doing something useful and leaving to fetch the missing things.
memories.source_text: "I'll get Scabbers's stuff, I'm packed," Harry said to Ron, and he went downstairs.

memories.description: That bird is Dumbledore's phoenix. It's here to help.
memories.source_text: "He’s Dumbledore’s," said Harry, squeezing through himself.

memories.description: I somehow ended up with a sword and the Sorting Hat on me. I need to keep them safe and get out before I explain.
memories.source_text: "How come you’ve got a sword?" said Ron, gaping at the glittering weapon in Harry’s hand.

memories.description: We have to figure out how to climb back up that pipe if we want to get out.
memories.source_text: "Have you thought how we’re going to get back up this?" he said to Ron.

memories.description: Fawkes is not an ordinary bird at all. He can carry us and do things no normal bird could.
memories.source_text: "Fawkes," said Harry, "isn’t an ordinary bird."

memories.description: If I hold on to Fawkes and we link together, he can lift us up through that pipe. It actually works.
memories.source_text: Harry reached out and took hold of Fawkes’s strangely hot tail feathers. An extraordinary lightness seemed to spread through his whole body and the next second, in a rush of wings, they were flying upward through the pipe.

memories.description: I made it out alive and I am hurt and covered in slime and blood, but we're out and Ginny is in pieces and needs helping.
memories.source_text: "You’re alive," she said blankly to Harry. "There’s no need to sound so disappointed," he said grimly, wiping flecks of blood and slime off his glasses.

memories.description: Ginny is in distress. Right now, getting her out and safe comes before any explanations.
memories.source_text: "I’ll explain when we get out of here," said Harry with a sideways glance at Ginny, who was crying harder than ever.

memories.description: Of course you have to stroke the books. Who knew they'd try to bite if you didn't
memories.source_text: "Yeh've got ter stroke 'em," said Hagrid

memories.description: Shut up, Malfoy. I was defending Hagrid because I wanted his first lesson to work and I don't want him made to feel small
memories.source_text: "Shut up, Malfoy," said Harry quietly

memories.description: There are a dozen really strange creatures coming towards us. That's mental
memories.source_text: "Trotting toward them were a dozen of the most bizarre creatures"

memories.description: That woman speaks like she's from another world, all misty and spooky. She looks like a huge glittering insect to me and she's clearly weird and dramatic.
memories.source_text: "A voice came suddenly out of the shadows, a soft, misty sort of voice. 'Welcome,' it said. 'How nice to see you in the physical world at last.'"

memories.description: Divination is treated like a real gift, not something you just learn from a book. If you don't have the Sight, she says there's not much she can teach you.
memories.source_text: "Welcome to Divination," said Professor Trelawney... "I must warn you at the outset that if you do not have the Sight, there is very little I will be able to teach you."

memories.description: She goes straight for personal readings and single people out. She pointed at Neville and asked about his gran right away.
memories.source_text: "You, boy," she said suddenly to Neville... "Is your grandmother well?"

memories.description: I heard you and Mrs Weasley talking last night, so I already know about Sirius Black and what he's done.
memories.source_text: I already know.

memories.description: I don't feel terrified about Black like everyone expects. Honestly, how much worse can he be than Voldemort? I'm not trying to act brave, I just don't feel scared.
memories.source_text: Sirius Black can’t be worse than Voldemort, can he?

memories.description: I can't go into Hogsmeade because the Dursleys won't sign my permission and Cornelius Fudge won't either. That's that.
memories.source_text: The Dursleys didn’t sign my permission form, and Fudge wouldn’t either.

memories.description: I don't go looking for trouble. Trouble finds me, and that's just how it is.
memories.source_text: Trouble usually finds me.

memories.description: They're beautiful and dangerous. I couldn't believe how weird they were, half horse and half eagle, but also how proud they are.
memories.source_text: Hippogriffs! Beau'iful, aren' they?

memories.description: You have to be polite with a hippogriff. Walk up, bow, and wait for it to bow back. If it bows you can touch it. If it doesn't, get out of the way fast.
memories.source_text: Yeh always wait fer the hippogriff ter make the firs' move... Yeh walk toward him, and yeh bow, an' yeh wait. If he bows back, yeh're allowed ter touch him.

memories.description: I thought riding one would be like a broom but it's nothing like that. It's rough, it throws you about, and you have to hold on like mad. Still, it's brilliant when it goes right.
memories.source_text: Well done, Harry! Right - yeh can touch him! Pat his beak, go on!

memories.description: You don't mock a hippogriff. Being smart-alecky gets you hurt fast. Seeing Malfoy get cut made that totally clear.
memories.source_text: Are you, you great ugly brute?

memories.description: Malfoy'll scream and act like he's dying to get attention. I can't take him seriously when he overreacts like that, but his wound shows messing with creatures is actually dangerous.
memories.source_text: I’m dying! It’s killed me!

memories.description: He's milking it. Madam Pomfrey can fix anything, so Malfoy is pretending it's worse to get attention or punish Hagrid.
memories.source_text: "He’s faking it," said Harry at once.

memories.description: We're witnesses to what happened with the hippogriff and can tell Dumbledore the truth.
memories.source_text: "We’re witnesses," said Harry.

memories.description: Madam Pomfrey is brilliant at healing. If she can't fix something properly, it's not for lack of skill.
memories.source_text: "Madam Pomfrey can mend anything. She regrew half my bones last year."

memories.description: Those dementors are awful. They make you feel frozen inside and suck the happiness out of a place. They mess people up.
memories.source_text: "They’re horrible things, those dementors. . . ."

memories.description: Malfoy is a prat. He might act brave now, but he was terrified on the train and I'll remember that when we face him again on the Quidditch pitch.
memories.source_text: "That little git," he said calmly.

memories.description: Our first match against Slytherin will be a real chance to put Malfoy in his place. I'm actually looking forward to it.
memories.source_text: "Gryffindor versus Slytherin, first game of the season, remember?"

memories.description: Alright, Hagrid’s serious — I’m not supposed to wander around after dark. Got it. No more sneaking off at night.
memories.source_text: "WHAT D’YEH THINK YOU’RE DOIN’, EH?" he roared, so suddenly that they jumped a foot in the air. "YEH’RE NOT TO GO WANDERIN’ AROUND AFTER DARK, HARRY! AN’ YOU TWO! LETTIN’ HIM!"

memories.description: Hagrid’s drunk and upset; people are worried about him. I don’t like seeing him like that.
memories.source_text: "I think you’ve had enough to drink, Hagrid," said Hermione firmly.

memories.description: Malfoy is trying to goad me into hunting Black by himself. He's pushing the idea that I should be out looking for him rather than staying at school.
memories.source_text: "Thinking of trying to catch Black single-handed, Potter?"

memories.description: I haven't got a reason to want revenge on Black right now, but I know something might happen later and that worries me.
memories.source_text: "Why would I want revenge on Black? He hasn’t done anything to me, yet."

memories.description: People close to me think Malfoy is lying to provoke me. I should be careful about reacting to his taunts.
memories.source_text: "He’s making it up," said Ron savagely. "He’s trying to make you do something stupid."

memories.description: Snape favors Malfoy and lets him get away with things. I hate how he always looks at me like he loathes me while he coddles Malfoy.
memories.source_text: "Settle down, settle down," said Professor Snape idly.

memories.description: I get singled out and treated worse. Fine. I skinned the shrivelfig fast and threw it back. No point arguing.
memories.source_text: "Potter, you can skin Malfoy’s shrivelfig," said Snape, giving Harry the look of loathing he always reserved just for him.

memories.description: Malfoy is sneaky and smug. He teams up with Crabbe and Goyle to rile people up, and he enjoys winding Ron and me up.
memories.source_text: "Yeah," said Malfoy, putting on a brave sort of grimace. But Harry saw him wink at Crabbe and Goyle when Pansy had looked away.

memories.description: I grabbed Neville and pulled him up. I act fast when things go wrong and I step in to help without thinking twice.
memories.source_text: "Hullo, Neville," said Harry, feeling around in the dark and pulling Neville up by his cloak.

memories.description: I have no clue what is happening but I try to keep everyone calm. I tell people to sit and stay put when chaos breaks out.
memories.source_text: "No idea — sit down —"

memories.description: That cloaked figure gave me the creeps. I saw a filthy, slimy hand and it made my stomach drop. It felt like something trying to suck the air out of us.
memories.source_text: There was a hand protruding from the cloak and it was glistening, grayish, slimy-looking, and scabbed

memories.description: What the hell? She told me I have the Grim, a death omen. My stomach lurched and everyone stared at me like I was finished already.
memories.source_text: "The Grim, my dear, the Grim!"

memories.description: Tea-leaf readings are a load of guesswork and scary rubbish. One minute you get doom, the next you get happiness. It makes you want to laugh more than believe it.
memories.source_text: "Right, you’ve got a crooked sort of cross . . . That means you’re going to have ‘trials and suffering’ . . . but there’s a thing that could be the sun . . . hang on . . . that means ‘great happiness’ . . . so you’re going to suffer but be very happy. . . ."

memories.description: I snapped at everyone because I could not stand being treated like some doomed spectacle. I want mates who look me in the eye, not whisper or avoid me.
memories.source_text: "When you’ve all finished deciding whether I’m going to die or not!"

memories.description: Hermione's got an enormous ginger cat clamped in her arms. Great.
memories.source_text: Hermione came out, but she wasn’t carrying an owl. Her arms were clamped tightly around the enormous ginger cat.

memories.description: That cat looks proper grumpy and squashed, all fluffy but bowlegged. I can't pretend I think it's gorgeous.
memories.source_text: That was a matter of opinion, thought Harry. The cat’s ginger fur was thick and fluffy, but it was definitely a bit bowlegged and its face looked grumpy and oddly squashed, as though it had run headlong into a brick wall.

memories.description: They still haven't caught Sirius Black. He's still out there and the papers are full of him.
memories.source_text: “They still haven’t caught him, then?” he asked.

memories.description: That face is everywhere. I keep seeing his picture and it feels like it's staring at me.
memories.source_text: Harry saw the now-familiar picture of Sirius Black staring up at him.

memories.description: Chocolate actually helps after a dementor; when Lupin gave me some I felt warmth spread to my fingers and toes.
memories.source_text: "A loud snap made them all jump. Professor Lupin was breaking an enormous slab of chocolate into pieces. 'Here,' he said to Harry, handing him a particularly large piece. 'Eat it. It'll help.'"

memories.description: That hooded thing was a dementor from Azkaban. It drains you, makes you feel freezing and sick.
memories.source_text: "'A dementor,' said Lupin, who was now giving chocolate to everyone else. 'One of the dementors of Azkaban.'"

memories.description: I trusted Lupin enough to expect him to know things about me and the situation, but I'm embarrassed I went over the top and passed out when no one else did.
memories.source_text: "'Are you all right, Harry?' Harry didn't ask how Professor Lupin knew his name. 'Fine,' he muttered, embarrassed."

memories.description: McGonagall and the staff already know I was taken ill on the train because Lupin sent an owl ahead.
memories.source_text: "'Professor Lupin sent an owl ahead to say that you were taken ill on the train, Potter.'"

memories.description: I hate making a fuss. I absolutely do not want to be seen as weak or put in the hospital wing. The last thing I want is Malfoy hearing about it.
memories.source_text: "'I'm fine,' he said, 'I don't need anything —' 'Oh, it's you, is it?' said Madam Pomfrey... 'Of course you're not,' said Madam Pomfrey absentmindedly, now taking his pulse."

memories.description: Right, so if there's a crowd the boggart gets confused about what to turn into. Makes sense. More people, less chance it'll pick the right fright for any one of us.
memories.source_text: "Er — because there are so many of us, it won't know what shape it should be?"

memories.description: Okay, laughter beats a boggart. You have to force it to look funny, not terrifying. Sounds daft, but if it thinks you're laughing it stops being scary.
memories.source_text: "The charm that repels a boggart is simple, yet it requires force of mind. You see, the thing that really finishes a boggart is laughter. What you need to do is force it to assume a shape that you find amusing."

memories.description: I hate how Snape treats Neville, and seeing him sneer like that only makes me angrier with him. I don't trust Snape and I won't stand for him picking on people in front of everyone.
memories.source_text: Harry glared at Snape; it was bad enough that he bullied Neville in his own classes, let alone doing it in front of other teachers.

memories.description: I spent the whole summer wandering Diagon Alley and sitting under those bright café umbrellas. Everyone's showing off weird stuff and gossiping about Sirius Black. People are scared for the kids and say they won't let any of us out alone until Black is locked up again
memories.source_text: Harry spent the long sunny days exploring the shops and eating under the brightly colored umbrellas outside cafés, where his fellow diners were showing one another their purchases (“It’s a lunascope, old boy — no more messing around with moon charts, see?”) or else discussing the case of Sirius Black (“Personally, I won’t let any of the children out alone until he’s back in Azkaban”).

memories.description: I don't need to hide under the covers with a flashlight. I can do my essays in the sun at Florean Fortescue's and Florean actually helps me with them. Also he keeps giving me free sundaes every half hour which is brilliant
memories.source_text: Harry didn’t have to do his homework under the blankets by flashlight anymore; now he could sit in the bright sunshine outside Florean Fortescue’s Ice Cream Parlor, finishing all his essays with occasional help from Florean Fortescue himself, who, apart from knowing a great deal about medieval witch burnings, gave Harry free sundaes every half an hour.

memories.description: I've got my vault money back at Gringotts and it's a nightmare trying not to blow it all at once
memories.source_text: Once Harry had refilled his money bag with gold Galleons, silver Sickles, and bronze Knuts from his vault at Gringotts, he had to exercise a lot of self-control not to spend the whole lot at once.

memories.description: I kept telling myself I've got five more years at Hogwarts so I can't waste my money now. I don't want to end up begging the Dursleys for books later
memories.source_text: He had to keep reminding himself that he had five years to go at Hogwarts, and how it would feel to ask the Dursleys for money for spellbooks, to stop himself from buying a handsome set of solid gold Gobstones (a Wizarding game rather like marbles, in which the stones squirt a nasty-smelling liquid into the other player’s face when they lose a point).

memories.description: That moving model of the galaxy was exactly my sort of thing. It would have saved me taking Astronomy classes but I didn't buy it
memories.source_text: He was sorely tempted, too, by the perfect, moving model of the galaxy in a large glass ball, which would have meant he never had to take another Astronomy lesson.

memories.description: Quality Quidditch Supplies nearly broke me. A week after I got to the Leaky Cauldron something there tested every bit of my self-control
memories.source_text: But the thing that tested Harry’s resolution most appeared in his favorite shop, Quality Quidditch Supplies, a week after he’d arrived at the Leaky Cauldron.

memories.description: He's faking that injury to try to get Hagrid fired. I could tell he was putting it on, and it made me angry.
memories.source_text: "So that's why you're putting it on," said Harry, accidentally beheading a dead caterpillar because his hand was shaking in anger.

memories.description: Malfoy expects his cronies to do his dirty work, even making Weasley slice his caterpillars. Typical, using people to be nasty.
memories.source_text: "Well," said Malfoy, lowering his voice to a whisper, "partly, Potter. But there are other benefits too. Weasley, slice my caterpillars for me."

memories.description: Sirius Black has reportedly been sighted nearby. That could mean he's really close to us.
memories.source_text: "Hey, Harry," said Seamus Finnigan, leaning over to borrow Harry’s brass scales, "have you heard? Daily Prophet this morning — they reckon Sirius Black’s been sighted."

memories.description: A Muggle spotted Black and probably does not understand who he is. They just see an ordinary criminal, which could make this sighting messy.
memories.source_text: "It was a Muggle who saw him. ’Course, she didn’t really understand. The Muggles think he’s just an ordinary criminal, don’t they?"

memories.description: You can fight a boggart by making it ridiculous. Say Riddikulus and it loses its terror and changes into something silly.
memories.source_text: "Riddikulus!" shouted Seamus.

memories.description: When the spell works the fear goes quiet. It actually takes away the horrible, wailing part so you can face it.
memories.source_text: The banshee made a rasping noise and clutched her throat; her voice was gone.

memories.description: He's faking it. Malfoy is pretending his arm is injured so we won't play Slytherin.
memories.source_text: "There’s nothing wrong with Malfoy’s arm! He’s faking it!"

memories.description: We're not playing Slytherin; the match has been changed to Hufflepuff instead.
memories.source_text: "Flint’s excuse is that their Seeker’s arm’s still injured... We’re playing Hufflepuff instead."

memories.description: Cedric Diggory is Hufflepuff's new Seeker and he is good, so we can't take them lightly.
memories.source_text: "Diggory’s put a very strong side together! He’s an excellent Seeker!"

memories.description: Snape is actively trying to punish Gryffindor and is hostile in class right now.
memories.source_text: "Five more points from Gryffindor, and if I have to ask you to sit down again, it will be fifty."

memories.description: Lupin isn't teaching today; Snape says Lupin is too ill to teach.
memories.source_text: "He says he is feeling too ill to teach today," said Snape with a twisted smile.

memories.description: I'm butting heads with Snape again; he's looking for any excuse to take points off us and wind me up.
memories.source_text: Harry's refusal to sit and exchanges with Snape throughout the scene

memories.description: That Snape will strip Gryffindor points from Hermione just for answering. He treats her harshly and plays favorites.
memories.source_text: "Five more points from Gryffindor for being an insufferable know-it-all."

memories.description: Snape will hand out detentions to students who speak up against him. He does it quietly, but he means it.
memories.source_text: "Detention, Weasley,"

memories.description: I thought teachers like Lupin were fair. Snape is the kind of teacher who belittles the class and enjoys catching people out.
memories.source_text: "I was under the impression that I am teaching this lesson, not you."

memories.description: Dementors come onto the pitch in a swarm and they give off this horrible freezing feeling that sits in your chest like ice.
memories.source_text: "At least a hundred dementors, their hidden faces pointing up at him, were standing beneath him."

memories.description: When dementors are near, sound goes weird and everything gets quiet like someone switched it off and my head fills with cold and panic.
memories.source_text: "It was as though freezing water were rising in his chest, cutting at his insides."

memories.description: They shove images and voices into your head, real or not, and they can make you relive things or hear desperate cries like that woman begging.
memories.source_text: "Someone was screaming, screaming inside his head . . . a woman . . . 'Not Harry, not Harry, please not Harry!'"

memories.description: I couldn't ignore someone screaming for help even when it's dangerous. I had to try and help her instead of just chasing the Snitch.
memories.source_text: "She was going to die. . . . She was going to be murdered. . . . He was falling, falling through the icy mist."

memories.description: So Lupin thinks the boggart would turn into Voldemort if it faced me. Of course it would. That explains why he stepped in.
memories.source_text: “I would have thought that was obvious, Harry,” he said, sounding surprised. "Well," said Lupin, frowning slightly, "I assumed that if the boggart faced you, it would assume the shape of Lord Voldemort."

memories.description: Filch thinks I should be in Hogsmeade messing about with the others. Great. He still treats me like I don't belong.
memories.source_text: “A likely story! Sneaking around on your own — why aren’t you in Hogsmeade buying Stink Pellets and Belch Powder and Whizzing Worms like the rest of your nasty little friends?”

memories.description: I pretended I wasn't worried about being left behind and other things. I won't admit it out loud right now.
memories.source_text: “You’re not worried, are you?” “No,” Harry lied.

memories.description: I didn't actually cast the spell to finish the boggart but I still got five points because I answered Lupin's questions right at the start of class
memories.source_text: "You and Hermione answered my questions correctly at the start of the class, Harry," Lupin said lightly.

memories.description: Lupin steps in and leads the class, helping direct how the boggart is tackled
memories.source_text: "Forward, Neville, and finish him off!" said Lupin as the boggart landed on the floor as a cockroach.

memories.description: The boggart can change into terrifying things like a huge spider but a proper Ridikkulus makes it ridiculous and harmless
memories.source_text: "Riddikulus!" bellowed Ron, and the spider's legs vanished

memories.description: When someone properly makes themselves laugh at the boggart's new form the boggart breaks apart and goes
memories.source_text: "Riddikulus!" he shouted, and they had a split second's view of Snape in his lacy dress before Neville let out a great "Ha!" of laughter, and the boggart exploded

memories.description: Lupin just said Voldemort’s name out loud. That surprised me because hardly anyone says it.
memories.source_text: Not only was this the last answer he’d expected, but Lupin had said Voldemort’s name.

memories.description: Lupin thinks I did well facing the boggart. He actually seems impressed with me and a bit proud.
memories.source_text: “I see,” said Lupin thoughtfully. “Well, well . . . I’m impressed.”

memories.description: Lupin figures that what I fear most is fear itself. That makes sense to me now.
memories.source_text: “I’m impressed.” He smiled slightly at the look of surprise on Harry’s face.

memories.description: Snape brewed a complicated potion for Lupin that Lupin is drinking to feel better.
memories.source_text: “Professor Snape has very kindly concocted a potion for me,” he said.

memories.description: People reckon Snape would do anything to get the DADA job. That makes me even more wary of him.
memories.source_text: “Some people reckon he’d do anything to get the Defense Against the Dark Arts job.”

memories.description: Lupin drank the smoking goblet Snape brought. That looked risky and I wanted to stop him.
memories.source_text: “Lupin drank it?” he gasped. “Is he mad?”

memories.description: Dissendium is the word to open that statue. I said it, tapped the stone witch, and the hump opened.
memories.source_text: The tiniest speech bubble had appeared next to his figure. The word inside said, 'Dissendium.'

memories.description: That hump opens into a passage I can squeeze into if I go headfirst.
memories.source_text: At once, the statue’s hump opened wide enough to admit a fairly thin person.

memories.description: There’s a stone slide behind that statue that spits you out into a damp, dark tunnel.
memories.source_text: He slid a considerable way down what felt like a stone slide, then landed on cold, damp earth.

memories.description: Lumos works down there. The passage is narrow and low, like a burrow, so I have to watch my head and feet.
memories.source_text: He held up his wand, muttered, 'Lumos!' and saw that he was in a very narrow, low, earthy passageway.

memories.description: If I say Mischief managed the Marauder’s Map clears itself on command. It hides whatever it showed.
memories.source_text: He raised the map, tapped it with the tip of his wand, and muttered, 'Mischief managed!' The map went blank at once.

memories.description: Thinking of something I want, like Honeydukes, keeps me going when the passage drags on.
memories.source_text: It took ages, but Harry had the thought of Honeydukes to sustain him.

memories.description: At the top of that long climb there’s a trapdoor. It’s easy to hit your head on it if you’re not careful.
memories.source_text: Then, without warning, his head hit something hard. It seemed to be a trapdoor.

memories.description: The trapdoor opens into a cellar stacked with crates and boxes.
memories.source_text: He was in a cellar, which was full of wooden crates and boxes.

memories.description: That trapdoor blends into the floor perfectly. If you shut it nobody would notice it.
memories.source_text: Harry climbed out of the trapdoor and replaced it — it blended so perfectly with the dusty floor that it was impossible to tell it was there.

memories.description: Snape's acting different now. He's got it in for Lupin, and I can't work out if it's because of that boggart or something else. It feels personal.
memories.source_text: Snape’s never been like this with any of our other Defense Against the Dark Arts teachers, even if he did want the job, Why’s he got it in for Lupin? D’you think this is all because of the boggart?

memories.description: I get annoyed by pointless shouting. A good bowl of porridge helps me wake up and focus when I'm knackered.
memories.source_text: Oh, shut up, He revived a bit over a large bowl of porridge, and by the time he’d started on toast, the rest of the team had turned up.

memories.description: Quidditch can be chaos when I'm soaked and freezing. I hate not being able to see my team or the Snitch. It makes me feel useless until I get a grip.
memories.source_text: He flew backward and forward across the field past blurred red and yellow shapes, with no idea of what was happening in the rest of the game.

memories.description: I thought Voldemort would be the worst thing, the absolute worst. A Voldemort back to full strength would terrify me.
memories.source_text: Harry thought . . . What scared him most in the world? His first thought was Lord Voldemort — a Voldemort returned to full strength.

memories.description: That dementor image hit me harder than Voldemort. The cold, the drowning feeling, the rotting hand — that's the thing that makes me shudder more than anything.
memories.source_text: But before he had even started to plan a possible counterattack on a boggart-Voldemort, a horrible image came floating to the surface of his mind. . . . A rotting, glistening hand, slithering back beneath a black cloak . . . a long, rattling breath from an unseen mouth . . . then a cold so penetrating it felt like drowning.

memories.description: I couldn't let everyone see me freak out. I need to hide how scared I am, even if inside I feel like I'm drowning.
memories.source_text: Harry shivered, then looked around, hoping no one had noticed. Many people had their eyes shut tight.

memories.description: I woke up in the hospital wing and everything aches like I was beaten.
memories.source_text: "Harry’s eyes snapped open. He was lying in the hospital wing."

memories.description: I saw those hooded black figures and screaming. That was the scariest thing I have ever seen.
memories.source_text: "Scariest . . . the scariest thing . . . hooded black figures . . . cold . . . screaming . . ."

memories.description: Cedric caught the Snitch right after I fell. He did not know what had happened to me.
memories.source_text: "Diggory got the Snitch," said George. "Just after you fell. He didn’t realize what had happened."

memories.description: I honestly thought I was dead for a moment. I cannot believe I survived that.
memories.source_text: "We thought you’d died," said Alicia, who was shaking.

memories.description: My teammates were there for me, all muddy and worried. That matters.
memories.source_text: "The Gryffindor Quidditch team, spattered with mud from head to foot, was gathered around his bed."

memories.description: Of course Hermione’s spell worked. Once she tapped my glasses with Impervius I could actually see in that downpour.
memories.source_text: “They’ll repel water!”

memories.description: What the hell? There was a huge shaggy black dog up in the top row and it completely distracted me. My hands slipped and my broom dropped a few feet.
memories.source_text: the silhouette of an enormous shaggy black dog, clearly imprinted against the sky, motionless in the topmost, empty row of seats

memories.description: I thought I stood no chance trying to play with water on my glasses, but after Hermione fixed them I felt determined and ready to go after the Snitch.
memories.source_text: “I’ve got no chance with these on,”

memories.description: Where is Wood? He wasn't there when we lost. I can't believe he's not around.
memories.source_text: "Where is Wood?" said Harry, suddenly realizing he wasn’t there.

memories.description: Did someone get my Nimbus? My broom went somewhere when I fell.
memories.source_text: "Did someone get my Nimbus?"

memories.description: My broom hit the Whomping Willow. Of course it did. That's awful.
memories.source_text: "Well . . . when you fell off, it got blown away," said Hermione hesitantly. "And?" "And it hit — it hit — oh, Harry — it hit the Whomping Willow."

memories.description: I've never lost before. I lost this match. That actually happened and it knocks me over.
memories.source_text: "We lost . . . for the first time ever, he had lost a Quidditch match."

memories.description: The Whomping Willow hates being hit. No wonder my Nimbus got battered.
memories.source_text: "It — it doesn't like being hit."

memories.description: Dumbledore was furious. He slowed me as I fell and blasted the dementors off the field. That saved me.
memories.source_text: "Dumbledore was really angry," Hermione said in a quaking voice. "I’ve never seen him like that before. He ran onto the field as you fell, waved his wand, and you sort of slowed down before you hit the ground. Then he whirled his wand at the dementors. Shot silver stuff at them. They left the stadium right away."

memories.description: They gave me an old bit of parchment and said it was the secret of their success. I actually got handed something that matters to them.
memories.source_text: "This, Harry, is the secret of our success," said George, patting the parchment fondly.

memories.description: You tap the parchment with a wand and say, 'I solemnly swear that I am up to no good,' and the map shows itself. That's how you make it work.
memories.source_text: "I solemnly swear that I am up to no good."

memories.description: The map shows every corner of Hogwarts, even secret passages and places I never knew about. It is freakingly detailed.
memories.source_text: It was a map showing every detail of the Hogwarts castle and grounds.

memories.description: There are secret passages I never knew existed. Some of them lead straight out of the castle where you would not expect.
memories.source_text: And as Harry’s eyes traveled up and down the familiar corridors, he noticed something else. This map showed a set of passages he had never entered.

memories.description: One of the passages leads straight into Honeydukes cellar. Fred and George have used it loads, so it's a proper shortcut into Hogsmeade sweets.
memories.source_text: "This one here, this one leads right into the cellar of Honeydukes. We\'ve used it loads of times."

memories.description: To hide the map you tap it and say, 'Mischief managed,' and it goes blank. You have to remember to wipe it or anyone can read it.
memories.source_text: "Don\'t forget to wipe it after you\'ve used it," "Just tap it again and say, \'Mischief managed!\' And it\'ll go blank."

memories.description: The map was made by Moony, Wormtail, Padfoot, and Prongs. They called it the Marauder's Map and they seem to have been proper legends at mischief.
memories.source_text: "Messrs. Moony, Wormtail, Padfoot, and Prongs Purveyors of Aids to Magical Mischief-Makers are proud to present THE MARAUDER\'S MAP"

memories.description: There are seven secret passages out of the castle. Some Filch knows about, some he does not. At least one goes right into Hogsmeade.
memories.source_text: "Right into Hogsmeade," said Fred, tracing one of them with his finger.

memories.description: One passage behind the fourth floor mirror is completely blocked off now. We can't use that one anymore.
memories.source_text: "We\'ve used it until last winter, but it\'s caved in \- completely blocked."

memories.description: Fred and George trusted me enough to give me this map. They chose to hand it over because they said my need was greater than theirs.
memories.source_text: "We bequeath it to you. We don\'t really need it anymore."

memories.description: The map shows moving ink dots with names. It actually shows where people are right now and even put a tiny Harry on the map tapping the witch where I was standing.
memories.source_text: What did he have to do? He pulled out the map again and saw, to his astonishment, that a new ink figure had appeared upon it, labeled Harry Potter.

memories.description: I can't stop seeing Black's face grinning at me, like the photo is pasted over my eyes. He was laughing with Mum and Dad and now I'm supposed to believe he betrayed them? I trusted people and I trusted my parents' friends and now that feels shattered.
memories.source_text: "If he hadn’t known it was the same person, he would never have guessed it was Black in this old photograph."

memories.description: Every time a dementor comes near, I hear my mum being murdered. That's burned into me and it makes me furious. I won't just sit and do nothing while Black is free.
memories.source_text: "I can hear my mum screaming and pleading with Voldemort."

memories.description: Malfoy said he'd hunt Black down. I don't trust Malfoy, but he was right about Black being part of Voldemort's circle. Knowing that makes Black feel even more like an enemy I should go after.
memories.source_text: "Malfoy knows," he said abruptly. "Remember what he said to me in Potions? 'If it was me, I'd hunt him down myself. . . . I'd want revenge.'"

memories.description: The worst thing is Black might not even be punished properly by Azkaban. If the dementors don't hurt him, then him being locked up isn't justice. That idea makes me furious and desperate to do something.
memories.source_text: "The dementors don't affect him, Harry thought, staring into the handsome, laughing face."

memories.description: I've got the Marauder's Map and I can sneak around the castle using its passages. I'm not about to tell anyone or hand it in.
memories.source_text: "'Course I haven't,' said Harry. He dropped his voice so that none of the sixth years could hear him and told them all about the Marauder's Map.

memories.description: There are seven tunnels on the map. Four Filch probably knows. One is caved in. One is blocked by the Whomping Willow. The one I used is hidden in the cellar and hard to spot unless you already know it's there.
memories.source_text: "There are seven secret tunnels on the map, right? Fred and George reckon Filch already knows about four of them. And of the other three — one of them's caved in, so no one can get through it. One of them's got the Whomping Willow planted over the entrance, so you can't get out of it. And the one I just came through — well — it's really hard to see the entrance to it down in the cellar, so unless he knew it was there . . ."

memories.description: I'm not handing the map to McGonagall. Are they insane? I'd never give up something that could help me find out what's really going on.
memories.source_text: "No, I'm not!' said Harry. 'Are you mad?' said Ron, goggling at Hermione. 'Hand in something that good?'

memories.description: The snow is thick outside. It would make it harder for anyone to spot me in Hogsmeade right now.
memories.source_text: Ron nodded through the mullioned windows at the thick, swirling snow.

memories.description: Sirius Black is after me and McGonagall thinks he might have sent the Firebolt. I can barely believe it but I have to treat it like it could be true.
memories.source_text: He’s supposed to be after me. So McGonagall reckons he might have sent it.

memories.description: There is a Patronus Charm that can drive off dementors. It is advanced magic and not easy, but it actually can work if I concentrate on one very happy memory.
memories.source_text: The spell I am going to try and teach you is highly advanced magic, Harry — well beyond Ordinary Wizarding Level. It is called the Patronus Charm.

memories.description: The incantation is Expecto Patronum. Saying it while holding a single strong happy memory can make something to protect you from dementors.
memories.source_text: Expecto Patronum!

memories.description: Hagrid's broken. He's crying and terrified about Buckbeak getting taken to that Committee. I can't heap on him about Sirius right now; he's already got too much to bear.
memories.source_text: Hagrid, are you in there?

memories.description: The Board cleared Hagrid of direct blame but the Committee for the Disposal of Dangerous Creatures wants Buckbeak in London and they might be biased because of Malfoy. Buckbeak could be in real danger.
memories.source_text: Dear Mr. Hagrid, Further to our inquiry into the attack by a hippogriff on a student in your class, we have accepted the assurances of Professor Dumbledore that you bear no responsibility for the regrettable incident.

memories.description: I want to help Hagrid. Hermione's right about finding a defense and I'm willing to stand up for him. He isn't alone in this.
memories.source_text: You can call us as witnesses

memories.description: Someone's sent me a Firebolt. I don't know who, and whoever it is just changed everything about the way I can fly.
memories.source_text: Who sent it to you?

memories.description: I had a Firebolt for Christmas, but it's been taken away and they are stripping it down to check for jinxes.
memories.source_text: "I haven’t got it anymore. It was confiscated."

memories.description: Because Black is supposedly after me, McGonagall thinks the broom might be dangerous and that it could have been sent for me. I hate that she suspects something so personal, but I can't argue with her worry.
memories.source_text: "Sirius Black," Harry said wearily. "He’s supposed to be after me. So McGonagall reckons he might have sent it."

memories.description: Remus agreed to teach us anti-dementor lessons at eight on Thursday in the History of Magic classroom. I want to get started as soon as possible.
memories.source_text: "Ah yes," said Lupin, when Harry reminded him of his promise at the end of class. "Let me see . . . how about eight o'clock on Thursday evening? The History of Magic classroom should be large enough."

memories.description: Oliver Wood promised to try to convince McGonagall to let me use the Firebolt. It feels good that the team wants me as Seeker and will try to help.
memories.source_text: "I'll go and talk to her, Harry," he promised. "I'll make her see reason."

memories.description: All right, I want to go. I made up my mind. I’m going to ask McGonagall to let me go to Hogsmeade.
memories.source_text: "Definitely," said Harry.

memories.description: This is my last chance to win the Quidditch Cup before I leave. I’ve got to make it count.
memories.source_text: "I’ll be leaving at the end of this year. I’ll never get another shot at it."

memories.description: Ron’s offered to help with my Astronomy work. He’s backing me up and I can rely on him to pitch in when I need it.
memories.source_text: "You can copy mine, if you like," said Ron, labeling his last star with a flourish and shoving the chart toward Harry.

memories.description: A dementor comes right at me from that box. It moves silent and it makes the whole place go freezing.
memories.source_text: "A dementor rose slowly from the box, its hooded face turned toward Harry, one glistening, scabbed hand gripping its cloak."

memories.description: When a dementor gets near I feel this horrible piercing cold and I messed up my Patronus the first time because the memory dissolved.
memories.source_text: "A wave of piercing cold broke over him — 'Expecto Patronum!' Harry yelled."

memories.description: The dementor drags up my mum's voice and other memories and I could hear Voldemort and my mum louder than before.
memories.source_text: "I could hear her louder that time — and him — Voldemort —"

memories.description: For the first time I actually heard my dad shouting and trying to hold Voldemort off. I never heard him before and it hit me hard.
memories.source_text: "'I heard my dad,' Harry mumbled. 'That's the first time I've ever heard him — he tried to take on Voldemort himself, to give my mum time to run for it.'"

memories.description: It's getting worse. I can't afford to fail practicing Patronus again because the sight of them makes everything worse and brings up darker stuff.
memories.source_text: "'It's getting worse,' Harry muttered, biting off the Frog's head. 'I could hear her louder that time — and him — Voldemort —'"

memories.description: I have to get this right. If dementors show up at a Quidditch match I could fall off my broom and we'd lose the Cup. I won't let that happen.
memories.source_text: "'I've got to! What if the dementors turn up at our match against Ravenclaw? I can't afford to fall off again. If we lose this game we've lost the Quidditch Cup!'"

memories.description: Lupin's patient and quietly supportive. He doesn't push me and he knows the Patronus won't come easily. He even gives me a Chocolate Frog and lets me try again when I'm ready.
memories.source_text: "'Are you all right?' said Lupin. 'Yes'... 'Here —' Lupin handed him a Chocolate Frog. 'Eat this before we try again. I didn't expect you to do it your first time; in fact, I would have been astounded if you had.'"

memories.description: Lupin told me to pick a strong happy memory to focus on for the Patronus, not the scary stuff I keep getting pulled into.
memories.source_text: "'You might want to select another memory, a happy memory, I mean, to concentrate on.'"

memories.description: I got my Firebolt back. It's perfect and I can have it for the match.
memories.source_text: "She was holding out his Firebolt, and it looked as magnificent as ever."

memories.description: We should patch things up with Hermione. She was trying to help, not sabotage me.
memories.source_text: "You know what — we should make up with Hermione. . . . She was only trying to help. . . ."

memories.description: I need to practice on the Firebolt before Saturday's match so I'm ready.
memories.source_text: "I daresay you’ll need to get the feel of it before Saturday’s match, won’t you?"

memories.description: Hermione's knuckled down into tons of work. She's exhausted, but stubbornly refusing to drop anything.
memories.source_text: "She’s in the common room now — working, for a change —"

memories.description: My Firebolt is absolutely the fastest broom out there. Once I kick off it just rockets and I can outfly almost anyone.
memories.source_text: the Firebolt zoomed higher and faster than any other broom

memories.description: Diving is my specialty. When I drop in on a Snitch I go all out and it usually works for me.
memories.source_text: dives were his speciality

memories.description: Cho was right on my tail the whole time. She kept cutting me off and forcing me to change direction.
memories.source_text: Cho Chang was tailing him closely

memories.description: She decided to mark me instead of looking for the Snitch. Fine. If she wants to shadow me she can deal with what happens next.
memories.source_text: She'd decided to mark him rather than search for the Snitch herself

memories.description: The crowd went mad when the Ravenclaw Beater nearly ruined my catch. Gryffindor were gutted and Ravenclaw cheered their Beater.
memories.source_text: There was a great "Ooooooh" of disappointment from the Gryffindor supporters, but much applause for their Beater from the Ravenclaw end

memories.description: We were way ahead, eighty to zero, and I was pushing the Firebolt hard to keep us in control.
memories.source_text: Gryffindor leads by eighty points to zero, and look at that Firebolt go

memories.description: Ravenclaw clawed back with three goals and suddenly the lead was only fifty. If Cho got the Snitch we would lose.
memories.source_text: they had now scored three goals, which put Gryffindor only fifty points ahead

memories.description: Then three dementors appeared under me. I froze inside for a second because they are terrifying and I did not hang around to think about it.
memories.source_text: Three dementors, three tall, black, hooded dementors, were looking up at him

memories.description: I wasn't going to be a gentleman. If I had to be brutal to stop a collision or to catch the Snitch I would. I swerve to avoid people but I won't let politeness slow me down.
memories.source_text: "HARRY, THIS IS NO TIME TO BE A GENTLEMAN!" Wood roared as Harry swerved to avoid a collision

memories.description: I can fire a full Patronus when it matters. I did it and something huge and silver-white blasted out of my wand and sent whatever it was flying.
memories.source_text: "Expecto Patronum!"

memories.description: I didn't feel anything when those things attacked. I was clear-headed enough to keep going and catch the Snitch.
memories.source_text: "I didn't feel a thing!"

memories.description: Okay, so they weren't dementors after all. That explains why I wasn't affected. Turned out I'd been attacked by something else pretending to be dementors.
memories.source_text: "That would be because they — er — weren't dementors," said Professor Lupin.

memories.description: I caught the Snitch. I actually closed my hand around it while still flying and won the match.
memories.source_text: he stretched out the hand still grasping his wand and just managed to close his fingers over the small, struggling Snitch

memories.description: Lupin knows about the Patronus and seemed relieved and proud. I feel like he sees me differently now and I can trust him a bit more.
memories.source_text: "That was quite some Patronus," said a voice in Harry's ear. Harry turned around to see Professor Lupin, who looked both shaken and pleased.

memories.description: My broom might be cursed with a Hurling Hex and McGonagall said I can’t have it back until they finish checking it.
memories.source_text: "We’ve checked for most of the usual curses, but Professor Flitwick believes the broom might be carrying a Hurling Hex."

memories.description: I can make an indistinct, silvery Patronus but it’s too weak to drive a dementor off and it drains me when I try to keep it up.
memories.source_text: "Several sessions on, he was able to produce an indistinct, silvery shadow every time the boggart-dementor approached him, but his Patronus was too feeble to drive the dementor away."

memories.description: Lupin says an indistinct Patronus is actually a big deal for someone my age, so I’m doing better than I feel sometimes.
