memories.description: Mr Weasley says they searched Lucius's home and confiscated anything dangerous, so if something was still needed from Borgin then maybe it's something tricky or new.
memories.source_text: ["You see, when Lucius Malfoy was arrested, we raided his house. We took away everything that might have been dangerous."]

memories.description: Ginny's not going to stick with me at school the whole time and yeah, it annoys me a bit. I got used to her being around over the summer and it stings when she walks off to meet Dean.
memories.source_text: [He felt a strange twinge of annoyance as she walked away, her long red hair dancing behind her; he had become so used to her presence over the summer that he had almost forgotten that Ginny did not hang around with him, Ron, and Hermione while at school.]

memories.description: People are staring because of the Ministry story and the Prophet garbage. Neville and Luna sticking with me means they've been with me through all of it, and I actually think they're good company.
memories.source_text: ["They’re staring at you because you were at the Ministry too," said Harry...]

memories.description: I kept thinking that Voldemort might've targeted Neville instead of me. The prophecy could've meant him, and if he'd been chosen then he'd be bearing the scar and the whole burden. That stuff about mothers dying to save their kids makes me think Lily's sacrifice is why I'm the one now.
memories.source_text: ["We didn’t face him, though," said Neville, emerging from under the seat...]

memories.description: I tried "Alohomora" on the gate and it did nothing. Great, so I can't just charm my way in.
memories.source_text: "Alohomora!" he said confidently, pointing his wand at the padlock, but nothing happened.

memories.description: Tonks told me the gates were bewitched by Dumbledore himself. So they're specially locked down.
memories.source_text: "That won't work on these," said Tonks. "Dumbledore bewitched them himself."

memories.description: There are anti-intruder jinxes on the walls and security has been cranked up a hundredfold. Climbing's not an option.
memories.source_text: "No, you couldn't," said Tonks flatly. "Anti-intruder jinxes on all of them. Security's been tightened a hundredfold this summer."

memories.description: I thought maybe I could sneak in by climbing, but clearly that's impossible now. So my usual impulse to try something simple won't work.
memories.source_text: "I could climb a wall," he suggested. "No, you couldn't," said Tonks flatly.

memories.description: I'm cold, hungry, and fed up with having to deal with a gloomy Tonks. I just want to get inside.
memories.source_text: He was cold, he was hungry, and he was quite keen to leave this new, gloomy Tonks behind.

memories.description: I reckon Malfoy might already be one of them. I can't shake the feeling he's up to something dangerous and I think we should take it seriously.
memories.source_text: "He’s a Death Eater," said Harry slowly. "He’s replaced his father as a Death Eater!"

memories.description: Madam Malkin tried to touch his left arm and he jumped like he'd been burned. I'm sure he's been branded with the Dark Mark.
memories.source_text: "In Madam Malkin’s. She didn’t touch him, but he yelled and jerked his arm away from her when she went to roll up his sleeve. It was his left arm. He’s been branded with the Dark Mark."

memories.description: Malfoy went into Borgin and Burkes and was forcing Borgin to fix something and to keep another thing for him. They seem connected.
memories.source_text: "He went into Borgin and Burkes," said Harry, "and started bullying the bloke in there, Borgin, to help him fix something. And he said he wanted Borgin to keep something else for him."

memories.description: Because his father is in Azkaban, I think Malfoy might want revenge and that could explain why he's acting so dangerous.
memories.source_text: "Malfoy’s father’s in Azkaban. Don’t you think Malfoy’d like revenge?"

memories.description: I followed Malfoy because I genuinely thought he was up to something, and I wasn't just being nosy.
memories.source_text: "When we were in Diagon Alley," Harry began, but Mr. Weasley forestalled him with a grimace. "Am I about to discover where you, Ron, and Hermione disappeared to while you were supposed to be in the back room of Fred and George’s shop?"

memories.description: I wanted everyone to think I did something brave, like took on Death Eaters and a dementor. That would keep people guessing and make Malfoy look ridiculous.
memories.source_text: [He hoped very much that they would all assume he had been involved in something heroic, preferably involving a couple of Death Eaters and a dementor.]

memories.description: Has Dumbledore brought up Voldemort yet? He always saves the proper speech for after the feast so it can't be long.
memories.source_text: [Dumbledore mentioned Voldemort at all?]

memories.description: I missed the Sorting. That was obvious to Hermione and I missed it, so I don't know what happened there.
memories.source_text: [You missed the Sorting, anyway]

memories.description: I couldn't change into my robes in time. I tried to explain it straight away because I knew he'd jump on it.
memories.source_text: “I couldn’t change, I didn’t have my —” Harry began, but Snape cut across him.

memories.description: Snape is openly hostile and sneering at me as always. He delights in putting me down and I loathe him for it.
memories.source_text: “Well, well, well,” sneered Snape, taking out his wand and tapping the padlock once, so that the chains snaked backward and the gates creaked open. “Nice of you to turn up, Potter, although you have evidently decided that the wearing of school robes would detract from your appearance.”

memories.description: Snape says I'm 'safe in his hands' but that sounds like a putdown, not protection. I still don't trust him.
memories.source_text: “There is no need to wait, Nymphadora, Potter is quite — ah — safe in my hands.”

memories.description: We need to get out of here now. I'm tense and ready to go, not hanging about while Vernon fumes.
memories.source_text: "Aren't — aren't we leaving, sir?"

memories.description: Something strange happens at midnight. I woke up as if someone switched the world off, and I react fast when odd things happen.
memories.source_text: "the minute hand on the alarm clock reached the number twelve and, at that precise moment, the streetlamp outside the window went out"

memories.description: I know Vernon panics and gets loud at anything unusual. I can't rely on him to act calmly or help me.
memories.source_text: "Who the blazes is calling at this time of night?"

memories.description: I messed up by not warning them. I get panicky and do stupid, hurried things when I think trouble is about to happen.
memories.source_text: "He had completely forgotten to warn the Dursleys that Dumbledore might be coming."

memories.description: I keep my distance from Vernon. Years of being pushed around have taught me to stay out of his reach and avoid confrontation.
memories.source_text: "as long experience had taught him to remain out of arm’s reach of his uncle whenever possible."

memories.description: If Dumbledore says the name, then I'm going to say it too. I won't stop just because others want me to.
memories.source_text: "Dumbledore uses that name," said Harry stubbornly.

memories.description: I was late because I got held up on the train.
memories.source_text: "Got held up on the train," said Harry.

memories.description: Grawp's better than I expected. I don't want to admit it to Ron, but Hagrid thinks Grawp's improved loads.
memories.source_text: "Oh yeah, he’s really come on," said Hagrid proudly. "Yeh’ll be amazed. I’m thinkin’ o’ trainin’ him up as me assistant."

memories.description: Hagrid's looking out for me and he still gets excited to see me. I smiled and waved back because he cares, plain and simple.
memories.source_text: "Hagrid was only a few minutes late," said Hermione. "Look, he’s waving at you, Harry."

memories.description: I used to think Trelawney was a joke, but she actually made that prophecy about my parents and me. I don't like being near her, and I'm not taking Divination this year.
memories.source_text: "Having always considered her a bit of a fraud, Harry had been shocked to discover at the end of the previous term that it had been she who had made the prediction that caused Lord Voldemort to kill Harry’s parents and attack Harry himself."

memories.description: Professor Slughorn wanted to know what happened at the Ministry. Everyone's been asking about it and trying to pin down the full story.
memories.source_text: "So what did Professor Slughorn want?" Hermione asked. "To know what really happened at the Ministry," said Harry.

memories.description: Malfoy getting away with mocking me just digs at me. I want to sort him out one-on-one more than anything right now.
memories.source_text: "Draco Malfoy was miming the shattering of a nose to raucous laughter and applause."

memories.description: Dumbledore hurt his hand. His fingers are blackened and he was having trouble with the stopper, so he is injured and it looks nasty.
memories.source_text: "No matter, Harry —" Dumbledore pointed his wand at the bottle and the cork flew out.

memories.description: I can speak Parseltongue. I heard that man speak and suddenly I could follow him, which was weird and a bit sickening when I thought about snakes.
memories.source_text: "You understand him, I'm sure, Harry?" "Yes, of course," said Harry.

memories.description: Merope survived the attack at the cottage. She did not die in that scene.
memories.source_text: "Oh, she survived," said Dumbledore.

memories.description: Merope Gaunt was Voldemort's mother. That hits hard and makes everything about him even darker.
memories.source_text: "It does," said Dumbledore.

memories.description: Tom Riddle senior is Voldemort's father and he was a Muggle who rode past the Gaunts. I can picture him on a horse, totally ordinary.
memories.source_text: "Yes, that was Tom Riddle senior, the handsome Muggle who used to go riding past the Gaunt cottage"

memories.description: It makes sense that Merope probably used a love potion on Tom Riddle. It explains how a Muggle ended up married to her when everything else seems impossible.
memories.source_text: "Personally, I am inclined to think that she used a love potion."

memories.description: Morfin and Marvolo were convicted. Morfin got three years in Azkaban and Marvolo got six months, so the whole Gaunt family was punished and taken away.
memories.source_text: "Morfin, who already had a record of Muggle attacks, was sentenced to three years in Azkaban. Marvolo... received six months."

memories.description: Dumbledore's hand is still injured. It's not healed and Madam Pomfrey hasn't fixed it.
memories.source_text: [His hand was like that when I saw him over the summer,]

memories.description: Snape has been given the Defense Against the Dark Arts job. I can't believe they'd give him that after everything.
memories.source_text: [Professor Snape, meanwhile, will be taking over the position of Defense Against the Dark Arts teacher.]

memories.description: I want Snape gone by the end of the year. I hate him and I'm sure he'd be happy if he didn't stick around.
memories.source_text: [Well, there's one good thing, Snape'll be gone by the end of the year.]

memories.description: I thought Slughorn was going to teach Defense Against the Dark Arts, but I must have been mistaken because Snape got it.
memories.source_text: [But you said —] [Professor Snape, meanwhile, will be taking over the position of Defense Against the Dark Arts teacher.]

memories.description: Merope stopped using the love potion and Tom Riddle left her while she was still pregnant. He never came back or looked for his son.
memories.source_text: "Perhaps, besotted as she was, she had convinced herself that he would by now have fallen in love with her in return. Perhaps she thought he would stay for the baby’s sake. If so, she was wrong on both counts. He left her, never saw her again, and never troubled to discover what became of his son."

memories.description: Tom Riddle returned to Little Hangleton alone after the marriage. Merope was gone.
memories.source_text: "Within a few months of their runaway marriage, Tom Riddle reappeared at the manor house in Little Hangleton without his wife."

memories.description: A lot of this is deduction, but it all points the same way. Voldemort's early life needs some piecing together.
memories.source_text: "Yes, indeed," said Dumbledore. "We must do a certain amount of guessing here, although I do not think it is difficult to deduce what happened."

memories.description: Merope did give birth to Tom Riddle's child. That child ended up growing up without his parents.
memories.source_text: "But she did have his baby."

memories.description: Voldemort was brought up in an orphanage after Merope's death. He did not have a father who knew him.
memories.source_text: "Yes, indeed," said Dumbledore. "We must do a certain amount of guessing here, although I do not think it is difficult to deduce what happened. You see, within a few months of their runaway marriage, Tom Riddle reappeared at the manor house in Little Hangleton without his wife."

memories.description: Dumbledore says Voldemort's past is directly connected to the prophecy. This is not just gossip, it matters to why I'm involved.
memories.source_text: "It has everything to do with the prophecy."

memories.description: Dumbledore told me I can tell Ron and Hermione what I now know. They are trustworthy, but I must make them promise to keep it to themselves.
memories.source_text: "Yes, I think Mr. Weasley and Miss Granger have proved themselves trustworthy. But Harry, I am going to ask you to ask them not to repeat any of this to anybody else."

memories.description: I snapped at Snape. Calling him ‘sir’ felt wrong and I wasn’t going to take his cheek quietly. That got me detention.
memories.source_text: There’s no need to call me ‘sir,’ Professor.

memories.description: I can cast a Shield Charm without thinking, even when I'm caught off guard. I blasted Snape across a desk with Protego when he aimed at me.
memories.source_text: Do you remember me telling you we are practicing nonverbal spells, Potter?

memories.description: Snape doesn’t just teach the Dark Arts. He likes them. That makes me uneasy.
memories.source_text: He loves them! All that unfixed, indestructible stuff

memories.description: I don’t need an Outstanding to continue Potions because Slughorn will accept Exceeds Expectations. I also haven’t bought any books or ingredients yet so I’ll have to borrow some.
memories.source_text: Professor Slughorn, however, is perfectly happy to accept N.E.W.T. students with ‘Exceeds Expectations’ at O.W.L. Do you wish to proceed with Potions?

memories.description: I’m the Captain now and people expect me to run trials. I told Ron he didn’t need to try out because I’d watched him play for years, but I know I have to be fair and not favour mates.
memories.source_text: Oh, by the way — twenty hopefuls have already put down their names for the Gryffindor Quidditch team. I shall pass the list to you in due course and you can fix up trials at your leisure.

memories.description: I shouted Liberacorpus to get Ron down. I used the counter-jinx from that old potion book and it worked.
memories.source_text: "Praying that this was the counter-jinx, Harry thought Liberacorpus!"

memories.description: I told them my dad used the spell. Truth is, I saw my dad do it on Snape and I kept quiet about that. Now I'm thinking maybe the Half-Blood Prince could be connected to my dad. Could be, right?
memories.source_text: "My dad used this spell," said Harry.

memories.description: I defended it as a laugh. I don't want Hermione to make out we're doing something terrible. We're messing about, not being Death Eaters.
memories.source_text: "It was a laugh!" said Ron, upending a ketchup bottle over his sausages.

memories.description: I’m going to make time for Hagrid later. I miss him and I’ll sort it out after the trials.
memories.source_text: "We’ll go down after Quidditch," Harry assured her.

memories.description: I’ve swapped the Prince’s copy with a new book so Slughorn gets a fresh one and I keep the useful copy. Practical and tidy.
memories.source_text: "I’ll give Slughorn back the new one, he can’t complain, it cost nine Galleons."

memories.description: Fine. I’ll get the team organized and deal with the trials. Being captain means handling this, even if it’s stressful.
memories.source_text: "Right," said Harry.

memories.description: I've been saying I had Quidditch practice every time Slughorn sent one of those ribboned invitations so I could avoid his practice nights.
memories.source_text: "Well, I've had Quidditch practice, Professor,"

memories.description: I told him I had an appointment with Dumbledore to get out of another invitation, and I can bluff my way through it when I need to.
memories.source_text: "I can't, Professor, I've got — er — an appointment with Professor Dumbledore that evening."

memories.description: I schedule those fake practices partly so Ron won't feel left out and we can all have a laugh with Ginny about the ridiculous pairings.
memories.source_text: "This strategy meant that Ron was not left out, and they usually had a laugh with Ginny, imagining Hermione shut up with McLaggen and Zabini."

memories.description: I'm fed up with wasting time on people who can't even fly. If you're not Gryffindor, go. Seriously, this is a trial, not a social.
memories.source_text: If there’s anyone else here who’s not from Gryffindor, leave now, please!

memories.description: Those first years can't fly for love or money. That was obvious as soon as they tried to get off the ground.
memories.source_text: The first ten was made up of first years and it could not have been plainer that they had hardly ever flown before.

memories.description: So someone called themselves the Half-Blood Prince. That name exists and it could be important.
memories.source_text: "The Half-Blood Prince, he was called,"

memories.description: If Dumbledore says this ties into the prophecy, then whatever he is about to tell me could count toward why Voldemort picked me. This might actually help me stay alive.
memories.source_text: "It has a very great deal to do with the prophecy,"

memories.description: Snape and I still have that whole detention business, but Dumbledore has some control over when I deal with him. I can delay it for now.
memories.source_text: "I have arranged with Professor Snape that you will do your detention next Saturday instead."

memories.description: Dumbledore is letting me into a Pensieve memory on purpose. I'm going in with him and I'm supposed to be prepared for whatever I see.
memories.source_text: "This time, you enter the Pensieve with me . . . and, even more unusually, with permission."

memories.description: We're going to see a memory from someone called Bob Ogden who worked for the Department of Magical Law Enforcement. This could show me things Dumbledore thinks I need to know.
memories.source_text: "For a trip down Bob Ogden's memory lane,"

memories.description: Katie almost died from that cursed necklace. She only touched it with a tiny bit of skin through a hole in her glove. If she'd actually put it on or held it barehanded she would have been dead straight away.
memories.source_text: Still very unwell, although she was relatively lucky. She appears to have brushed the necklace with the smallest possible amount of skin: There was a tiny hole in her glove. Had she put it on, had she even held it in her ungloved hand, she would have died, perhaps instantly.

memories.description: Snape stepped in and stopped the curse spreading fast. He did what was needed to keep her alive when it could have been instant death.
memories.source_text: Luckily Professor Snape was able to do enough to prevent a rapid spread of the curse

memories.description: I can't pretend I like Snape, but he clearly knows his stuff about the Dark Arts. Pomfrey's brilliant at healing, but this was darker magic and Snape was the one who could deal with it.
memories.source_text: Professor Snape knows much more about the Dark Arts than Madam Pomfrey, Harry.

memories.description: Dumbledore was away this weekend and he won't tell me where yet. He says he'll tell me later, so there's something he's keeping to himself for now.
memories.source_text: I would rather not say just now. However, I shall tell you in due course.

memories.description: Mundungus has been messing about with my inheritance and he's hiding since I confronted him in Hogsmeade. Dumbledore already knows about it and thinks Mundungus is avoiding him as well.
memories.source_text: Ah yes, I am already aware that Mundungus has been treating your inheritance with light-fingered contempt. He has gone to ground since you accosted him outside the Three Broomsticks; I rather think he dreads facing me.

memories.description: I've got detention with Snape at half past eight and I'm stuck sorting rotten flobberworms for Potions. No gloves. Great.
memories.source_text: "He says you’re to come to his office at half past eight tonight to do your detention — er — no matter how many party invitations you’ve received. And he wanted you to know you’ll be sorting out rotten flobberworms from good ones, to use in Potions and — and he says there’s no need to bring protective gloves."

memories.description: Slughorn fawns over me and tries to bend things my way, but Snape won't be fooled. Slughorn's all charm; he expects favours.
memories.source_text: "Oh dear! Dear, dear, I was counting on you, Harry! Well, now, I’ll just have to have a word with Severus and explain the situation. I’m sure I’ll be able to persuade him to postpone your detention."

memories.description: If I wasn't searched on arrival, then Malfoy could have brought something into Hogwarts by slipping in after the checks. That actually makes sense now.
memories.source_text: "We were all searched when we arrived, weren’t we?" "Were you?" "Oh no, of course you weren’t, I forgot you were late."

memories.description: Dad went to the Malfoys' house on a tip-off. If they didn't find anything there, whatever Malfoy has might be elsewhere.
memories.source_text: "It just says he’s been to visit the Malfoys’ house. ‘This second search of the Death Eater’s residence does not seem to have yielded any results. Arthur Weasley of the Office for the Detection and Confiscation of Counterfeit Defensive Spells and Protective Objects said that his team had been acting upon a confidential tip-off.'"

memories.description: I thought maybe it was sent to Malfoy by owl, but that idea falls apart because they're checking all the owls. So that route's blocked.
memories.source_text: "Someone’s sent it to him by owl, then,"

memories.description: That goblet came from Sirius's house. I know it, it had the Black crest on it and someone nicked it.
memories.source_text: You took that from Sirius's house, That had the Black family crest on it.

memories.description: Mundungus is a thief and I won't stand for it. I don't trust him at all and I'll go after him.
memories.source_text: Give it to me!

memories.description: I'm not going to let things like this go. If someone takes something that belonged to my friends, I will chase them down.
memories.source_text: COME BACK, YOU THIEVING - !

memories.description: I wanted to get out of the cold and go somewhere warm, like the Three Broomsticks.
memories.source_text: Let's go to the Three Broomsticks, It'll be warm.

memories.description: Maybe my dad used that spell. I said Lupin told me even though I actually saw Dad do it in the Pensieve. I kept that to myself because it felt important and complicated.
memories.source_text: “My dad,” said Harry. He had only just remembered. “What?” said Ron and Hermione together. “My dad used this spell,” said Harry. “I — Lupin told me.”

memories.description: If the Half Blood Prince was a wannabe Death Eater he would not have called himself half blood. So maybe he wasn’t a Death Eater after all.
memories.source_text: “If he’d been a budding Death Eater he wouldn’t have been boasting about being ‘half-blood,’ would he?”

memories.description: Dumbledore's next lesson is on Monday evening. Ginny handed me the parchment so I know exactly when it is.
memories.source_text: “Hey, Harry, I’m supposed to give you this.” It was a scroll of parchment with Harry’s name written upon it in familiar thin, slanting writing. “Thanks, Ginny . . . It’s Dumbledore’s next lesson!”

memories.description: Slughorn keeps fussing over me and trying to feed me. He calls me m'boy and is determined to have me at his little suppers.
memories.source_text: “Harry, m’boy!” said a booming voice from behind them. “Oh no,” muttered Harry. The three of them turned to see Professor Slughorn...

memories.description: We're going into Dumbledore's memory. He says it's full of detail and accurate, and I'm expected to go first.
memories.source_text: "This time," said Dumbledore, "we are going to enter my memory. I think you will find it both rich in detail and satisfyingly accurate. After you, Harry . . ."

memories.description: Hogwarts has a fund to help students buy books and robes. Some things I might have to get secondhand but they can help me out.
memories.source_text: "There is a fund at Hogwarts for those who require assistance to buy books and robes. You might have to buy some of your spellbooks and so on secondhand, but —"

memories.description: Diagon Alley is where you buy spellbooks and school gear. Dumbledore even has my list and can help me get everything.
memories.source_text: "In Diagon Alley," said Dumbledore. "I have your list of books and school equipment with me. I can help you find everything —"

memories.description: To get to the Leaky Cauldron from the orphanage I can see it even if Muggles can't. I should ask for Tom the barman.
memories.source_text: "You will be able to see it, although Muggles around you — non-magical people, that is — will not. Ask for Tom the barman — easy enough to remember, as he shares your name —"

memories.description: My start at Hogwarts is all written down. I leave from King's Cross on September first.
memories.source_text: "All the details are on the second piece of parchment in your envelope," said Dumbledore. "You will leave from King’s Cross Station on the first of September."

memories.description: I expected Dumbledore to insist on going with Riddle, but he didn't. I'm surprised by how he trusts people to manage on their own sometimes.
memories.source_text: Harry thought that Dumbledore would insist upon accompanying Riddle, but once again he was surprised.

memories.description: Dumbledore helps people quietly and practically. He gave Riddle the envelope and directions without making a fuss, which makes me feel like he handles things carefully and thoughtfully.
memories.source_text: Dumbledore handed Riddle the envelope containing his list of equipment, and after telling Riddle exactly how to get to the Leaky Cauldron from the orphanage, he said, "You will be able to see it..."

memories.description: He wouldn't have wanted to carry the necklace in public. He'd be worried about how he'd look if he was seen with it.
memories.source_text: "What he actually said was, ‘How would I look carrying that down the street?’" said Hermione.

memories.description: Malfoy couldn't have handed the necklace to Katie in Hogsmeade today because he was doing detention with McGonagall. Right now I'm deflated because I was sure he was involved.
memories.source_text: “But —” “— and what is more," said Professor McGonagall, with an air of awful finality, "Mr Malfoy was not in Hogsmeade today."

memories.description: That necklace could have been intended for plenty of targets—Dumbledore, Slughorn, maybe even me. Voldemort's side would want Dumbledore gone and they had reasons to want Slughorn.
memories.source_text: “It could’ve been meant for loads of people,” said Harry.

memories.description: If Malfoy wasn't there, then whoever sent the necklace must have used someone else to get it into Hogwarts. It could be Crabbe or Goyle or someone else helping them.
memories.source_text: “He must have used an accomplice, then,” said Harry.

memories.description: Dumbledore showed Tom Riddle how to get to the Leaky Cauldron and gave him his school list. He told Tom to ask for Tom the barman and explained Muggles won't see it. I was watching the whole thing.
memories.source_text: "Dumbledore handed Riddle the envelope containing his list of equipment, and after telling Riddle exactly how to get to the Leaky Cauldron from the orphanage, he said, 'You will be able to see it, although Muggles around you — non-magical people, that is — will not. Ask for Tom the barman — easy enough to remember, as he shares your name'"

memories.description: The envelope Dumbledore gave Tom has all the Hogwarts details and a ticket for the first of September. So Tom's set for school unless he throws it away.
memories.source_text: "All the details are on the second piece of parchment in your envelope,' said Dumbledore. 'You will leave from King's Cross Station on the first of September. There is a train ticket in there too.'"

memories.description: Tom told Dumbledore he can speak to snakes. That sounded creepy and important.
memories.source_text: "I can speak to snakes. I found out when we've been to the country on trips — they find me, they whisper to me.'"

memories.description: Tom is fiercely independent and doesn't want help. He made it clear he thinks he can manage on his own.
memories.source_text: "I don't need you,' said Riddle. 'I'm used to doing things for myself, I go round London on my own all the time.'"

memories.description: I expected Dumbledore to insist on coming along, but he didn't. That left Tom and Dumbledore oddly detached from each other in front of me.
memories.source_text: "You’re coming with me?' asked Riddle, looking up. 'Certainly, if you —' 'I don't need you,' said Riddle."

memories.description: Right that's my private lesson with Dumbledore on Saturday at eight. And the password for his study is Acid Pops. Good to know.
memories.source_text: Dear Harry, I would like to start our private lessons this Saturday. Kindly come along to my office at 8 p.m. I hope you are enjoying your first day back at school. Yours sincerely, Albus Dumbledore P.S. I enjoy Acid Pops.

memories.description: If Dumbledore uses Acid Pops as a password then he’s a bit more ordinary and mischievous than people make out. I actually like that.
memories.source_text: He enjoys Acid Pops? "It’s the password to get past the gargoyle outside his study," said Harry in a low voice.

memories.description: Slughorn will lend me and Ron old Advanced Potion-Making books and scales so we can do the N.E.W.T. practical even though we did not bring kit.
memories.source_text: Ah, yes, Professor McGonagall did mention . . . not to worry, my dear boy, not to worry at all. You can use ingredients from the store cupboard today, and I’m sure we can lend you some scales, and we’ve got a small stock of old books here, they’ll do until you can write to Flourish and Blotts.

memories.description: Veritaserum forces someone to tell the truth. That could be dangerous if it falls into the wrong hands.
memories.source_text: It’s Veritaserum, a colorless, odorless potion that forces the drinker to tell the truth," said Hermione.

memories.description: Polyjuice Potion changes you into someone else. Hermione made it before so she knows exactly what it looks like.
memories.source_text: It’s Polyjuice Potion, sir," she said.

memories.description: Amortentia is the strongest love potion. It does not create true love but causes powerful infatuation and obsession. That sounds dangerous.
memories.source_text: It’s the most powerful love potion in the world!" said Hermione.

memories.description: Felix Felicis is liquid luck. If brewed properly it makes things go your way for about twelve hours.
memories.source_text: Well, that one, ladies and gentlemen, is a most curious little potion called Felix Felicis.

memories.description: Slughorn says he has taken Felix Felicis twice and remembers them as perfect days. It really does seem to work when used properly.
memories.source_text: "Once when I was twenty-four, once when I was fifty-seven. Two tablespoonfuls taken with breakfast. Two perfect days."

memories.description: Slughorn is offering a tiny bottle of Felix Felicis as a prize for the best potion in class. I could win that if I focus.
memories.source_text: "One tiny bottle of Felix Felicis," said Slughorn, taking a minuscule glass bottle with a cork in it out of his pocket and showing it to them all.

memories.description: Slughorn already thinks well of Hermione because of something I said earlier. That could make him fond of our group.
memories.source_text: Oho! 'One of my best friends is Muggle-born, and she's the best in our year!' I’m assuming this is the very friend of whom you spoke, Harry?

memories.description: I tried crushing the sopophorous bean with the flat side of Hermione's silver dagger and it worked. The bean poured out loads of juice and my potion changed exactly like the book described. That trick actually does what it says.
memories.source_text: "Crush with flat side of silver dagger, releases juice better than cutting."

memories.description: Following the marginal note about seven counterclockwise stirs then one clockwise made my potion go pale lilac. The scribbled instructions in that old book can be right and useful.
memories.source_text: "According to the addition the previous owner had made, however, he ought to add a clockwise stir after every seventh counterclockwise stir."

memories.description: Slughorn's taken a shine to me for potions. He praised me in front of everyone and gave me a bottle of Felix Felicis. That felt huge and made the Slytherins seethe.
memories.source_text: "Excellent, excellent, Harry! Good lord, it’s clear you’ve inherited your mother’s talent. She was a dab hand at Potions, Lily was! Here you are, then, here you are — one bottle of Felix Felicis, as promised, and use it well!"

memories.description: Ginny and Hermione worried the book might be odd or dangerous, but I told them it's just marginal notes, not a cursed diary. I still don't want people thinking I cheated though.
memories.source_text: "It’s not like, you know, Riddle’s diary. It’s just an old textbook someone’s scribbled on."

memories.description: Malfoy clearly expected special treatment, but Slughorn ignored him and praised me instead. Malfoy can't rely on connections here; talent matters, and that annoys him.
memories.source_text: "Yes," said Slughorn, without looking at Malfoy, "I was sorry to hear he had died, although of course it wasn’t unexpected, dragon pox at his age. . . ."

memories.description: So he’s a Curse-Breaker and he likes a bit of adventure and glamour. Fine, that explains why he picked Fleur.
memories.source_text: "He’s a Curse-Breaker, isn’t he, he likes a bit of adventure, a bit of glamour."

memories.description: Okay, Fleur’s not an idiot. She’s actually capable if she made it into the Triwizard Tournament.
memories.source_text: "Fleur’s not stupid, she was good enough to enter the Triwizard Tournament," said Harry.

memories.description: Tonks and Sirius hardly knew each other. I can’t see any reason she should blame herself for what happened to him.
memories.source_text: "Tonks and Sirius barely knew each other!" said Ron. "Sirius was in Azkaban half her life and before that their families never met —"

memories.description: Tonks feels guilty about Sirius. She thinks if she’d finished Bellatrix, Sirius might still be alive. That’s survivor guilt, not sense.
memories.source_text: "She thinks it was her fault he died!" said Hermione.

memories.description: I got Outstanding in Defense Against the Dark Arts. That’s a proper result. We’ve done all right.
memories.source_text: "Harry James Potter has achieved: ... Defense Against the Dark Arts O"

memories.description: I told McGonagall about Draco and Dumbledore knows I said something. I'm keeping an eye on him.
memories.source_text: "Professor," said Harry, after a short pause, "did Professor McGonagall tell you what I told her after Katie got hurt? About Draco Malfoy?"

memories.description: Dumbledore says he'll investigate whoever hurt Katie. I want him to follow through.
memories.source_text: "I shall take all appropriate measures to investigate anyone who might have had a hand in Katie’s accident," said Dumbledore.

memories.description: I was annoyed that he seemed to care more about the lesson than the Draco situation. It felt important and I resented the delay.
memories.source_text: "But what concerns me now, Harry, is our lesson."

memories.description: Merope Riddle was in London and pregnant with the child who becomes Voldemort.
memories.source_text: "Merope was left alone in London, expecting the baby who would one day become Lord Voldemort."

memories.description: A desperate, pregnant Merope sold the Slytherin locket to Borgin and Burke for just ten Galleons. That's outrageously little.
memories.source_text: "It was brought in by a young witch just before Christmas, oh, many years ago now... Happy to get ten Galleons for it. Best bargain we ever made!"

memories.description: Merope must have stopped using magic after Tom left her. That would explain why she couldn't get by and had to sell the locket.
memories.source_text: "But it is my belief — I am guessing again, but I am sure I am right — that when her husband abandoned her, Merope stopped using magic."

memories.description: Burke is stingy. He only gave her ten Galleons because he could get away with it.
memories.source_text: "Caractacus Burke was not famed for his generosity," said Dumbledore.

memories.description: I patched her up with Episkey. Quick fix. Someone has to keep things from getting nastier.
memories.source_text: "I can fix that," said Harry, landing beside the two girls, pointing his wand at Demelza’s mouth, and saying "Episkey."

memories.description: I’ll stand by Ron, but I won't let him bully the team. If he keeps it up, I will drop him. Simple as that.
memories.source_text: "You’re my best mate, but carry on treating the rest of them like this and I’m going to kick you off the team."

memories.description: Ron can be brilliant as Keeper when he’s on it. The problem is his nerves, not his ability.
memories.source_text: "You’re the best Keeper I tried out, Ron. Your only problem is nerves."

memories.description: I care about Ron as my mate, but I'm captain first. I won't let friendship ruin the team.
memories.source_text: "You’re my best mate, but carry on treating the rest of them like this and I’m going to kick you off the team."

memories.description: Malfoy being out smells odd. Either he’s actually sick or he’s up to something.
memories.source_text: "He’s ill? What’s wrong with him?"

memories.description: He says this is important and it will help me survive. I have to take it seriously if Dumbledore says it'll keep me safe.
memories.source_text: But he says it’s all important and it’ll help me survive.

memories.description: I'm worried about how relationships change things. If Ron and Hermione get together then break up I could end up stuck in the middle again and that would be a nightmare.
memories.source_text: He and Cho were now too embarrassed to look at each other, let alone talk to each other; what if Ron and Hermione started going out together, then split up? Could their friendship survive it?

memories.description: Team practice is tonight at seven. I need to be there and sort the team out.
memories.source_text: There’s a practice tonight, seven o’clock.

memories.description: Winning would shut people up and make them back me. I know a good result changes how people treat you.
memories.source_text: If Gryffindor won, Harry knew that the whole House would forget that they had criticized him and swear that they had always known it was a great team.

memories.description: We have to get on with the work or we fall behind. Neville has already got a pod so we can't waste time.
memories.source_text: You’re lagging behind, everybody else has started, and Neville’s already got his first pod!

memories.description: I caught the Snitch. I grabbed it and shouted YES as we won.
memories.source_text: "He made a great swipe for the tiny, fluttering ball and caught it. 'YES!' Harry yelled."

memories.description: I pretended I had given Ron Felix Felicis so he'd think I was responsible for his luck, but I did not actually put anything in his juice.
memories.source_text: "I wanted Ron to think I’d done it, so I faked it when I knew you were looking."

memories.description: Someone shoved me midmatch on purpose. Harper deliberately hit me and tried to interfere with the pursuit of the Snitch.
memories.source_text: "Thinks he’s something special today, doesn’t he?" said a snide voice, and Harry was nearly knocked off his broom as Harper collided with him hard and deliberately."

memories.description: Calling Harper out about Malfoy was a desperate move, but it worked. I said it on the spur of the moment and it distracted him so I could catch the Snitch.
memories.source_text: "How much did Malfoy pay you to come on instead of him?" He did not know what made him say it, but Harper did a double-take; he fumbled the Snitch..."

memories.description: Ginny smashed into the commentator's podium in her excitement. She's that reckless when she's thrilled.
memories.source_text: "Ginny sped right on past them until, with an almighty crash, she collided with the commentator’s podium."

memories.description: She just left Cormac after an awkward mistletoe moment. I grabbed her and told her off for coming with him.
memories.source_text: "Oh, I’ve just escaped — I mean, I’ve just left Cormac, Under the mistletoe,"

memories.description: I'm not having any of that biography nonsense. I told the bloke flat out I'm not interested in interviews or making money from my name.
memories.source_text: "I’m definitely not interested," said Harry firmly, "and I’ve just seen a friend of mine, sorry."

memories.description: Hermione says she won't tell Ron about the Keeper tryouts. Good. If Ron finds out now he'd fall apart and we'd lose the next Quidditch match.
memories.source_text: "I’ve got no plans to tell Ron anything about what might, or might not, have happened at Keeper tryouts."

memories.description: Hermione hates McLaggen's behavior. She actually says she'd have preferred Zacharias Smith to McLaggen. That's saying something.
memories.source_text: "Yes, I did, and I’m starting to wish I’d chosen him, McLaggen makes Grawp look a gentleman."

memories.description: I tell Molly I always look after myself. I like to pretend I want a quiet life and that trouble is not my thing.
memories.source_text: "I always do, Mrs. Weasley," said Harry. "I like a quiet life, you know me."

memories.description: I came through the Floo link from the Burrow and landed straight in Professor McGonagall's office. Quick and a bit messy with ash.
memories.source_text: "Hogwarts!" (stepping into the emerald fire and arriving in Professor McGonagall's office)

memories.description: Molly worries about me like I'm one of her own. I let her fuss and promise to be careful because it calms her down.
memories.source_text: Mrs. Weasley enfolded Harry in her arms. "Promise me you’ll look after yourself. . . . Stay out of trouble. . . ."

memories.description: I won\'t give the book back. I\'ve learned more from the Half-Blood Prince than I have from Snape or Slughorn.
memories.source_text: "I am not giving back this book, I\'ve learned more from the Half-Blood Prince than Snape or Slughorn have taught me in —"

memories.description: People are trying to slip me love potions so they can get into Slughorn\'s party. Fred and George\'s things actually work, so I have to watch what I drink.
memories.source_text: "They\'re all hoping they\'re going to get you to take them to Slughorn\'s party, and they all seem to have bought Fred and George\'s love potions, which I\'m afraid to say probably work —"

memories.description: Filch isn\'t catching everything. If stuff can be smuggled in disguised as perfumes or cough medicine, then Malfoy could have brought things into the school too.
memories.source_text: "The point is, Filch is being fooled, isn\'t he? These girls are getting stuff into the school disguised as something else! So why couldn\'t Malfoy have brought the necklace into the school — ?"

memories.description: I can\'t stop thinking about Ginny. It\'s getting in the way of everything and I\'m trying not to let it show.
memories.source_text: "I\'m still trying not to think about Ginny any more than I could help, despite the fact that she kept cropping up in his dreams in ways that made him devoutly thankful that Ron could not perform Legilimency."

memories.description: Hermione was upset after seeing Ron with Lavender. She tried to hide her tears and left quickly.
memories.source_text: "\"Hi, Luna. Hermione, you left your stuff. . . .\" He held out her books. \"Oh yes,\" said Hermione in a choked voice, taking her things and turning away quickly to hide the fact that she was wiping her eyes on her pencil case."

memories.description: I asked if what I saw was normal. It isn't common, but it's not unheard of either.
memories.source_text: Is that normal for a wizard?

memories.description: I remembered how I didn't believe Hagrid at first and realized Tom believed he was special way quicker than I believed I was a wizard.
memories.source_text: I didn’t believe Hagrid at first, when he told me.

memories.description: I heard that he could talk to snakes. That's rare and creepy, and it links him to Dark stuff even if not everyone who can do it is evil.
memories.source_text: And he was a Parselmouth,

memories.description: He wasn't just doing random spells. He was using magic on purpose to frighten, punish, and control people. That made him dangerous.
memories.source_text: His powers, as you heard, were surprisingly well-developed for such a young wizard and — most interestingly and ominously of all — he had already discovered that he had some measure of control over them, and begun to use them consciously.

memories.description: He wanted to be alone and didn't want friends. He preferred to act on his own. That fits with what Voldemort is like now.
memories.source_text: I trust that you also noticed that Tom Riddle was already highly self-sufficient, secretive, and, apparently, friendless?

memories.description: He kept trophies from the people he hurt. He stole things as souvenirs. That is cold and twisted and it stuck with me.
memories.source_text: And lastly — I hope you are not too sleepy to pay attention to this, Harry — the young Tom Riddle liked to collect trophies. You saw the box of stolen articles he had hidden in his room.

memories.description: I asked Luna to Slughorn's party. I blurted it out before I could stop myself.
memories.source_text: "How would you like to come to Slughorn’s party with me tonight?"

memories.description: I made it clear I'm asking her as a friend. I wanted there to be no confusion.
memories.source_text: "I mean, just as friends, you know."

memories.description: I told Luna I'll meet her at eight and that Hermione will fix my eyebrow. I'm arranging the practical bits.
memories.source_text: "No, said Harry firmly, "that was a mistake. I’ll get Hermione to put it right for me. So, I’ll meet you in the entrance hall at eight o’clock then."

memories.description: Peeves shouted about it and suddenly the whole school knew. I can't keep things private.
memories.source_text: "Potty asked Loony to go to the party! Potty lurves Loony! Potty luuuuurves Looooooony!"

memories.description: Ginny's glad I'm taking Luna. That should have made me pleased, but I couldn't quite manage it.
memories.source_text: "I’m really glad you’re taking her, Harry, she’s so excited."

memories.description: So people like Trelawney think I'm the 'Chosen One' and that the omens around me are bad. Great, just what I needed.
memories.source_text: "The rumors! The stories! 'The Chosen One'! Of course, I have known for a very long time. The omens were never good, Harry."

memories.description: Slughorn's been raving that I'm a natural at Potions and even compared me to my mum. That sounds good and awkward all at once.
memories.source_text: "But I don't think I've ever known such a natural at Potions! Instinctive, you know - like his mother!"

memories.description: Slughorn's trying to buddy up, dragging Snape in and saying I got some credit for my skill from him. It's obvious Slughorn wants to be useful to someone impressive.
memories.source_text: "I was just talking about Harry's exceptional potion-making! Some credit must go to you, of course, you taught him for five years!"

memories.description: Snape still sneers that he never taught me anything. He'll probably look for any excuse to doubt my ability and maybe dig into where it came from.
memories.source_text: "Funny, I never had the impression that I managed to teach Potter anything at all."

memories.description: I told them I want to be an Auror. Hearing Snape's sneer didn't change that. If anything, I want it more. I'll be an Auror.
memories.source_text: "Remind me what other subjects you're taking, Harry?" ... "All the subjects required, in short, for an Auror," said Snape

memories.description: Luna just told a mad idea that Aurors are a conspiracy using dark magic and gum disease. I laughed so hard I nearly inhaled my drink. Luna's mental, but she made me laugh when I needed it.
memories.source_text: "The Aurors are part of the Rotfang Conspiracy, I thought everyone knew that. They're working to bring down the Ministry of Magic from within using a combination of Dark Magic and gum disease."

memories.description: Filch dragged Malfoy in for gate-crashing. Malfoy wasn't invited and he was caught snooping around. That's satisfying to see.
memories.source_text: "I discovered this boy lurking in an upstairs corridor. He claims to have been invited to your party and to have been delayed in setting out."

memories.description: Right, I'm taking Luna to Slughorn's party. I'll lead and keep her away from the staring lot.
memories.source_text: "Hi," he said. "Shall we get going then?"

memories.description: Hermione's going to the party with Cormac McLaggen. Of course she'd pick a Quidditch player.
memories.source_text: "Yes, I'm meeting Cormac at eight, and we're —" "— we're going up to the party together."

memories.description: Luna tells me Rufus Scrimgeour is a vampire. I don't buy it, but she says it like it's fact so I stayed quiet.
memories.source_text: "Yes, he's a vampire," said Luna matter-of-factly.

memories.description: Loads of girls were glaring at me in the entrance hall. They're not subtle about it.
memories.source_text: "When he arrived in the entrance hall at eight o'clock that night, he found an unusually large number of girls lurking there, all of whom seemed to be staring at him resentfully as he approached Luna."

memories.description: Snape told me he promised Malfoy’s mum to protect him and said he’d made an Unbreakable Oath or something. I heard him offer to help Malfoy and that sounds serious.
memories.source_text: "He said he’d promised Malfoy’s mother to protect him, that he’d made an Unbreakable Oath or something"

memories.description: No one could have been acting that well. I’m convinced Snape really was offering help and not just pretending to trick Malfoy.
memories.source_text: "They didn’t hear him," said Harry flatly. "No one’s that good an actor, not even Snape."

memories.description: I promised Dumbledore I would not wander off while I am staying here so I can’t go off poking about on my own.
memories.source_text: "I promised Dumbledore I wouldn’t wander off while I’m staying here."

memories.description: I’m going to tell Dumbledore what I heard and I might talk to Mr Weasley as well. I want someone who can stop whatever Malfoy is up to to know about it.
memories.source_text: "I’m going to tell anyone who can put a stop to it, and Dumbledore’s top of the list. I might have another word with your dad too."

memories.description: I can't believe it I found out Tom Riddle actually framed Morfin by killing those Muggles himself and planted the fake memory in Morfin's head
memories.source_text: "Voldemort Stupefied his uncle, took his wand, and proceeded across the valley to ‘the big house over the way.’ There he murdered the Muggle man who had abandoned his witch mother, and, for good measure, his Muggle grandparents, thus obliterating the last of the unworthy Riddle line and revenging himself upon the father who never wanted him. Then he returned to the Gaunt hovel, performed the complex bit of magic that would implant a false memory in his uncle’s mind, laid Morfin’s wand beside its unconscious owner, pocketed the ancient ring he wore, and departed."

memories.description: Morfin confessed even though he did not do it and never realized he had not done those murders
memories.source_text: "He gave, as I say, a full and boastful confession."

memories.description: The Ministry can sense magic happened but they cannot tell who did it so underage wizards can get blamed for things they did not do if it happened in someone else's house
memories.source_text: "You are quite right — they can detect magic, but not the perpetrator: You will remember that you were blamed by the Ministry for the Hover Charm that was, in fact, cast by —"

memories.description: I used to think the Ministry would protect kids from being blamed But now I know they rely on parents and they can't identify the person who cast a spell
memories.source_text: "They will certainly be unable to tell who performed the magic," said Dumbledore, smiling slightly at the look of great indignation on Harry’s face. "They rely on witch and wizard parents to enforce their offspring’s obedience while within their walls."

memories.description: Dumbledore showed me memories in the Pensieve and one of them was supposed to be the most important he had collected
memories.source_text: "This will not take long," said Dumbledore, when he had finally emptied the phial. "We shall be back before you know it. Once more into the Pensieve, then . . ."

memories.description: Tom Riddle asked Slughorn about Horcruxes when he was a student and he already had Marvolo's ring on his hand
memories.source_text: "Sir, I wondered what you know about . . . about Horcruxes?"

memories.description: Slughorn has altered his recollection of that conversation to hide what he really remembered about Horcruxes
memories.source_text: "I don't know anything about Horcruxes and I wouldn't tell you if I did! Now get out of here at once and don't let me catch you mentioning them again!"

memories.description: Dumbledore wants me to convince Slughorn to give up the true memory myself because Slughorn will expect force or Veritaserum and Dumbledore does not want to push him out of Hogwarts
memories.source_text: "I am giving you homework, Harry. It will be your job to persuade Professor Slughorn to divulge the real memory,"

memories.description: I used to think memories shown in the Pensieve were fixed But now I know someone can tamper with their own memory and cover things up
memories.source_text: "Professor Slughorn has meddled with his own recollections."

memories.description: Phineas thinks I should not be the one to get the memory but Dumbledore trusts me to try anyway
memories.source_text: "I wouldn’t expect you to, Phineas," replied Dumbledore, and Fawkes gave another low, musical cry.

memories.description: Snape called someone 'your master' when talking to Malfoy. That sounds like Voldemort to me. He was referring to someone powerful and dangerous.
memories.source_text: "Snape definitely said 'your master,' and who else would that be?"

memories.description: Someone might be pretending to help Malfoy just so they can trick him into revealing his plans. I wouldn't put it past people to play both sides.
memories.source_text: "— he was pretending to offer help so that he could trick Malfoy into telling him what he’s doing?"

memories.description: Malfoy is definitely up to something. All the bits I've heard point to him planning something dangerous.
memories.source_text: "But this definitely proves Malfoy’s planning something, you can’t deny that."

memories.description: Lupin's having a rough time with his work among the werewolves. He's under strain and it's serious.
memories.source_text: "Not great," (about Lupin) and the subsequent talk about his mission among the werewolves

memories.description: Malfoy mentioned Fenrir Greyback to Borgin in Knockturn Alley. That links Malfoy to some nasty people and makes him look a lot more dangerous.
memories.source_text: "Malfoy threatened Borgin with him!"

memories.description: Hermione and I disagree about how serious this is. I'm fed up with her trying to downplay things when I know something bad is going on.
memories.source_text: "You’ll be eating your words, Hermione, just like the Ministry."

memories.description: I won't be anyone's puppet. I refuse to be used as a mascot to make the Ministry look good.
memories.source_text: “I don’t want to be used,” said Harry.

memories.description: Umbridge is still at the Ministry and they're using her to try and manipulate me by dangling an Auror career.
memories.source_text: “Dolores Umbridge has told me that you cherish an ambition to become an Auror.”

memories.description: If anyone thinks I'm Dumbledore's stooge, fine. Yes, I'm with Dumbledore. I back him over the Ministry any day.
memories.source_text: “Well, it is clear to me that he has done a very good job on you,” said Scrimgeour.

memories.description: The Ministry is imprisoning people like Stan. That's wrong and I won't stand for it.
memories.source_text: “Locking up Stan Shunpike, for instance.”

memories.description: You're telling me Greyback bit him when he was a kid. Bloody hell, Greyback is the one who does it on purpose.
memories.source_text: “It was Greyback who bit me.”

memories.description: So Greyback plans attacks, picks victims and waits for the full moon. He isn't some sad, out-of-control fool, he's dangerous and deliberate.
memories.source_text: “At the full moon, he positions himself close to victims, ensuring that he is near enough to strike. He plans it all.”

memories.description: I felt sorry for Lupin once thinking werewolves had no choice. Not anymore. If Greyback does this on purpose then pity's not the whole story.
memories.source_text: “I even felt pity for him, thinking that he had had no control, knowing by then how it felt to transform.”

memories.description: The Half-Blood Prince isn't me. There is a Potions book full of notes from some Prince who invented spells like Levicorpus.
memories.source_text: “Have you ever heard of someone called the Half-Blood Prince?”

memories.description: I saw Dad using Levicorpus on Snape in the Pensieve. That Prince's book really helped me in Potions.
memories.source_text: “My dad used it,” said Harry. “I saw him in the Pensieve, he used it on Snape.”

memories.description: Lupin said a Patronus can change after a big shock or emotional upheaval. That could explain Tonks's change.
memories.source_text: “Sometimes a great shock an emotional upheaval”

memories.description: Tonks's Patronus looked big and had four legs. That doesn't sound like her usual one. That's worrying.
memories.source_text: “It looked big, and it had four legs,” said Harry.

memories.description: Percy arrived with the Minister, Rufus Scrimgeour. Percy's clearly gone proper Ministry and he's not exactly thrilled to be with the family.
memories.source_text: “He’s — he’s with the Minister!”

memories.description: Kreacher sent me a parcel full of maggots. Classy present from a house-elf.
memories.source_text: The package contained a large number of maggots.

memories.description: He gave me Chocolate Cauldrons spiked with a love potion. That explains why Ron went mad.
memories.source_text: "They were mine, I chucked them out of my trunk when I was looking for the map, they’re the Chocolate Cauldrons Romilda gave me before Christmas, and they’re all spiked with love potion!"

memories.description: Fine, I’ll play this. I decided to introduce Ron to Romilda to stop him making an idiot of himself while he was under the potion.
memories.source_text: "Yeah, I’ll introduce you," said Harry, thinking fast.

memories.description: Professor Slughorn actually has an antidote and potion kit right there and can make remedies if he wants to.
memories.source_text: "I’ve got the necessary here in my bag, it’s not a difficult antidote. . . ."

memories.description: Slughorn is all charm and indulgence. I figured keeping him happy might help get what we needed.
memories.source_text: "Pick-me-up, that’s what he needs," Slughorn continued, now bustling over to a table loaded with drinks.

memories.description: A bezoar will act as an antidote to most poisons. Right now that’s exactly the kind of desperate measure I need to use.
memories.source_text: "Just shove a bezoar down their throats."

memories.description: Doing something bold to get Slughorn’s attention can pay off. I can be cheeky if it helps me get closer to what I want from him.
memories.source_text: "You’ve got nerve, boy!"

memories.description: I’m going to play things cool with Slughorn for now. Let him think I’ve forgotten about Horcruxes so I can come back at him later.
memories.source_text: "I had to try and soften him up so I could ask him about Voldemort, didn’t I?"

memories.description: Being bold can win more than respect. It can score points too, and that matters in its own way.
memories.source_text: "An extra ten points to Gryffindor for sheer cheek!"

memories.description: I shoved a bezoar down Ron's throat and it saved him. He'll be stuck in the hospital wing for about a week and has to keep taking essence of rue.
memories.source_text: "...and then I got the bezoar down his throat and his breathing eased up a bit, Slughorn ran for help, McGonagall and Madam Pomfrey turned up, and they brought Ron up here. They reckon he’ll be all right. Madam Pomfrey says he’ll have to stay here a week or so... keep taking essence of rue..."

memories.description: If there hadn't been a bezoar in that room I don't know what would have happened. That was terrifyingly close.
memories.source_text: "Lucky there was one in the room,"

memories.description: Slughorn was the one who poured out Ron's drink.
memories.source_text: "Slughorn poured it out —"

memories.description: Dumbledore thinks Voldemort wanted Slughorn. That makes Slughorn a possible target and the whole thing more dangerous.
memories.source_text: "Dumbledore reckons Voldemort wanted Slughorn on his side,"

memories.description: The Weasleys are incredibly grateful to me right now. Mrs Weasley hugged me like she'd lost her mind.
memories.source_text: "Half our family does seem to owe you their lives, now I stop and think about it,"

memories.description: Cormac McLaggen's already assuming he'll take Ron's place as Keeper and wants to talk strategy. Great.
memories.source_text: "There you are, Potter!"

memories.description: Lavender's obsessed with Ron and keeps cornering me about him. It's exhausting and awkward.
memories.source_text: "Is Hermione Granger still visiting him?"

memories.description: Firenze is an outcast in the forest and Dumbledore can't send him back or make Trelawney leave. So things are awkward in Divination and Dumbledore is stuck keeping both of them around.
memories.source_text: "Professor Trelawney still isn’t happy Firenze is teaching, then?" "No," said Dumbledore, "Divination is turning out to be much more trouble than I could have foreseen, never having studied the subject myself. I cannot ask Firenze to return to the forest, where he is now an outcast, nor can I ask Sybill Trelawney to leave."

memories.description: Trelawney actually made the prophecy about me and Voldemort and she does not know it. Dumbledore thinks I should not tell her.
memories.source_text: "She does not know — and I think it would be unwise to enlighten her — that she made the prophecy about you and Voldemort, you see."

memories.description: Dumbledore gives me that look that makes me feel like he can see right through me. He is disappointed with how I handled the task.
memories.source_text: "There was a little silence. "I see," said Dumbledore eventually, peering at Harry over the top of his half-moon spectacles and giving Harry the usual sensation that he was being X-rayed."

memories.description: That Slughorn memory is the most crucial thing for our plans. I can't shrug this off any more and need to get it no matter what.
memories.source_text: "I thought I made it clear to you how very important that memory is. Indeed, I did my best to impress upon you that it is the most crucial memory of all and that we will be wasting our time without it."

memories.description: The Pensieve and more memory vials are back on Dumbledore's desk. We're going to be diving into memories again.
memories.source_text: "Please close the door and sit down, Harry," said Dumbledore, sounding rather tired. Harry obeyed, noticing as he took his usual seat in front of Dumbledore’s desk that the Pensieve lay between them once more, as did two more tiny crystal bottles full of swirling memory."

memories.description: He ended up working at Borgin and Burkes. I can't believe someone like him was in that shop.
memories.source_text: “At Borgin and Burkes?” Harry repeated, stunned.

memories.description: Tom Riddle actually tried to stay on at Hogwarts as a teacher. He wanted to stick around the school.
memories.source_text: “He wanted to stay here? Why?” asked Harry, more amazed still.

memories.description: He wanted the Defense Against the Dark Arts post. Of all things, that was the subject he aimed for.
memories.source_text: “Defense Against the Dark Arts. It was being taught at the time by an old professor by the name of Galatea Merrythought,”

memories.description: I feel worse about failing to get that Horcrux memory because Dumbledore clearly values my opinion a lot. I shouldn't have messed it up.
memories.source_text: “I hope you are not tired of diving into other people’s memories, for they are curious recollections, these two,” he said.

memories.description: He loved Hogwarts in his own way. That makes me uneasy because I know how much this place means to me too.
memories.source_text: “Firstly, and very importantly, Voldemort was, I believe, more attached to this school than he has ever been to a person. Hogwarts was where he had been happiest; the first and only place he had felt at home.”

memories.description: Dumbledore didn't want him teaching here and he warned Professor Dippet. I get why Dumbledore was worried.
memories.source_text: “I had advised Armando against the appointment — I did not give the reasons I have given you, for Professor Dippet was very fond of Voldemort and convinced of his honesty. But I did not want Lord Voldemort back at this school, and especially not in a position of power.”

memories.description: He is impossible to work with. I can't stand him telling everyone what to do and acting like he could play every position better than the rest of us.
memories.source_text: "he keeps trying to tell everyone what to do, he thinks he could play every position better than the rest of us. I can’t wait to be shot of him."

memories.description: Malfoy was up at the castle with a couple of girlfriends and I want to know what he's up to.
memories.source_text: "I met Malfoy"

memories.description: If I catch the Snitch quickly I might get back to the castle and use the Marauder's Map to find out what Malfoy is doing.
memories.source_text: "If he could catch it good and early, there might be a chance he could get back up to the castle, seize the Marauder’s Map, and find out what Malfoy was doing."

memories.description: Lavender is making life awkward for Ron and that's getting on my nerves too.
memories.source_text: "She’s driving me mad as well."

memories.description: I ended up with a cracked skull and I'm stuck in the hospital wing overnight.
memories.source_text: "Cracked skull," said Madam Pomfrey

memories.description: We got hammered. That match was a disaster and McLaggen cost us badly.
memories.source_text: "Final score was three hundred and twenty to sixty."

memories.description: I'm not allowed to leave the hospital wing even if I want to get back to whatever Malfoy is doing.
memories.source_text: "You will stay here until I discharge you, Potter, or I shall call the headmaster."

memories.description: Luna was commentating and she was saying odd things about the game that distracted from the play.
memories.source_text: "I could hear the match commentary from here," said Ron

memories.description: Of course! Malfoy has been using the Room of Requirement. That explains why he keeps vanishing from the map.
memories.source_text: "The Room of Requirement!" said Harry, smacking himself hard on the forehead with Advanced Potion-Making.

memories.description: He nicked Polyjuice Potion from that huge vat in the dungeon. That's why he needed to go to the Room and why Crabbe and Goyle are only there as lookouts.
memories.source_text: "There was a great vat of it down in the dungeon. . . . He could've nicked some any time during that lesson."

memories.description: Slughorn's memory matters more than worrying about marks or arguing with Snape. Getting that memory is proper priority for me.
memories.source_text: "Slughorn's memory was the most important thing to him now."

memories.description: Kreacher and Dobby have been tailing Malfoy for me. Good, I can use what they found to get on top of this.
memories.source_text: "They've been following Malfoy for me," he said. "Night and day," croaked Kreacher.

memories.description: I couldn't believe Hermione had never heard of Horcruxes. I was banking on her to give me a clue and she had nothing.
memories.source_text: You haven't?

memories.description: If the Prince's notes aren't going to help me with this kind of theory, I can't rely on those so-called shortcuts anymore.
memories.source_text: It's a shame that the Prince won't be able to help you much with this, Harry

memories.description: There were no helpful notes in the Prince's writing about Golpalott's Third Law. I'm stuck with the book and my own head.
memories.source_text: Nothing, said Harry gloomily.

memories.description: Hermione's smug about outdoing me in Potions. I feel like my reputation as the best potion-maker in the class is taking a hit and I don't like it.
memories.source_text: You have to understand the principles involved this time. No shortcuts or cheats!

memories.description: My attempt at the antidote went horribly wrong and even Slughorn couldn't hide how bad it was. That's humiliating.
memories.source_text: Slughorn had peered hopefully into his cauldron on his first circuit of the dungeon, preparing to exclaim in delight as he usually did, and instead had withdrawn his head hastily, coughing, as the smell of bad eggs overwhelmed him.

memories.description: He's up to something shady. I heard Malfoy and Snape talking and I am not about to shrug that off.
memories.source_text: “I want to know what he’s up to,” said Harry. “And don’t tell me it’s all in my head, not after what I overheard between him and Snape —”

memories.description: Malfoy disappears from the map and I want to know where he goes and who he meets.
memories.source_text: “I want to catch him at it!” said Harry in frustration. “I mean, where’s he going when he disappears off the map?”

memories.description: I can use house-elves to tail Malfoy round the clock. That is how I will find out what he's doing.
memories.source_text: “I’ve got a job for you.” … “Okay then . . . I want you to tail Draco Malfoy.”

memories.description: Dobby is loyal to me and desperate to help. He'll obey me and wants to do this for me.
memories.source_text: “Dobby will do it, Harry Potter!” … “And if Dobby does it wrong, Dobby will throw himself off the topmost tower, Harry Potter!”

memories.description: Kreacher will obey my orders even though he hates doing this and would prefer to serve the Malfoys. He'll follow instructions begrudgingly.
memories.source_text: “Master wants me to follow the youngest of the Malfoys?” croaked Kreacher. “Master wants me to spy upon the pure-blood great-nephew of my old mistress?”

memories.description: I shouldn't be skipping matches, I'm the Captain, but my fix on Malfoy is driving me to bend that rule in my head.
memories.source_text: “Don’t be stupid,” said Ron sharply. “You couldn’t have missed a Quidditch match just to follow Malfoy, you’re the Captain!”

memories.description: He messed with people's memories. Of course he did it to Hokey, just as he did to Morfin. That explains the false confession.
memories.source_text: "Voldemort modified her memory, just like he did with Morfin!"

memories.description: Hepzibah Smith was dead shortly after Voldemort visited her and took her treasures.
memories.source_text: "Hepzibah Smith died two days after that little scene,"

memories.description: The locket made sense to him, but the cup mattered too. Voldemort was after objects tied to Hogwarts and not just sentimental things.
memories.source_text: "The locket maybe," said Harry, "but why take the cup as well?"

memories.description: Hermione and Ron are friends again. It's back to normal between them.
memories.source_text: "Hermione even escorted them down to breakfast, bringing with her the news that Ginny had argued with Dean."

memories.description: Ginny and Dean had a row and I want to know what it was about.
memories.source_text: "What did they row about?" he asked, trying to sound casual

memories.description: The diary was not just a creepy book. It held a piece of someone inside it. It was a Horcrux and that soul-piece could live on and act through the book.
memories.source_text: "The diary had been a Horcrux."

memories.description: If Voldemort treated a Horcrux so carelessly, he must have made more than one. He was planning ahead so losing one would not finish him.
memories.source_text: "The careless way in which Voldemort regarded this Horcrux seemed most ominous to me. It suggested that he must have made — or been planning to make — more Horcruxes"

memories.description: Voldemort said he had gone further toward immortality than anyone else and Dumbledore thinks he meant Horcruxes in the plural. He made multiple Horcruxes, not just one.
memories.source_text: "I, who have gone further than anybody along the path that leads to immortality.' ... He was referring to his Horcruxes, Horcruxes in the plural, Harry"

memories.description: Voldemort liked the idea of splitting his soul into several parts and he seemed to aim for seven pieces because he thought seven was a powerful number.
memories.source_text: "Wouldn't it be better, make you stronger, to have your soul in more pieces ... isn't seven the most powerfully magical number ..."

memories.description: There are six Horcruxes out there and the seventh piece of his soul is the bit that lives in his body. To kill him you have to destroy those six Horcruxes first.
memories.source_text: "But firstly, no, Harry, not seven Horcruxes: six. The seventh part of his soul, however maimed, resides inside his regenerated body."

memories.description: I destroyed one Horcrux already when I got rid of the diary. That means I'm already part of the fight to finish him.
memories.source_text: "You are forgetting . . . you have already destroyed one of them."

memories.description: Dumbledore told me he destroyed a Horcrux too. He killed the piece in Marvolo Gaunt's ring but it cost him badly.
memories.source_text: "I have destroyed another." "The ring, Harry. Marvolo's ring."

memories.description: Aragog is dead. Hagrid wants me, Ron and Hermione to go to his burial tonight and he even says we can use the cloak.
memories.source_text: Dear Harry, Ron, and Hermione, Aragog died last night.

memories.description: If I can make Slughorn like my potion I might get the memory out of him. Brewing the Half-Blood Prince recipe could put him in a good mood and that could be my chance.
memories.source_text: I want you all to brew me up something amusing!

memories.description: I have that Felix Felicis bottle and I am tempted to use it if Slughorn will not give me the memory otherwise. It feels like cheating but it might be necessary.
memories.source_text: Felix Felicis?

memories.description: Slughorn might be playing me. He acts friendly but I reckon he is dodging my questions on purpose.
memories.source_text: Harry could not help wondering whether this meant that Slughorn was not quite as forgetful as he appeared, simply determined to give Harry no additional opportunities to question him.

memories.description: I waited for one of Slughorn's parties and he never invited me. If he wanted me there he'd have asked.
memories.source_text: He awaited an invitation to one of his little evening parties, determined to accept this time, even if he had to reschedule Quidditch practice. Unfortunately, however, no such invitation arrived.

memories.description: If I want backup on something, I tell my mates. I don't hide it and expect them to guess.
memories.source_text: I tell my friends what I’m up to, if I want them to keep a lookout for me," Harry said, just loud enough for Malfoy to hear him.

memories.description: The Marauder's Map shows exactly where people are. I can use it to track Malfoy and catch him out.
memories.source_text: Help me find Malfoy," said Harry urgently. He laid the map upon his bed, and he and Ron leaned over it, searching.

memories.description: Malfoy is someone I need to watch closely. If he starts skulking about with Crabbe and Goyle I will follow him under the Cloak and find out what he is doing.
memories.source_text: Well, I’m keeping an eye on him from now on," he said firmly. "And the moment I see him lurking somewhere with Crabbe and Goyle keeping watch outside, it’ll be on with the old Invisibility Cloak and off to find out what he’s —

memories.description: Snape cares when McGonagall shouts at a Slytherin more than the actual rudeness. He sees House pride before manners.
memories.source_text: Harry glanced quickly at Snape, who also looked annoyed, though Harry strongly suspected that this was less because of Malfoy’s rudeness than the fact that McGonagall had reprimanded one of his House.

memories.description: Carefully planned things like Hogsmeade trips can be canceled at a moment's notice. People get furious about it, especially Ron.
memories.source_text: To general indignation, a sign went up on all common room notice boards that the next trip into Hogsmeade had been canceled.

memories.description: The luck potion's fading. I can feel it going and I can't rely on it anymore.
memories.source_text: "I could feel the Felix Felicis wearing off as he crept back into the castle."
