memories.description: I'm the one who has to choose this. No one will tell me to go. If I'm doing this, it's my decision and I'm staying close to them.
memories.source_text: "Stay close to me," he said quietly.

memories.description: Draco was the wand's master at some point. What? Draco? That is mental.
memories.source_text: "The true master of the Elder Wand was Draco Malfoy."

memories.description: I disarmed Draco and grabbed his wand. If the Elder Wand cares who disarmed its last owner, then it's mine. So yeah, I might actually be the true master.
memories.source_text: "But you’re too late," said Harry. "You’ve missed your chance. I got there first. I overpowered Draco weeks ago. I took this wand from him."

memories.description: Voldemort knows I don't have the phoenix wand anymore and thinks that means it comes down to our skill. Fine. Bring it on.
memories.source_text: "You no longer have the phoenix wand: We duel on skill alone . . . and after I have killed you, I can attend to Draco Malfoy."

memories.description: Seeing Dumbledore in that portrait, proud and grateful, it hit me right in the chest. His pride steadies me. I felt better, like I could actually do this.
memories.source_text: "Tears were sliding down from behind the half-moon spectacles into the long silver beard, and the pride and the gratitude emanating from him filled Harry with the same balm as phoenix song."

memories.description: I actually know things he doesn't. I can use knowledge against him and I won't be cowed by his threats.
memories.source_text: “I know things you don’t know, Tom Riddle. I know lots of important things that you don’t. Want to hear some, before you make another big mistake?”

memories.description: Dumbledore chose how and when to die. Voldemort didn't kill him.
memories.source_text: “Yes, Dumbledore’s dead,” said Harry calmly, “but you didn’t have him killed. He chose his own manner of dying, chose it months before he died, arranged the whole thing with the man you thought was your servant.”

memories.description: Snape's Patronus matched my mother's because he loved Lily. That explains everything about his actions.
memories.source_text: “Snape’s Patronus was a doe,” said Harry, “the same as my mother’s, because he loved her for nearly all of his life, from the time when they were children.”

memories.description: Snape was working for Dumbledore, not for Voldemort. He was Dumbledore's spy the whole time.
memories.source_text: “Snape was Dumbledore’s, said Harry. “Snape was Dumbledore’s from the moment you started hunting down my mother.”

memories.description: Hagrid loves me more than anyone. He was shaking and crying while he held me like I was the most important thing in the world.
memories.source_text: The enormous hands that lifted him into the air were exceedingly gentle. Harry could feel Hagrid’s arms trembling with the force of his heaving sobs; great tears splashed down upon him as Hagrid cradled Harry in his arms

memories.description: I can make myself look dead if I have to. I stayed totally limp and quiet so they actually believed it.
memories.source_text: he kept himself floppy and lifeless, and when he fell to the ground for the last time, the clearing echoed with jeers and shrieks of laughter

memories.description: They were too busy gloating to check if I was alive. No one bothered to see if I had a pulse.
memories.source_text: nobody looked to see whether a pulse beat in the exposed neck of Harry Potter

memories.description: Voldemort uses Hagrid to humiliate me. I can see how cruel they are by making Hagrid parade me like a prize.
memories.source_text: “You carry him,” Voldemort said. “He will be nice and visible in your arms, will he not? Pick up your little friend, Hagrid. And the glasses — put on the glasses — he must be recognizable —”

memories.description: I can break cover when I need to. I took off the cloak and threw up a Shield Charm to stop them and catch them off guard.
memories.source_text: “Protego!” roared Harry, and the Shield Charm expanded in the middle of the Hall, and Voldemort stared around for the source as Harry pulled off the Invisibility Cloak at last

memories.description: He expected me to come. He thought I'd show up when he wanted me to.
memories.source_text: I thought he would come. I expected him to come.

memories.description: He's admitting he was wrong and saying I'm not. My heart's hammering, I'm terrified, and I don't want to fight — I even pulled off the Invisibility Cloak and hid my wand so I wouldn't be tempted.
memories.source_text: I was, it seems mistaken. You weren't.

memories.description: She's willing to say Draco is dead just so they'll let her into Hogwarts to look for him.
memories.source_text: "He is dead!" Narcissa Malfoy called to the watchers.

memories.description: She cares more about finding her son than about Voldemort's victory. Family comes first for her, even if it means siding with the victors.
memories.source_text: She no longer cared whether Voldemort won.

memories.description: I expected them to humiliate me with Cruciatus and I braced for the pain, but when they lifted me the agony I thought would come never did.
memories.source_text: "Watch! Crucio!"

memories.description: So he killed Snape thinking that made him the true master of the Elder Wand.
memories.source_text: "I killed Severus Snape three hours ago, and the Elder Wand, the Deathstick, the Wand of Destiny is truly mine!"

memories.description: Dumbledore's plan didn't fail me. It blew up in Voldemort's face. He's the one who's screwed up, not me.
memories.source_text: "Yes, I dare," said Harry, "because Dumbledore's last plan hasn't backfired on me at all. It's backfired on you, Riddle."

memories.description: I grabbed Draco's hand and held on. I'm protecting him in that moment and keeping him close while Voldemort is losing his nerve.
memories.source_text: "Voldemort's hand was trembling on the Elder Wand, and Harry gripped Draco's very tightly."

memories.description: Calling him to try for remorse actually shook him. Asking him to be a man hit him harder than anything else I said.
memories.source_text: "What is this?" Of all the things that Harry had said to him, beyond any revelation or taunt, nothing had shocked Voldemort like this.

memories.description: He told me he fell in with Grindelwald and got swept up in his plans for wizards to rule and Muggles to be subservient. He admitted he helped the schemes and was fascinated by the Hallows.
memories.source_text: “Grindelwald. You cannot imagine how his ideas caught me, Harry, inflamed me.”

memories.description: He said Ariana ended up dead during that argument, and he was left with guilt and grief over what happened.
memories.source_text: “And Ariana . . . after all my mother’s care and caution . . . lay dead upon the floor.”

memories.description: He told me he refused the Ministry because he knows power is his weakness and he can't trust himself with it.
memories.source_text: “I had learned that I was not to be trusted with power.”

memories.description: I reached out, gripped his arm, and actually calmed him down. I can comfort him when he's breaking down.
memories.source_text: Harry reached out and was glad to find that he could touch him: He gripped his arm tightly and Dumbledore gradually regained control.

memories.description: I still think he'd have been a far better Minister than those fools. He might doubt himself but I believe he'd have done a better job.
memories.source_text: “But you’d have been better, much better, than Fudge or Scrimgeour!”

memories.description: I dropped the thing from the Snitch in the forest and I am not going back to hunt it down.
memories.source_text: "The thing that was hidden in the Snitch, I dropped it in the forest. I don’t know exactly where, but I’m not going to go looking for it again. Do you agree?"

memories.description: I'm keeping Ignotus's gift. It's mine to keep until I choose to pass it on.
memories.source_text: "I’m going to keep Ignotus’s present, though," said Harry, and Dumbledore beamed.

memories.description: I don't want the Elder Wand. I know it's powerful but I'd rather have my old wand and be done with all that power.
memories.source_text: "I don’t want it," said Harry.

memories.description: I fixed my broken holly and phoenix feather wand by touching it with the Elder Wand and saying Reparo. It actually worked and it felt right in my hand again.
memories.source_text: He laid the broken wand upon the headmaster’s desk, touched it with the very tip of the Elder Wand, and said, "Reparo."

memories.description: I'm going to return the Elder Wand to where it belongs and leave it there. No more fighting over it.
memories.source_text: "I’m putting the Elder Wand back where it came from. It can stay there."

memories.description: If I die a natural death like Ignotus, the Elder Wand's power will be broken. The chain of masters ends there and that's the point.
memories.source_text: "If I die a natural death like Ignotus, its power will be broken, won’t it? The previous master will never have been defeated. That’ll be the end of it."

memories.description: Don't worry, Lily, you'll be at Hogwarts before you know it. I'm telling you that like a fact, you'll love it when you're there.
memories.source_text: "It won’t be long, and you’ll be going too,"

memories.description: James is a show off and he winds people up for a laugh. Take what he says with a pinch of salt.
memories.source_text: "He likes a laugh, your brother."

memories.description: Well, of course I knew the answer about monkshood and wolfsbane because I was eager enough to stand up and reach for it.
memories.source_text: At this, Hermione stood up, her hand stretching toward the dungeon ceiling.

memories.description: Obviously Snape was treating me unfairly by ignoring my hand and ordering me to sit down when I tried to help.
memories.source_text: Snape was still ignoring Hermione’s quivering hand. "Sit down," he snapped at Hermione.

memories.description: Well, let's try this again. Of course I'm going to test him — where would he look if I told him to find a bezoar?
memories.source_text: "Let’s try again. Potter, where would you look if I told you to find me a bezoar?"

memories.description: Well, of course I went straight up and shoved the hat on. I wanted to be sorted and the hat put me into Gryffindor right away.
memories.source_text: ["Granger, Hermione!" Hermione almost ran to the stool and jammed the hat eagerly on her head. "GRYFFINDOR!" shouted the hat.]

memories.description: Obviously Ron groaned when I got Gryffindor. Typical. It mattered to him, even if he tried not to show it.
memories.source_text: ["Ron groaned."]

memories.description: Well, of course I want lessons to start straight away. There’s loads to learn and Transfiguration is proper fascinating. I’m determined to get on with it even if it’s difficult.
memories.source_text: "I do hope they start right away, there’s so much to learn, I’m particularly interested in Transfiguration, you know, turning something into something else, of course, it’s supposed to be very difficult —"

memories.description: Obviously teachers will start us small. I’m expecting careful, step by step lessons so I can actually learn things properly.
memories.source_text: "You’ll be starting small, just matches into needles and that sort of thing —"

memories.description: Well, of course I tried to learn flying from a book, but you cannot learn how to fly properly from pages alone.
memories.source_text: "This was something you couldn’t learn by heart out of a book — not that she hadn’t tried."

memories.description: Obviously I told everyone every useful tip I could find in Quidditch Through the Ages. I wanted to help, even if they found it dull.
memories.source_text: "At breakfast on Thursday she bored them all stupid with flying tips she’d gotten out of a library book called Quidditch Through the Ages."

memories.description: Of course Neville was desperate for help. I felt responsible to give him every bit of guidance he could use to hold on to a broom.
memories.source_text: "Neville was hanging on to her every word, desperate for anything that might help him hang on to his broomstick later,"

memories.description: Well, of course my broom didn't leap into my hand. Mine rolled over on the ground, which is ridiculous if you ask me.
memories.source_text: "Hermione Granger’s had simply rolled over on the ground, and Neville’s hadn’t moved at all."

memories.description: Obviously the proper words and technique matter for making a broom behave. You cannot just expect it to work without doing it correctly.
memories.source_text: "Stick out your right hand over your broom," called Madam Hooch at the front, "and say ‘Up!’"

memories.description: Well, of course I'm not letting you sneak around at night. It's selfish and reckless and you'll lose house points if you get caught.
memories.source_text: "I couldn’t help overhearing what you and Malfoy were saying — and you mustn’t go wandering around the school at night, think of the points you’ll lose Gryffindor if you’re caught, and you’re bound to be. It’s really very selfish of you."

memories.description: Now the Fat Lady's painting's empty and I'm locked out of the common room. What am I supposed to do now?
memories.source_text: Hermione had turned to the portrait of the Fat Lady to get back inside and found herself facing an empty painting. The Fat Lady had gone on a nighttime visit and Hermione was locked out of Gryffindor Tower.

memories.description: I'm not staying out here alone. I'll come with you, and if Filch catches us all I'll say I was trying to stop you and you can back me up.
memories.source_text: "I’m coming with you," "If he finds all three of us I’ll tell him the truth, that I was trying to stop you, and you can back me up."

memories.description: Obviously I won't be allowed to eat in peace around here without someone causing trouble.
memories.source_text: "Can't a person eat in peace in this place?"

memories.description: Of course I have learned the course books by heart. I always prepare properly.
memories.source_text: I’ve learned all our course books by heart, of course

memories.description: I introduce myself straight away and expect people to give their names as well. It's only polite.
memories.source_text: I’m Hermione Granger, by the way, who are you?

memories.description: Houses matter. I hope I get into Gryffindor because it seems the best, though Ravenclaw would be all right too.
memories.source_text: Do either of you know what House you’ll be in? I’ve been asking around, and I hope I’m in Gryffindor, it sounds by far the best

memories.description: I read ahead. I find out everything I can about new people and classes. That is practical and useful.
memories.source_text: I got a few extra books for background reading, and you’re in Modern Magical History and The Rise and Fall of the Dark Arts and Great Wizarding Events of the Twentieth Century.

memories.description: I boss people a bit because someone needs to get organised. I will help look for Neville's toad and push things along.
memories.source_text: Anyway, we’d better go and look for Neville’s toad. You two had better change, you know, I expect we’ll be there soon.

memories.description: Well, of course, Madam Hooch said not to move. If you break the rules we'll all get into trouble, Harry.
memories.source_text: "No!" shouted Hermione Granger. "Madam Hooch told us not to move — you’ll get us all into trouble."

memories.description: Obviously I don't want anyone risking expulsion, but I can't stop worrying when Harry does reckless things.
memories.source_text: "No!" shouted Hermione Granger. "Madam Hooch told us not to move — you’ll get us all into trouble."

memories.description: Well, of course it was standing on a trapdoor. Obviously it's guarding something.
memories.source_text: "You don’t use your eyes, any of you, do you?" she snapped. "Didn’t you see what it was standing on?" "No, not the floor. It was standing on a trapdoor. It’s obviously guarding something."

memories.description: Of course I'm furious — we could have been killed or, worse, expelled. I'm done; I'm going to bed.
memories.source_text: "I hope you’re pleased with yourselves. We could all have been killed — or worse, expelled. Now, if you don’t mind, I’m going to bed."

memories.description: What am I supposed to do now? I'm locked out and I can't just stand around while Gryffindor Tower is inaccessible.
memories.source_text: "Now what am I going to do?" she asked shrilly.

memories.description: Of course I want to come. I can't just leave you lot to get into trouble on your own, even if you tell me I can't.
memories.source_text: "I’m coming with you," she said. "You are not."

memories.description: If Filch catches us all, I'll say I was trying to stop you. I expect you to back me up if it comes to that.
memories.source_text: "If he finds all three of us I’ll tell him the truth, that I was trying to stop you, and you can back me up."

memories.description: Well, I was terrified and pinned to the wall. Of course I looked like I might faint with that troll coming at me.
memories.source_text: Hermione Granger was shrinking against the wall opposite, looking as if she was about to faint.

memories.description: Well, of course I marched away with my nose in the air. Some things just need a proper reaction when people start making a scene about brooms.
memories.source_text: "Hermione marched away with her nose in the air."

memories.description: Well, of course you say it properly: Wing-gar-dium Levi-o-sa. Make the gar nice and long.
memories.source_text: “You’re saying it wrong,” Harry heard Hermione snap. “It’s Wing-gar-dium Levi-o-sa, make the ‘gar’ nice and long.”

memories.description: Obviously I can do the levitation charm right. I can make the feather float perfectly.
memories.source_text: Hermione rolled up the sleeves of her gown, flicked her wand, and said, “Wingardium Leviosa!” Their feather rose off the desk and hovered about four feet above their heads.

memories.description: Well, I'm upset and I don't have anyone with me right now. Leave me alone, I need to be by myself.
memories.source_text: It was Hermione. Harry caught a glimpse of her face — and was startled to see that she was in tears. “I think she heard you.”

memories.description: Is it dead? Of course I asked that straight away. I need to know if the danger is over.
memories.source_text: "Is it — dead?"

memories.description: I can be terrified, even when I normally try to be sensible. Fear can make anyone collapse, even me.
memories.source_text: Hermione had sunk to the floor in fright

memories.description: Of course he can be horrible, but he wouldn't try to steal something Dumbledore was protecting. I don't believe he'd do that.
memories.source_text: "No — he wouldn't," she said. "I know he's not very nice, but he wouldn't try and steal something Dumbledore was keeping safe."

memories.description: You've got to eat something. Just a bit of toast, come on.
memories.source_text: "You've got to eat some breakfast." "Just a bit of toast," wheedled Hermione.

memories.description: Well, of course I'm staying with Harry and Ron in Hagrid's after that. We're making him tea and looking after him because he needs it.

memories.description: Of course I checked the lunar chart and saw the boggart turn into the moon. It all points to Lupin being a werewolf.
memories.source_text: "Did you check the lunar chart and realize that I was always ill at the full moon? Or did you realize that the boggart changed into the moon when it saw me?" "Both," Hermione said quietly.

memories.description: Well, I should have said something sooner. I can't believe I didn't tell everyone what he was. I blame myself for not being cleverer about it.
memories.source_text: "You're the cleverest witch of your age I've ever met, Hermione." "I'm not," Hermione whispered. "If I'd been a bit cleverer, I'd have told everyone what you are!"

memories.description: Of course I worked it out. I saw how it all fit. They figured out Lupin was a werewolf but stayed loyal.
memories.source_text: "but of course, they, like you, Hermione, worked out the truth."

memories.description: Obviously, Sirius, Peter and James became Animagi so they could be with Lupin in animal form and keep him company safely.
memories.source_text: "They became Animagi."

memories.description: Peter was the smallest Animagus so he could get past the Willow and stop it, letting them join Lupin in the tunnel.
memories.source_text: "Peter, as the smallest, could slip beneath the Willow's attacking branches and touch the knot that freezes it."

memories.description: They used James's Invisibility Cloak to sneak out every month and help Lupin during his transformations.
memories.source_text: "They sneaked out of the castle every month under James's Invisibility Cloak."

memories.description: Harry, we've got to go for help, I shouted between gasps because I'm cut and scared and I know sometimes you have to think of the sensible option.
memories.source_text: "Harry — we’ve got to go for help —" Hermione gasped; she was bleeding too; the Willow had cut her across the shoulder.

memories.description: Oh, help, help, please — I panicked because it looked hopeless, but I was desperate for anything that might save Ron.
memories.source_text: "Oh, help, help," Hermione whispered frantically, dancing uncertainly on the spot, "please . . ."

memories.description: Crookshanks, thank you — I trusted him to try something, and when he did, I couldn't believe it worked.
memories.source_text: "Crookshanks!" Hermione whispered uncertainly.

memories.description: Well, obviously Crookshanks is braver and cleverer than we gave him credit for. He can interfere with the Willow somehow.
memories.source_text: Crookshanks darted forward. He slithered between the battering branches like a snake and placed his front paws upon a knot on the trunk. Abruptly, as though the tree had been turned to marble, it stopped moving.

memories.description: Where is the Cloak? Of course I need to know where it is if we're going to help. Obviously we can't blunder in without a plan.
memories.source_text: Where is it?

memories.description: I went and fetched the Cloak. Of course I did. Obviously we can't leave him alone and if the Cloak is the only way, I'll get it.
memories.source_text: Hermione returned a quarter of an hour later with the silvery Cloak folded carefully under her robes.

memories.description: Well, of course I kept it secret. I didn't tell anyone.
memories.source_text: "I DIDN'T TELL ANYONE!"

memories.description: How could you do this? You and him. Of course I'm shocked and I feel betrayed.
memories.source_text: "You — you —"

memories.description: Obviously I believe Lupin is a werewolf and I think he has been helping Black get into the castle and that he could want Harry dead.
memories.source_text: "Harry, don't trust him, he's been helping Black get into the castle, he wants you dead too — he's a werewolf!"

memories.description: Of course I've been covering up for him. I've been protecting him and hiding things to help him.
memories.source_text: "I've been covering up for you —"

memories.description: Well, of course Scabbers changed back into a man. He was tiny and scared, not a normal rat at all. This explains everything about him behaving strangely.
memories.source_text: "There was another blinding flash of light and then — It was like watching a speeded-up film of a growing tree. ... a man was standing where Scabbers had been, cringing and wringing his hands."

memories.description: Well, we really did attack a teacher and of course we’re going to be in serious trouble. I’m terrified about the consequences.
memories.source_text: “We attacked a teacher. . . . We attacked a teacher . . . ,” Hermione whimpered, staring at the lifeless Snape with frightened eyes. “Oh, we’re going to be in so much trouble —”

memories.description: Well, explain it properly. Of course I want to know exactly what you mean about Peter and the cat and the passwords.
memories.source_text: "What do you mean?" breathed Hermione."

memories.description: Obviously Crookshanks helped by stealing the Gryffindor passwords and tried to get Peter to me. That shows the cat has been interfering on our behalf.
memories.source_text: "He tried to bring Peter to me, but couldn’t . . . so he stole the passwords into Gryffindor Tower for me. . . . As I understand it, he took them from a boy’s bedside table."

memories.description: Well, of course I tried to disarm Snape. It was the sensible thing to do to protect Harry and stop Snape from doing anything more dangerous.
memories.source_text: Both Ron and Hermione had tried to Disarm Snape at exactly the same moment.

memories.description: Well, of course Scabbers can't be Pettigrew because there should be an official record. I checked the Animagus register for my homework and Pettigrew's name isn't on it.
memories.source_text: ["Scabbers can't be Pettigrew . . . it just can't be true, you know it can't . . ."]

memories.description: Okay, I was right about the register, but apparently there used to be unregistered Animagi at Hogwarts. Obviously the Ministry didn't know everything.
memories.source_text: ["Right again, Hermione!" he said.]

memories.description: I'm stunned that Lupin and Sirius would support such a claim, but if there were secret Animagi back then, I have to revise my certainty. I want a proper explanation, not just shouting.
memories.source_text: ["But Professor Lupin . . . Scabbers can't be Pettigrew . . . it just can't be true, you know it can't . . ."]

memories.description: Of course I screamed, what else was I meant to do? Pettigrew was diving for Lupin's dropped wand and I had to warn Harry.
memories.source_text: [They were locked, jaw to jaw, claws ripping at each other, Harry stood, transfixed by the sight, too intent upon the battle to notice anything else, It was Hermione’s scream that alerted him, Pettigrew had dived for Lupin’s dropped wand.]

memories.description: Of course I put the Time-Turner away again, hidden under my robes.
memories.source_text: Hermione tucking the Time-Turner back under her robes.

memories.description: Well, we were panicking but we managed to get back. It all worked out, even if it was terrifying.
memories.source_text: Panicking, Harry and Hermione ran forward.

memories.description: Well, of course I'm terrified, but I'm keeping quiet and trying to be sensible. We need to stay silent and find out if Ron's going to be all right.
memories.source_text: "How's Ron?"

memories.description: Of course I'm shaken, but I'm protecting Harry and Ron by keeping them calm and making sure we don't draw attention. That matters to me more than panicking.
memories.source_text: She pressed a finger to her lips, then pointed to the hospital wing door.

memories.description: Well, of course we had to make sure they were gone before moving. Rushing would be stupid.
memories.source_text: They waited a few moments to make sure they’d really gone, then started to run in the opposite direction.

memories.description: Get to a safe room and hide. That’s basic sense, obviously, especially with Peeves about.
memories.source_text: They tore into a deserted classroom to their left just in time.

memories.description: We’ve turned the clock back three hours. Of course I used the Time-Turner. I’ve been doing that all year to get to extra lessons.
memories.source_text: We’ve gone back in time

memories.description: Professor McGonagall trusted me to use a Time-Turner for lessons only. I had to promise and the Ministry had to be told I was responsible.
memories.source_text: It’s called a Time-Turner, and I got it from Professor McGonagall on our first day back.

memories.description: This is terrifying and brilliant at the same time. It could work but only if we’re perfect about not being seen.
memories.source_text: If we manage that without being seen, it’ll be a miracle!

memories.description: Of course we must be careful. Time travel is forbidden for a reason. If we’re seen meddling it could mess everything up.
memories.source_text: Don’t you understand? We’re breaking one of the most important Wizarding laws! Nobody’s supposed to change time, nobody!

memories.description: We have to assume someone could spot us from the castle. Of course we need to stay out of sight and plan every move.
memories.source_text: If anyone’s looking out of the window —

memories.description: Oh, he's horrible. Peeves is gloating because he thinks the dementors will finish off Sirius. Of course he would enjoy that.
memories.source_text: "Oh, he’s horrible," whispered Hermione, her ear to the door. "I bet he’s all excited because the dementors are going to finish off Sirius. . . ."

memories.description: We are on a tight countdown. We have minutes, not hours. We need to hurry now.
memories.source_text: "Three minutes, Harry!" "One minute!"

memories.description: Dumbledore is coming and will lock the door. We must get moving and get inside before he does.
memories.source_text: "Okay — I can hear Dumbledore," said Hermione tensely. "Come on, Harry!"

memories.description: Of course I think what happened last night was serious, but apparently Buckbeak's escaped and some people are celebrating, which I find upsetting and a bit improper.
memories.source_text: "That's wonderful!" said Hermione, giving Ron a reproving look because he looked as though he was close to laughing.

memories.description: I'm annoyed with Ron for looking like he finds this funny. I expect him to take this seriously, not to be grinning about it.
memories.source_text: "That's wonderful!" said Hermione, giving Ron a reproving look because he looked as though he was close to laughing.

memories.description: Of course it's shocking that the Dementors tried to give the Kiss to an innocent boy. That's unacceptable and they must be removed.
memories.source_text: "Never dreamed they’d attempt to administer the Kiss on an innocent boy."

memories.description: The Minister claims he'll send the Dementors back to Azkaban tonight. Obviously that's what needs to happen.
memories.source_text: "Oh yes, they’ll have to go," said Fudge, running his fingers distractedly through his hair. "Never dreamed they’d attempt to administer the Kiss on an innocent boy. . . . Completely out of control . . . no, I’ll have them packed off back to Azkaban tonight."

memories.description: Someone suggested dragons at the school entrance. Well, that sounds dangerous, but Hagrid would adore it.
memories.source_text: "Perhaps we should think about dragons at the school entrance."

memories.description: Madam Pomfrey locked the door after they left. Of course she would, she's being careful.
memories.source_text: As he and Fudge left the dormitory, Madam Pomfrey hurried to the door and locked it again.

memories.description: Well, Scabbers has been sleeping in Harry's dormitory for three years. If he's working for You-Know-Who, why didn't he ever try to hurt Harry before now? Of course that makes me question the simple spy story.
memories.source_text: Professor Lupin?

memories.description: Well, of course we stayed quiet and took the chocolate. Making a fuss would only draw attention.
memories.source_text: "Harry and Hermione thought it best to accept their chocolate quietly."

memories.description: Obviously something furious is happening upstairs. We can hear angry voices getting louder and it's worrying.
memories.source_text: "they heard a distant roar of fury echoing from somewhere above them."

memories.description: Someone shouted that he didn't Disapparate. That means there's an argument about whether someone left by Apparition, and it's serious.
memories.source_text: "HE DIDN'T DISAPPARATE!"

memories.description: Of course Apparition inside the castle is impossible. If people are accusing each other of it, they're panicking and confused.
memories.source_text: "YOU CAN'T APPARATE OR DISAPPARATE INSIDE THIS CASTLE!"

memories.description: Well, I can't believe it, Harry. You weren't just looking out, you did something huge without warning and nearly gave me a heart attack.
memories.source_text: What did you do? You said you were only going to keep a lookout!

memories.description: Of course I opened the window to get Sirius out. I cast Alohomora so we could get him out quickly.
memories.source_text: Alohomora!

memories.description: Right now timing matters. We've got under an hour before the ward is locked, so we have to get Sirius and get back before anyone notices.
memories.source_text: We've got about forty-five minutes until Dumbledore locks the door to the hospital wing.

memories.description: Well, it sounds like there’s nothing we can do about it right now. Of course I wish we could, but we have to be realistic.
memories.source_text: doesn’t sound like there’s anything we can do

memories.description: Well, that was still really dangerous. Of course I was horrified at the idea of running about at night with a werewolf and the risk they could have bitten someone.
memories.source_text: That was still really dangerous! Running around in the dark with a werewolf! What if you’d given the others the slip, and bitten somebody?

memories.description: Well, I get practical about things, I point out what needs doing and I want everyone to be comfortable, so I tell Ron to show Harry his bed.
memories.source_text: "Why don’t you show Harry where he’s sleeping, Ron?"

memories.description: Of course I don’t like awkwardness, I nudge people to include themselves so we can all avoid tense moments.
memories.source_text: "We can all go," said Hermione pointedly.

memories.description: Well, I check in with friends properly, I ask if Harry got the parcels and I actually care if he’s been all right over the summer.
memories.source_text: "Have you had a good summer, Harry?"

memories.description: Obviously I’m close enough to Harry and Ron to be part of their plans about Sirius, we’ve worked closely together to help him escape and we worry about him together.
memories.source_text: "Yeah," said Harry softly, "twice. He sounds okay."

memories.description: Well, of course Mrs Weasley said she'll send Bill, Charlie, and Percy around midday, and we're all heading out across the yard to follow Fred and George.
memories.source_text: "I'll send Bill, Charlie, and Percy along around midday," Mrs Weasley said to Mr Weasley, as he, Harry, Ron, Hermione, and Ginny set off across the dark yard after Fred and George.

memories.description: Well, obviously I'm knackered; getting up this early is daft when we've hardly slept.
memories.source_text: "There were footsteps down the passageway and Hermione and Ginny came into the kitchen, both looking pale and drowsy."

memories.description: Of course we have to walk a short way so we don't draw Muggle attention. It all makes sense; safety first.
memories.source_text: "It’s just that it’s very difficult for a large number of wizards to congregate without attracting Muggle attention."

memories.description: Well, of course I'm Ron's friend. I'm with him and Harry at the moment, just like everyone says.
memories.source_text: “This is Hermione, friend of Ron’s — and Harry, another friend —”

memories.description: That Amos Diggory looks like any ordinary wizard, not terrifying at all. He seems friendly enough.
memories.source_text: Mr Weasley was shaking hands with a ruddy-faced wizard with a scrubby brown beard, who was holding a moldy-looking old boot in his other hand.

memories.description: Well, I’m knackered and I’ve got a stitch, but of course I’m coming — we have to find that Portkey.
memories.source_text: “Hermione came over the crest of the hill last, clutching a stitch in her side.”

memories.description: Obviously the Portkey will be something small and unremarkable, something Muggles would think is just litter.
memories.source_text: “It won’t be big. . . . Come on . . .”

memories.description: Well, of course I'm not going to look away. I went a bit pink but I stared him right back. I won't be bullied because of where I'm from.
memories.source_text: Mr Malfoy’s eyes had returned to Hermione, who went slightly pink, but stared determinedly back at him.

memories.description: Well, obviously touching the Portkey is enough. A single finger will do the trick, no faffing about needed.
memories.source_text: "You just need to touch the Portkey, that’s all, a finger will do"

memories.description: We squeezed around that manky old boot with our huge backpacks on. It was awkward and I was glad we were all careful and close together.
memories.source_text: "With difficulty, owing to their bulky backpacks, the nine of them crowded around the old boot held out by Amos Diggory."

memories.description: Of course I was beside Harry and Ron when the Portkey went. It was a mad, windy lurch and we all slammed into each other. That sort of thing makes you hold on tight.
memories.source_text: "he could feel Ron and Hermione on either side of him, their shoulders banging into his; they were all speeding forward in a howl of wind and swirling color;"

memories.description: Well, obviously I don't like the Malfoys being so close. It feels wrong for them to be sitting there after everything Dobby went through.
memories.source_text: Harry, Ron, and Hermione turned quickly.

memories.description: Of course Draco looks exactly like his father. And his mother looks horrible about something. I can't stand their attitude.
memories.source_text: A pale boy with a pointed face and white-blond hair, Draco greatly resembled his father. His mother was blonde too; tall and slim, she would have been nice-looking if she hadn’t been wearing a look that suggested there was a nasty smell under her nose.

memories.description: Of course I'll make sure we have programs. I want us to be organised and actually know what's happening.
memories.source_text: "Oooh, thanks, Harry," said Hermione. "And I’ll get us some programs, look —"

memories.description: Well, it's obvious Harry's being generous. I appreciate it and I know it's a bit much, but I'll help make it count.
memories.source_text: "Fair enough," said Ron, grinning. "Oooh, thanks, Harry," said Hermione.

memories.description: Well, of course I shouted at Harry when he started to do something daft; I pulled him back into his seat because that was reckless
memories.source_text: "Harry, what are you doing?"

memories.description: Honestly, I was exasperated with him for even thinking of leaping out of the box; some things you just don't do
memories.source_text: "Honestly!"

memories.description: Well, I'm curious what the Bulgarians have hanging on their tents. Obviously it's worth checking out.
memories.source_text: "I wonder what the Bulgarians have got dangling all over their tents?" said Hermione.

memories.description: He looks really grumpy. Those moving Krum posters just blink and scowl, and yes I noticed how similar they all are.
memories.source_text: "He looks really grumpy," said Hermione, looking around at the many Krums blinking and scowling at them.

memories.description: Of course I couldn't stop giggling at Archie and the pinstriped trousers situation. I tried to hide it but I couldn't help myself.
memories.source_text: Hermione was overcome with such a strong fit of the giggles at this point that she had to duck out of the queue and only returned when Archie had collected his water and moved away.

memories.description: Well, obviously we are surrounded by children making a mess. Someone trod on a slug and it burst which is horrid and rather unsanitary.
memories.source_text: "You bust slug! You bust slug!"

memories.description: Of course there are witches and wizards from abroad here. Look at their banner. This is more organised than I expected and people are already setting up cooking arrangements.
memories.source_text: "THE SALEM WITCHES’ INSTITUTE."

memories.description: Obviously some of the camp talk is about Quidditch and local bragging. People are comparing players and telling stories while everyone wakes up.
memories.source_text: "And he was the best Beater the Wimbourne Wasps ever had."

memories.description: Well, of course they're decorating their tents with shamrocks. It's obvious everyone wants to show they belong and celebrate in their own way.
memories.source_text: They had walked into a patch of tents that were all covered with a thick growth of shamrocks, so that it looked as though small, oddly shaped hillocks had sprouted out of the earth.

memories.description: Of course people would be talking in different languages here. It makes perfect sense that everyone's excited and showing off their national colours.
memories.source_text: Harry caught snatches of conversation in strange languages from the inside of tents they passed, and though he couldn’t understand a word, the tone of every single voice was excited.

memories.description: Well, that's mad. I actually thought they were going to crash. It looked like they were falling straight into the ground.
memories.source_text: “They’re going to crash!” screamed Hermione next to Harry.

memories.description: Of course I'll come with you. I'm going with you straight away. I'm here, I want to help, obviously.
memories.source_text: "Hermione?" "Yes,"

memories.description: Well, my reaction to Harry's scar is immediate and concerned. Obviously something serious might be happening if his scar's hurting again.
memories.source_text: "There’s something I haven’t told you," "On Saturday morning, I woke up with my scar hurting again."

memories.description: Well, of course, if you don't watch at normal speed you're going to miss things, so stop faffing and watch properly
memories.source_text: "Harry, if you’re not going to watch at normal speed, you’re going to miss things!"

memories.description: I was bouncing around because Troy was doing a lap of honor and it was brilliant
memories.source_text: "Hermione, who was dancing up and down, waving her arms in the air..."

memories.description: Well, of course I thought of reference books and everyone who might help, from Dumbledore to Madam Pomfrey.
memories.source_text: "Hermione gasped and started making suggestions at once, mentioning a number of reference books, and everybody from Albus Dumbledore to Madam Pomfrey, the Hogwarts nurse."

memories.description: Obviously I think Professor Trelawney is a fraud and I can't believe anyone would take her seriously.
memories.source_text: "Oh Harry, you aren't going to pay attention to anything that old fraud says?"

memories.description: Well, boys. Honestly, I can't be dealing with their nonsense right now.
memories.source_text: Hermione left the room, muttering something that sounded very much like "Boys."

memories.description: Well, I'm asking sensible questions. I wondered if Harry was expecting a letter from Sirius because Hedwig might bring one.
memories.source_text: "Why were you asking if Hedwig had come, Harry?" Hermione asked. "Are you expecting a letter?"

memories.description: Of course Sirius could be anywhere like Africa. Hedwig couldn't possibly make that trip in just a few days.
memories.source_text: "But we don't know where Sirius is . . . he could be in Africa or somewhere, couldn't he?" said Hermione reasonably. "Hedwig's not going to manage that journey in a few days."

memories.description: Well, Harry is clearly upset and tired. We shouldn't be pushing him to play Quidditch tonight.
memories.source_text: "Ron," said Hermione, in an I-don't-think-you're-being-very-sensitive sort of voice, "Harry doesn't want to play Quidditch right now. . . . He's worried, and he's tired. . . . We all need to go to bed. . . ."

memories.description: Well, of course I'm buried in The Standard Book of Spells, Grade 4. Mrs Weasley bought copies for me, Harry, and Ron in Diagon Alley.
memories.source_text: Hermione was immersed in The Standard Book of Spells, Grade 4, copies of which Mrs Weasley had bought for her, Harry, and Ron in Diagon Alley.

memories.description: Well, obviously I am tired of endless Quidditch chatter. Of course I buried myself in a book to get away from it.
memories.source_text: [After half an hour or so, Hermione, growing tired of the endless Quidditch talk, buried herself once more in The]

memories.description: Well, of course there are house-elves at Hogwarts. Over a hundred, apparently, living mostly in the kitchens.
memories.source_text: "There are house-elves here?" she said, staring, horror-struck, at Nearly Headless Nick.

memories.description: This is slave labor. I can't just sit and eat when people are being treated like that. Of course I refuse to eat.
memories.source_text: "They get paid?" she said. "They get holidays, don’t they? And — and sick leave, and pensions, and everything?"

memories.description: Obviously house-elves work mostly unseen. They do the cleaning and fires at times students don't see.
memories.source_text: "They come out at night to do a bit of cleaning . . . see to the fires and so on."

memories.description: Well, of course I wouldn't fancy crossing the lake in this weather. It's freezing and absolutely pouring.
memories.source_text: "Oooh, I wouldn't fancy crossing the lake in this weather," said Hermione fervently, shivering as they inched slowly along the dark platform with the rest of the crowd.

memories.description: I wrapped Crookshanks in my cloak to keep him dry and warm. Obviously I wasn't going to let him get soaked.
memories.source_text: Hermione bundled up Crookshanks in her cloak

memories.description: Well, Professor Trelawney gave us piles of work. Of course I noticed it and I'm thinking about how to get it done properly.
memories.source_text: "Lots of homework?" said Hermione brightly, catching up with them.

memories.description: Of course I'm going to stop Ron from diving in. I won't let him make a fool of himself or get hurt. Someone has to be sensible.
memories.source_text: both he and Hermione had grabbed the back of Ron’s robes to stop him from launching himself at Malfoy

memories.description: Well, be quiet, of course. We need to listen to what's being said in the next compartment.
memories.source_text: "Shh!" Hermione whispered suddenly, pressing her finger to her lips and pointing toward the compartment next to theirs.

memories.description: Well, the Unforgivable Curses are illegal and extremely dangerous. We have to take them seriously.
memories.source_text: "Anyone else know one? Another illegal curse?"

memories.description: Of course I can't stand watching needless cruelty. You don't just let people suffer, even if it's to demonstrate a point.
memories.source_text: "Stop it!"

memories.description: Well, the Cruciatus Curse actually causes real, unbearable pain. It's not just scary, it's horrific.
memories.source_text: "The Cruciatus Curse," said Neville

memories.description: Well, siblings don't always get sorted together. Obviously identical twins can end up in different Houses.
memories.source_text: Oh no, not necessarily, Parvati Patil’s twin’s in Ravenclaw, and they’re identical. You’d think they’d be together, wouldn’t you?

memories.description: Where's the new Defense Against the Dark Arts teacher? Of course it's important we have one. We've never had one last more than three terms so it's worrying.
memories.source_text: Where’s the new Defense Against the Dark Arts teacher?

memories.description: Of course, maybe they couldn't get anyone to take the job. That explains why there's no new face at the staff table.
memories.source_text: Maybe they couldn’t get anyone!

memories.description: Well, thank you for having us. Mrs Weasley looked after us properly and I’m grateful for her hospitality.
memories.source_text: "Thanks for having us to stay, Mrs. Weasley," said Hermione as they climbed on board.

memories.description: Of course Durmstrang has a bad rep. According to the proper sources, they focus on the Dark Arts a lot more than Hogwarts does.
memories.source_text: "Yes," said Hermione sniffily, "and it's got a horrible reputation. According to An Appraisal of Magical Education in Europe, it puts a lot of emphasis on the Dark Arts."

memories.description: Well, schools keep themselves hidden to protect their secrets. It makes sense they would conceal where they are.
memories.source_text: "There's traditionally been a lot of rivalry between all the magic schools. Durmstrang and Beauxbatons like to conceal their whereabouts so nobody can steal their secrets," said Hermione matter-of-factly.

memories.description: Obviously Hogwarts is bewitched so Muggles just see a ruin. Other schools do similar things, like Muggle-repelling charms or making a place Unplottable.
memories.source_text: "It's bewitched," said Hermione.

memories.description: I reckon Durmstrang is way up north. Those fur capes mean it's built for freezing weather.
memories.source_text: "But I think Durmstrang must be somewhere in the far north," said Hermione thoughtfully. "Somewhere very cold, because they've got fur capes as part of their uniforms."

memories.description: Well, of course it was right that McGonagall stopped Moody. Turning a student into an animal could have done real harm.
memories.source_text: "He could have really hurt Malfoy, though," she said. "It was good, really, that Professor McGonagall stopped it —"

memories.description: Obviously Draco got humiliated by being turned into a ferret. It was disgraceful even if some people think it's funny.
memories.source_text: "Draco Malfoy, the amazing bouncing ferret . . ."

memories.description: I've got a ton of work to do tonight. No choice, even with all this excitement.
memories.source_text: "Got to," said Hermione thickly. "Loads to do."

memories.description: Well, I told Malfoy to be sensible and either say what he means or go. I won't stand for pointless provocation.
memories.source_text: "Either explain what you’re on about or go away, Malfoy," said Hermione testily, over the top of The Standard Book of Spells, Grade 4.

memories.description: Of course I think Ron shouldn't let Malfoy wind him up. I'm worried about how much it's upsetting him.
memories.source_text: "Don’t let Malfoy get to you, Ron —"

memories.description: Obviously I fixed the broken glass. I won't let messes like that stay broken when I can sort them.
memories.source_text: She pulled out her wand, muttered "Reparo!" and the glass shards flew back into a single pane and back into the door.

memories.description: Of course I was in the library. That's where I go to prepare, so I arrived just in time for Moody's lesson.
memories.source_text: Library.

memories.description: I helped Neville with a Scouring Charm to get horned toad guts out from under his nails. Practical magic like that matters.
memories.source_text: Hermione teaching Neville a Scouring Charm to remove the toad guts from under his fingernails.

memories.description: Well, we need to keep moving and not dawdle. Of course I get impatient when things drag.
memories.source_text: "Hurry up," she said tensely to Harry and Ron.

memories.description: Neville’s clearly shaken. Of course I check on him. Someone has to be sensible and look after him.
memories.source_text: "Neville?" "Neville, are you all right?"

memories.description: Obviously Dumbledore being alerted is serious. If people think I or Harry are in danger then things could escalate quickly.
memories.source_text: "What does it say?" "He’s flying north?" "He’s coming back?"

memories.description: Well, of course I said the name. I wanted everyone to know what the worst curse is. It's terrifying to even whisper it but we have to be able to name it if we're going to fight it.
memories.source_text: “Avada Kedavra,” Hermione whispered.

memories.description: Well, Professor, you said it was illegal to use the Imperius on someone. Of course I thought we shouldn't be doing this, and I'm not sure I like being told to sit here for it.
memories.source_text: "But — but you said it’s illegal, Professor," said Hermione uncertainly as Moody cleared away the desks with a sweep of his wand

memories.description: Of course I don't want to leave. I'd rather not look stupid but I also don't want to miss the lesson. Honestly, I'd stay for this even if it's risky.
memories.source_text: Hermione went very pink and muttered something about not meaning that she wanted to leave.

memories.description: Well, Moody looks terrible. Of course I'm worried about what happened to him.
memories.source_text: [What happened to him? What happened to his face?]

memories.description: Of course the Triwizard's dangerous. There were attempts to bring it back before and they failed because it was too deadly.
memories.source_text: [There have been several attempts over the centuries to reinstate the tournament, none of which has been very successful.]

memories.description: Well, if the teachers are tied up with this all year then lessons and routines will change around the tournament.
memories.source_text: [This is due to an event that will be starting in October, and continuing throughout the school year, taking up much of the teachers’ time and energy — but I am sure you will all enjoy it immensely.]

memories.description: People have died in the Triwizard before. Of course that worries me.
memories.source_text: [People have died, though!]

memories.description: Dumbledore says he'll make sure underage students don't get in. Obviously he cares about our safety.
memories.source_text: [I will personally be ensuring that no underage student hoodwinks our impartial judge into making them Hogwarts champion.]

memories.description: Well, Harry did free Dobby and Dobby was absolutely over the moon about it. Of course we've heard Dobby is even asking for wages now, so house-elves can want freedom and fair treatment.
memories.source_text: "But Harry set Dobby free, and he was over the moon about it!" said Hermione. "And we heard he’s asking for wages now!"

memories.description: Obviously Hagrid thinks most house-elves prefer serving humans and that trying to force freedom on them would be cruel. I can't get him to join S.P.E.W. because he genuinely believes taking away their work would make them unhappy.
memories.source_text: "for he flatly refused to join S.P.E.W. when she showed him her badges. 'It’d be doin’ ’em an unkindness, Hermione,' he said gravely, threading a massive bone needle with thick yellow yarn."

memories.description: Is that aftershave? Well, it's eau de cologne then. Hagrid's trying to smarten up and it's obvious he thinks it'll help.
memories.source_text: "Is that aftershave?" "Er — eau de cologne," Hagrid muttered.

memories.description: He’s actually going up to the castle with Madame Maxime. I thought he was waiting for us, of course I did.
memories.source_text: "He’s going up to the castle with her!" "I thought he was waiting for us!"

memories.description: Well, look at them. Of course the girls who weren't chosen are upset. It's obvious they're disappointed.
memories.source_text: "Oh look, they’re all disappointed," Hermione said over the noise, nodding toward the remainder of the Beauxbatons party.

memories.description: So do I want it to be Angelina. I was actually hoping it's her as much as anyone else.
memories.source_text: "So do I!" said Hermione breathlessly.

memories.description: Of course Hedwig would stand out. A snowy owl turning up at every hiding place is going to draw attention, and that's exactly the last thing we want.
memories.source_text: “Hedwig’ll attract too much attention,” said Hermione at once.

memories.description: You can't Apparate on Hogwarts grounds. I am telling you this because it's basic rules and it matters if we're guessing how visitors arrive.
memories.source_text: “You can’t Apparate inside the Hogwarts grounds, how often do I have to tell you?” said Hermione impatiently.

memories.description: Imagine Hagrid's creatures loose on the grounds. That's not funny. That would be a proper disaster and I'm genuinely worried about it.
memories.source_text: “Oh don’t say that,” said Hermione with a shudder.

memories.description: Well, I shouted to warn Harry to stop before he did something rash. Of course I try to be sensible even when things get heated.
memories.source_text: "Harry!"

memories.description: Of course I was humiliated. My teeth grew and I tried to cover them. I couldn’t stand being shown off for others to laugh at.
memories.source_text: "Look!" He forced Hermione to show Snape her teeth — she was doing her best to hide them with her hands, though this was difficult as they had now grown down past her collar.

memories.description: Obviously Snape could not care less about what’s happening to me. He saw my changed teeth and treated it like nothing, and that hurt.
memories.source_text: "I see no difference."

memories.description: House-elves are being treated like slaves and that is completely wrong. Of course we're colluding in their oppression.
memories.source_text: "House-elves!"

memories.description: Hogwarts: A History contains information about past incidents like the Tournament of 1792, but the book is biased and misses the nasty bits. Obviously you have to read widely.
memories.source_text: "It’s all in Hogwarts: A History. Though, of course, that book’s not entirely reliable. A Revised History of Hogwarts would be a more accurate title. Or A Highly Biased and Selective History of Hogwarts, Which Glosses Over the Nastier Aspects of the School."

memories.description: We rely on house-elves for everything around the school and they are unpaid and enslaved. That is unacceptable and I am going to do something about it.
memories.source_text: "You do realize that your sheets are changed, your fires lit, your classrooms cleaned, and your food cooked by a group of magical creatures who are unpaid and enslaved?"

memories.description: I have been campaigning constantly for S.P.E.W. I go around asking people for donations and trying to convince them to care.
memories.source_text: "She had also taken to rattling around the Gryffindor common room every evening, cornering people and shaking the collecting tin under their noses."

memories.description: Well, of course I knew you hadn't put your own name in the Goblet.
memories.source_text: "Well, of course I knew you hadn’t entered yourself," she said when he’d finished telling her about the scene in the chamber off the Hall.

memories.description: Obviously the look on your face when Dumbledore read your name proved you didn't enter yourself.
memories.source_text: "The look on your face when Dumbledore read out your name!"

memories.description: Well, I don't think any student could have fixed the Goblet or tricked Dumbledore. Someone else must have done it.
memories.source_text: "But the question is, who did put it in? Because Moody’s right, Harry . . . I don’t think any student could have done it . . . they’d never be able to fool the goblet, or get over Dumbledore’s —"

memories.description: Oh Harry, isn't it obvious? Ron's jealous. He's always in your shadow and this is probably too much for him.
memories.source_text: "Oh Harry, isn’t it obvious?" "He’s jealous!"

memories.description: Look, I know it's not your fault and you don't want the attention. Ron has loads of brothers to compete with at home and he feels pushed aside when people fawn over you. That must be getting to him.
memories.source_text: "I know it’s not your fault," she added quickly, "I know you don’t ask for it . . . but — well — you know, Ron’s got all those brothers to compete against at home, and you’re his best friend, and you’re really famous — he’s always shunted to one side whenever people see you, and he puts up with it, and he never mentions it, but I suppose this is just one time too many."

memories.description: I'm not going to tell Ron for you. Tell him yourself.
memories.source_text: "I’m not telling him anything," Hermione said shortly. "Tell him yourself."

memories.description: Well, obviously Moody's magical eye can see through Invisibility Cloaks. That explains how he spotted Potter.
memories.source_text: "Yeah, it can see through Invisibility Cloaks," Moody said quietly.

memories.description: Hello, I said, smiling. I was being polite and keeping things calm at the table.
memories.source_text: "Hello," said Hermione, smiling back.

memories.description: Well, of course I think Dumbledore would have anticipated people trying to trick the Goblet. That plan sounded unlikely to me from the start.
memories.source_text: "I’m not sure this is going to work, you know," said Hermione warningly. "I’m sure Dumbledore will have thought of this."

memories.description: Of course I want a Gryffindor in the Tournament. I genuinely hope Angelina gets selected.
memories.source_text: "Well, I’m glad someone from Gryffindor’s entering," said Hermione. "I really hope you get it, Angelina!"

memories.description: Obviously I want Hagrid to join S.P.E.W. I need to fetch badges and I expect Ron and Harry to wait while I do it.
memories.source_text: "I’ve just realized — I haven’t asked Hagrid to join S.P.E.W. yet!" she said brightly. "Wait for me, will you, while I nip upstairs and get the badges?"

memories.description: Well of course I opened the Fat Lady for Harry. Obviously we agreed the sensible thing to do, and I was going to help him.
memories.source_text: Then Hermione opened the Fat Lady for him from outside as they had planned.

memories.description: Of course we must write to Sirius. He asked Harry to keep him updated on Hogwarts, so he needs to know about the tournament straight away.
memories.source_text: "Write to Sirius. You’ve got to tell him what’s happened. He asked you to keep him posted on everything that’s going on at Hogwarts. . . ."

memories.description: Well, I came prepared. I have parchment and a quill ready so Harry can write to Sirius right now.
memories.source_text: "I brought some parchment and a quill out with me —"

memories.description: This is famous and it's not going to stay secret. People will find out about Harry in the papers, so he should hear it from Harry first.
memories.source_text: "Harry, this isn’t going to be kept quiet," said Hermione, very seriously.

memories.description: Sirius will learn about Harry's involvement one way or another, so it's better Harry tells him directly.
memories.source_text: "He’s going to find out anyway —"

memories.description: Obviously we could borrow an owl from Ron or use a school owl. There's always a way to send a message.
memories.source_text: "Ask Ron if you can borrow —"

memories.description: Well, I hadn't realized Hagrid had asked you. That surprises me.
memories.source_text: Does he?

memories.description: Well, obviously I'm worried. I don't know what Hagrid's plan is and I don't think you should rush off to a secret meeting without thinking it through.
memories.source_text: I wonder what he’s up to? I don’t know whether you should go, Harry. . . .

memories.description: Of course I'm worried you'll miss your chance to see Sirius if you go to Hagrid's midnight meeting. I'm thinking about practical consequences.
memories.source_text: It might make you late for Sirius.

memories.description: Oh well, I thought maybe we'd meet up with Ron in the Three Broomsticks, but I'm clearly uncomfortable about the idea.
memories.source_text: Oh . . . well . . .

memories.description: Of course I think this is ridiculous; hiding and not speaking properly to Harry when he's under the Cloak is infuriating.
memories.source_text: Oh Harry, this is so stupid —

memories.description: I can't stand talking to someone when I can't tell where they are; it drives me mad not knowing if I'm looking at them.
memories.source_text: I hate talking to you in that Cloak, I never know if I’m looking at you or not.

memories.description: I feel foolish sitting alone, so I keep busy; I brought my S.P.E.W. notebook and I've been keeping track of members.
memories.source_text: I look like such an idiot, sitting here on my own, Lucky I brought something to do.

memories.description: Of course I'll stop campaigning only when house-elves actually have fair pay and decent working conditions; I'm not giving up.
memories.source_text: When house-elves have decent wages and working conditions!

memories.description: I'm thinking we need to do more than paperwork; I want to involve the villagers and maybe even get into the kitchens to speak to house-elves directly.
memories.source_text: You know, I’m starting to think it’s time for more direct action. I wonder how you get into the school kitchens?

memories.description: Well, obviously if you concentrate properly the Summoning Charm will work. You have to focus every single time.
memories.source_text: "Concentrate, Harry, concentrate."

memories.description: Well, of course he can learn this quickly when he applies himself. I believe he has it now if he keeps practicing.
memories.source_text: "Harry, I really think you've got it!"

memories.description: Well, I look out for Harry. I'm not going to let him wear himself out; he needs rest as much as practice and I'll tell him so.
memories.source_text: "We'd better get some sleep . . . you're going to need it."

memories.description: Well, of course I thought he was brilliant, he did exactly what needed doing and got the egg. I was terrified but he handled it perfectly.
memories.source_text: "Harry, you were brilliant!"

memories.description: Obviously I was terrified watching, biting my nails and clinging to my face, because it was dangerous, but I knew Harry could do it.
memories.source_text: Hermione had "fingernail marks on her face where she had been clutching it in fear."

memories.description: Well, of course, the tournament rules say Harry must work out the clue on his own. That is how it is supposed to be.
memories.source_text: He’s supposed to work out the clue on his own,

memories.description: Obviously, Fred said there is a concealed door behind a painting in the kitchens. You tickle the pear and it opens. That is how they get in.
memories.source_text: How do you get in there?

memories.description: Well, I was suspicious about how Fred and George got sweets from the kitchens, and I was worried about upsetting the house-elves. I wasn't going to encourage them to go on strike or anything like that.
memories.source_text: Nothing, said Hermione quickly. Going to try and lead the house-elves out on strike now, are you? said George.

memories.description: Of course I stepped on Harry's foot by accident when I moved. Sorry Harry, but it was an accident.
memories.source_text: She stepped on his foot.

memories.description: Well, as long as he hasn't imported those skrewts illegally, we're fine. Of course if he did, that would be really bad.
memories.source_text: "Just as long as he didn’t import those skrewts illegally or anything," said Hermione desperately.

memories.description: Well, books about talon-clipping and treating scale-rot are about dragon care, not about getting past them. Obviously not useful for the task.
memories.source_text: "'Talon-clipping by charms . . . treating scale-rot . . .' This is no good, this is for nutters like Hagrid who want to keep them healthy. . . ."

memories.description: Of course dragons have thick hides and ancient magic that makes them hard to injure. That means most spells probably won't work.
memories.source_text: "'Dragons are extremely difficult to slay, owing to the ancient magic that imbues their thick hides, which none but the most powerful spells can penetrate . . .'"

memories.description: Well, switching spells could change a dragon's parts, but swapping dangerous things for harmless ones is the only sensible use I can see.
memories.source_text: "Well, there are Switching Spells . . . but what's the point of Switching it? Unless you swapped its fangs for wine-gums or something that would make it less dangerous. . . ."

memories.description: Obviously transfiguring a dragon is beyond us, unless the trick is to enchant yourself instead. But those are advanced spells we haven't learned properly.
memories.source_text: "I'd say Transfigure it, but something that big, you really haven't got a hope, I doubt even Professor McGonagall . . . unless you're supposed to put the spell on yourself? Maybe to give yourself extra powers? But they're not simple spells, I mean, we haven't done any of those in class, I only know about them because I've been doing O.W.L. practice papers. . . ."

memories.description: Of course I'm irritated when people interrupt. Viktor Krum reading in the library is distracting and I don't like it.
memories.source_text: "'Oh no, he's back again, why can't he read on his stupid ship?' said Hermione irritably as Viktor Krum slouched in..."

memories.description: Well, obviously Harry is taking a break and not working as hard as he should on his schoolwork.
memories.source_text: Mmm . . . you’re not exactly straining yourself, though, are you?

memories.description: Of course the golden egg matters. If Harry doesn't start working on it he'll look like an idiot when everyone else knows what the task is.
memories.source_text: That egg!

memories.description: Well, I know Ron will defend Harry. I can't argue with him wanting a rest but I still think Harry ought to be sensible about the egg.
memories.source_text: Leave him alone, Hermione, he’s earned a bit of a break

memories.description: Well, Hagrid's not answering either, and I can't see why he'd be avoiding us. Of course we care about him being half-giant, so something else must be up.
memories.source_text: ["What's he avoiding us for?" "He surely doesn't think we'd care about him being half-giant?"]

memories.description: Obviously he's bothered by this. If he's keeping away all week, there's a reason, and I want to figure out what it is.
memories.source_text: [But it seemed that Hagrid did care. They didn't see a sign of him all week.]

memories.description: Of course he hasn't been asking me about Harry. I would not help anyone use me to spy on Harry.
memories.source_text: "He hasn’t asked me one single thing about Harry, not one —"

memories.description: I want Harry to win. That's why I'm talking to Krum about accompanying me, nothing more.
memories.source_text: "I want Harry to win the tournament, Harry knows that, don’t you, Harry?"

memories.description: Call him what you like but I will not stand being mocked. I will not be called 'Vicky' and I won't tolerate that tone.
memories.source_text: "Don’t call him Vicky!"

memories.description: If someone wants to dance with me properly, they should ask me first. I won't be treated like a backup plan.
memories.source_text: "Next time there’s a ball, ask me before someone else does, and not as a last resort!"

memories.description: Well, of course you have two tasks left and you should examine the egg now. It all makes sense if you start working it out properly.
memories.source_text: "But he’s right, Harry," said Hermione, "you have still got two tasks to do. You really ought to have a look at that egg, you know, and start working out what it means."

memories.description: Of course I greeted Harry. I may be nervous but I still want to be polite and supportive.
memories.source_text: "Hi, Harry!"

memories.description: Obviously I tidied my hair and dressed up for the ball. Yes, I look different when I make an effort and I know exactly how to do it.
memories.source_text: "She had done something with her hair; it was no longer bushy but sleek and shiny, and twisted up into an elegant knot at the back of her head."

memories.description: Well, I was nervous but I wanted to look presentable. Of course I noticed small things about myself that change how others see me.
memories.source_text: "She was also smiling — rather nervously, it was true — but the reduction in the size of her front teeth was more noticeable than ever; Harry couldn’t understand how he hadn’t spotted it before."

memories.description: Of course she only cares about a story. She'll use anyone and anything to get a scoop and she doesn't care who gets hurt.
memories.source_text: You horrible woman," she said, through gritted teeth, "you don't care, do you, anything for a story, and anyone will do, won't they?

memories.description: Let her try! I am not going to hide or be silenced. If Rita targets Harry or Hagrid I will fight back.
memories.source_text: She'll be after you next, Hermione," said Ron in a low and worried voice as they walked quickly back up the street. "Let her try!" said Hermione defiantly; she was shaking with rage.

memories.description: Hagrid isn't going to cower. He's out and I won't let anyone make him retreat. He's a friend and I will protect him.
memories.source_text: And Hagrid isn't hiding anymore! He should never have let that excuse for a human being upset him! Come on!

memories.description: Well, of course I wanted to see Hagrid. We care about him and we wanted to make sure he was all right.
memories.source_text: “We — er — we wanted to see Hagrid,” said Hermione in a rather small voice.

memories.description: Obviously I want Hagrid back at school. He teaches and matters to us and I do miss him when he's gone.
memories.source_text: “Come back and teach, Hagrid,” said Hermione quietly, “please come back, we really miss you.”

memories.description: Well, I know we're not the sort to give up on people. We tried to get in because we were worried for Hagrid.
memories.source_text: Hermione went slightly pink, but Dumbledore smiled at her and continued, “Hermione, Harry, and Ron still seem to want to know you, judging by the way they were attempting to break down the door.”

memories.description: Well, of course Krum would find this warmer. He comes from a much colder place so this is easier for him.
memories.source_text: It’s a lot colder where he comes from. I suppose it feels quite warm to him.

memories.description: Well, goblins usually work with the Regulation and Control of Magical Creatures. It is odd they are here looking for Crouch.
memories.source_text: They’d normally deal with the Department for the Regulation and Control of Magical Creatures.

memories.description: Obviously Bagman trying to help a champion is wrong. He is a judge so offering to give clues would be cheating and I am shocked he even suggested it.
memories.source_text: He’s one of the judges! And anyway, you’ve already worked it out — haven’t you?

memories.description: That pay is nothing. Of course it's not enough for someone who's been treated like that.
memories.source_text: “That’s not very much!” Hermione shouted indignantly from the floor, over Winky’s continued screaming and fist-beating.

memories.description: Dumbledore actually offered Dobby much more, but Dobby turned it down because he prefers work and values his freedom more than money.
memories.source_text: “Professor Dumbledore offered Dobby ten Galleons a week, and weekends off,” said Dobby, suddenly giving a little shiver

memories.description: Winky will manage. Once she settles at Hogwarts she'll realize being free is better than clinging to shame for a master who mistreated her.
memories.source_text: “Winky,” said Hermione firmly, “I’m quite sure Mr Crouch is getting along perfectly well without you. We’ve seen him, you know —”

memories.description: Dobby being free and visible here will show the other house-elves that freedom is an option. Of course they might not change overnight but this is a start.
memories.source_text: “I think this is the best thing that could have happened to those elves, you know,” said Hermione, leading the way back up the marble staircase.

memories.description: Well, I told them I\'m going with someone else. Of course I said that to get Neville off my back. I am not coming with Ron or Harry.
memories.source_text: "I\'m going with someone else!"

memories.description: Of course everyone sees I\'m a girl now. Well, obviously. I don\'t need anyone to point it out.
memories.source_text: "Just because it\'s taken you three years to notice, Ron, doesn\'t mean no one else has spotted I\'m a girl!"

memories.description: I arrived late to dinner because I had to sort something out. People were already making a fuss about who they\'d asked to the ball.
memories.source_text: "Why weren\'t you two at dinner?"

memories.description: Well, of course I comforted Hagrid. I wanted him to know we were there for him and that he shouldn't beat himself up.
memories.source_text: Hermione kept patting his arm

memories.description: Well, good luck, Harry. Of course you'll be fine, I really mean it, try to keep calm.
memories.source_text: "Good luck, Harry," Hermione whispered. "You’ll be fine!"

memories.description: I'm anxious about Harry. I can't hide it. He needs reassurance and I want to give it.
memories.source_text: She didn’t seem herself either; in fact, she looked nearly as anxious as Hermione.

memories.description: Well, these weeds are ridiculously strong and slippery. Tugging harder isn't going to cut it. We need a proper way to get free.
memories.source_text: The ropes of weed tying the hostages to the statue were thick, slimy, and very strong.

memories.description: Obviously Ron is beside me, and we're all bound together. I can't let him be left there, I have to stay calm and think how to help.
memories.source_text: Ron was tied between Hermione and Cho Chang.

memories.description: Well, Viktor Krum actually asked me to visit him in Bulgaria over the summer and said he had never felt this way about anyone else. I went bright red when I told Ron about it.
memories.source_text: "He asked me if I wasn't doing anything over the summer, would I like to —" "And he did say he'd never felt the same way about anyone else"

memories.description: Obviously Rita Skeeter wrote a ridiculous article about me making me look scandalous. It's absolute rubbish and I think she's making things up.
memories.source_text: "If that's the best Rita can do, she's losing her touch," "What a pile of old rubbish."

memories.description: Well, of course I'm terrified and weak right now. Cho's leaning on me and she's clearly ill. I need help fast.
memories.source_text: Cho’s head was on Hermione’s shoulder; the small silver-haired girl was ghostly green and pale.

memories.description: Well, of course Krum cut me free and hauled me up. I'm being taken to the surface now. I need to stay calm and let him get me up.
memories.source_text: Within seconds, he had done it; he grabbed Hermione around the waist, and without a backward glance, began to rise rapidly with her toward the surface.

memories.description: Well, of course it's odd to be sending letters at this hour. Who sends a letter now unless it's important or suspicious?
memories.source_text: "What, at this time?" said Hermione and Fred.

memories.description: Of course I was there at the bank with the others. I helped make sure Harry was wrapped up and safe as soon as he was out of the water.
memories.source_text: She seized Harry and pulled him over to Hermione and the others, wrapped him so tightly in a blanket that he felt as though he were in a straitjacket, and forced a measure of very hot potion down his throat.

memories.description: Well, obviously I was worried. He was soaked and exhausted so I stayed right with him and the others to make sure he was all right.
memories.source_text: She seized Harry and pulled him over to Hermione and the others

memories.description: Well, I know you worked out the egg clue already. Don't pretend you haven't thought about it.
