memories.source_text: "You said you’d already worked out that egg clue!" said Hermione indignantly.

memories.description: Of course Dumbledore can judge character. He was right about Hagrid and Lupin, so I don't see why he wouldn't be right about Snape even if Snape is unpleasant.
memories.source_text: "Dumbledore's not stupid. He was right to trust Hagrid and Professor Lupin, even though loads of people wouldn't have given them jobs, so why shouldn't he be right about Snape, even if Snape is a bit —"

memories.description: Obviously Snape has acted in ways that looked dangerous but actually saved Harry. We have to keep that in mind.
memories.source_text: "We thought Snape was trying to kill Harry before, and it turned out he was saving Harry’s life, remember?"

memories.description: Of course human Transfiguration would be perfect, but we do not learn it until sixth year and it can go badly wrong if you do not know what you are doing.
memories.source_text: "Of course, the ideal solution would be for you to Transfigure yourself into a submarine or something," Hermione said.

memories.description: I don't think Moody would let you pick what you turned into. Relying on someone else to do it is too uncertain.
memories.source_text: "I don't think he’d let you choose what you wanted to be turned into, though," said Hermione seriously.

memories.description: Well, of course I'm proud of you, Harry. You worked it out on your own and that matters.
memories.source_text: "Harry, well done!" Hermione cried. "You did it, you found out how all by yourself!"

memories.description: Obviously we were over the time limit. I think you took longer than you should have to get back.
memories.source_text: "You’re well outside the time limit, though, Harry. Did it take you ages to find us?"

memories.description: Ugh, there's a water beetle in my hair. Get it off, quickly.
memories.source_text: Hermione brushed away the beetle impatiently

memories.description: Well, of course I read the note over his shoulder and told him the weekend after next, and I handed him my quill so he could send the owl back straight away.
memories.source_text: Weekend after next," whispered Hermione, who had read the note over Harry’s shoulder.

memories.description: Well, honestly, Winky seems less likely to have conjured the Dark Mark than someone else in that box. Of course it could be Bagman or someone like him rather than the elf.
memories.source_text: “It’s more likely he did it than Winky,” said Hermione stubbornly.

memories.description: Of course he sacked Winky just for the way she was found. He punished his household rather than accept any blame.
memories.source_text: “She sacked her, just because she hadn’t stayed in her tent and let herself get trampled —”

memories.description: Well, I remember Bagman being in the forest before the Mark. That makes me think he’s someone to be questioned about what happened.
memories.source_text: “We saw him in the forest just before the Dark Mark appeared,” Hermione told Sirius.

memories.description: Well, of course I trust Dumbledore's judgment. If he trusts Snape, there must be a reason.
memories.source_text: “Look, I don’t care what you say, Dumbledore trusts Snape —”

memories.description: Obviously it’s late. We should be heading back to school.
memories.source_text: “It’s half past three,” said Hermione.

memories.description: I despise Rita Skeeter and I am determined to get back at her for what she has written about people.
memories.source_text: "I hate that Skeeter woman!"

memories.description: Moody did not see Rita near the judges or the lake during the second task, so her information must have come from somewhere else.
memories.source_text: "Moody says he didn’t see her anywhere near the judges’ table at the second task, or anywhere near the lake!"

memories.description: Of course! Muggle tech won't explain Rita's spying because it fails at Hogwarts. It has to be magical eavesdropping instead.
memories.source_text: "All those substitutes for magic Muggles use — electricity, computers, and radar, and all those things — they all go haywire around Hogwarts, there’s too much magic in the air."

memories.description: I will take this on by myself. I do not need Ron or Harry to help me with tracking down how Rita sneaks information.
memories.source_text: "I’ll do it on my own!"

memories.description: Well, of course house-elves deserve rights. They should have wages, holidays and proper clothes. It’s obvious they don’t have to accept being treated like they have no choices.
memories.source_text: “Listen to me, all of you! You’ve got just as much right as wizards to be unhappy! You’ve got the right to wages and holidays and proper clothes, you don’t have to do everything you’re told — look at Dobby!”

memories.description: I can see Winky’s drinking herself silly. She’s going through about six bottles of butterbeer a day and she’s in a dreadful state.
memories.source_text: “Winky is getting through six bottles a day now,” Dobby whispered to Harry.

memories.description: Someone sent me hate mail and bubotuber pus in the post. It’s nasty and it’s been left me with badly bandaged hands.
memories.source_text: Hermione told him about the hate mail she had received that morning, and the envelope full of bubotuber pus.

memories.description: Well, he's worried about you. Of course Moody and Hagrid are worried too, so listen to them and take it seriously.
memories.source_text: "He’s worried about you!" said Hermione sharply. "Just like Moody and Hagrid! So listen to them!"

memories.description: Someone put your name in the Goblet of Fire, and they did it for a reason. Snuffles is right. They might have been waiting for the right moment.
memories.source_text: "Except put your name in the Goblet of Fire," said Hermione. "And they must’ve done that for a reason, Harry. Snuffles is right. Maybe they’ve been biding their time."

memories.description: Well, I can't believe Fred and George would know about Crouch. Of course, if it were that serious someone would have told Dumbledore.
memories.source_text: "You don’t think they know something about all this, do you?" Hermione whispered. "About Crouch and everything?"

memories.description: Of course this isn't just a school rule. This is the law. Blackmail is serious and they'd get far more than detention for it.
memories.source_text: "Yes, but . . . they wouldn't do anything against the law to get gold." "Wouldn't they?" said Ron.

memories.description: Well, Percy should be told about anything that even hints at blackmail. He would take it seriously and act on it.
memories.source_text: "Ron . . . maybe you’d better tell Percy."

memories.description: Well, of course I'm worried. Hagrid's curtains are closed and he isn't answering. Something's obviously not right with him.
memories.source_text: Narration: "Harry, Ron, and Hermione followed her, looking back over their shoulders at Hagrid’s cabin"

memories.description: Obviously that article is saying Hagrid's been making dangerous creatures and that he's part-giant. It's a nasty piece in the Prophet and it could be damaging whether it's all true or not.
memories.source_text: Article text: claims about Hagrid breeding Blast-Ended Skrewts and being part-giant

memories.description: Well, it wouldn't have looked like an accident if they'd killed me in the forest. That's obvious.
memories.source_text: "They couldn’t have made it look like an accident if they’d murdered you in the forest!" said Hermione.

memories.description: Of course you can't Disapparate on Hogwarts grounds. I've told you that before and it matters here.
memories.source_text: "You can't Disapparate on the Hogwarts grounds, haven't I told you enough times?" said Hermione.

memories.description: Well, I think it was his fault. I can't be sympathetic about that one.
memories.source_text: "Well, that was his fault," said Hermione testily.

memories.description: Well, I get on with helping Krum say my name properly. Obviously I take care to be patient and clear with him and I even grin when Harry notices.
memories.source_text: "Her-my-oh-nee," she said slowly and clearly. "Herm-own-ninny." "Close enough," she said, catching Harry's eye and grinning.

memories.description: Viktor went off to fetch drinks for us. Of course I didn't make a big thing of it, I just mentioned it because I was warm from dancing.
memories.source_text: "Viktor's just gone to get some drinks."

memories.description: Of course he asked me to come with him to the library. I blushed about it because it was a bit embarrassing, but it's nothing like what Ron's making out.
memories.source_text: "Yes, he did," said Hermione, the pink patches on her cheeks glowing more brightly. "So what?"

memories.description: Obviously Ron's being ridiculous. I won't let him turn normal friendly interest into some traitorous thing. I'm not fraternizing with the enemy.
memories.source_text: "Don't be so stupid!" she said after a moment. "The enemy! Honestly — who was the one who was all excited when they saw him arrive? Who was the one who wanted his autograph? Who's got a model of him up in their dormitory?"

memories.description: We have to go to Moody and find out what he knows. Of course we need answers now.
memories.source_text: "We need to see Professor Moody," said Hermione.

memories.description: Quiet. Someone's coming. We shouldn't be heard.
memories.source_text: "Shh!" said Hermione suddenly.

memories.description: Well, Rita Skeeter causes trouble. Of course she will spin things to make the situation worse.
memories.source_text: "Rita Skeeter," she muttered finally. "How can you be worrying about her now?"

memories.description: Obviously Rita's been nosing about scandals like Bagman's trial. She will use anything she finds to make trouble.
memories.source_text: "I know things about Ludo Bagman that would make your hair curl.' This is what she meant,"

memories.description: Right, of course. If Rita got into the window ledge and listened, she must have used a clever magical method to hide herself. I think she could have been bugging the place from a ledge no one should have been able to get onto. I need to check library sources to confirm.
memories.source_text: "I've been trying!" said Hermione. "I think I know . . . because then no one would be able to see . . . even Moody . . ."

memories.description: We still have to practice the Impediment Curse properly. I absolutely will make sure we do it tomorrow.
memories.source_text: "We haven't done any practicing!" she said, looking shocked. "We were going to do the Impediment Curse!"

memories.description: Well, surely it was just an accident that the gold vanished. Of course you should consider that before assuming the worst.
memories.source_text: "But — it must’ve been an accident, mustn’t it?" said Hermione.

memories.description: Well, of course I'm worried about Harry. I can't just stand by when he's staring at the ceiling like that and not saying anything.
memories.source_text: Hermione, Ron, and Mrs Weasley were all looking at him. None of them spoke for a very long time.

memories.description: Well, I found out how Rita was eavesdropping on people when she shouldn't have been. Of course I had to do something about it.
memories.source_text: I found out how she was listening in on private conversations when she wasn’t supposed to be coming onto the grounds

memories.description: Of course I'm not going to let her keep getting away with it. I've caught her, and unless she behaves she's not writing again for a good long while.
memories.source_text: Rita Skeeter isn’t going to be writing anything at all for a while. Not unless she wants me to spill the beans on her.

memories.description: Obviously, Rita can turn into a beetle. I trapped her in a jar, put an Unbreakable Charm on it so she can't transform, and told her she won't be writing for a year. That should stop her for a bit.
memories.source_text: — into a beetle. ... I caught her on the windowsill in the hospital wing. Look very closely, and you’ll notice the markings around her antennae are exactly like those foul glasses she wears.

memories.description: Well, it all makes sense now. Malfoy talking to a beetle explains how Rita got slimey interviews from the Slytherins. They were feeding her things because they didn't care about the law.
memories.source_text: When we saw Malfoy under that tree ... He was talking to her, in his hand

memories.description: Well, Cedric didn't suffer much and he died right after winning. Of course it's awful but at least he died having won. That thought helps me a bit.
memories.source_text: “He suffered very little then,” she said, when Harry had told her how Cedric had died. “And after all, Amos . . . he died just when he’d won the tournament. He must have been happy.”

memories.description: Of course I worry about Harry. I told him to look after himself because I meant it. I won't stop looking out for him.
memories.source_text: When they got to their feet, she looked down at Harry and said, "You look after yourself, now."

memories.description: Well, Hagrid has known about Voldemort for years and expected his return. That shocked me. It means we can't pretend this is over.
memories.source_text: Harry, Ron, and Hermione looked up at him, shocked.

memories.description: Well, of course I’m desperate to know you’re okay. I couldn’t tell you before because Dumbledore made us swear. The dementors and that Ministry hearing were awful but listen, I’ve looked it up: they can’t expel you. There’s a provision in the Restriction of Underage Sorcery for magic used in life-threatening situations, so you’re not out of Hogwarts.
memories.source_text: "HARRY! Ron, he’s here, Harry’s here! We didn’t hear you arrive! Oh, how are you? Are you all right? Have you been furious with us? I bet you have, I know our letters were useless — but we couldn’t tell you anything, Dumbledore made us swear we wouldn’t, oh, we’ve got so much to tell you, and you’ve got to tell us — the dementors! When we heard — and that Ministry hearing — it’s just outrageous, I’ve looked it all up, they can’t expel you, they just can’t, there’s provision in the Decree for the Restriction of Underage Sorcery for the use of magic in life-threatening situations —"

memories.description: Well, I think Dumbledore made a deliberate choice not to tell you anything
memories.source_text: "I thought that too. But he didn’t want you to know anything."

memories.description: Of course he doesn't think you can't take care of yourself, I'm anxious about the situation but I don't believe Dumbledore doubts you
memories.source_text: "Of course he doesn’t think that!"

memories.description: Of course I can't accept Fudge's denial. Everything Dumbledore, Snape, and Harry are saying fits together logically so I believe them
memories.source_text: "Bill, Ron, and Hermione were staring at Fudge."

memories.description: We were all shell-shocked and thinking about what to do next after hearing Voldemort is back and after Crouch died
memories.source_text: "None of them spoke for a very long time."

memories.description: Well, we really wanted to tell him. Of course we did. I feel awful for not having managed to tell him properly.
memories.source_text: “Harry, we wanted to tell you, we really did —” Hermione began.

memories.description: Obviously, the Order of the Phoenix is a secret society. Dumbledore set it up and they're the ones who fought You-Know-Who before.
memories.source_text: “It’s a secret society,” said Hermione quickly. “Dumbledore’s in charge, he founded it. It’s the people who fought against You-Know-Who last time.”

memories.description: Well, I'm sorry to him. I don't want him to hate us. I care about him and I can't stand seeing him like this.
memories.source_text: “Harry, we’re really sorry!” said Hermione desperately, her eyes now sparkling with tears.

memories.description: Well, of course I’m upstairs with Ron waiting. The meeting’s for Order members only so we’re supposed to hold back and be quiet in the hall.
memories.source_text: "No, Harry, the meeting’s only for members of the Order. Ron and Hermione are upstairs, you can wait with them until the meeting’s over..."

memories.description: Of course some people in the Order are trying to recruit more members. That’s what you do when you need support.
memories.source_text: "some of them are working on recruiting more people to the Order —"

memories.description: We have been cleaning the place out thoroughly. I mean obviously it was filthy and needed sorting, and I’m the one keeping things organised so we actually got a lot done.
memories.source_text: "We’ve been decontaminating this house, it’s been empty for ages and stuff’s been breeding in here. We’ve managed to clean out the kitchen, most of the bedrooms, and I think we’re doing the drawing room tomo — AARGH!"

memories.description: I know Harry’s angry and I don’t blame him. I tried to explain that we did try to persuade Dumbledore so he should understand why we acted the way we did.
memories.source_text: "We knew you’d be angry, Harry, we really don’t blame you, but you’ve got to understand, we did try and persuade Dumbledore —"

memories.description: Well, of course Dumbledore thought I was safest with the Muggles. He was trying to protect me and Harry by keeping things quiet.
memories.source_text: "He seemed to think it was best," said Hermione rather breathlessly. "Dumbledore, I mean."

memories.description: Obviously I was frantic about Harry being alone. I genuinely believed he'd do something dangerous if he had no information or support.
memories.source_text: "Hermione was going spare, she kept saying you’d do something stupid if you were stuck all on your own without news,"

memories.description: Well, I am worried about the Ministry finding out what happened. I think Harry should care about that too, even if he says he does not.
memories.source_text: "Aren’t you . . . aren’t you worried about the Ministry of Magic hearing?" said Hermione quietly.

memories.description: Of course I wanted to be reunited properly, but it's clear Harry is upset with us for following Dumbledore's instructions. I feel guilty and frustrated because I was only trying to help.
memories.source_text: "The warm glow that had flared inside him at the sight of his two best friends was extinguished as something icy flooded the pit of his stomach."

memories.description: Well, of course I think Kreacher might be too old to have done everything people blame him for. Don’t be quick to condemn him.
memories.source_text: Kreacher’s really old, he probably couldn’t manage

memories.description: Obviously I’m not afraid to show my disapproval when someone jumps to conclusions about a house-elf.
memories.source_text: Hermione’s face was half concealed by a tea towel but Harry distinctly saw her throw a reproachful look at Mrs. Weasley at these words.

memories.description: Of course I told Kreacher who Harry is, because he needed to know that the famous Harry Potter was right there.
memories.source_text: This is Harry, Kreacher, Harry Potter.

memories.description: I think Kreacher's muddled and talking to himself. He might not understand people can hear him, so we shouldn't assume he's malicious in the normal way.
memories.source_text: Sirius, he’s not right in the head, I don’t think he realizes we can hear him.

memories.description: I honestly hoped setting Kreacher free might help him. I wanted to try the humane option even if others said it was impossible.
memories.source_text: If you just set him free, maybe

memories.description: We told Harry he couldn’t be in the Order. I agreed with that at the time. Of course, I wanted him safe and that’s why we kept him out of it.
memories.source_text: "I asked Ron and Hermione but they said we’re not allowed in the Order, so —"

memories.description: I was distracted and amused by Tonks showing off her nose tricks. It was a ridiculous way to pass the time but it cheered us up.
memories.source_text: Tonks was entertaining Hermione and Ginny by transforming her nose between mouthfuls. "Do that one like a pig snout, Tonks . . ."

memories.description: Well, of course Ginny should be asleep. Try not to wake her, alright?
memories.source_text: "We’ve got a busy day tomorrow. I expect Ginny’s asleep," she added to Hermione, "so try not to wake her up."

memories.description: Well, good night then. I'm saying good night because people are meant to actually go to bed.
memories.source_text: after Hermione bade them good night

memories.description: Of course we should all share what we know. I’m glad Harry will tell Ron and me.
memories.source_text: "’Course I will," Harry said. Ron and Hermione beamed.

memories.description: If Voldemort’s back then everyone will have to face a mess the Ministry hasn’t handled in years. We can’t ignore that.
memories.source_text: "Because accepting that Voldemort’s back would mean trouble like the Ministry hasn’t had to cope with for nearly fourteen years," said Sirius bitterly.

memories.description: It's not 'spew', obviously. I think people should take the whole thing seriously.
memories.source_text: It's not 'spew'!

memories.description: The group is called the Society for the Promotion of Elfish Welfare. Dumbledore says we should be kind to Kreacher too, so of course I defend him.
memories.source_text: It's the Society for the Promotion of Elfish Welfare, and it's not just me, Dumbledore says we should be kind to Kreacher too

memories.description: We must keep our voices down in the hall. Be quiet and stay sharp.
memories.source_text: And don't forget to keep your voice down in the hall, Harry

memories.description: Of course they had to clear you. There was no case against you. It was obvious from the evidence.
memories.source_text: "They were bound to clear you," said Hermione, who had looked positively faint with anxiety when Harry had entered the kitchen

memories.description: You belong at Hogwarts and you must not feel guilty. Sirius is being a bit selfish about wanting you to stay here but you should be at school.
memories.source_text: "Don't you go feeling guilty!" said Hermione sternly

memories.description: Sirius kept quiet because he did not want to build his hopes higher. He was trying not to get disappointed by getting his hopes up.
memories.source_text: "He just didn't want to get his own hopes up even more," said Hermione wisely.

memories.description: We should raise awareness for house-elf rights. Doing a sponsored clean would show people how awful it is and we could raise money for S.P.E.W. Obviously we must act.
memories.source_text: "You know, maybe it wouldn't be a bad idea to show people exactly how horrible it is to clean all the time - we could do a sponsored scrub of Gryffindor common room, all proceeds to S.P.E.W., it would raise awareness as well as funds -"

memories.description: I got my Hogwarts letter and I am going back this year. I am excited and I want to help with everything, especially making sure Ron is okay about his new responsibilities.
memories.source_text: "Me too, Harry, me too!" She spotted the badge in Harry's hand and let out a shriek.

memories.description: Well, I worry Hagrid might be hurt if he's not here. I want to know what's happened to him.
memories.source_text: "You don’t think he’s . . . hurt, or anything, do you?"

memories.description: Of course, Umbridge was at my hearing and she works for Fudge. That explains why I recognize her.
memories.source_text: "She was at my hearing, she works for Fudge!"

memories.description: What on earth is Umbridge doing at Hogwarts? It doesn't make sense that she's sitting at the staff table.
memories.source_text: "What on earth’s she doing here, then?"

memories.description: Well, the Sorting Hat sounded like it was warning the school. That made me anxious about what it meant.
memories.source_text: "I wonder if it’s ever given warnings before?"

memories.description: Well, the Quibbler is rubbish. Obviously it prints daft stories and you shouldn't treat it as reliable evidence.
memories.source_text: "Of course not," said Hermione scathingly, before Harry could answer, "The Quibbler's rubbish, everyone knows that."

memories.description: Well, I won't stand for Malfoy's sneering. I stepped in to shut him up because he was being obnoxious and trying to rile us.
memories.source_text: "Shut up, Malfoy," said Hermione sharply.

memories.description: Obviously Malfoy's comment about dogging struck a nerve. I got unnerved too and I want to treat this seriously rather than laugh it off.
memories.source_text: Hermione slammed the compartment door behind them and turned to look at Harry, who knew at once that she, like him, had registered what Malfoy had said and been just as unnerved by it.

memories.description: Well, I made them leave because we needed privacy and I was worried about what Malfoy might have overheard or realised.
memories.source_text: "Get out!" said Hermione, standing up.

memories.description: Well, of course I'm revolted by that. The idea of a hat deciding things and everyone being cheery about it is gross.
memories.source_text: [Hermione looked revolted]

memories.description: Of course I called them over and told them where to go. Someone has to be sensible about guiding the new students.
memories.source_text: "First years!" Hermione called commandingly along the table. "This way, please!"

memories.description: Well, my parents sent Hedwig back so I have to bring her cage along. Of course I want her safe.
memories.source_text: "Mum and Dad just sent Hedwig back"

memories.description: Ginny's been patched up by Mum. Obviously she's shaken but she'll be all right.
memories.source_text: "Mrs Weasley’s patched her up," said Hermione.

memories.description: Mad eye says we must wait for Sturgis Podmore or the guard will be one short. So we are waiting because of security procedures.
memories.source_text: "But now Mad-Eye’s complaining that we can’t leave unless Sturgis Podmore’s here, otherwise the guard will be one short."

memories.description: Of course we need a guard for the journey. It isn't paranoia, it's what Mad eye insists on and we follow his orders.
memories.source_text: "You have to go to King’s Cross with a guard," Hermione corrected him.

memories.description: Well, Ron and I are prefects so we have to go to the carriage for some instructions but it should not ruin our whole trip together. I still want to stick with Harry where possible.
memories.source_text: "I don't think we'll have to stay there all journey," said Hermione quickly.

memories.description: Well, of course I defend people when they're being unfairly mocked. I wasn't going to let Ron make Nick feel worse about his death.
memories.source_text: "Nick, he wasn’t really laughing at you!"

memories.description: Obviously the speech wasn't just empty words. It explained a lot and made things line up in my head about what's been going on.
memories.source_text: "It explained a lot."

memories.description: It means the Ministry is interfering at Hogwarts. Of course that changes everything about how the school is being run.
memories.source_text: "It means the Ministry’s interfering at Hogwarts."

memories.description: Of course I keep up with what people are saying. You have to know the facts even if it’s unpleasant.
memories.source_text: It’s best to know what the enemy are saying

memories.description: Obviously rules matter. I won’t let the noticeboard be used for that nonsense and I’ll say so.
memories.source_text: You can’t advertise for testers on the Gryffindor notice board

memories.description: My notes are crucial. I could make them fail their O.W.L.s if I wanted but that would be petty so I’ll keep helping, though I won’t be happy about them not trying.
memories.source_text: If I refused to lend you my notes this year?

memories.description: I want a job that actually makes a difference. Helping causes like S.P.E.W. matters to me and I’m thinking about turning that into real work.
memories.source_text: I think I’d really like to do something worthwhile. I mean, if I could take S.P.E.W. further

memories.description: Well, of course I knew Hermione wanted everyone to get changed and ready. She pins on her prefect badge properly and expects the same of others.
memories.source_text: "We'd better change," said Hermione at last.

memories.description: Well, Hermione is furious about Malfoy bullying younger students and she's ready to take action and report him.
memories.source_text: "Malfoy was being absolutely foul to a first year back there, I swear I'm going to report him, he's only had his badge three minutes and he's using it to bully people worse than ever."

memories.description: Of course Hermione wants us to get organized quickly. She's practical and moves straight away to secure seats.
memories.source_text: "Come on, let's get a carriage together before they all fill up"

memories.description: Well, of course there are two prefects from each House. It's the rules. It matters who they pick.
memories.source_text: Well, there are two fifth-year prefects from each House, Boy and girl from each.

memories.description: How Pansy became a prefect is ridiculous. Obviously she shouldn't be one if she can't do the job properly.
memories.source_text: And that complete cow Pansy Parkinson, How she got to be a prefect when she’s thicker than a concussed troll

memories.description: Ernie Macmillan and Hannah Abbott are the Hufflepuff prefects. Of course I remembered who belongs where.
memories.source_text: Who’s Hufflepuff? Ernie Macmillan and Hannah Abbott

memories.description: Obviously prefects are not meant to bully students. Of course I worry Ron might take it the wrong way.
memories.source_text: You’re not supposed to abuse your position, Ron!

memories.description: Well, I told Ron not to mind Fred and George. Of course I'm defending him because he deserves the praise and it's important to be supportive.
memories.source_text: "Don’t pay any attention to them, Ron, they’re only jealous!"

memories.description: Well, I wanted to tell my parents about Ron's prefect badge at once because it's the sort of thing they'll understand and be proud of.
memories.source_text: "Thanks," said Hermione. "Erm — Harry — could I borrow Hedwig so I can tell Mum and Dad? They’ll be really pleased — I mean, prefect is something they can understand —"

memories.description: Of course I wanted to share the good news quickly. I think small things like a prefect badge matter to families and we should celebrate them.
memories.source_text: Hermione and Hedwig had gone. Harry returned slowly to his bed and sank onto it, gazing unseeingly at the foot of the wardrobe.

memories.description: Well, of course we didn't completely get frightened into thinking we'd be attacked every day. We actually learned things that mattered.
memories.source_text: "No we haven't,"

memories.description: Harry, obviously, don't make this worse. Keep your temper under control even if it's unfair.
memories.source_text: "Harry, no!"

memories.description: Umbridge will shut people down and bully her way through class. We have to be smart about how we respond or she'll punish us.
memories.source_text: "Your hand is not up, Miss Granger!"

memories.description: How could Dumbledore let someone like her teach us? That's just not right.
memories.source_text: "How can Dumbledore have let this happen?" Hermione cried suddenly, making Harry and Ron jump;

memories.description: Obviously it's outrageous that she's stopping us from doing magic, especially in our O.W.L. year.
memories.source_text: "Yes, but to employ someone who’s actually refusing to let us do magic! What’s Dumbledore playing at?"

memories.description: Of course she's here to spy on us. Why else would Fudge have sent her? It all makes sense now.
memories.source_text: "Of course she’s here to spy on us all, that’s obvious, why else would Fudge have wanted her to come?" snapped Hermione.

memories.description: That's completely unacceptable. You can't test dangerous stuff on first years, no matter what you think.
memories.source_text: "It is NOT excellent!" she said when Fred and George shrugged about the fainting first years.

memories.description: I will write to your mother if you keep giving those sweets to first years. I mean it.
memories.source_text: "No," she said, her voice quivering with anger, "but I will write to your mother."

memories.description: I made hats for house-elves over the summer. I'm going to give them to the elves so they can have something.
memories.source_text: "They’re hats for house-elves," she said briskly, now stuffing her books back into her bag. "I did them over the summer."

memories.description: Of course house-elves want freedom. Don't you dare try to stop me from helping them.
memories.source_text: "Of course they want to be free!"

memories.description: Bowtruckles are tree guardians and they usually live in wand-quality trees.
memories.source_text: "Bowtruckles," said Hermione. "They’re tree-guardians, usually live in wand-trees."

memories.description: Bowtruckles eat wood lice and, if they can, fairy eggs. If you need wood or leaves from their tree you should distract them with wood lice.
memories.source_text: "Wood lice," said Hermione promptly, "But fairy eggs if they can get them."

memories.description: I'm protective of my plans for the house-elves and I'm not having Ron interfere with the things I think will free them.
memories.source_text: "Don’t you dare touch those hats, Ron!"

memories.description: Bowtruckles might look harmless but they can be dangerous and will gouge out human eyes if they get angry.
memories.source_text: "They may not look dangerous, but if angered they will gouge out human eyes with their fingers,"

memories.description: Well, obviously the weather shouldn't matter, but of course we need to stay focused on getting everything done. We can't let anything distract us from the work.
memories.source_text: "What's that got to do with our homework?" said Hermione, her eyebrows raised.

memories.description: Well, of course I want to see the letter right away. It could be important, especially if it’s from Percy about Ron being a prefect.
memories.source_text: "Open it!" said Hermione eagerly.

memories.description: Obviously Percy’s letter will matter. I’m curious and a bit worried about what he’s going to say to Ron.
memories.source_text: Hermione eagerly

memories.description: Well, you think Umbridge might be controlled the same way Quirrell was, but I don't think possession fits now that You-Know-Who has his own body.
memories.source_text: "You’re worried that You-Know-Who's controlling her like he controlled Quirrell?"

memories.description: Of course, if he's behind it he might have put her under the Imperius Curse. That would make more sense than possession.
memories.source_text: "He could have her under the Imperius Curse, I suppose"

memories.description: Obviously your scar links to what You-Know-Who feels, so this could be about him rather than Umbridge at all.
memories.source_text: "But last year your scar hurt when nobody was touching you, and didn't Dumbledore say it had to do with what You-Know-Who was feeling at the time?"

memories.description: You should tell Dumbledore about your scar hurting. He would want to know and might help.
memories.source_text: "Harry, I think you ought to tell Dumbledore your scar hurt."

memories.description: Don't write about this to Sirius. Moody warned us that letters could be intercepted, so it's too dangerous to put it in writing.
memories.source_text: "Harry, you can't put something like that in a letter!" and "Don't you remember, Moody told us to be careful what we put in writing!"

memories.description: I'm exhausted because I was up making woolly hats that keep disappearing around the place.
memories.source_text: "I was up until one o'clock making more hats. They're disappearing like mad!"

memories.description: Well, of course I hoped Snape might behave better now that he's in the Order. It made sense to expect some change.
memories.source_text: I did think he might be a bit better this year ... Now he's in the Order and everything.

memories.description: Honestly, Harry's potion wasn't that bad. It was unfair how Snape treated him compared to what others did.
memories.source_text: That was really unfair ... Your potion wasn’t nearly as bad as Goyle’s

memories.description: Trelawney is going to be all misty and dreamy as usual. Divination is useless for me but she thinks she knows everything about our fortunes.
memories.source_text: I have, of course, been following your fortunes most carefully over the holidays, and am delighted to see that you have all returned to Hogwarts safely

memories.description: Obviously the Ministry has forced a whole new theory syllabus on Defense Against the Dark Arts. That means practical work is being cut out and that's unacceptable.
memories.source_text: You will be pleased to know, however, that these problems are now to be rectified. We will be following a carefully structured, theory-centered, Ministry-approved course of defensive magic this year.

memories.description: Of course the course aims say nothing about practising spells. That's exactly the problem. Defense is supposed to be practical and there's no mention of that.
memories.source_text: There’s nothing written up there about using defensive spells.

memories.description: When Umbridge asks if I'm a Ministry expert I know she's shutting me down. Well, obviously I'm not a Ministry puppet and I'm not going to accept lessons that don't actually teach defence.
memories.source_text: Are you a Ministry-trained educational expert, Miss Granger?

memories.description: Well, it's not a dreadful punishment, really. Of course I think she should be punished less harshly, but at least it's only lines.
memories.source_text: "At least it's only lines,"

memories.description: Well, I asked Ron why he had not done his homework and where he had been, because he should have been studying.
memories.source_text: "Well, why didn’t you do any last night? Where were you anyway?"

memories.description: Well, of course I'm sitting by the fire. I'm in the common room over by the armchair.
memories.source_text: "She’s there," said Fred, who was also swigging butterbeer, and pointed to an armchair by the fire.

memories.description: Of course Dumbledore would know if Hagrid was in trouble. We shouldn't be showing panic because it just feeds Malfoy and his lot.
memories.source_text: "Dumbledore would know if something had happened to Hagrid," said Hermione at once.

memories.description: Ignore Malfoy. Focus on what matters and keep calm. Also, hold the bowtruckle so I can sketch it for proper notes.
memories.source_text: "We’ve got to ignore him, Harry. Here, hold the bowtruckle for a moment, just so I can draw its face . . ."

memories.description: Well, Grubbly-Plank might be competent, but she will never match Hagrid's way with creatures. I believe Hagrid's lessons are far superior.
memories.source_text: "I wasn’t going to," said Hermione calmly. "Because she’ll never be as good as Hagrid," said Harry firmly.

memories.description: Obviously you help your friends when they get hurt. I gave Harry my handkerchief to wrap his hand because that's what you do.
memories.source_text: Hermione's handkerchief was used to wrap Harry's hand.

memories.description: Well, practice matters and I want to know how it went. Of course I asked straight away.
memories.source_text: “How was practice?” asked Hermione rather coolly half an hour later, as Harry and Ron climbed through the portrait hole into the Gryffindor common room.

memories.description: Well, he might have been a bit off, but I was right that it takes time. Of course I expected that.
memories.source_text: “Well, I suppose he could’ve played better,” Harry muttered, “but it was only the first training session, like you said . . .”

memories.description: Obviously, Ganymede is Jupiter's biggest moon and Io is the volcanic one. I corrected Ron so his essay isn't wrong.
memories.source_text: “Jupiter’s biggest moon is Ganymede, not Callisto,” she said, pointing over Ron’s shoulder at a line in his Astronomy essay, “and it’s Io that’s got the volcanos.”

memories.description: Hermes is Percy and Lavender's owl. Of course I recognised him when he landed on the windowsill.
memories.source_text: “Isn’t that Hermes?” said Hermione, sounding amazed.

memories.description: Well, obviously I have already read the textbook. I know what Slinkhard says about counterjinxes because I read it all.
memories.source_text: I’ve read the whole book.

memories.description: Of course I disagree with Slinkhard. Jinxes can be useful defensively and I will say so out loud even if Umbridge tries to shut me up.
memories.source_text: He says 'counterjinx' is just a name people give their jinxes when they want to make them sound more acceptable.

memories.description: Umbridge took points from Gryffindor for speaking up. I will keep arguing for what is right even if she punishes me.
memories.source_text: Miss Granger, I am going to take five points from Gryffindor House.

memories.description: Of course the Hog's Head is allowed. I checked with Flitwick and the rules let us be here so long as we're careful about publicity.
memories.source_text: I specifically asked Professor Flitwick whether students were allowed to come in the Hog's Head, and he said yes

memories.description: I looked up everything about study groups and homework groups. They're allowed. We just mustn't parade what we're doing.
memories.source_text: I've double- and triple-checked the school rules.

memories.description: Lord Voldemort is back. We need proper training in Defense Against the Dark Arts, not Umbridge's rubbish.
memories.source_text: Because Lord Voldemort's back.

memories.description: I organized the meeting and got people to come. I intend to speak first so Harry doesn't have to if he doesn't want to.
memories.source_text: I told them to be here about now and I'm sure they all know where it is

memories.description: People want Harry's story, but the group's here because they want real instruction on Defense, not just to hear gossip.
memories.source_text: I told you, they just want to hear what you've got to say

memories.description: Of course I don't like the points being taken, but losing my temper with Umbridge is exactly what she wants. I need to keep calm.
memories.source_text: "I wish she hadn't taken points from you, but I think she's right to warn you not to lose your temper with Umbridge," said Hermione’s voice

memories.description: Well, sometimes I stay quiet and read. I'm paying attention even when I don't speak up.
memories.source_text: Hermione merely rustled the pages of her Daily Prophet and said nothing.

memories.description: Well, of course I think Harry should teach. It is the sensible thing to do. We need proper Defense and he can help us.
memories.source_text: whether you'd thought any more about Defense Against the Dark Arts, Harry.

memories.description: Obviously Harry can do things most people his age can't. He threw off Imperius and can produce a Patronus. Viktor even said Harry knows things he did not.
memories.source_text: You were the only person last year who could throw off the Imperius Curse completely, you can produce a Patronus, you can do all sorts of stuff that full-grown wizards can't, Viktor always said

memories.description: We must not hold lessons at Hogwarts because Umbridge would shut them down. We should meet outside school where she won't overhear us.
memories.source_text: I don't think Umbridge would be very happy if she found out what we were up to.

memories.description: Sirius has to stay hidden until Voldemort shows himself and the Ministry admits Dumbledore was right. Then people will see Sirius isn't a Death Eater.
memories.source_text: until V-Voldemort comes out into the open, Sirius is going to have to stay hidden, isn't he?

memories.description: I've arranged for interested students to meet us in the Hog's Head in Hogsmeade. It's less busy than the Three Broomsticks and more private.
memories.source_text: I've told the others to meet us in the Hog's Head.

memories.description: Of course I want things written properly. Get the notes down and copy the conclusion I gave you. It will save time and it makes sense.
memories.source_text: [Okay, write that down, and then copy out this conclusion that I’ve written for you]

memories.description: I thought Harry had simply misheard Professor Sinistra. I'm practical about mistakes like that and I want him to correct it now.
memories.source_text: [Harry, yours is okay except for this bit at the end, I think you must have misheard Professor Sinistra, Europa’s covered in ice, not mice]

memories.description: Of course this is dangerous. I can't help being anxious when someone takes risks that could get them caught. I say so out loud because it matters.
memories.source_text: [But Sirius, this is taking an awful risk —]

memories.description: Well, obviously I'll go through your essays and correct them. That's what I do.
memories.source_text: “Give them to me, I’ll look through them and correct them,” she said.

memories.description: Of course I'm helping because I care about you lot. I'll fix this now, and you can promise never to leave it so late again.
memories.source_text: “What you can say is, ‘We promise we’ll never leave our homework this late again,’” she said, holding out both hands for their essays

memories.description: I'm checking facts and editing sentences. I'm making sure everything is correct before dawn.
memories.source_text: The only sound was that of Hermione’s quill scratching out sentences here and there on their essays and the ruffle of pages as she checked various facts in the reference books strewn across the table.

memories.description: Obviously I'm a bit surprised by Ron right now, but I'm still focused on sorting things out properly.
memories.source_text: Hermione was looking at Ron with an odd expression on her face.

memories.description: Of course there's a bright side. No Quidditch means more time for coursework, even if it's Potions and miserable.
memories.source_text: "Well, look on the bright side — at least now you’ll have time to do Snape’s essay!"

memories.description: Rules matter. I can't just stop Fred and George if what they're doing isn't technically against the rules.
memories.source_text: "I can’t find a rule that says the other idiots aren’t entitled to buy them, not unless they’re proven to be dangerous in some way, and it doesn’t look as though they are . . ."

memories.description: Busy public places can actually be better for hiding conversations. The Hog's Head was a poor choice for secrecy.
memories.source_text: "That’s always packed with people —" "— which means you’d have been harder to overhear,"

memories.description: The Shrieking Shack won't work for our whole group. Twenty-eight people are too many and we don't have Animagi or a single cloak.
memories.source_text: "Well, Sirius, it’s just that there were only four of you meeting in the Shrieking Shack when you were at school, and all of you could transform into animals and I suppose you could all have squeezed under a single Invisibility Cloak if you’d wanted to."

memories.description: The secret passage behind the fourth floor mirror is blocked. We can't use that either.
memories.source_text: "Fred and George told me it’s blocked," said Harry, shaking his head.

memories.description: Obviously the note meant the fire in the common room. That was the only thing that made sense to me.
memories.source_text: "Obviously," said Hermione, also reading the note.

memories.description: Well, someone could magically reseal the message and anyone monitoring the Floo could intercept things. We can't be sure it's safe.
memories.source_text: "It wouldn't be exactly difficult to reseal the scroll by magic. . . . And if anyone's watching the Floo Network. . . ."

memories.description: Of course I worry that other people might've seen the note. If anyone else read it this could be a disaster.
memories.source_text: "I just hope nobody else has read this . . ."

memories.description: I really think Harry shouldn't miss Divination again. He already missed History of Magic and he can't afford to miss more.
memories.source_text: "You can’t skive off Divination," said Hermione severely.

memories.description: Of course she's been reading your mail. It explains everything. There simply is no other sensible explanation.
memories.source_text: "Umbridge has been reading your mail, Harry. There’s no other explanation."

memories.description: Well, Filch accusing you of ordering dungbombs always struck me as a ridiculous lie. It fits if somebody wanted an excuse to read your post.
memories.source_text: "I’ve been suspecting this ever since Filch accused you of ordering Dungbombs, because it seemed such a stupid lie," Hermione whispered.

memories.description: Obviously Umbridge could have used Filch to get hold of your letters. She'd tip him off and he'd do the rest because he's never going to stand up for us.
memories.source_text: "Well then, it would be a perfect way for Umbridge to manage it — tip off Filch, let him do the dirty work and confiscate the letter, then either find a way of stealing it from him or else demand to see it — I don’t think Filch would object, when’s he ever stuck up for a student’s rights?"

memories.description: I'm worried Umbridge might know how near she came to catching Sirius. That would make things far more dangerous for him and for us.
memories.source_text: "It was a very, very close call last night," said Hermione. "I just wonder if Umbridge knows how close it was."

memories.description: Well, if Voldemort is back then Harry's scar is bound to hurt more often and we need to be careful.
memories.source_text: "Well, now he's back it's bound to hurt more often," said Sirius.

memories.description: Honestly, it's ridiculous to waste energy rounding up merpeople when creatures like Kreacher are dangerous and need sorting out.
memories.source_text: "Imagine wasting your time and energy persecuting merpeople when there are little toerags like Kreacher on the loose —"

memories.description: Of course Umbridge is stopping practical lessons; she won't let us use magic in Defense which is completely wrong.
memories.source_text: "No," said Harry, ignoring Hermione's affronted look at being cut off in her defense of Kreacher. "She's not letting us use magic at all!"

memories.description: Honestly, I expect Sirius to try with Kreacher because he's the only family Kreacher has left, and I feel responsible for making him see that.
memories.source_text: "Sirius!" she said reproachfully. "Honestly, if you made a bit of an effort with Kreacher I’m sure he’d respond, after all, you are the only member of his family he’s got left, and Professor Dumbledore said —"

memories.description: Well, Madame Maxime says Hagrid got separated on the journey but there's no clear sign he's hurt, though I'm still worried.
memories.source_text: "Madame Maxime was with him, we’ve been in touch with her and she says they got separated on the journey home — but there’s nothing to suggest he’s hurt or — well, nothing to suggest he’s not perfectly okay."

memories.description: Of course we must learn how to handle real danger. Sitting through Umbridge's lessons won't prepare us.
memories.source_text: "We need to know what it’s r-really like . . . facing him . . . facing V-Voldemort."

memories.description: If we do not get proper Defense training from teachers, we must organize and teach ourselves. That is the sensible thing to do.
memories.source_text: "I was thinking that — maybe the time's come when we should just — just do it ourselves."

memories.description: Harry's experiences make him the best candidate to show us what facing Voldemort is like. This is practical, not sentimental.
memories.source_text: "I'm talking about you, Harry."

memories.description: I believe in Harry and I care enough to ask him to help us learn. I'm pleading because it's important and because I trust him.
memories.source_text: "Well . . . think about it," said Hermione quietly. "Please?"

memories.description: I got permission to re-form the Quidditch team. McGonagall pushed it through and Umbridge had to give in.
memories.source_text: "I’ve got permission!" she said. "To re-form the Quidditch team!"

memories.description: Well, I can't help worrying that Sirius has become reckless from being stuck at Grimmauld Place. Of course I want him on our side but I suspect he might be living through us a bit.
memories.source_text: "Do you honestly trust his judgment?" said Hermione. "You don’t think he has become . . . sort of . . . reckless . . . since he’s been cooped up in Grimmauld Place?"

memories.description: Talking to Snuffles made me less certain. I care about Sirius, but I'm not sure following his lead without question is right.
memories.source_text: "But after talking to Snuffles . . ."

memories.description: Of course there are proper textbooks here. This has everything we need for practical defensive work.
memories.source_text: A Compendium of Common Curses and Their Counter-Actions . . . The Dark Arts Outsmarted . . . Self-Defensive Spellwork . . .

memories.description: Well of course this proves it's the right thing to do. Everything we need is here and that settles it.
memories.source_text: Harry, this is wonderful, there’s everything we need here!

memories.description: Of course I jinxed the parchment. If anyone tried to copy the signatures or tamper with it they would be found out.
memories.source_text: "No, they can\'t have done because I put a jinx on that piece of parchment we all signed," said Hermione grimly.

memories.description: I don\'t think people necessarily blabbed. There could be other ways information leaked, but I still believe my protections matter.
memories.source_text:
"Someone must have blabbed to her!" Ron said angrily.

"They can\'t have done," said Hermione in a low voice.

memories.description: People who look even slightly suspicious must avoid hanging around us now. Having random students near our corner will draw attention and that is dangerous.
memories.source_text: "Here comes Ernie and Hannah Abbott," said Ron, looking over his shoulder. "And those Ravenclaw blokes and Smith . . . and no one looks very spotty." Hermione looked alarmed. "Never mind spots, the idiots can\'t come over here now, it\'ll look really suspicious \u2014 sit down!" she mouthed to Ernie and Hannah, gesturing frantically to them to rejoin the Hufflepuff table.

memories.description: If someone betrayed us they will regret it badly. I will not tolerate traitors and I will take action to make them pay.
memories.source_text: "What\'ll happen to them?" said Ron eagerly. "Well, put it this way," said Hermione, "it\'ll make Eloise Midgen\'s acne look like a couple of cute freckles."

memories.description: Well, of course we need to be back on time. It's already ten past nine and we must get to our common rooms now or we'll be punished.
memories.source_text: "Hey, Harry," Hermione called from the other end of the room, "have you checked the time?"

memories.description: Well, of course we should elect a leader to make things official, and I think Harry should be it because it gives him authority.
memories.source_text: "I think we ought to elect a leader," said Hermione. "Harry's leader," said Cho at once.

memories.description: We need a name to promote team spirit and to be able to refer to the group safely, so we should pick something that doesn't give away our purpose.
memories.source_text: "I also think we ought to have a name," she said brightly. "It would promote a feeling of team spirit and unity, don't you think?"

memories.description: A formal vote works; if a majority agrees on a name like the D.A. then it's official and I will organize it properly.
memories.source_text: "All in favor of the D.A.?" said Hermione bossily, kneeling up on her cushion to count. "That's a majority — motion passed!"

memories.description: Well, of course I took turns practising the basics with Neville and Ron when asked. Practicing the fundamental spells first is the sensible thing to do.
memories.source_text: "Listen, Neville, can you take it in turns to practice with Ron and Hermione for a couple of minutes so I can walk around and see how the rest are doing?"

memories.description: Of course I joined in straight away. Standing around won't help anyone learn properly.
memories.source_text: "Everybody got to their feet at once and divided up."

memories.description: Well, you have to jab the wand, not wave it. Of course the movement matters if you want the charm to work properly.
memories.source_text: "It’s the way you’re moving your wand," said Hermione, watching Ron critically. "You don’t want to wave it, it’s more a sharp jab."

memories.description: Obviously swapping the creature can help demonstrate the charm. Sometimes you have to change the variables to see what’s actually happening.
memories.source_text: "Fine, let’s swap," said Hermione, seizing Ron’s raven and replacing it with her own fat bullfrog. "Silencio!"

memories.description: Well, Angelina got permission and that means the team is coming back. Of course I want them to have their practice and match plans sorted.
memories.source_text: "I’ve got permission! To re-form the Quidditch team!"

memories.description: I'm worried. I keep thinking about Snuffles, and I can't decide if what we're doing is the right thing. I need to work it out.
memories.source_text: "Just thinking . . ." she said, still frowning at the rain-washed window. "About Siri . . . Snuffles?"

memories.description: Well, I asked whether the giants had attacked Hagrid because his injuries looked like a beating.
memories.source_text: "Did the giants beat you up, Hagrid?" asked Hermione quietly.

memories.description: Of course Madame Maxime went with Hagrid. I wanted to be sure who he’d been traveling with.
memories.source_text: "Madame Maxime went with you, then?" Hermione interjected.

memories.description: Obviously Muggles sometimes find giants by accident and those deaths get blamed on mountaineering. That explains why the giants are hidden but not unknown.
memories.source_text: "They do," said Hagrid darkly.

memories.description: Well, we had guessed Hagrid had been looking for giants. It seemed obvious from what led up to this.
memories.source_text: "We guessed," said Hermione apologetically.

memories.description: Well, Dobby's ideas can be dangerous. Remember when he got you hurt? I don't trust every one of his schemes on instinct.
memories.source_text: "Well . . . it’s just that Dobby’s plans aren’t always that safe. Don’t you remember when he lost you all the bones in your arm?"

memories.description: Of course Dumbledore knows about the Room of Requirement. He actually mentioned it to me at the Yule Ball, so it's not just Dobby being madly inventive.
memories.source_text: "This room isn’t just some mad idea of Dobby’s; Dumbledore knows about it too, he mentioned it to me at the Yule Ball."

memories.description: Once Harry said Dumbledore had been mentioned, I dropped my objections. If Dumbledore's involved, I'm willing to go along.
memories.source_text: "Dumbledore told you about it?" "Oh well, that’s all right then," said Hermione briskly and she raised no more objections.

memories.description: Well, I tried to get Hagrid to follow the proper lesson plan. He ignored me and turned up late after coming out of the Forest. Obviously he's not listening properly.
memories.source_text: "He wasn’t even there when I arrived, I was knocking for at least half an hour. And then he came stumping out of the forest —"

memories.description: Of course I know Hagrid was talking about chimaeras and eggs. He said he might try to get dangerous things even if it sounds mad.
memories.source_text: "He kept saying nobody in their right mind would rather study knarls than chimaeras — oh I don’t think he’s got a chimaera," she added

memories.description: Well, I thought explaining Umbridge would make him cautious, but he doesn't seem to understand how serious she is.
memories.source_text: "I tried to explain about Umbridge, but he just doesn’t get it."

memories.description: Well, obviously we should check that door. Of course it's worth going in when it appears like that.
memories.source_text: "Harry," said Hermione sharply, as they wheeled around after their third walk past.

memories.description: Well, of course the Ministry is meddling. Educational Decree Number Twenty five gives Umbridge ridiculous powers and that changes everything at Hogwarts.
memories.source_text: "Hem, hem . . . 'Educational Decree Number Twenty-five . . .'"

memories.description: Obviously Umbridge intends to punish more harshly than McGonagall wanted. She's out to make examples of us.
memories.source_text: "I think they deserve rather more than detentions," said Umbridge

memories.description: I can see Ron blaming himself. Of course he's feeling terrible, but that doesn't mean he caused this.
memories.source_text: "This is all my fault --"

memories.description: Well, Hagrid coming back could actually cheer us up. It matters who we have on our side right now.
memories.source_text: "I can think of one thing that might cheer you both up." "Hagrid's back."

memories.description: When I heard about the Gubraithian fire I was impressed. Of course it's called everlasting fire. Flitwick mentioned it in class so I knew what it was.
memories.source_text: "Wow" softly

memories.description: I couldn't believe Hagrid and Olympe went straight up to the giant camp knowing how dangerous giants are. Of course they'd be at risk.
memories.source_text: "But didn’t they try and kill you when they saw you?"

memories.description: Dumbledore wanted them to be patient, bring gifts over several visits and prove they kept promises. That slow approach was meant to build trust and let the giants test the present.
memories.source_text: "Why couldn’t you speak to them that day?"

memories.description: I was shocked and upset hearing how badly things went. Of course I feel sorry for Hagrid and furious that giants are so dangerous and unstable.
memories.source_text: "Blimey, Hagrid," said Ron quietly. (Hermione reacts elsewhere)

memories.description: Of course. Only people who have seen death can see thestrals. It all makes sense now.
memories.source_text: "The only people who can see thestrals," she said, "are people who have seen death."

memories.description: Well, obviously she is horrible. She is awful, twisted and vicious and I despise her.
memories.source_text: "You hag, you evil hag!"

memories.description: Well, I took the Knight Bus straight after term ended. Dumbledore told me what happened early on so I could get here as soon as possible.
memories.source_text: I came on the Knight Bus," said Hermione airily, pulling off her jacket before Harry had time to speak.

memories.description: Of course I know about what you heard on the Extendable Ears. I don't think you're imagining things and we want to talk, not shout.
memories.source_text: The others have told me what you overheard last night on the Extendable Ears

memories.description: Obviously hiding won't help. You're not the only one who's had a rough time and sitting alone isn't going to make anything clearer.
memories.source_text: Oh, don't lie, Harry," she said impatiently. "Ron and Ginny say you've been hiding from everyone since you got back from St. Mungo's.

memories.description: Well, Hagrid's mother is dead. Of course that hurts, but Hagrid seems resigned and not keen to dwell on it.
memories.source_text: Dead, died years ago. They told me.

memories.description: Obviously Umbridge will use any excuse to get rid of teachers who are close to Dumbledore. We have to be careful and make Hagrid teach things that look harmless so she can't punish him.
memories.source_text: Professor Umbridge won't be at all happy if you bring anything to class that's too dangerous

memories.description: I look out for the group and I won't let anyone take risks unnecessarily. I'm the one who thinks ahead and makes sure we don't get caught.
memories.source_text: Not yet. She might not be gone yet

memories.description: Well, of course I can see what Umbridge is doing. She's trying to twist things to make Hagrid look stupid because of his background and it is not fair.
memories.source_text: That foul, lying, twisting old gargoyle! You see what she's up to? It's her thing about half-breeds all over again

memories.description: Well, I noticed Neville was upset and flustered when he was asked about seeing someone die. He isn't being silly about it, he was clearly shaken.
memories.source_text: Well, they're . . . er . . . okay . . .

memories.description: Of course I think thestrals are fascinating and I got carried away saying I wanted to see them, but I didn't actually mean I wanted to see someone die.
memories.source_text: they are very interesting, aren't they? The way some people can see them and some can't! I wish I could.

memories.description: I'm furious about the way Umbridge treats Hagrid and Neville. I'll defend them and I'm not afraid to say so to Harry and Ron.
memories.source_text: It looked more like a leer to Harry. 'That foul, lying, twisting old gargoyle!' stormed Hermione half an hour later

memories.description: Is it Cho who cornered him after the meeting? Of course I'm going to ask straight away.
memories.source_text: "Is it Cho?" she asked in a businesslike way. "Did she corner you after the meeting?"

memories.description: Obviously Cho has been crying all the time lately. She's upset and it's everywhere, not just a one-off.
memories.source_text: "Because Cho spends half her time crying these days," said Hermione vaguely. "She does it at mealtimes, in the loos, all over the place."

memories.description: Of course. Cho's feelings are a complete mess right now. She's grieving Cedric, confused about liking two people, feeling guilty, worrying about gossip, scared about Quidditch, and everything is tangled up.
memories.source_text: "Well, obviously, she's feeling very sad, because of Cedric dying. Then I expect she's feeling confused because she liked Cedric and now she likes Harry, and she can't work out who she likes best. Then she'll be feeling guilty, thinking it's an insult to Cedric's memory to be kissing Harry at all, and she'll be worrying about what everyone else might say about her if she starts going out with Harry. And she probably can't work out what her feelings toward Harry are anyway, because he was the one who was with Cedric when Cedric died, so that's all very mixed up and painful. Oh, and she's afraid she's going to be thrown off the Ravenclaw Quidditch team because she's been flying so badly."

memories.description: I'm writing to Viktor Krum. Yes, I'm actually writing to him.
memories.source_text: "Viktor." "Krum?" "How many other Viktors do we know?"

memories.description: Don't be daft. People feel things in complicated ways. You can't treat everyone like they're emotionless.
memories.source_text: "Just because you've got the emotional range of a teaspoon doesn't mean we all have," said Hermione nastily.

memories.description: Well, obviously Mrs Longbottom knows who I am because Neville's talked about me. I felt a bit surprised but I still shook her hand.
memories.source_text: Hermione looked rather startled that Mrs. Longbottom knew her name, but shook hands all the same.

memories.description: Of course it's horrible, but it's clear now that Neville's parents were tortured by Voldemort's followers and that's why they're in this ward.
memories.source_text: "My son and his wife were tortured into insanity by You-Know-Who's followers."

memories.description: Well, I couldn't pretend this wasn't shocking. I can't stop feeling upset about what Neville's family has gone through.
memories.source_text: Hermione and Ginny both clapped their hands over their mouths.

memories.description: Well, Harry, you handled that badly. You should have explained things properly so Cho would not get jealous.
memories.source_text: "You shouldn't have told her that you wanted to meet me halfway through your date."

memories.description: Of course I can see why boys are baffled by girls. It makes sense to try and explain their behaviour.
memories.source_text: "You should write a book translating mad things girls do so boys can understand them."

memories.description: Obviously Quidditch causes tensions and bad feeling between students. It is only a game but it affects everyone.
memories.source_text: "That's the trouble with Quidditch," "it creates all this bad feeling and tension between the Houses."

memories.description: Well, I am not going to let my happiness hinge on Ron's performance. I care about him but I will not base my mood on Quidditch.
memories.source_text: "at least my happiness doesn't depend on Ron's goalkeeping ability."

memories.description: Well, Dumbledore has arranged Occlumency lessons so Harry won't keep having those dreams about Voldemort
memories.source_text: "Dumbledore wants to stop you having those dreams about Voldemort," said Hermione at once.

memories.description: Of course, it all makes sense now. The weapon has to be in the Department of Mysteries
memories.source_text: "In the Department of Mysteries, it's got to be," Harry whispered.

memories.description: Well, Sturgis trying to get through that door is not a coincidence so something important is definitely being kept in there
memories.source_text: "Sturgis Podmore was trying to get through a door at the Ministry of Magic."

memories.description: Obviously anyone would be shaken after repeated mind attacks so Harry being shaky is totally understandable
memories.source_text: "I expect anyone would feel shaky if they'd had their mind attacked over and over again," said Hermione sympathetically.

memories.description: Well, of course I explained exactly how the coins work. I put a Protean Charm on them so they all mirror the date Harry sets. That way we can pass messages safely and no one gets suspicious carrying a Galleon.
memories.source_text: "You see the numerals around the edge of the coins?" Hermione said, holding one up for examination at the end of their fourth meeting. "On real Galleons that’s just a serial number referring to the goblin who cast the coin. On these fake coins, though, the numbers will change to reflect the time and date of the next meeting. The coins will grow hot when the date changes, so if you’re carrying them in a pocket you’ll be able to feel them. We take one each, and when Harry sets the date of the next meeting he’ll change the numbers on his coin, and because I’ve put a Protean Charm on them, they’ll all change to mimic his."

memories.description: Well, obviously casting a Protean Charm is advanced, but I can do it. I tried to stay modest even though it matters for what we are setting up.
memories.source_text: "You can do a Protean Charm?" said Terry Boot. "Yes," said Hermione. "But that’s . . . that’s N.E.W.T. standard, that is," he said weakly. "Oh," said Hermione, trying to look modest. "Oh . . . well . . . yes, I suppose it is . . ."

memories.description: Of course the Sorting Hat thought about Ravenclaw. I still belong in Gryffindor though. I like to point that out when people act surprised about my ability.
memories.source_text: "Well, the Sorting Hat did seriously consider putting me in Ravenclaw during my Sorting," said Hermione brightly, "but it decided on Gryffindor in the end."

memories.description: Obviously I told them to practice. The Cup staying in Gryffindor matters and Snape is desperate to hand it over to Slytherin, so we'd better be sharp.
memories.source_text: "I’ve become accustomed to seeing the Quidditch Cup in my study, boys, and I really don’t want to have to hand it over to Professor Snape, so use the extra time to practice, won’t you?"

memories.description: Well, if we’re going to learn Defense, we need a plan. We have to decide how often we meet and where. Of course we need structure.
memories.source_text: So . . . like I was saying . . . if you want to learn some defense, then we need to work out how we’re going to do it, how often we’re going to meet, and where we’re going to —

memories.description: Obviously once a week is the minimum. This isn’t a casual thing, it’s important and we need regular practice.
memories.source_text: I really don’t think there’s any point in meeting less than once a week

memories.description: Well, everyone should sign so we know who came, but of course we must keep this secret from Umbridge and anyone else. Don’t blab.
memories.source_text: I-I think everybody should write their name down, just so we know who was here. But I also think that we all ought to agree not to shout about what we’re doing. So if you sign, you’re agreeing not to tell Umbridge — or anybody else — what we’re up to.

memories.description: Well, I think Umbridge is terrified of Dumbledore having any power, so she’s stopped proper training because she’s paranoid we’d be used as soldiers. It’s obvious when you think about it.
memories.source_text: We think the reason Umbridge doesn’t want us trained in Defense Against the Dark Arts is that she’s got some . . . some mad idea that Dumbledore could use the students in the school as a kind of private army. She thinks he’d mobilize us against the Ministry.

memories.description: Well, of course banning the interview just made everyone desperate to read it; Umbridge ensured the whole school now knows what you said.
memories.source_text: “If she could have done one thing to make absolutely sure that every single person in this school will read your interview, it was banning it!”

memories.description: Obviously everyone’s talking about the interview everywhere, even in the girls’ toilets and during lessons.
memories.source_text: Hermione telling Harry about girls’ toilets and cubicles

memories.description: Well, I don't like horses. Obviously that makes Firenze's appearance awkward for me.
memories.source_text: "Not really," said Hermione indifferently, who was reading the Daily Prophet. "I've never really liked horses."

memories.description: Of course, I pointed out that having four legs doesn't change anything for me. It's just common sense.
memories.source_text: "He's not a horse, he's a centaur!" said Lavender. "A gorgeous centaur . . ." sighed Parvati. "Either way, he's still got four legs," said Hermione coolly.

memories.description: I have a bad feeling Umbridge is only starting. She's going to get worse, mark my words.
memories.source_text: "I've got a feeling Umbridge has only just started being horrible," said Hermione darkly.

memories.description: Obviously she'll want revenge on Dumbledore for this. Of course she'll hate that he appointed a part-human like Firenze without asking her.
memories.source_text: "You mark my words, she's going to want revenge on Dumbledore for appointing a new teacher without consulting her," said Hermione, closing the newspaper. "Especially another part-human. You saw the look on her face when she saw Firenze . . ."

memories.description: Well, of course I was there watching the game with them. When I see trouble I try to help, even if it means holding Crookshanks back.
memories.source_text: Hermione, Ginny, and Crookshanks, “could you come down to the kitchen? Professor Snape would like a word with you.”

memories.description: Honestly, the Knight Bus is unbearable. I cover my eyes because it is just far too chaotic for words, and I want everyone to be all right.
memories.source_text: Looking toward the front of the bus Harry saw Hermione cover her eyes with her hands, Pigwidgeon still swaying happily on her shoulder.

memories.description: Of course I’m thinking ahead. I always think about practical, comforting things like knitting to keep everyone calm.
memories.source_text: Hermione was already talking about knitting a few elf hats before bedtime.

memories.description: This is serious. Read the paper quietly so we don't cause a scene or make things worse.
memories.source_text: “Shhh!” whispered Hermione desperately. “Not so loud — just read it!”

memories.description: We actually saw Broderick Bode at St. Mungo's and we saw a Devil's Snare get delivered. That looks like a deliberate, disguised attack.
memories.source_text: “We saw him,” Hermione whispered. “In St. Mungo’s, remember? He was in the bed opposite Lockhart’s, just lying there, staring at the ceiling. And we saw the Devil’s Snare arrive. She — the Healer — said it was a Christmas present . . .”

memories.description: I'm going to write and send a letter right now. I might be the only one who can do it and it's worth trying.
memories.source_text: “To send a letter,” said Hermione, swinging her bag onto her shoulder.

memories.description: Of course Fudge won't admit we were right. He's spent months discrediting us so he can't suddenly accept Dumbledore's warnings now.
memories.source_text: “He can hardly say, ‘Sorry everyone, Dumbledore warned me this might happen, the Azkaban guards have joined Lord Voldemort’ — stop whimpering, Ron — ‘and now Voldemort’s worst supporters have broken out too.’ I mean, he’s spent a good six months telling everyone you and Dumbledore are liars, hasn’t he?”

memories.description: Well, of course I insisted we would be in the library and I dragged Ron off so we'd actually get work done.
memories.source_text: "We'll be in the library, Harry,"

memories.description: I asked Harry about his Christmas because I'm concerned and I want to keep things normal and sensible between us.
memories.source_text: "Had a good Christmas?"

memories.description: Well, of course, Patronuses are more than spells. I think they're lovely and useful. My otter made me really happy.
memories.source_text: They are sort of nice, aren't they?

memories.description: I saw Dobby burst in terrified and understood immediately that something awful was happening. Of course I joined in getting everyone to safety.
memories.source_text: Hi, Dobby!

memories.description: Well, of course Sturgis Podmore was arrested for trying to get through a door and I think Lucius Malfoy had a hand in it
memories.source_text: "Sturgis Podmore," said Hermione, breathlessly. "Arrested for trying to get through a door. Lucius Malfoy got him too."

memories.description: Of course it all makes sense now. If Sturgis had Moody's cloak he could have been guarding the door and been found or controlled by Malfoy
memories.source_text: "Sturgis had Moody's Invisibility Cloak, right? So what if he was standing guard by the door, invisible..."

memories.description: Obviously Rookwood used to work there and could have told Voldemort how to get at the weapon
memories.source_text: "And now Rookwood's told Voldemort how to get the weapon?"

memories.description: Well, Harry, you were never meant to be seeing this. You need to work harder on Occlumency and try to forget what you saw
memories.source_text: "But you shouldn't have seen this at all, Harry. You're supposed to be learning how to close your mind to this sort of thing"

memories.description: Well, obviously Umbridge is enjoying the power she has been given and she is exactly the sort of person to lord it over everyone.
