memories.source_text: "Oh, I expect she really fancied herself sitting up there in the Head's office," said Hermione viciously

memories.description: Of course I know we must be careful. If anyone gives Umbridge a reason she will use it to expel students, so we cannot be reckless.
memories.source_text: "You really mustn’t! She'd love a reason to expel you!" whispered Hermione.

memories.description: Well, obviously I trust that Harry and Ron are not the ones starting trouble. I'm worried though because this new regime will punish even minor things.
memories.source_text: "He was bluffing," said Ernie, looking appalled.

memories.description: Well, of course you can’t Apparate inside Hogwarts. Hogwarts: A History says so and it’s obvious.
memories.source_text: "One day," said Hermione, sounding thoroughly exasperated, "you’ll read Hogwarts: A History, and perhaps that will remind you that you can’t Apparate or Disapparate inside Hogwarts."

memories.description: Of course I gave Harry a diary-style planner. He needs something to stay organized and that silly book actually nags you into doing work.
memories.source_text: "It’s Harry!" said George, pointing at the back of the picture. "Says so on the back!" "Good likeness," said Fred, grinning. Harry threw his new homework diary at him; it hit the wall opposite and fell to the floor where it said happily, "If you’ve dotted the i’s and crossed the t’s then you may do whatever you please!"

memories.description: Well, I gave Kreacher a patchwork quilt. It isn’t clothes but it ought to brighten his space and be more comfortable than that filthy rags he sleeps on.
memories.source_text: "Kreacher," said Hermione brightly. "It had better not be clothes!" said Ron warningly. "It isn’t clothes," said Hermione, "although if I had my way I’d certainly give him something to wear other than that filthy old rag. No, it’s a patchwork quilt, I thought it would brighten up his bedroom."

memories.description: Of course he sleeps under the boiler in that cupboard off the kitchen. That’s Kreacher’s den, if you can call it that.
memories.source_text: "Apparently he sleeps under the boiler in that cupboard off the kitchen."

memories.description: I’m pretty sure leaving Kreacher’s present where he sleeps is best. He’ll find it when he wants to and I won’t force him.
memories.source_text: "I think I’ll just leave his present here," said Hermione, laying the package neatly in the middle of the depression in the rags and blankets and closing the door quietly. "He’ll find it later, that’ll be fine . . ."

memories.description: Well, of course I don't believe Harry should stop Occlumency until he's absolutely sure he can control those dreams. He needs to go back to Snape and ask for more lessons.
memories.source_text: "So you’ve stopped having funny dreams?" "Pretty much," said Harry.

memories.description: Well, I always make study schedules for us because it's sensible and obvious that if we follow them we'll stand a much better chance in the exams.
memories.source_text: "It was the first day of the Easter holidays and Hermione, as was her custom, had spent a large part of the day drawing up study schedules for the three of them."

memories.description: Of course I scheduled Ron an evening off every week for Quidditch practice because practice matters even if he's moaning about our chances.
memories.source_text: "That’s for Quidditch practice," said Hermione.

memories.description: Well, obviously I think Harry is making a terrible mistake. Of course I am begging him not to go. This is dangerous and reckless.
memories.source_text: "Harry, don’t do it, please don’t do it!" Hermione said in anguished tones as the bell rang at the end of the class.

memories.description: I can see Ron wants to back off and not argue. Fine. But I still think he needs sense talked into him.
memories.source_text: "Give it a rest, okay? He can make up his own mind."

memories.description: Well, I know waking Grawp was a terrible idea. He’s unpredictable and we did not need him awake right then.
memories.source_text: "Wha — no!" said Hermione, jumping up, "Hagrid, no, don’t wake him, really, we don’t need —"

memories.description: Of course I agreed to be called Hermy if it helps, but that doesn’t mean I’m comfortable with the whole situation.
memories.source_text: "No, not at all," squeaked Hermione.

memories.description: Well, I don’t trust Hagrid’s plan to leave Grawp with us. It’s far too risky and I’m genuinely worried about being responsible for him.
memories.source_text: "I don’t believe him," said Hermione in a very unsteady voice, the moment they were out of earshot of Hagrid. "I don’t believe him. I really don’t believe him . . ."

memories.description: Obviously teaching Grawp English sounds impossible given his size and behaviour. The whole idea seems completely impractical and frightening.
memories.source_text: "A giant! A giant in the forest! And we’re supposed to give him English lessons!"

memories.description: Of course I’m convinced now we can’t just trust Hagrid’s assurances. This is a mess and it affects our safety and studies.
memories.source_text: "Of course, it all makes sense now" is forbidden so using original quote: "I really don’t believe him"

memories.description: Of course McGonagall has been taken to St. Mungo's after being stunned. That leaves Hogwarts thin on protection.
memories.source_text: "She was transferred to St. Mungo's this morning."

memories.description: I think Harry's visions are dreams, not proof. He hasn't actually been to the Department of Mysteries.
memories.source_text: "You've dreamed about the place, that's all."

memories.description: It's five in the afternoon so the Ministry should be full of people. It seems impossible for Voldemort and Sirius to be in there unnoticed.
memories.source_text: "it's five o'clock in the afternoon. The Ministry of Magic must be full of workers."

memories.description: I'm worried Harry has a habit of throwing himself into danger to save people and I think we need to be sensible about it.
memories.source_text: "You do sort of I mean don't you think you've got a bit of a a saving-people-thing?"

memories.description: Well, Hagrid is badly hurt. Of course I am worried and upset about how bad his injuries look.
memories.source_text: “Hagrid’s nose was gently dripping blood. His eyes were both blackened.”

memories.description: Obviously Umbridge is looking for a reason to dismiss Hagrid. It makes no sense but she is determined.
memories.source_text: “Umbridge reckons it was me that put tha’ niffler in her office.”

memories.description: Well, Hagrid expects to be fired soon and he thinks he needs to confess something important before that happens.
memories.source_text: “There’s a good chance I’m goin’ ter be gettin’ the sack any day now.”

memories.description: Of course the injuries make sense now. Grawp has been lashing out because he does not understand his own strength.
memories.source_text: “He’s been hurting you all this time, hasn’t he? That’s why you’ve had all these injuries!”

memories.description: What on earth. Grawp is Hagrid’s half brother. That explains Hagrid’s attachment and why he brought him back.
memories.source_text: “He’s my brother!” and “Well — half-brother.”

memories.description: Well, I did not expect to be asked to keep an enormous, awkward giant company, but Hagrid asked and I agreed. It feels like a terrible responsibility.
memories.source_text: “You want us to teach him” and “Look after him.”

memories.description: Obviously what Grawp needs most is company and someone to try to teach him how to interact with people.
memories.source_text: “If yeh jus’ talk ter him a bit... if he can talk ter people, he’ll understand more that we all like him really.”

memories.description: Well, it might be like a fever. Things can get worse before they get better so Harry has to stick with Occlumency and work harder.
memories.source_text: "Maybe it's a bit like an illness," said Hermione, looking concerned.

memories.description: Of course Dumbledore has a reason for sending Snape. If Dumbledore wants Harry to stop dreaming about that corridor then Harry must do the Occlumency lessons properly.
memories.source_text: "Dumbledore doesn't want you to have dreams about that corridor at all, or he wouldn't have asked Snape to teach you Occlumency."

memories.description: Well, if Dumbledore trusts Snape then we should accept that. We can't go around doubting everyone's motives when Dumbledore has chosen him.
memories.source_text: "Dumbledore trusts him," Hermione repeated.

memories.description: Of course I know Hagrid wouldn't hide anything dangerous where students could find it. I'm not going to let Umbridge blame him for everything.
memories.source_text: "Of course not," said Hermione scathingly. "Hagrid might have set it off accidentally."

memories.description: Obviously the thing would be hidden where students won't stumble on it. That's why I'm pointing into the deeper part of the forest.
memories.source_text: "In there, of course," said Hermione, pointing into the dark trees. "It had to be somewhere that students weren't going to find it accidentally, didn't it?"

memories.description: Well I meant for us to be heard. Making a scene was part of the plan. I wanted them to react and for Umbridge to look foolish.
memories.source_text: "I want us heard," she answered quietly, as Umbridge jogged noisily after them. "You'll see . . ."

memories.description: I won't stand for Umbridge insulting the centaurs like that. Of course I'm going to defend them and try to stop her when she insults them.
memories.source_text: "Don't call them that!" Hermione said furiously, but Umbridge did not appear to have heard her.

memories.description: Harry reacts without hesitation to protect me when things go wrong. We're a team when it turns dangerous and he looks out for me.
memories.source_text: "Harry grabbed Hermione and pulled her to the ground."

memories.description: Well, of course Umbridge hates part-humans. She's always been that way, and she was bound to try to get Hagrid out.
memories.source_text: ["Umbridge hates part-humans," said Hermione bitterly, flopping down into an armchair.]

memories.description: Obviously I did okay in Arithmancy. At least that's one exam I can be confident about.
memories.source_text: ["Well, I think I’ve done all right in Arithmancy," she said, and Harry and Ron both sighed with relief.]

memories.description: Of course I would say we needed to tell Dumbledore because something we worked on is ready now and he must know about it
memories.source_text: “We . . . we wanted to tell him it’s r-ready!”

memories.description: We finished a weapon or some method of resistance that Dumbledore told us to work on and we cannot find him to tell him
memories.source_text: “The . . . the weapon,”

memories.description: I would never let Umbridge use an illegal curse if I can stop it. I tried to stop her and it terrified me but I still fought
memories.source_text: “No!”

memories.description: Well, obviously he should be careful. I don't trust touching things that might be important or dangerous. Of course we should be cautious.
memories.source_text: Harry, I don’t think you should touch it

memories.description: What if Montague is permanently injured? We should be sensible and consider whether he needs proper help.
memories.source_text: "That’s all very well, but what if Montague's permanently injured?"

memories.description: Well, I wasn't going to go on about Fred and George. Of course I was worried in a different way.
memories.source_text: "I wasn't going to say anything about Fred and George!"

memories.description: You're trying to block your mind and keep up with Occlumency. Obviously you need to continue properly.
memories.source_text: "You are trying to block your mind, aren't you? You are keeping going with your Occlumency?"

memories.description: I really think Ron would gain confidence if Fred and George weren't always around undermining him.
memories.source_text: "I think Ron might do better without Fred and George around. They never exactly gave him a lot of confidence . . ."

memories.description: I suspect Mundungus might have been involved with Fred and George somehow, maybe in dodgy business, so we should be cautious.
memories.source_text: "I’ve been wondering whether Mundungus has persuaded them to sell stolen goods or something awful . . ."

memories.description: If they've actually got a shop in Diagon Alley, they must have planned it for ages. Of course that would explain a lot.
memories.source_text: "But I'm sure she won't, I mean, if it's really true they've got premises in Diagon Alley now, they must have been planning this for ages . . ."

memories.description: We have to get back to the castle now. That's the sensible starting point even if everything's gone wrong.
memories.source_text: "We need to get back up to the castle," said Hermione faintly.

memories.description: Without our wands we are seriously limited. Of course we need them if we're going to try anything.
memories.source_text: "Well, we can't do anything without wands," said Hermione hopelessly, dragging herself up again.

memories.description: I refuse to be left behind. Of course I'm coming. This is too important for me to sit out.
memories.source_text: "I'm not staying behind!" said Hermione furiously.

memories.description: We need enough thestrals for everyone who is going. That is practical and it matters.
memories.source_text: "Well, we need three," said Hermione, who was still looking a little shaken, but determined just the same.

memories.description: Well, Umbridge expects people to just whip up things like Veritaserum, but of course she doesn't understand how long it actually takes
memories.source_text: "You can make some more, can’t you?" she said, her voice becoming more sweetly girlish as it always did when she was furious.

memories.description: Obviously Snape will pretend not to know, but that doesn't mean he's uninterested. We have to be careful what we say in front of Umbridge
memories.source_text: "You’re on probation!" shrieked Professor Umbridge, and Snape looked back at her, his eyebrows slightly raised.

memories.description: Right, we have to try the Floo. We have to check Grimmauld Place before we rush off to London
memories.source_text: "We’ll have to use Umbridge’s fire and see if we can contact him," said Hermione, who looked positively terrified at the thought.

memories.description: Of course I will go with you if we need to. I'm terrified but I'm with you every step, I won't let you go alone without checking first
memories.source_text: "I’m begging you, please! Please let’s just check that Sirius isn’t at home before we go charging off to London ... if we find out he’s not there then I swear I won’t try and stop you, I’ll come, I’ll d-do whatever it takes to try and save him"

memories.description: Obviously we have to move fast. We can't wait around when Sirius could be hurt right now
memories.source_text: "Five minutes’ll be enough," said Harry. "C’mon, let’s go —" "Now?" said Hermione, looking shocked. "Of course now!" said Harry angrily.

memories.description: Well, we can check Grimmauld Place by using the Floo while I keep watch. The window is a weak spot so be careful.
memories.source_text: “I mean, you can — can check whether Sirius is at home or not while I keep watch, I don’t think you should be in there alone, Lee’s already proved the window’s a weak spot, sending those nifflers through it.”

memories.description: Of course Dumbledore wanted Harry to learn Occlumency. If he'd done it properly he might not have had these visions.
memories.source_text: “Dumbledore wanted you to learn to shut these things out of your mind, if you’d done Occlumency properly you’d never have seen this —”

memories.description: Well, we have to use Umbridge's fire to contact Grimmauld Place and check whether Sirius is there before risking London.
memories.source_text: “We’ll have to use Umbridge’s fire and see if we can contact him,”

memories.description: Of course I'll go with Harry into Umbridge's office. I'm not letting him do this alone. I'll do whatever it takes to help save Sirius.
memories.source_text: Even through his anger and impatience Harry recognized Hermione’s offer to accompany him into Umbridge’s office as a sign of solidarity and loyalty.

memories.description: We need a diversion. Someone must lead Umbridge away while lookouts keep people from her office.
memories.source_text: “Right . . . well . . . One of us has to go and find Umbridge and — and send her off in the wrong direction, keep her away from her office. They could tell her — I don’t know — that Peeves is up to something awful as usual . . .”

memories.description: Obviously we have very little time. If Harry insists it's now, we move immediately and act fast.
memories.source_text: “Five minutes’ll be enough,” said Harry. “C’mon, let’s go —” “Now?” said Hermione, looking shocked. “Of course now!” said Harry angrily.

memories.description: Well, of course I tried to explain we aren\'t like Umbridge. I begged them not to attack because we only wanted help to get rid of her, not to insult or use them.
memories.source_text: "Please," said Hermione breathlessly, "please, don\'t attack us, we don\'t think like her, we aren\'t Ministry of Magic employees! We only came in here because we hoped you\'d drive her off for us —"

memories.description: I kept saying we hadn\'t hurt anyone and that we just wanted to go back to school. I was desperate and terrified because pleading seemed to be our only option.
memories.source_text: "We haven\'t done anything to hurt you, we haven\'t used wands or threats, we just want to go back to school, please let us go back —"

memories.description: Obviously I realised Grawp was trying to say Hagrid. I said it quietly because it might mean Grawp knows Hagrid and that changes what he might do.
memories.source_text: "I think he\'s trying to say \'Hagrid\'!"

memories.description: Of course I clung to Harry when Grawp recognised Hagrid. I was shaking and relieved that Grawp remembered, and I relied on Harry in that moment.
memories.source_text: "Goodness," said Hermione, gripping Harry\'s arm so tightly it was growing numb and looking as though she was about to faint, "he \u2014 he remembered!"

memories.description: Well, I could feel something significant was happening, like a moment had finally arrived. Obviously it was important and weird.
memories.source_text: "It's time," said Hermione in an awestruck voice. "Time . . ."

memories.description: Of course I won't let anyone harm a child, even if that child is part of something monstrous. There are lines you don't cross.
memories.source_text: "You can’t hurt a baby!"

memories.description: I can stop someone speaking when I need to. Sometimes taking away their voice is the quickest way to stop them from giving orders.
memories.source_text: "Silencio!" cried Hermione, and the man's voice was extinguished.

memories.description: Of course I mark doors. If something’s dangerous we put a fiery cross on it so we don’t keep going in circles.
memories.source_text: Flagrate!

memories.description: I actually felt scared here. Even though I try to be sensible, this archway felt wrong and I wanted us out.
memories.source_text: This isn’t right, Harry, come on, let’s go

memories.description: I know it sounds impossible but logically there shouldn’t be anyone inside that archway. It doesn’t make sense for people to be there.
memories.source_text: There isn’t any ‘in there,’ it’s just an archway, there’s no room for anybody to be there

memories.description: We’re here for Sirius and I keep that in my head. I push Harry away from things that would distract or endanger us so we can focus on rescuing him.
memories.source_text: Harry, we are supposed to be here for Sirius!

memories.description: I can read the layout and the numbers. I know which row we need. It’s row ninety-seven and we need to go right to find him.
memories.source_text: ‘Ninety-seven!’ whispered Hermione.

memories.description: Well, Harry and I only watched Davies’s first goal. Obviously we missed the rest.
memories.source_text: "As a matter of fact, the only bit of the match Harry and I saw was Davies’s first goal."

memories.description: Grawp is enormous, destructive, and he knows me by name. Of course that complicates things.
memories.source_text: "Grawp’s about sixteen feet tall, enjoys ripping up twenty-foot pine trees, and knows me, as Hermy."

memories.description: Well, I’m beginning to think Hagrid has genuinely lost his mind over this Grawp situation, even though I hate that it’s true.
memories.source_text: "Yes, I’m starting to think he has."

memories.description: Hagrid made Harry and me promise to help. Of course I feel bound by that promise even if it seems daft.
memories.source_text: "But unfortunately, he made Harry and me promise."

memories.description: I confiscated a bunch of junk, including Dingle’s powdered dragon claw, because none of it is what people think. It’s nonsense and dangerous.
memories.source_text: "I confiscated that too. None of these things actually works you know —" "Dragon claw does work!"

memories.description: Of course, that powdered dragon claw was actually dried doxy droppings. That’s disgusting and it proves these so called brain boosters are fake.
memories.source_text: "This stuff can, I’ve had a look at it, and it’s actually dried doxy droppings."

memories.description: Of course we are going with Harry. We don't leave him to face something like this alone.
memories.source_text: “You could be miles away.” “We’re coming with you, Harry,” said Neville. “Let’s get on with it,” said Ron firmly.

memories.description: Well obviously those creatures in the tanks are brains. That explains everything about what they are.
memories.source_text: “They’re brains.” “Brains?” “Yes . . .”

memories.description: I grabbed the visitor badges quickly. Practical things like that matter when we're sneaking around.
memories.source_text: Half a dozen badges slid out of the metal chute where returned coins usually appeared. Hermione scooped them up and handed them mutely to Harry over Ginny’s head;

memories.description: Well, someone grabbed my wand and tried to use it. If I can't get my wand back, others will be left using it for them.
memories.source_text: "STUBEFY!" shouted Neville, wheeling around and waving Hermione’s wand at the oncoming Death Eaters.

memories.description: Of course I got knocked out at some point and was lying still. I couldn't help while unconscious, and that left the others vulnerable.
memories.source_text: "Luna hit a desk, slid over its surface and onto the floor on the other side where she lay sprawled, as still as Hermione."

memories.description: Of course I need to know when the results come out. It's sensible to plan ahead and an owl in July means I can stop worrying about it until the holidays.
memories.source_text: "Please, Professor, when will we find out our results?"

memories.description: Well, Arithmancy really does feel like the hardest thing right now. Obviously I must study it properly or I won't get the grade I want.
memories.source_text: "I’ve got Arithmancy and it’s probably the toughest subject there is!"

memories.description: Because I'm stressed I snap at people when they underestimate how much there is to do. I can't stand complacency when exams are so important.
memories.source_text: "Only!" said Hermione snappishly.

memories.description: Of course I will seal doors to keep us safe when I can. Locking the door buys us time.
memories.source_text: “Colloportus!”

memories.description: I will trust and follow Harry when he hisses a plan under his breath. I act fast to help make his plan work.
memories.source_text: “Smash shelves —”

memories.description: We cannot stay and wait. We must move and think logically even when we are terrified.
memories.source_text: “What do we do?”

memories.description: If I can get a wand back to someone in the middle of a mess I will. I try to be the practical one and keep everyone fighting.
memories.source_text: “Accio Wand!”

memories.description: Well, the situation is getting worse. The Prophet is full of panic about dementors and Death Eaters, and of course trouble is coming.
memories.source_text: "It hasn’t really started yet," sighed Hermione gloomily, folding up the newspaper again. "But it won’t be long now"

memories.description: Well, I heard Cho might be seeing someone else. I told Harry in case he cared, though of course his mind is elsewhere.
memories.source_text: "I — er — heard she’s going out with someone else now," said Hermione tentatively.

memories.description: Of course I was reading the Prophet. I want to know everything that's happening so we can be prepared.
memories.source_text: "Hermione was reading the Daily Prophet again, Ginny was doing a quiz in The Quibbler"

memories.description: Well, the Prophet is finally saying Harry was right, but of course they won\'t admit they were the ones doing the ridiculing and slandering. That is infuriating.
memories.source_text: '\'A lone voice of truth . . . perceived as unbalanced, yet never wavered in his story . . . forced to bear ridicule and slander . . .\' Hmmm,' said Hermione, frowning, 'I notice they don\'t mention the fact that it was them doing all the ridiculing and slandering, though . . .'

memories.description: Obviously Umbridge is not speaking and Pomfrey thinks she\'s in shock. Of course I\'m suspicious she might be sulking instead.
memories.source_text: 'Madam Pomfrey says she\'s just in shock,' whispered Hermione.

memories.description: Of course the prophecy broke. That is unfortunate, but it means people did not get the full truth from it.
memories.source_text: 'It is a pity it broke,' said Hermione quietly, shaking her head.

memories.description: Well, school is trying to move on. Flitwick removed the swamp but left a bit as a monument. It seems some normality is returning, even if it\'s only small things.
memories.source_text: 'So anyway, what\'s going on in school?' 'Well, Flitwick\'s got rid of Fred and George\'s swamp,' said Ginny.

memories.description: No, you lot are staying put. This is risky, of course it is, but running off would be daft. I'm not letting you go anywhere.
memories.source_text: "You two stay here," whispered Hermione. "What are you — ?"

memories.description: Well, I'm desperate for someone better than Umbridge. Of course I want to know if Slughorn will actually teach properly.
memories.source_text: "So, um, did Slughorn seem like he’ll be a good teacher?"

memories.description: Well, I think Mrs Weasley is being treated oddly by Fleur. Of course it annoys me to hear people talk down about her.
memories.source_text: "She’s so full of herself."

memories.description: Of course I care how Harry is. I was watching him like he might be ill. I want to protect him and make sure he is all right.
memories.source_text: "No, of course not! So, um, did Slughorn seem like he’ll be a good teacher?"

memories.description: Well, of course being captain gives you the same status as prefects. You can use our special bathroom and all the privileges that come with it.
memories.source_text: "That gives you equal status with prefects! You can use our special bathroom now and everything!"

memories.description: Well, of course they think we're scum. I can't believe they'd say that out loud and walk out like it's nothing.
memories.source_text: "now I know the kind of scum that shops here. . . . We’ll do better at Twilfitt and Tatting’s."

memories.description: Of course this is serious. If Ollivander is with the other side then our wand supplies and whoever's helping them are in trouble.
memories.source_text: "They'll make do with other makers," said Lupin. "But Ollivander was the best, and if the other side have got him it's not so good for us."

memories.description: Well, obviously if you get to be part of the Inquisitorial Squad, being a prefect would seem boring by comparison.
memories.source_text: Maybe being a prefect seems a bit tame after that

memories.description: Well, I did worry about hiding like that. Of course it felt risky, and I hesitated because it didn't seem entirely right.
memories.source_text: "Oh - I don’t know, Harry,"

memories.description: Of course the Cloak is tricky when more than one person is under it. Feet showing means we could be spotted, so we must be careful.
memories.source_text: "Our feet’ll be seen!"

memories.description: I can tell when someone's moved off. We're not imagining it, that's Malfoy heading left into Knockturn Alley.
memories.source_text: "That’s him, isn’t it?"

memories.description: Well, of course I wanted to know what they were saying. Of course I thought hearing them would help.
memories.source_text: If only we could hear what they’re saying!

memories.description: I pinched Harry to get his attention and whispered that Malfoy was inside. Obviously I was tense and wanted them to be quiet and careful.
memories.source_text: Hermione gave his arm a hard pinch. “Ouch!” “Shh! Look! He’s in there!” she breathed in Harry’s ear.

memories.description: Well, of course I tried to stop him. Think, Harry. You mustn't do this, you'll get into so much trouble. I was trying to make him see the consequences.
memories.source_text: "Harry, no!" moaned Hermione, grabbing his arm and attempting to push it down by his side. "Think. . . . You mustn’t. . . . You’ll be in such trouble. . . ."

memories.description: Well, of course we're travelling in a roomy Ministry car. It's more comfortable than the Burrow and clearly meant to keep us safe.
memories.source_text: He, Harry, Hermione, and Ginny were all sitting in roomy comfort in the wide backseat.

memories.description: Well, obviously Harry has been granted top-grade security. That explains the driver and the way the front seat stretches into a sofa.
memories.source_text: "He’s been given top-grade security status."

memories.description: Well, I saw his face was covered in blood and I panicked a bit because we had all been terrified.
memories.source_text: "You’re covered in blood!"

memories.description: Of course I moved in and used Tergeo to siphon the dried blood off his face so he was clean again.
memories.source_text: "Come here —" "Tergeo!"

memories.description: I checked his nose and said it looked normal, asking him urgently what had happened.
memories.source_text: "Normal,"

memories.description: Well, it was odd, but of course there could be loads of other explanations. We shouldn't jump to conclusions.
memories.source_text: "Yes, I’ve already agreed it was fishy, Harry," said Hermione a little impatiently. "But haven’t we agreed there could be a lot of explanations?"

memories.description: Obviously it seems unlikely that You-Know-Who would let a sixteen year old like Malfoy join up, so I don't think that's right.
memories.source_text: "It seems very unlikely, Harry," said Hermione in a repressive sort of voice. "What makes you think — ?"

memories.description: Well, maybe Malfoy just wanted to leave quickly. That could be why he reacted the way he did.
memories.source_text: "I think he just wanted to get out of there, Harry," said Hermione.

memories.description: Of course I had duties to get to on the train. I couldn't ignore being a prefect.
memories.source_text: "We can’t, Harry," said Hermione, looking apologetic. "Ron and I’ve got to go to the prefects’ carriage first and then patrol the corridors for a bit."

memories.description: Well, you missed the Sorting anyway. Obviously you weren't listening to the Hat.
memories.source_text: [You missed the Sorting, anyway]

memories.description: Of course I asked what the Hat said. I want to know if it said anything useful or different this year.
memories.source_text: [Hat say anything interesting?]

memories.description: The Hat just went on about unity in the face of our enemies. That's the same warning again and it's getting a bit predictable.
memories.source_text: [More of the same, really . . . advising us all to unite in the face of our enemies, you know.]

memories.description: Well, Hagrid is late but he's here and he waved at Harry. Of course I pointed it out because it's obvious and important.
memories.source_text: "Hagrid was only a few minutes late," said Hermione. "Look, he’s waving at you, Harry."

memories.description: Obviously everyone's curious about what happened at the Ministry. They're all asking Harry questions and it's driving Hermione mad.
memories.source_text: "Him and everyone else here," sniffed Hermione.

memories.description: What the hell happened to Dumbledore's hand? It's black and dead looking and that's worrying.
memories.source_text: "What happened to his hand?" gasped Hermione.

memories.description: Well, Dumbledore's hand looks like it's dead. Some injuries can't be cured and there are poisons without antidotes, obviously.
memories.source_text: [It looks as if it's died,]

memories.description: Of course I thought Slughorn would teach Defense Against the Dark Arts. I was surprised to hear Snape got the job instead.
memories.source_text: [But Harry, you said that Slughorn was going to be teaching Defense Against the Dark Arts!]

memories.description: We have to report anything suspicious to a teacher straight away. It's important for everyone's safety.
memories.source_text: [I implore you, should you notice anything strange or suspicious within or outside the castle, to report it to a member of staff immediately.]

memories.description: Of course nonverbal spells give you the element of surprise. That split second can make all the difference.
memories.source_text: Your adversary has no warning about what kind of magic you’re about to perform

memories.description: Well, when Snape described fighting the Dark Arts it reminded me of what Harry says about facing Voldemort. Brave and quick thinking matter as much as the spells themselves.
memories.source_text: I thought he sounded a bit like you.

memories.description: I gasped when Harry called Snape on that. It felt like he’d crossed a line but part of me admired his spine.
memories.source_text: There’s no need to call me ‘sir,’ Professor.

memories.description: Well, of course this book probably isn't approved. Using handwritten spells without knowing what they do is irresponsible.
memories.source_text: "Because it’s probably not Ministry of Magic–approved," said Hermione.

memories.description: Of course I think the Prince was dodgy. Who writes spells to dangle people by their ankles? That tells you something about the person.
memories.source_text: "I’m starting to think this Prince character was a bit dodgy."

memories.description: Obviously the Death Eaters won't all be pure-blood. Lots of them must be half-bloods pretending otherwise. It's the Muggle-borns they really hate.
memories.source_text: "The Death Eaters can’t all be pure-blood, there aren’t enough pure-blood wizards left," said Hermione stubbornly.

memories.description: Well, of course we have to explain to Hagrid. I hate leaving things unsaid and I can’t stand that he thinks we abandoned him.
memories.source_text: "We’ve got to go and explain," said Hermione, looking up at Hagrid’s huge empty chair at the staff table the following Saturday at breakfast.

memories.description: Obviously people are interested in Harry because of what he’s been through, not just because of Quidditch. He’s suddenly very noticed.
memories.source_text: "It’s not Quidditch that’s popular, it’s you! You’ve never been more interesting, and frankly, you’ve never been more fanciable."

memories.description: Well, Harry’s reputation has changed. People finally believe him about Voldemort and that changes how everyone treats him.
memories.source_text: "Everyone knows you’ve been telling the truth now, don’t they? The whole Wizarding world has had to admit that you were right about Voldemort being back and that you really have fought him twice in the last two years and escaped both times."

memories.description: Well, I do love them, don't I? Of course I do, they're really something.
memories.source_text: "Yes," said Hermione helplessly, "they're really —"

memories.description: I can't believe you've wriggled out of another one. They're not that bad, you know.
memories.source_text: "I can't believe you've wriggled out of another one," said Hermione, shaking her head.

memories.description: Well, I can't just stand there. Of course I'm going to try to help Hagrid when he's upset. I put my arm around him because someone has to be sensible and comforting.
memories.source_text: What is it?

memories.description: Obviously Aragog is very ill and Hagrid is terrified. Of course I asked if there was anything we could do, even if it probably isn't safe.
memories.source_text: Is there anything we can do?

memories.description: Well, the handwriting could be a girl's. It might not be a man behind the Half-Blood Prince notes after all.
memories.source_text: "Or herself," said Hermione irritably, ... "It might have been a girl. I think the handwriting looks more like a girl's than a boy's."

memories.description: Obviously she was reading fortunes and got a whole load of gloomy cards. She thought the knave sounded wrong for the situation and stopped herself.
memories.source_text: "Two of spades: conflict, Seven of spades: an ill omen. Ten of spades: violence. Knave of spades: a dark young man, possibly troubled, one who dislikes the questioner —"

memories.description: Of course I want Harry to be all right and I want to know what Dumbledore tells him. I'm staying up for it and I expect him to come back with answers.
memories.source_text: "Ooooh! Good luck! We'll wait up, we want to hear what he teaches you!"

memories.description: Well, the Time-Turners at the Ministry were smashed. Of course they weren't an option for squeezing Hagrid into our timetables.
memories.source_text: "We smashed the entire stock of Ministry Time-Turners when we were there last summer. It was in the Daily Prophet."

memories.description: Of course Filch used Secrecy Sensors on us when we arrived. Any Dark object should have been caught then. Crabbe even had a shrunken head taken.
memories.source_text: "Filch ran over all of us with Secrecy Sensors when we got into the entrance hall. Any Dark object would have been found, I know for a fact Crabbe had a shrunken head confiscated."

memories.description: Well, if all the owls are being checked as well, then sending something by owl is unlikely. That rules out that possibility.
memories.source_text: "All the owls are being checked too," said Hermione. "Filch told us so when he was jabbing those Secrecy Sensors everywhere he could reach."

memories.description: I really don't want to go to Slughorn's party alone. Of course I'm nervous about who'll be there, like McLaggen.
memories.source_text: "I wish you could come, I don’t want to go on my own!"

memories.description: Well, those deluxe sugar quills would last ages, they sound brilliant for studying and staying sweet while working.
memories.source_text: Oh, look, they've got deluxe sugar quills, those would last hours!

memories.description: Harry, of course you mustn't choke someone, that's not the way to deal with this even if it's awful.
memories.source_text: Harry!

memories.description: I care about Harry and I'll yell at him when he goes too far. I won't let him hurt someone like that.
memories.source_text: You mustn't!

memories.description: Well, it’s not just Harry’s dad. I know we’ve seen loads of people use that spell, even to abuse people by making them float helplessly.
memories.source_text: “Maybe your dad did use it, Harry,” said Hermione, “but he’s not the only one. We’ve seen a whole bunch of people use it, in case you’ve forgotten. Dangling people in the air. Making them float along, asleep, helpless.”

memories.description: Of course it’s irresponsible to use spells you don’t understand. And calling someone 'the Prince' like it’s a title is daft. I reckon it’s just a stupid nickname and he doesn’t sound like a nice person.
memories.source_text: “I just think it’s very irresponsible to start performing spells when you don’t even know what they’re for, and stop talking about ‘the Prince’ as if it’s his title, I bet it’s just a stupid nickname, and it doesn’t seem as though he was a very nice person to me!”

memories.description: Obviously the Death Eaters cannot all be pure blood. I expect a lot of them are half bloods pretending otherwise. Their real target is Muggle-borns, not half bloods like us.
memories.source_text: “The Death Eaters can’t all be pure-blood, there aren’t enough pure-blood wizards left,” said Hermione stubbornly. “I expect most of them are half-bloods pretending to be pure. It’s only Muggle-borns they hate, they’d be quite happy to let you and Ron join up.”

memories.description: Of course he didn't want to touch it. He was worried about appearances. He asked Borgin to keep the item so he wouldn't have to be seen with it.
memories.source_text: “Because he didn’t want to touch it, obviously!” said Harry angrily. “What he actually said was, ‘How would I look carrying that down the street?’” said Hermione.

memories.description: Well, I went into Borgin and Burkes and saw the necklace. Borgin only told me the price and didn't say it was sold. I was being obvious and he twigged that straight away.
memories.source_text: “I asked Borgin about the necklace, don’t you remember? When I went in to try and find out what Malfoy had asked him to keep, I saw it there. And Borgin just told me the price, he didn’t say it was already sold or anything —”

memories.description: Obviously Malfoy couldn't have been the one in Hogsmeade today. I'm frustrated because that means someone else must have been involved.
memories.source_text: “Harry, Malfoy wasn’t in Hogsmeade!” said Hermione, actually stamping her foot in frustration.

memories.description: Of course the seller could wrap the necklace so the buyer wouldn't touch it. It would be easy to hide in a cloak and slip it into Hogwarts unnoticed if they tried.
memories.source_text: “It was all wrapped up, so he wouldn’t have to touch it, and quite easy to hide inside a cloak, so nobody would see it!”

memories.description: Well, Veritaserum forces someone to tell the truth. Obviously that makes it a very dangerous tool in the wrong hands.
memories.source_text: It’s Veritaserum, a colorless, odorless potion that forces the drinker to tell the truth," said Hermione.

memories.description: Of course Polyjuice Potion lets you take someone else's appearance. I made it before so I know how it looks and smells.
memories.source_text: It’s Polyjuice Potion, sir," she said.

memories.description: Amortentia is the most powerful love potion. It causes obsession rather than true love. Obviously that is why it is so risky.
memories.source_text: It’s the most powerful love potion in the world!" said Hermione.

memories.description: Of course Amortentia smells different to each person. Right now I can smell freshly mown grass and new parchment and something else that made me blush.
memories.source_text: And the steam rising in characteristic spirals," said Hermione enthusiastically, "and it’s supposed to smell differently to each of us, according to what attracts us, and I can smell freshly mown grass and new parchment and —

memories.description: Well I had to tell Slughorn my name and explain I'm Muggle-born. He still thinks I might be connected to famous potioneers but I had to say I am Muggle-born.

memories.description: Well, of course I'm worried about you, Harry. Are you all right?
memories.source_text: "Are you all right, Harry?"

memories.description: Dumbledore is dead. Well, of course that's devastating. We have to keep our heads even though everything's awful.
memories.source_text: "Yes," said Harry.

memories.description: The Horcrux we went after was already taken and replaced with a fake. Obviously that changes our whole plan.
memories.source_text: "No," said Harry. "Someone had already taken it and left a fake in its place."

memories.description: Of course we're going to have to rethink everything now. We can't just carry on as before after losing Dumbledore and failing to retrieve the Horcrux.
memories.source_text: Harry stood up, murmured "See you in a bit" to Ron, Hermione, and Ginny, and followed Professor McGonagall back down the ward.

memories.description: Well, it sounds impossible, but you're saying you did magic without meaning to, that you reacted on instinct.
memories.source_text: "But that’s impossible, Harry. You mean that you did magic without meaning to; you reacted instinctively."

memories.description: Of course I find it hard to believe at first, but if your wand moved and cast something without your intent then we have to accept you can produce magic under extreme pressure.
memories.source_text: "But that’s impossible, Harry. You mean that you did magic without meaning to; you reacted instinctively."

memories.description: Well, Kingsley and I got back. Obviously getting everyone home is a mess and we still do not know where some people are.
memories.source_text: "Hermione and Kingsley," said Harry.

memories.description: Of course I am worried. We all shared our journeys, yet the fact that Bill, Fleur, Mad-Eye, and Mundungus are missing feels like a threat hanging over us.
memories.source_text: "They recounted the stories of their own journeys, but all the time the continued absence of Bill, Fleur, Mad-Eye, and Mundungus seemed to lie upon them like a frost, its icy bite harder and harder to ignore."

memories.description: Obviously we have to keep track of everyone. I will make sure to tell the others as soon as anyone returns.
memories.source_text: "Let me know when they’re back."

memories.description: Well, Stan Shunpike isn't where we thought he was. He was supposed to be in Azkaban, but he's out.
memories.source_text: "Stan?" repeated Hermione. "But I thought he was in Azkaban?"

memories.description: Obviously, there's been a mass breakout from prison and the Ministry is covering it up. Of course they'd try to hide it.
memories.source_text: "Hermione, there's obviously been a mass breakout which the Ministry has hushed up."

memories.description: George has lost an ear. That's horrific and I can't stop thinking about how much he'll be hurt.
memories.source_text: "He lost an ear," said Lupin."Lost an — ?" repeated Hermione in a high voice.

memories.description: Of course I expected Harry to be stubborn, but I also knew he would come round when he understood how dangerous it is if we do nothing.
memories.source_text: "I told them you’d take it like this," said Hermione with a hint of complacency.

memories.description: I notice details about how the potion changes people. I compare results and I make awkward jokes to lighten the tension even when it is serious.
memories.source_text: "Ooh, you look much tastier than Crabbe and Goyle, Harry," said Hermione, before catching sight of Ron’s raised eyebrows, blushing slightly, and saying, "Oh, you know what I mean - Goyle’s potion looked like bogies."

memories.description: I know Harry's cooperation is crucial. He is central to the plan and my confidence in the plan depends on him agreeing to help.
memories.source_text: "You can’t do it if I don’t cooperate, you need me to give you some hair."

memories.description: Well, it was easy. I did a Summoning Charm, Accio, and the books flew straight through the open window into the girls' dormitory.
memories.source_text: "Well, it was easy," said Hermione in a small voice. "I just did a Summoning Charm. You know, Accio. And, they zoomed out of Dumbledore’s study window right into the girls’ dormitory."

memories.description: Obviously I took them right after Dumbledore's funeral, after we'd agreed to leave and hunt Horcruxes. I was alone, it occurred to me that the more we knew, the better, so I tried and it worked.
memories.source_text: "Just after his Dumbledore’s funeral," said Hermione in an even smaller voice. "Right after we agreed we’d leave school and go and look for the Horcruxes. When I went back upstairs to get my things it, it just occurred to me that the more we knew about them, the better it would be... and I was alone in there... so I tried... and it worked. They flew straight in through the open window and I packed them."

memories.description: Of course Dumbledore wouldn't have wanted us taking things, but I don't think he'd be angry if we use the info to stop Voldemort rather than to make a Horcrux.
memories.source_text: "I can’t believe Dumbledore would have been angry, it’s not as though we’re going to use the information to make a Horcrux, is it?"

memories.description: This book, Secrets of the Darkest Art, gives explicit instructions on how to make a Horcrux. It's horrible and full of evil magic.
memories.source_text: "This is the one that gives explicit instructions on how to make a Horcrux. Secrets of the Darkest Art — it’s a horrible book, really awful, full of evil magic."

memories.description: Well, the more I read the worse it gets. Making one Horcrux already makes the rest of your soul horribly unstable. I can hardly believe he made six.
memories.source_text: "And the more I’ve read about them," said Hermione, "the more horrible they seem, and the less I can believe that he actually made six. It warns in this book how unstable you make the rest of your soul by ripping it, and that’s just by making one Horcrux!"

memories.description: Of course you can put yourself back together but only through remorse and it would be excruciatingly painful.
memories.source_text: "Yes," said Hermione with a hollow smile, "but it would be excruciatingly painful."

memories.description: Obviously the only way to mend a torn soul is real remorse. You have to truly feel what you've done.
memories.source_text: "Remorse," said Hermione. "You’ve got to really feel what you’ve done."

memories.description: Well, a Horcrux can only be destroyed by something so viciously destructive that it cannot possibly mend itself. Of course that makes sense.
memories.source_text: "It doesn't have to be a basilisk fang," said Hermione patiently. "It has to be something so destructive that the Horcrux can't repair itself."

memories.description: The book warns Dark wizards how strong Horcrux protections must be, and stabbing a Horcrux with basilisk venom is one of the very few reliable methods to destroy one.
memories.source_text: "From all that I've read, what Harry did to Riddle's diary was one of the few really foolproof ways of destroying a Horcrux."

memories.description: Obviously basilisk venom is almost irreversibly deadly and the only cure is phoenix tears, which are incredibly rare.
memories.source_text: "Basilisk venom only has one antidote, and it's incredibly rare —"

memories.description: Well, of course, a Horcrux is the complete opposite of a human being. The fragment of soul inside depends entirely on its enchanted container for survival and it cannot exist without that container.
memories.source_text: "Because a Horcrux is the complete opposite of a human being."

memories.description: Obviously, whatever happens to your body your soul will survive untouched, but a Horcrux fragment is the other way round and needs its container to keep existing.
memories.source_text: "Look, if I picked up a sword right now, Ron, and ran you through with it, I wouldn’t damage your soul at all."

memories.description: Well, we have to decide where we go after we leave. Horcruxes should be our priority even if I can see why Harry wants Godric's Hollow first.
memories.source_text: What we really need to decide," said Hermione, tossing Defensive Magical Theory into the bin without a second glance and picking up An Appraisal of Magical Education in Europe, "is where we’re going after we leave here.

memories.description: Well, Dumbledore took the Horcrux books off the shelves but he didn't destroy them. They were still library books.
memories.source_text: There weren’t," said Hermione, who had turned pink. "Dumbledore removed them all, but he didn’t destroy them.

memories.description: Of course I didn't steal them. I just took the books. They were still library property even if Dumbledore had hidden them. I'm desperate to help and I would never do something wrong on purpose.
memories.source_text: It — it wasn’t stealing!" said Hermione, looking from Harry to Ron with a kind of desperation. "They were still library books, even if Dumbledore had taken them off the shelves.

memories.description: Well, I’ve put a charm on the Wilkins so they don’t even know they have a daughter. I’m trying to protect them.
memories.source_text: "If I don’t — well, I think I’ve cast a good enough charm to keep them safe and happy."

memories.description: Of course it makes sense for me to seem to have gone off with my Muggle parents. Lots of Muggle-borns are planning to hide, so it looks plausible.
memories.source_text: "But hopefully it’ll look like I’ve gone away with Mum and Dad; a lot of Muggle-borns are talking about going into hiding at the moment," said Hermione.

memories.description: Obviously I can’t get my whole family to vanish. It would draw attention and they can’t just abandon their lives.
memories.source_text: "We can’t hide my whole family, it’ll look too fishy and they can’t all leave their jobs," said Ron."

memories.description: Well, Moody fell a long way. Even if the Killing Curse missed, he still hit the ground from a great height, so we can't ignore the likelihood he's dead.
memories.source_text: "We were just talking about Mad-Eye," Ron told Harry. "I reckon he might have survived." "But Bill saw him hit by the Killing Curse," said Harry. "Yeah, but Bill was under attack too," said Ron. "How can he be sure what he saw?" "Even if the Killing Curse missed, Mad-Eye still fell about a thousand feet," said Hermione.

memories.description: Of course it would be awful if Moody is dead, but we have to be realistic and face the facts rather than hope for miracles.
memories.source_text: "It’s dreadful that he’s dead! But we’re being realistic!"

memories.description: I've already packed and done hard magic to prepare. I even smuggled Moody's Polyjuice stock without Mrs Weasley noticing, so we're ready to leave whenever.
memories.source_text: "I’ve been packing for days, so we’re ready to leave at a moment’s notice, which for your information has included doing some pretty difficult magic, not to mention smuggling Mad-Eye’s whole stock of Polyjuice Potion right under Ron’s mum’s nose."

memories.description: Obviously I altered Mum and Dad's memories so Voldemort can't use them to find me. They're now convinced they've moved to Australia and have new identities until I undo it.
memories.source_text: "I’ve also modified my parents’ memories so that they’re convinced they’re really called Wendell and Monica Wilkins, and that their life’s ambition is to move to Australia, which they have now done."

memories.description: I will go back for my parents if I make it through this. I can't leave it forever; I'm determined to lift the charm and bring them home when it's safe.
memories.source_text: "Assuming I survive our hunt for the Horcruxes, I’ll find Mum and Dad and lift the enchantment."

memories.description: Well, obviously I was stunned to see Viktor. Of course I blushed and made a fuss. It was embarrassing but lovely to see him.
memories.source_text: "You look vunderful." "Viktor!" she shrieked, and dropped her small beaded bag... "I didn't know you were — goodness — it's lovely to see — how are you?"

memories.description: Well, this shows I'm flustered around Viktor. It matters to me enough to lose my composure in front of everyone.
memories.source_text: "Viktor!" she shrieked, and dropped her small beaded bag...

memories.description: Well, of course your soul survives if your body is damaged, but a Horcrux is the other way round. The bit of soul inside a Horcrux needs its magical container to survive. It can't exist on its own.
memories.source_text: "It should be, actually! But my point is that whatever happens to your body, your soul will survive, untouched," said Hermione. "But it’s the other way round with a Horcrux. The fragment of soul inside it depends on its container, its enchanted body, for survival. It can’t exist without it."

memories.description: Obviously, if the container's intact the soul bit can flit into someone who gets emotionally close to it. I mean emotionally close. Ginny poured her heart into that diary and made herself vulnerable. Be careful getting fond of or dependent on a Horcrux.
memories.source_text: "While the magical container is still intact, the bit of soul inside it can flit in and out of someone if they get too close to the object. I don’t mean holding it for too long, it’s nothing to do with touching it," she added before Ron could speak. "I mean close emotionally. Ginny poured her heart out into that diary, she made herself incredibly vulnerable. You’re in trouble if you get too fond of or dependent on the Horcrux."

memories.description: Of course they held onto Dumbledore's things so they could examine them. That is why it took so long to release the will.
memories.source_text: "Isn't it obvious?" said Hermione

memories.description: Well, I believed the Ministry had no right to seize Dumbledore's bequests unless they had real proof the items were dangerous.
memories.source_text: "They wanted to examine whatever he’s left us. You had no right to do that!"

memories.description: Dumbledore left me The Tales of Beedle the Bard. He must have thought I'd like and learn from it, which of course means it's important to me.
memories.source_text: "'To Miss Hermione Jean Granger, I leave my copy of The Tales of Beedle the Bard, in the hope that she will find it entertaining and instructive.'"

memories.description: I'm really touched. Of course I'm upset and emotional about what Dumbledore left me; it matters to me more than anyone outside Hogwarts might understand.
memories.source_text: "She held the book in her lap and gazed at it. Harry saw that the title was in runes; he had never learned to read them. As he looked, a tear splashed onto the embossed symbols."

memories.description: Well, we're in Tottenham Court Road now. We need to walk, move, find somewhere safe.
memories.source_text: "Tottenham Court Road," panted Hermione.

memories.description: Of course I packed essentials. I used an Undetectable Extension Charm to fit the Cloak and clothes in my bag.
memories.source_text: "It’s okay, I’ve got the Cloak, I’ve got clothes for both of you,"

memories.description: Obviously, the Extension Charm works. I can hide a lot in a tiny bag when I need to.
memories.source_text: "Undetectable Extension Charm," said Hermione.

memories.description: Put the Cloak on now. Hurry and hide yourself so we can move without drawing more attention.
memories.source_text: "Please, Harry, get that Cloak on!"

memories.description: When things get dangerous I will act straight away. I will freeze an attacker if it helps protect my friends.
memories.source_text: "Petrificus Totalus!" screamed Hermione

memories.description: I will do whatever I can to free people, even if my hand is shaking and I mess it up and hurt them by accident.
memories.source_text: "D-diffindo," she said, pointing her wand at Ron,

memories.description: How did they find us? Obviously something gave our location away and we need to figure out what it was.
memories.source_text: "But how did they find us?" Hermione asked, looking from one inert man to the other.

memories.description: Well, it could be the Trace. Of course the Trace should break at seventeen, but what if someone has found a way round that? We have to consider that possibility.
memories.source_text: "You — you don’t think you’ve still got your Trace on you, do you, Harry?"

memories.description: That tongue-tying curse was set up for Snape. Of course Mad-Eye would put protections like that on for someone like him.
memories.source_text: "That m-must have b-been the T-Tongue-Tying Curse Mad-Eye set up for Snape!"

memories.description: We are not splitting up. We have to stick together no matter what. Splitting up would be stupid and dangerous.
memories.source_text: "We’re not splitting up!" said Hermione firmly.

memories.description: Well, I asked Harry to come to Ginny's room. Of course I wanted to keep things steady and sensible, even if everyone is a bit wound up.
memories.source_text: Harry, will you come in here a moment?

memories.description: Obviously I pulled Ron along and tried to keep things calm. I'm nervous about them, but I try to hold it together.
memories.source_text: He took him by the elbow and tugged him on up the stairs.

memories.description: I felt nervous after Ron barged in on Ginny and Harry. Of course it was awkward and I worried how everyone was feeling.
memories.source_text: There was a strained silence, then Ginny said in a flat little voice, 'Well, happy birthday anyway, Harry.' Hermione looked nervous.

memories.description: Of course I think the sword choosing a person matters. If it presented itself to Harry it might mean he’s worthy.
memories.source_text: "It chose him, he was the one who found it, it came to him out of the Sorting Hat"

memories.description: Well, Dumbledore left things for a reason and he knew the Ministry would meddle. He must have been trying to hide meaning in plain sight.
memories.source_text: "He couldn’t tell us in the will why he was leaving us these things, but that still doesn’t explain"

memories.description: Obviously the Snitch is enchanted to reveal a message. I saw the writing appear and then disappear again.
memories.source_text: "Writing! There’s writing on it, quick, look!"

memories.description: Of course he expected us to understand something, but I’m not convinced it was as obvious as he thought. We’re missing a piece.
memories.source_text: "If these things are important enough to pass on right under the nose of the Ministry, you’d think he’d have let us know why . . . unless he thought it was obvious?"

memories.description: The Tales of Beedle the Bard are important enough for Dumbledore to leave to me, yet I had never heard of them before this.
memories.source_text: "I’ve never even heard of them!"

memories.description: Well, of course the clippings are about Voldemort. Regulus seemed obsessed with him for a while before he joined the Death Eaters.
memories.source_text: They’re all about Voldemort,

memories.description: Obviously, if Regulus turned against Voldemort he would try to hide something that could undermine him.
memories.source_text: If he was a Death Eater he had access to Voldemort, and if he became disenchanted, then he would have wanted to bring Voldemort down!

memories.description: There was a locket in the cabinet in the drawing room that nobody could open. That has to be the one.
memories.source_text: There was a locket.

memories.description: I can pick basic locks. I opened Regulus's door so we could search his room properly.
memories.source_text: Alohomora.

memories.description: Well, the Ministry are openly hunting Muggle-borns and demanding proof of Wizarding ancestry to attend school. That is terrifying and unjust.
memories.source_text: '"The Ministry is determined to root out such usurpers of magical power..."' (reading the Prophet)

memories.description: Of course Tonks should be included in decisions about Remus. I don't like the idea of leaving her isolated or ignored.
memories.source_text: 'But what about Tonks?' 'What about her?'

memories.description: I'm protective of Remus. I can't stand him putting himself down or treating Tonks and their baby like they don't matter.
memories.source_text: 'Remus!' whispered Hermione, tears in her eyes. 'Don’t say that — how could any child be ashamed of you?'

memories.description: Of course they'd send Snape if they knew. If he had been able to, he would have led them straight in.
memories.source_text: "I don't think so," said Hermione, though she looked frightened, "or they'd have sent Snape in after us, wouldn't they?"

memories.description: Well, the Trace can't have been on Harry. That's obviously not how they tracked them in Tottenham Court Road. Something else is going on and that's worrying.
memories.source_text: "We wondered," said Hermione tentatively, "whether Harry could still have the Trace on him?" "Impossible," said Lupin.

memories.description: This is mental. The Prophet is being used to blame Harry instead of exposing Voldemort. People will be misled and frightened.
memories.source_text: "So Death Eaters have taken over the Daily Prophet too?" asked Hermione furiously.

memories.description: Of course Voldemort would have overlooked house-elf magic; pureblood arrogance blindfolds them to other kinds of magic.
memories.source_text: "Of course, Voldemort would have considered the ways of house-elves far beneath his notice, just like all the purebloods who treat them like animals . . . It would never have occurred to him that they might have magic that he didn’t."

memories.description: House-elves obey their masters above all else, so Kreacher did exactly what he was told.
memories.source_text: "The house-elf’s highest law is his Master’s bidding,"

memories.description: Well, house-elves accept abuse as normal, so Kreacher wasn't thinking politics, he was reacting to how people treated him.
memories.source_text: "He’s a slave; house-elves are used to bad, even brutal treatment; what Voldemort did to Kreacher wasn’t that far out of the common way."

memories.description: Sirius treated Kreacher badly, and that affected how Kreacher behaved around the rest of the family and who he trusted.
memories.source_text: "Sirius was horrible to Kreacher, Harry, and it’s no good looking like that, you know it’s true."

memories.description: Regulus brought back a locket Horcrux and tried to have Kreacher destroy it after swapping it.
memories.source_text: "M-Master Regulus took from his pocket a locket like the one the Dark Lord had,"

memories.description: Well, I could see right away she was using that locket to pretend she belonged to proper wizarding families. It was insulting and obvious.
memories.source_text: "That’s — that’s pretty, Dolores," she said, pointing at the pendant gleaming in the ruffled folds of Umbridge’s blouse.

memories.description: Of course I can duplicate an object quickly. I made a copy of the locket so Mrs. Cattermole would not wake and realize it was gone.
memories.source_text: "Geminio! There . . . That should fool her."

memories.description: I can break restraints and get people free. I used Relashio to release Mrs. Cattermole from the chair.
memories.source_text: "Relashio!" The chains clinked and withdrew into the arms of the chair.

memories.description: I worry about Patronuses, but I got one. At first I struggled and nothing happened, then I managed to produce an otter to push the dementors back.
memories.source_text: "Expecto patronum!" A silver otter burst from the end of Hermione’s wand

memories.description: Well, I want Harry to show some mercy. Of course I care about how Kreacher is treated even if he is unpleasant.
memories.source_text: Hermione closed her eyes. "Harry, let him up!" whispered Hermione.

memories.description: Of course this is important. Kreacher's story about Regulus and the cave fits with what we know about Horcrux protection and dark magic.
memories.source_text: Hermione closed her eyes and reacted to Kreacher's confession about the Dark Lord and the cave

memories.description: Well, of course I was checking that we all made it in. I worried about you lot the whole time.
memories.source_text: "You got in all right, then?" Hermione whispered to Harry.

memories.description: Of course I recognised what those carvings meant. They are treating Muggles like they belong beneath wizards.
memories.source_text: "Muggles," whispered Hermione.

memories.description: Well, try Finite Incantatem first to stop the rain if it's a hex. If that fails then it's an Atmospheric Charm problem and it's nastier. Meanwhile cast Impervius to keep things dry.
memories.source_text: "If it doesn’t, something's gone wrong with an Atmospheric Charm, which will be more difficult to fix, so as an interim measure try Impervius to protect his belongings," said Hermione.

memories.description: Well, if we're going in, every tiny detail counts. We can't afford sloppy mistakes.
memories.source_text: "If we're going to get into the Ministry and not give ourselves away when they're bound to be on the lookout for intruders, every little detail matters!"

memories.description: Of course I remember what the bearded man said. Dolores wants someone on level one, so that's where her office is.
memories.source_text: "'I'll be up on level one, Dolores wants to see me,'" Hermione recited immediately.

memories.description: Obviously I took hairs for the Polyjuice and finished the potion. We needed a perfect copy of Mafalda to get those tokens.
memories.source_text: "Hermione plucked a few hairs from the witch's head and added them to a flask of muddy Polyjuice Potion she had taken from the beaded bag."

memories.description: Right, I handed over the tokens and told Harry to get moving. Timing matters, so we went when we had to.
memories.source_text: "'Take one of Mafalda's tokens,' Hermione told Harry, 'and let's go, it's nearly nine.'"

memories.description: Of course I found hairs from the maintenance guy and got robes ready. We had to make Harry look the part.
memories.source_text: "She passed Harry several curly black hairs, 'but he's gone home with a dreadful nosebleed! Here, he's pretty tall, you'll need bigger robes...'"

memories.description: Well, when we Apparated I couldn't shake Yaxley off because he had hold of me. He was still hanging on when we reached Grimmauld Place.
memories.source_text: "As we Disapparated, Yaxley caught hold of me and I couldn’t get rid of him, he was too strong, and he was still holding on when we arrived at Grimmauld Place,"

memories.description: Of course I tried a Revulsion Jinx to make him let go, but I'd already brought him inside the Fidelius protection first.
memories.source_text: "I — I forced him to let go with a Revulsion Jinx, but I’d already taken him inside the Fidelius Charm’s protection."

memories.description: I think I've accidentally given Yaxley the secret to Grimmauld Place by bringing him into the Fidelius, so he's basically got access now.
memories.source_text: "Since Dumbledore died, we’re Secret-Keepers, so I’ve given him the secret, haven’t I?"

memories.description: He's really badly hurt and bleeding a lot. I can't risk doing complicated magic in case I make it worse.
memories.source_text: "He’s lost so much blood already."

memories.description: If we're staying we need protections. I'm going to set up enchantments now.
memories.source_text: "If we’re staying, we should put some protective enchantments around the place," she replied, and raising her wand, she began to walk in a wide circle around Harry and Ron, murmuring incantations as she went.

memories.description: Right, Salvio Hexia, Protego Totalum, Repello Muggletum, Muffliato. Those should do the job.
memories.source_text: "Salvio Hexia . . . Protego Totalum . . . Repello Muggletum . . . Muffliato . . ."

memories.description: Obviously Perkins left the tent because of his lumbago and Ron's dad let me borrow it.
memories.source_text: "Apparently he didn’t want it back, his lumbago’s so bad," said Hermione, now performing complicated figure-of-eight movements with her wand, "so Ron’s dad said I could borrow it."

memories.description: Erecto to set the tent up and Cave Inimicum to protect the site. That's as much as I can do for now.
memories.source_text: "Erecto!" she added, pointing her wand at the misshapen canvas, which in one fluid motion rose into the air and settled, fully constructed, onto the ground before Harry... "Cave Inimicum," Hermione finished with a skyward flourish.

memories.description: Well, we should check for other people before moving on. Of course I will try a spell to reveal human presence.
memories.source_text: Before we go any farther, I think we’d better check,

memories.description: Homenum revelio is the spell I used to look for human presence here. Obviously it would show if anyone else was in the house.
memories.source_text: Homenum revelio.

memories.description: Of course I thought the connection was closed. I am frightened that Harry's scar is acting up again and that Voldemort might be getting through.
memories.source_text: Your scar, again? But what’s going on? I thought that connection had closed!

memories.description: Of course Harry must work on Occlumency and close his mind. Otherwise Voldemort can plant images in his head and trick him.
memories.source_text: But then you’ve got to close your mind!

memories.description: I do not want to be alone. Of course I suggested we camp in the drawing room together with my sleeping bags so we are safer.
memories.source_text: I don’t want to be on my own. Could we use the sleeping bags I’ve brought and camp in here tonight?

memories.description: Well, I stammered "Y-yes" when Umbridge addressed me because I was terrified and trying to do what I was told, even though this whole setup is unfair.
memories.source_text: “Y-yes,” squeaked Hermione.

memories.description: Of course I jumped when Harry whispered; I nearly knocked over my ink because I was already tense and frightened in that courtroom full of Dementors.
memories.source_text: she jumped so violently she nearly overturned the bottle of ink with which she was supposed to be recording the interview

memories.description: Well, I was white-faced and trying to record everything properly while Umbridge sat there like she owned the place. It was humiliating having to help her.
memories.source_text: Here, behind a balustrade, sat Umbridge, with Yaxley on one side of her, and Hermione, quite as white-faced as Mrs. Cattermole, on the other.

memories.description: Well, he has been Splinched. Of course I have to check the wound straight away.
memories.source_text: "Splinched," said Hermione, her fingers already busy at Ron's sleeve, where the blood was wettest and darkest.
