memories.description: Obviously I am buried in reading because we need answers. I'm not impressed with fooling around when there is work to be done.
memories.source_text: Hermione (nose buried in a book at the tent entrance) to scowl over at them.

memories.description: Well, of course I was asleep in the tent when they came back. They'll be relieved we're all together again.
memories.source_text: It was gloriously warm after the pool and the forest, the only illumination the bluebell flames still shimmering in a

memories.description: Of course I have a copy of The Tales of Beedle the Bard. I have the original with me.
memories.source_text: Hermione said, "I've got a copy, Mr Lovegood, I I've got it right here."

memories.description: Well, all right then. I'll read the Tale aloud so we all understand it.
memories.source_text: "Er . . . all right," said Hermione nervously.

memories.description: Well, he looked at me first. Obviously he was trying to work out what to do, and I was ready to be sensible about it.
memories.source_text: "looking first at Hermione, then at Ron, and finally at Harry"

memories.description: Well, of course the sword could be in Godric's Hollow. Dumbledore must have guessed you'd want to go there and Godric's Hollow is where Gryffindor came from.
memories.source_text: "Well, the sword, Harry! Dumbledore must have known you’d want to go back there, and I mean, Godric’s Hollow is Godric Gryffindor’s birthplace —"

memories.description: Obviously there is information in A History of Magic about Godric's Hollow. I dug the book out to check the history and the graveyard and stuff.
memories.source_text: "There’s a bit about the village in A History of Magic, wait . . ."

memories.description: Godric's Hollow has a graveyard full of old magical families. That explains the haunting stories about the little church.
memories.source_text: "The graveyard is full of the names of ancient magical families, and this accounts, no doubt, for the stories of hauntings that have dogged the little church beside it for many centuries.'"

memories.description: Of course. Bagshot doesn't cover recent history so Harry and his parents won't be in the book. But it all adds up. Godric's Hollow and Gryffindor's sword go together and Dumbledore would have expected Harry to work that out.
memories.source_text: "You and your parents aren’t mentioned," Hermione said, closing the book, "because Professor Bagshot doesn’t cover anything later than the end of the nineteenth century. But you see? Godric’s Hollow, Godric Gryffindor, Gryffindor’s sword; don’t you think Dumbledore would have expected you to make the connection?"

memories.description: Well, it's possible Dumbledore left the sword with Bathilda. We have to consider that even if Bathilda might be very old or not all there.
memories.source_text: "Harry, what if Bathilda’s got the sword? What if Dumbledore entrusted it to her?"

memories.description: We must plan everything. We should practice Disapparating under the Cloak, use Disillusionment Charms, and probably use Polyjuice Potion. The thicker our disguises the better. We will need to collect hair if we do Polyjuice.
memories.source_text: "Yes, but we’ll have to think it through carefully, Harry." "We’ll need to practice Disapparating together under the Invisibility Cloak for a start, and perhaps Disillusionment Charms would be sensible too, unless you think we should go the whole hog and use Polyjuice Potion? In that case we’ll need to collect hair from somebody. I actually think we’d better do that, Harry, the thicker our disguises the better."

memories.description: All this snow will leave prints. Of course we have to sort them out. I'll clear the prints if Harry goes ahead. We cannot be careless.
memories.source_text: "All this snow!" Hermione whispered beneath the cloak. "Why didn’t we think of snow? After all our precautions, we’ll leave prints! We’ll just have to get rid of them — you go in front, I’ll do it —"

memories.description: Well, I'm sure this is important. Of course we should take any lead that might matter.
memories.source_text: “I’m sure this is important!”

memories.description: Maybe this is something Harry needs to find out for himself. It might be personal and he has to learn it the hard way.
memories.source_text: “Maybe . . . maybe it’s something you need to find out for yourself,”

memories.description: Obviously a symbol connecting Dumbledore, Grindelwald and Godric's Hollow is worth investigating. We ought to know what it means.
memories.source_text: “A symbol that links Dumbledore, Grindelwald, and Godric’s Hollow? Harry, I’m sure we ought to know about this!”

memories.description: Well, obviously I'm not going to join in with gossip. I kept reading instead of making a scene.
memories.source_text: "For ten minutes or so Ron tapped and muttered, Hermione turned the pages of her book"

memories.description: Of course I've heard about Skeeter's piece on Dumbledore. It's ridiculous that they make it into a scandal.
memories.source_text: "Speaking of Dumbledore, have you heard what Skeeter wrote about him?"

memories.description: Well, obviously the tale doesn't call them 'Deathly Hallows', but that does not mean the story couldn't be describing three real objects.
memories.source_text: "But there's no mention of the words 'Deathly Hallows' in the story," said Hermione.

memories.description: Of course invisibility cloaks exist, but I am not convinced every cloak is the legendary one that renders someone eternally and completely invisible.
memories.source_text: "We all know that there are such things as Invisibility Cloaks. They are rare, but they exist. But —"

memories.description: Well, if the cloak could be true, the Resurrection Stone still sounds absurd. You cannot expect me to prove every pebble is not a magical relic.
memories.source_text: "Say the Cloak existed . . . what about the stone, Mr. Lovegood? The thing you call the Resurrection Stone?"

memories.description: I refuse to accept 'prove a negative' as a reasonable argument. Of course that is not how you establish something exists.
memories.source_text: "But that's — I'm sorry, but that's completely ridiculous! How can I possibly prove it doesn't exist? Do you expect me to get hold of — of all the pebbles in the world and test them?"

memories.description: I’ve got my wand on and I’m lighting the place up so we can see the sword properly.
memories.source_text: [“They both looked at the ornate silver sword, its rubied hilt glinting a little in the light from Hermione’s wand.”]

memories.description: Well, of course I had to ask what that enormous horn was. It looked wrong.
memories.source_text: "Mr Lovegood — what’s that?"

memories.description: Obviously it is not a Crumple-Horned Snorkack horn.
memories.source_text: "No it isn’t!"

memories.description: That's an Erumpent horn. It's Class B tradeable and it can explode at the slightest touch, so it is dangerously irresponsible to keep it inside a house.
memories.source_text: "But Harry, it’s an Erumpent horn! It’s a Class B Tradeable Material and it’s an extraordinarily dangerous thing to have in a house!"

memories.description: Of course I can tell by the grooved markings that it's an Erumpent horn. I don't care where he got it, he must get rid of it immediately.
memories.source_text: "Mr Lovegood, I recognize the grooved markings around the base, that’s an Erumpent horn and it’s incredibly dangerous — I don’t know where you got it —"

memories.description: Well, of course the tale opens with three brothers traveling on a lonely road at twilight; that's the whole set-up of the story.
memories.source_text: 'There were once three brothers who were traveling along a lonely, winding road at twilight —'

memories.description: Obviously the brothers were skilled wizards; they just conjured a bridge instead of risking the river.
memories.source_text: 'In time, the brothers reached a river too deep to wade through and too dangerous to swim across. However, these brothers were learned in the magical arts, and so they simply waved their wands and made a bridge appear across the treacherous water.'

memories.description: Of course the second asked for the power to bring people back from Death; he wanted to mock Death by undoing it.
memories.source_text: 'Then the second brother, who was an arrogant man, decided that he wanted to humiliate Death still further, and asked for the power to recall others from Death.'

memories.description: Well, I'm asking Harry if he trusts me because we need to act together. Of course I expect him to follow my lead.
memories.source_text: "Do you trust me, Harry?"

memories.description: Obviously the danger is right on top of us. We have to be as quick and quiet as possible.
memories.source_text: "All right," breathed Hermione, as the broken printing press blocking the top of the stairs began to tremble; Xenophilius was feet away from them.

memories.description: Of course I used a Hover Charm to free Ron. It worked and now he can put the Invisibility Cloak on.
memories.source_text: "She managed to free Ron with the use of a Hover Charm."

memories.description: Of course I expect cooperation from Ron and Harry. I'm taking charge because it's necessary and I need them to trust me.
memories.source_text: "Please, Ron! Harry, hold on tight to my hand, Ron, grab my shoulder."

memories.description: Well, hold tight. Of course, just hang on a moment, it'll happen any second.
memories.source_text: “Hold tight,” she whispered. “Hold tight . . . any second . . .”

memories.description: Obliviate, then Deprimo. Of course I need to erase his memory and then move the press downwards to clear the stairs.
memories.source_text: “Obliviate!” cried Hermione, pointing her wand first into his face, then at the floor beneath them. “Deprimo!”

memories.description: Well, Ignotus Peverell was the name on that grave in Godric's Hollow. Of course that link matters.
memories.source_text: That was the name on the grave with the mark on it, in Godric’s Hollow, Ignotus Peverell.

memories.description: Obviously the sign on Ignotus's grave suggests the Peverells are the three brothers from the tale and were the original owners of the Hallows.
memories.source_text: The sign of the Deathly Hallows on Ignotus’s grave is conclusive proof!

memories.description: Of course I wanted the Death Eaters to see Harry so they'd know Xenophilius wasn't lying about him.
memories.source_text: "That’s why I wanted the Death Eaters to get a glimpse of Harry before we left, so they knew Xenophilius hadn’t been lying!"

memories.description: I really hope Xenophilius isn't killed. I can't bear the thought of that happening to him.
memories.source_text: "Oh, I hope they don’t kill him!" groaned Hermione.

memories.description: My parents are in Australia and they should be safe because they don't know anything about what's going on.
memories.source_text: "They’re in Australia," said Hermione. "They should be all right. They don’t know anything."

memories.description: Well, I got seriously hurt. I was knocked out and looked very vulnerable at Bellatrix's mercy.
memories.source_text: "Hermione was lying at Bellatrix’s feet. She was barely stirring."

memories.description: Of course I know what Bellatrix will do. She is capable of aiming to terrorize and humiliate, and she used me as bait to force them to surrender.
memories.source_text: "'Drop your wands,' she whispered. 'Drop them, or we’ll see exactly how filthy her blood is!'"

memories.description: Obviously Bellatrix hates me in a very personal way. That is terrifying and makes her utterly dangerous to my friends and me.
memories.source_text: "Bellatrix was supporting Hermione, who seemed to be unconscious, and was holding her short silver knife to Hermione’s throat."

memories.description: We tried to be honest under torture and I kept shouting that we found the sword. I was desperate and terrified and said the same thing over and over.
memories.source_text: "We found it — we found it — PLEASE!"

memories.description: I said the sword is a copy to stop them believing we raided Gringotts. I argued it logically while being tortured because logic is what I reach for even when panicking.
memories.source_text: "We’ve never been inside your vault. . . . It isn’t the real sword! It’s a copy, just a copy!"

memories.description: I know how strong I am under pressure, but being screamed for and tortured felt unbearable. I keep fighting to stay upright and to think.
memories.source_text: "HERMIONE!"

memories.description: Harry? Well, I called his name because he was lost in thought and fiddling with the cloak, and I was worried.
memories.source_text: "Harry?"

memories.description: Well, I don't like this plan. It's clever and all, but it doesn't sit right with me emotionally even if it makes sense.
memories.source_text: "I don’t like it," said Hermione.

memories.description: Well, of course Lupin still insists Harry is alive. That should reassure anyone listening who wants evidence rather than panic.
memories.source_text: "Romulus, do you maintain, as you have every time you’ve appeared on our program, that Harry Potter is still alive?" "I do," said Lupin firmly.

memories.description: Well, obviously Lupin believes in Harry's instincts. Hearing that makes me cry because it's such a hopeful thing to say about someone we care about.
memories.source_text: "And I'd tell him to follow his instincts, which are good and nearly always right."

memories.description: Of course Hagrid escaped arrest and is on the run. That sounds reckless and worrying, but it also shows his commitment to supporting Harry.
memories.source_text: "Rubeus Hagrid... has narrowly escaped arrest within the grounds of Hogwarts... Hagrid was not taken into custody, and is, we believe, on the run."

memories.description: Well, goblins have been treated badly by wizards in the past. Of course that explains a lot of their anger.
memories.source_text: "Goblins have got good reason to dislike wizards, Ron," said Hermione. "They’ve been treated brutally in the past."

memories.description: Of course Griphook would spot a fake. He's far better at goblin-made things than we are.
memories.source_text: "Ron, he’d know the difference better than we would!" said Hermione. "He’s the only one who realized there had been a swap!"

memories.description: I can't stand the idea of tricking Griphook. We shouldn't double-cross him if we want his help and any chance of trust.
memories.source_text: "That," she said quietly, "is despicable. Ask for his help, then double-cross him? And you wonder why goblins don’t like wizards, Ron?"

memories.description: We named the baby Ted after Dora's father. Of course it's a lovely, proper name.
memories.source_text: ["We’ve named him Ted, after Dora’s father!"]

memories.description: Tonks has had the baby. Well, that's wonderful news, absolutely brilliant.
memories.source_text: ["Wha — ? Tonks — Tonks has had the baby?"]

memories.description: Well, I don't think the Deathly Hallows theory holds up. I really think Harry is jumping to the wrong conclusion.
memories.source_text: "I’m sorry, but I think you’ve got this wrong, all wrong."

memories.description: Of course, if Dumbledore had believed the Hallows meant mastery over death, he would have warned Harry. I can't see why he would hide something so important from him.
memories.source_text: "If the Deathly Hallows really existed, and Dumbledore knew about them, knew that the person who possessed all three of them would be master of Death — Harry, why wouldn’t he have told you? Why?"

memories.description: We must focus on destroying Horcruxes. This is not the time for fanciful quests after legendary objects.
memories.source_text: "Harry, this isn’t a game, this isn’t practice! This is the real thing, and Dumbledore left you very clear instructions: Find and destroy the Horcruxes!"

memories.description: Of course I'm taking responsibility for watch. We have to be practical and keep each other safe rather than chase distractions.
memories.source_text: "Thank you, Ron. I’ll take first watch."

memories.description: Well, of course I can see this is about more than just wizards and goblins. I am directly affected by the new order and I will stand up and say it.
memories.source_text: "We protest! And I’m hunted quite as much as any goblin or elf, Griphook! I’m a Mudblood!"

memories.description: Well, Harry has a history of standing up for others. That matters to Griphook and it strengthens his reasons to consider us.
memories.source_text: "Did you know that it was Harry who set Dobby free?"

memories.description: Of course I have wanted house-elves freed for a long time and I made that clear. It ties our cause to the wider injustices goblins face.
memories.source_text: "We’ve wanted elves to be freed for years"

memories.description: Well, I was tortured because of blood status. That gives me standing when arguing against the way wand-carriers treat other magical folk.
memories.source_text: "It was me they chose to torture, back at the Malfoys’!"

memories.description: I was badly shaken and exhausted, but I held myself together enough to help when it mattered.
memories.source_text: Hermione was wrapped in a borrowed dressing gown, pale and unsteady on her feet

memories.description: I know I was pushed to my limits, but I did what I had to. I can be brave and clever under pressure, even if it nearly breaks me.
memories.source_text: You were amazing - coming up with that story when she was hurting you like that -

memories.description: I need my friends. When I'm fragile, Ron and the others are the ones who steady me.
memories.source_text: Hermione gave a weak smile as Ron gave her a one-armed squeeze

memories.description: Well, we should get out of here right now. Disapparate and go.
memories.source_text: "Let’s just leave! Disapparate now!"

memories.description: Of course I'm terrified at the thought that Voldemort might learn your wand is broken. That would be horrible and dangerous.
memories.source_text: "No!" said Hermione, sounding frightened. "He can’t know that, Harry, how could he— ?"

memories.description: Obviously if they study those wands closely they can work out what happened. They might figure out my wand broke and that you've been using the blackthorn wand instead.
memories.source_text: "We left your wand and the blackthorn wand at the Malfoys', Hermione. If they examine them properly, make them re-create the spells they’ve cast lately, they’ll see that yours broke mine, they’ll see that you tried and failed to mend it, and they’ll realize that I’ve been using the blackthorn one ever since."

memories.description: Of course I tried summoning the cup first. It would have worked if the vault hadn't been tricked. I always go for the sensible spell.
memories.source_text: "Accio Cup!"

memories.description: I can hoist someone up by the ankle to reach things. It hurts them a bit but it buys crucial seconds.
memories.source_text: "Levicorpus."

memories.description: I use protective spells to try to keep us from burning. Quick, practical magic when things heat up.
memories.source_text: "Impervius!"

memories.description: I panic when Harry acts recklessly, but I will still climb and follow because leaving him isn't an option. Brains and bravery both matter.
memories.source_text: "Harry — Harry — what are you doing?"

memories.description: I can dig through rock when needed. I try to think ahead and solve problems even while everything is collapsing around us.
memories.source_text: "Defodio!"

memories.description: Well, of course I'm worrying about the dragon. What'll happen to it? Will it be all right?
memories.source_text: "What’ll happen to it, do you think? Will it be all right?"

memories.description: Well, I was not trying to keep the dragon as a pet. Obviously that was never realistic.
memories.source_text: "Don't exaggerate, Ron —"

memories.description: Neville helped me get into the tunnel. Of course I appreciated it and trusted him to get us moving.
memories.source_text: Neville held out his hand to Hermione and helped her to climb up onto the mantelpiece and into the tunnel;

memories.description: Well, of course I'm worried about the dragon, what will happen to it and will it be all right
memories.source_text: What'll happen to it, do you think? Will it be all right?

memories.description: Well, we were crawling along the wall, keeping absolutely quiet and trying not to make a sound, because the dementors were nearby.
memories.source_text: "He, Ron, and Hermione retreated down the side street, groping their way along the wall, trying not to make a sound."

memories.description: Well, that wand is not Bellatrix's. Obviously something about it is wrong and I had to say so.
memories.source_text: "No, no, that’s mine —"

memories.description: Of course the Thief's Downfall strips away enchantments. It washes foolproof disguises and enchantments right off.
memories.source_text: "The Thief’s Downfall!" said Griphook, clambering to his feet and looking back at the deluge onto the tracks, which, Harry knew now, had been more than water.

memories.description: Well, shielding spells can stop that enchanted water. I used Protego to halt the flow so we could get away.
memories.source_text: "Harry, I think I can hear people coming!" said Hermione, and she pointed Bellatrix’s wand at the waterfall and cried, "Protego!"

memories.description: Of course I knew the Cushioning Charm. But the Thief's Downfall proved that no matter how clever a disguise, some defenses will undo it.
memories.source_text: "C-Cushioning Charm," Hermione spluttered, as Ron pulled her to her feet, but to Harry’s horror he saw that she was no longer Bellatrix; instead she stood there in overlarge robes, sopping wet and completely herself;

memories.description: Of course Dumbledore cared about Harry. He cared enough to make plans for him even if he did not say everything.
memories.source_text: "Professor Dumbledore cared about Harry, very much," said Hermione in a low voice.

memories.description: Well, we all know the Order has been shattered and things look grim. That does not mean we stop thinking and acting.
memories.source_text: "‘The Order of the Phoenix is finished,’" Harry repeated.

memories.description: I feel horrified and sorry about what happened to Ariana. It makes me more determined that people who suffer because of lies or neglect need justice and care.
memories.source_text: "I’m so . . . I’m so sorry," Hermione whispered.

memories.description: Obviously the fake Galleons worked. Our secret communications kept going and gave people a lifeline even with the Carrows watching.
memories.source_text: "From his pocket he pulled a golden coin, and Harry recognized it as one of the fake Galleons that Dumbledore’s Army had used to send one another messages. 'These have been great,' said Neville, beaming at Hermione."

memories.description: Well, Neville looks to me like someone who really appreciated what we set up. Our efforts meant something to them.
memories.source_text: "These have been great," said Neville, beaming at Hermione.

memories.description: What the hell? They went after Neville's gran to try to get to him. That's vicious and completely unjustifiable.
memories.source_text: "They what?" said Harry, Ron, and Hermione together.

memories.description: Of course people here are relieved and excited to see us — this hideout is clearly a safe place for the D.A.
memories.source_text: "Look who it is! Didn’t I tell you?" As Harry emerged into the room beyond the passage, there were several screams and yells: "HARRY!" "It’s Potter, it’s POTTER!" "Ron!" "Hermione!"

memories.description: Well, I hate Bellatrix’s wand. Of course it feels wrong to me. It’s like carrying a piece of her and it unsettles me.
memories.source_text: “I hate this thing,” she said in a low voice. “I really hate it. It feels all wrong, it doesn’t work properly for me. . . . It’s like a bit of her.”

memories.description: Of course I know what that wand has done. It’s linked to terrible things and terrible people. That matters.
memories.source_text: “This is the wand that tortured Neville’s mum and dad, and who knows how many other people? This is the wand that killed Sirius!”

memories.description: Well, I miss my own wand. I wish Ollivander could have made me a replacement. It’s difficult working without it.
memories.source_text: “I miss my wand,” Hermione said miserably. “I wish Mr. Ollivander could have made me another one too.”

memories.description: I’ve transformed Ron into Bellatrix’s male lackey. Of course I need to know if the disguise is convincing enough for Harry.
memories.source_text: “There,” said Hermione, “how does he look, Harry?”

memories.description: Obviously I have to play the part precisely. I must be polite and commanding enough to make people believe I am Madam Lestrange.
memories.source_text: “Madam Lestrange,” murmured Tom, and as Hermione passed he inclined his head subserviently. “Good morning,” said Hermione, and as Harry crept past, still carrying Griphook piggyback under the Cloak, he saw Tom look surprised.

memories.description: Well, we cannot just rush off. We need a plan before we try anything.
memories.source_text: "Wait, wait!"

memories.description: Of course we do not have a plan yet. We need to think and prepare before attempting to get into Hogwarts.
memories.source_text: "We can’t just go, we haven’t got a plan, we need to"

memories.description: Well, the three of us do not fit properly under the cloak, at least not comfortably, though it might be dark enough that no one notices our feet.
memories.source_text: "But we don’t really fit —"

memories.description: I used an alias, Penelope Clearwater, and said I was a half-blood to try to fool them. Well, it was terrifying but necessary.
memories.source_text: "Penelope Clearwater," said Hermione. She sounded terrified, but convincing. "What’s your blood status?" "Half-blood," said Hermione.

memories.description: When they showed the picture from the Prophet I freaked out. Of course I shouted that it wasn't me, because they were trying to force a confession.
memories.source_text: "It isn’t! It isn’t me!" Hermione’s terrified squeak was as good as a confession.

memories.description: They're convinced I'm with Harry now because of that picture. Obviously that puts me in immediate danger.
memories.source_text: "' . . . known to be traveling with Harry Potter,'" repeated Greyback quietly.

memories.description: Well, it obviously makes more sense if I take the Cloak and go. I’m being practical about this.
memories.source_text: "No," said Hermione, "it makes much more sense if I take the Cloak and —"

memories.description: Well, obviously we don't know where the Horcrux is. That means we have to plan carefully and think logically about where to start.
memories.source_text: We don't know where it is.

memories.description: Of course I'm between Harry and Ron when they need to talk quietly. I'm trying to keep things calm and make sure we discuss this properly.
memories.source_text: She stood between them

memories.description: Well, Ron is right. We do not even know precisely what we are hunting. We need help from others to gather information.
memories.source_text: [I think Ron’s right. We don’t even know what we’re looking for, we need them.]

memories.description: Of course you do not have to do everything on your own, Harry. We can share the burden and help you.
memories.source_text: [You don’t have to do everything alone, Harry.]

memories.description: Well, of course, we have to try to Disapparate, Harry. We can't just stand here and wait.
memories.source_text: We're going to have to try to Disapparate, Harry!

memories.description: Of course I grabbed his arm and turned with him. We had to move together even if the charms might stop us.
memories.source_text: he felt Hermione take hold of his arm

memories.description: Well, Ron, I'm just as capable, of course I can do this and I will prove it.
memories.source_text: “Ron, I’m just as capable —”

memories.description: Of course the tapestry ripped and we ended up in a corridor full of duelers. That's ridiculous and dangerous.
memories.source_text: They ran down the next staircase and found themselves in a corridor full of duelers.

memories.description: Of course I understand what this means. If Voldemort knows a Horcrux is destroyed, we have to act immediately and precisely.
memories.source_text: He looked at Ron and Hermione, trying to tell them without words that Voldemort had just discovered the loss of one of the other Horcruxes. Time was running out fast

memories.description: Well, I get it. This is Dumbledore's task for the three of us. It is right that we see it through together and keep it private.
memories.source_text: They understood

memories.description: Well, of course I'm holding on to Harry's hand and running with him. We're getting away from the fighting straight away.
memories.source_text: he seized Hermione’s hand and tore down the steps into the grounds

memories.description: Well, we can’t just blast spells in the middle of that. Of course we risk hitting our own people, so we need to be careful and get out.
memories.source_text: [Harry, Ron, and Hermione raised their wands at once, ready to strike, but the duelers were weaving and darting around so much that there was a strong likelihood of hurting one of their own side if they cast curses.]

memories.description: Well, I'm completely knackered and I can hardly breathe. I can't speak properly right now.
memories.source_text: [Hermione so out of breath she could not speak.]

memories.description: Of course I think you can be a bit daft sometimes, but honestly, are you actually a wizard or what?
memories.source_text: [“Crookshanks?” wheezed Hermione, bent double, clutching her chest. “Are you a wizard, or what?”]

memories.description: Of course! The only way to end this is to get to the snake and to Voldemort. That's obvious and that's what we have to do.
memories.source_text: because that was, as Hermione said, the only way to end it

memories.description: Well, of course it was Fiendfyre. It is the one cursed fire that will destroy Horcruxes, but it's horrendously dangerous to use.
memories.source_text: "It must have been Fiendfyre!"

memories.description: What we can do is think fast and stick together. Panicking won't help. We have to get out and save anyone we can.
memories.source_text: "What can we do?" Hermione screamed over the deafening roars of the fire.

memories.description: We need to stay together and check everything. Also, that diadem on Harry's arm matters. It could be what we've been hunting for.
memories.source_text: "Let's stick together. I say we go — Harry, what's that on your arm?"

memories.description: Well, we were shoved aside before I could say anything because Hagrid thundered down the stairs with his umbrella, shouting not to hurt them.
memories.source_text: but before either Harry or Hermione could answer they were bowled aside: Hagrid had come thundering down the stairs, brandishing his flowery pink umbrella.

memories.description: Of course Hagrid ended up in the middle of the spiders, buried among them as spells drove the swarm back.
memories.source_text: Hagrid vanished amongst the spiders, and with a great scurrying, a foul swarming movement, they retreated under the onslaught of spells, Hagrid buried in their midst.

memories.description: Oh my! That's a giant. Of course I'm terrified, but we have to think this through.
memories.source_text: “Oh my — !”

memories.description: We're looking up at a giant trying to grab people from the upper windows. We must be careful and act logically.
memories.source_text: she and Ron caught up with Harry and gazed upward at the giant now trying to seize people through the window above.

memories.description: Well of course Ron can speak Parseltongue. He managed to open the Chamber of Secrets by getting the hissing right.
memories.source_text: "Show him, Ron!"

memories.description: Obviously the Room of Requirement is stopping summoning charms when it does not want items to be taken easily.
memories.source_text: "Accio Diadem!" cried Hermione in desperation, but nothing flew through the air toward them.

memories.description: Well this is obvious now. Ron and I are together. I couldn't hold back any longer. Of course I kissed him.
memories.source_text: There was a clatter as the basilisk fangs cascaded out of Hermione’s arms. Running at Ron, she flung them around his neck and kissed him full on the mouth.

memories.description: Of course I was the one to destroy the Hufflepuff cup. It had to be done and I did it.
memories.source_text: "Hermione stabbed it. Thought she should. She hasn't had the pleasure yet."

memories.description: Well, perfect. It's working the way it should.
memories.source_text: Perfect! panted Hermione.

memories.description: Of course I need to stop things if they're about to go wrong. Wait, hold on, make sure we're doing it right.
memories.source_text: Wait.

memories.description: Of course I know about the Horcruxes. We're keeping that knowledge safe between the three of us and now Neville will fill in if needed.
memories.source_text: "Ron and Hermione know that, but just in case they —"

memories.description: Well, obviously we must be methodical about this and have backups. Getting emotional won't help us, we need a plan and contingencies.
memories.source_text: "This was crucial, he must be like Dumbledore, keep a cool head, make sure there were backups, others to carry on."

memories.description: Well, of course I said the wand pieces looked beyond repair. I was convinced the damage was too severe to fix.
memories.source_text: Hermione had said that they could not be repaired, that the damage was too severe.

memories.description: Obviously I felt reverent about the Elder Wand at first, but I'm practical too and concerned about what keeping it would mean.
memories.source_text: Ron and Hermione looked at it with a reverence that, even in his befuddled and sleep-deprived state, Harry did not like to see.

memories.description: Well, of course Harry's right. It all makes sense when you think it through.
memories.source_text: "I think Harry’s right," said Hermione quietly.

memories.description: Blimey, it's platform nine and three quarters. Of course it is. That's where we're going.
memories.source_text: "Nine and three-quarters!" piped a small girl, also red-headed, who was holding her hand.

memories.description: I'm the youngest and a bit gangling and everyone knows it's my first time. Great, everyone's looking at me.
memories.source_text: "First time at Hogwarts? Ron's new, too." She pointed at the last and youngest of her sons. He was tall, thin, and gangling, with freckles, big hands and feet, and a long nose.

memories.description: I nearly passed out when I was sorted; I was dead green but then I collapsed into the chair next to Harry when it called Gryffindor.
memories.source_text: Harry clapped loudly with the rest as Ron collapsed into the chair next to him.

memories.description: I recognised Nearly Headless Nick because my brothers told me about him. I wasn't shy about saying it.
memories.source_text: “I know who you are!” said Ron suddenly. “My brothers told me about you — you’re Nearly Headless Nick!”

memories.description: I go proper green with nerves sometimes; being sorted was terrifying before it happened.
memories.source_text: He was pale green by now.

memories.description: Blimey, Fred and George were already shouting and catcalling when people started being sorted. They make everything louder, don't they?
memories.source_text: ["Harry could see Ron’s twin brothers catcalling."]

memories.description: When Hermione got Gryffindor I groaned. It was one of those 'oh, not again' sort of groans, but you know I was glad she wasn't anywhere else.
memories.source_text: ["Ron groaned."]

memories.description: Seeing Harry get sorted and the whole table cheering made me feel chuffed. I wanted him in our house, and when he got Gryffindor we all went a bit mad with happiness.
memories.source_text: ["The table on the far left exploded with cheers; Harry could see Ron's twin brothers catcalling."]

memories.description: Blimey, I want to know other people's stories. I asked Neville about his family because I’m interested in who’s from where and who’s got wizarding relatives.
memories.source_text: "What about you, Neville?"

memories.description: My brothers are proper mad about messing around. They’ll sing the daftest things and carry on, and I’m used to them being loud and ridiculous.
memories.source_text: Everybody finished the song at different times. At last, only the Weasley twins were left singing along to a very slow funeral march.

memories.description: My mum fusses over me loads. She still pokes my nose and calls me Ronnie even though I’m nearly as tall as Fred and George.
memories.source_text: “Ron, you’ve got something on your nose.”

memories.description: Percy’s a proper prefect now and he’s all proud about it. He’s got new robes and a shiny P badge.
memories.source_text: “Percy the Prefect.”

memories.description: My brothers are a pain but they look out for me in their own daft way.
memories.source_text: “Don’t worry, ickle Ronniekins is safe with us.”

memories.description: Chocolate Frog cards are a thing and everyone collects them. I’ve loads but I’m still missing Agrippa or Ptolemy. Typical.
memories.source_text: “I’m missing Agrippa.”

memories.description: School food is rubbish sometimes. My mum always forgets what I don’t like so I get stuck with the corned beef sandwiches.
memories.source_text: “You don’t want this, it’s all dry,” said Ron.

memories.description: Blimey, you're the Seeker? You must be the youngest House player in ages.
memories.source_text: “Seeker?” he said. “But first years never — you must be the youngest House player in about —”

memories.description: Wood told you? That's brilliant. I can't believe it, I'm gobsmacked.
memories.source_text: “Wood told me.” Ron was so amazed, so impressed, he just sat and gaped at Harry.

memories.description: You start training next week and it has to be secret. Right, my lips are shut.
memories.source_text: “I start training next week,” said Harry. “Only don’t tell anyone, Wood wants to keep it a secret.”

memories.description: I'm your second for any duel, alright? I'll stand by you, who does Malfoy have?
memories.source_text: “Of course he has,” said Ron, wheeling around. “I’m his second, who’s yours?”

memories.description: That lot won't walk all over us. I'm ready to back you up, no messing about.
memories.source_text: When Malfoy had gone, Ron and Harry looked at each other.

memories.description: You don't know you'll make a fool of yourself. Malfoy? He's all talk about Quidditch. I reckon he's full of it.
memories.source_text: "You don’t know that you’ll make a fool of yourself," said Ron reasonably. "Anyway, I know Malfoy’s always going on about how good he is at Quidditch, but I bet that’s all talk."

memories.description: Blimey, I keep saying how I nearly hit a hang glider on Charlie's old broom. It's a great story and it proves I've had my share of close calls.
memories.source_text: "Even Ron would tell anyone who’d listen about the time he’d almost hit a hang glider on Charlie’s old broom."

memories.description: I argued with Dean about soccer. I can't see what's good about a game where you can't fly and there's only one ball.
memories.source_text: "Ron had already had a big argument with Dean Thomas, who shared their dormitory, about soccer."

memories.description: Blimey, I wanted to take Malfoy on. When he grabbed Neville's Remembrall we were ready to fight.
memories.source_text: "Harry and Ron jumped to their feet. They were half hoping for a reason to fight Malfoy,"

memories.description: Ha, I loved it when Hooch told Malfoy he had his grip wrong. Good on her. Serves him right.
memories.source_text: "Harry and Ron were delighted when she told Malfoy he’d been doing it wrong for years."

memories.description: Bloody hell, Neville is hopeless on a broom when he's nervous. It's dangerous when someone gets that jumpy.
memories.source_text: "Come back, boy!" she shouted, but Neville was rising straight up like a cork shot out of a bottle — twelve feet — twenty feet."

memories.description: People only get killed in proper duels between skilled wizards. Harry and Malfoy will just throw sparks around and that's it. Malfoy probably thought Harry would turn him down.
memories.source_text: "But people only die in proper duels, you know, with real wizards. The most you and Malfoy’ll be able to do is send sparks at each other. Neither of you knows enough magic to do any real damage. I bet he expected you to refuse, anyway."

memories.description: If a wand fizzles, you chuck it and sock them. That's what I'd do.
memories.source_text: "Throw it away and punch him on the nose,"

memories.description: Blimey, I'm making a point here and calling attention when I need to.
memories.source_text: "Excuse me."

memories.description: Hermione can worry about being locked out herself. We've got to move or we'll be late and get into trouble.
memories.source_text: "That’s your problem," "We’ve got to go, we’re going to be late."

memories.description: I don't think Hermione believes she couldn't overhear us. I'm not surprised she jumped in to scold us.
memories.source_text: "Bet you could,"

memories.description: Dumbledore's a big name. If you don't know him, where have you been? He's famous, simple as that.
memories.source_text: Don’t tell me you’d never heard of Dumbledore!

memories.description: Moving pictures are the norm here. If Muggle photos don't move, that's proper weird to me.
memories.source_text: Do they? What, they don’t move at all? Weird!

memories.description: Bertie Bott's really does mean every flavour. You can get nasty ones like sprouts or even booger if you're unlucky.
memories.source_text: When they say every flavor, they mean every flavor

memories.description: Toads are a magnet for getting lost. I brought Scabbers instead, which is probably safer even if he's dull.
memories.source_text: If I’d brought a toad I’d lose it as quick as I could. Mind you, I brought Scabbers, so I can’t talk.

memories.description: Some of George's spells are rubbish. If a wand or spell came from him, it might not work properly.
memories.source_text: Stupid spell — George gave it to me, bet he knew it was a dud.

memories.description: I'm proper worried about the Sorting. If I'm not in Gryffindor Mum and Dad will be gutted. Slytherin would be a nightmare.
memories.source_text: I don’t know what they’ll say if I’m not. I don’t suppose Ravenclaw would be too bad, but imagine if they put me in Slytherin.

memories.description: Loads of Weasleys went into proper jobs after school. Charlie studies dragons and Bill works for Gringotts abroad.
memories.source_text: Charlie’s in Romania studying dragons, and Bill’s in Africa doing something for Gringotts

memories.description: Gringotts got targeted in a robbery attempt. Nobody's been caught and that freaked everybody out because it might be You-Know-Who.
memories.source_text: Did you hear about Gringotts? It’s been all over the Daily Prophet, but I don’t suppose you get that with the Muggles — someone tried to rob a high security vault.

memories.description: What the hell, Dean's shouting about a red card like this is a soccer match. I told him flat out, this isn't soccer, you can't just use those rules here.
memories.source_text: “What are you talking about, Dean?” said Ron. “Red card!” said Dean furiously. “In soccer you get shown the red card and you’re out of the game!” “But this isn’t soccer, Dean,” Ron reminded him.

memories.description: Blimey, even Hagrid reckons the rules should be tougher — people actually think Flint should've been sent off for that. That's mental.
memories.source_text: Hagrid, however, was on Dean’s side. “They oughta change the rules. Flint coulda knocked Harry outta the air.”

memories.description: Blimey, Harry! That was brilliant. Show him, Harry!
memories.source_text: He pulled his broomstick up a little to take it even higher, and heard screams and gasps of girls back on the ground and an admiring whoop from Ron.

memories.description: He's my mate and I'm right behind him. When Harry does something mad and brilliant, I'm cheering him on.
memories.source_text: He pulled his broomstick up a little to take it even higher, and heard ... an admiring whoop from Ron.

memories.description: Blimey, what do they think they're doing keeping a thing like that locked up? If any dog needs exercise, that one does.
memories.source_text: "What do they think they’re doing, keeping a thing like that locked up in a school?" "If any dog needs exercise, that one does."

memories.description: No, we don't mind. (I'm stuck for words, but I'm following Hermione anyway.)
memories.source_text: "No, we don’t mind," he said. "You’d

memories.description: That's your problem, not mine. We've got to hurry or we'll be late, so move it.
memories.source_text: "That’s your problem," said Ron. "We’ve got to go, we’re going to be late."

memories.description: You've really got some nerve, honestly. I'm not impressed with that at all.
memories.source_text: "You’ve got some nerve —" said Ron loudly.

memories.description: If you two get us caught I'll be furious. I swear I'll learn that Curse of the Bogies and use it on you if you let that happen.
memories.source_text: "If either of you get us caught, I’ll never rest until I’ve learned that Curse of the Bogies Quirrell told us about, and used it on you."

memories.description: Maybe he's not showing up. He might have chickened out, but I don't want to count on that.
memories.source_text: "He’s late, maybe he’s chickened out," Ron whispered.

memories.description: I thought I heard Mrs Norris at first, so I'm on edge and watching for Filch's cat or Filch himself.
memories.source_text: "Mrs Norris?" breathed Ron, squinting through the dark.

memories.description: Good idea, lock it in. We can use the lock to keep the troll contained. Simple and obvious.
memories.source_text: "Good idea," said Ron nervously.

memories.description: Oh no, it's the girls' bathroom. Blimey, Hermione's in there. We have to get back, even though that is terrible.
memories.source_text: "Oh, no," said Ron, pale as the Bloody Baron. "It's the girls' bathroom!"

memories.description: Blimey, that broom is a Nimbus Two Thousand. Comets might look flashy, but they're not in the same league as a Nimbus.
memories.source_text: "It’s not any old broomstick," he said, "it’s a Nimbus Two Thousand. What did you say you’ve got at home, Malfoy, a Comet Two Sixty?"

memories.description: Of course Comets are just showy. A Nimbus is proper quality. That's what matters.
memories.source_text: "Comets look flashy, but they’re not in the same league as the Nimbus."

memories.description: I took the bait and stuck up for Harry and the broom. I won't let Malfoy take the mickey about money and brooms.
memories.source_text: "What would you know about it, Weasley, you couldn’t afford half the handle," Malfoy snapped back. "I suppose you and your brothers have to save up twig by twig."

memories.description: Wow. Seeing that broom in person was something else. I'm well impressed and proper excited for Harry.
memories.source_text: "Wow," Ron sighed, as the broomstick rolled onto Harry’s bedspread.

memories.description: I joked that Harry rubbing it in would do us good. I'm cheeky and I like winding people up when we're on a roll.
memories.source_text: "Yes, don’t stop now," said Ron, "it’s doing us so much good."

memories.description: Trolls are supposed to be thick as two short planks, honestly. They'd be useless unless someone let them in.
memories.source_text: Don’t ask me, they’re supposed to be really stupid

memories.description: Could be Peeves messing about. Brilliant, a prank that nearly kills someone, that's just typical.
memories.source_text: Maybe Peeves let it in for a Halloween joke.

memories.description: There's this vile pong in the air, like old socks and a filthy loo. Whatever it is, it's huge and disgusting.
memories.source_text: Can you smell something?

memories.description: Blimey, I know the words, but I keep getting it wrong. I'm not the most graceful with my wand.
memories.source_text: “Wingardium Leviosa!” he shouted, waving his long arms like a windmill.

memories.description: Oh yeah? Do it yourself then, if you're that clever. I'm not having that smart-arse comment.
memories.source_text: “You do it, then, if you’re so clever,” Ron snarled.

memories.description: She rubs people up the wrong way. Honestly, no wonder she gets on people's nerves, she's a nightmare sometimes.
memories.source_text: “It’s no wonder no one can stand her,” he said to Harry as they pushed their way into the crowded corridor, “she’s a nightmare, honestly.”

memories.description: She must've noticed she hasn't got any friends. That's awkward, and I feel a bit guilty about it.
memories.source_text: Parvati Patil telling her friend Lavender that Hermione was crying in the girls’ bathroom and wanted to be left alone. Ron looked still more awkward at this,

memories.description: I can shout something daft and it might distract an opponent. Sometimes a bit of cheek does the trick.
memories.source_text: "Oy, pea-brain!"

memories.description: I actually did a spell in a crisis and it worked. Blimey, I managed to levitate the club and knock the troll out.
memories.source_text: "Wingardium Leviosa!"

memories.description: I didn't expect to pull that off. I can be useful when it matters, even if I don't always know what I'm doing.
memories.source_text: Ron was standing there with his wand still raised, staring at what he had done.

memories.description: Honestly, Hermione, you think teachers are saints? I'm with Harry. I wouldn't put anything past Snape. But what is he after? What is that dog guarding?
memories.source_text: "Honestly, Hermione, you think all teachers are saints or something," snapped Ron. "I'm with Harry. I wouldn't put anything past Snape. But what's he after? What's that dog guarding?"

memories.description: Neville, you can look! I was shouting that, buzzing that Harry could get back on his broom and wanting everyone to see.
memories.source_text: Neville, you can look!

memories.description: Blimey, Harry nearly swallowed the Snitch! That's mental. We're getting him a strong cup of tea and celebrating — we won by a massive amount.
memories.source_text: He was being made a cup of strong tea back in Hagrid’s hut, with Ron and Hermione.

memories.description: Come on, Hermione! Hurry up — Harry's broom is jumping all over the place and he can't hold on, for Merlin's sake.
memories.source_text: "Come on, Hermione," Ron muttered desperately.

memories.description: Blimey, you can’t let Malfoy push you around. He’s always walking all over people, but you’ve got to stand up to him and stop making it easy for him.
memories.source_text: “You’ve got to stand up to him, Neville!” said Ron. “He’s used to walking all over people, but that’s no reason to lie down in front of him and make it easier.”

memories.description: Fine, we'll find out about Flamel ourselves. Can't rely on Hagrid to tell us everything.
memories.source_text: "Just have to find out for ourselves, then," said Ron, and they left Hagrid looking disgruntled and hurried off to the library.

memories.description: I'd give anything for a cloak like that. It's brilliant, I'd love one.
memories.source_text: "I’d give anything for one of these," he said. "Anything."

memories.description: I hate maroon. Those sweaters are horrible, honestly.
memories.source_text: "I hate maroon," Ron moaned halfheartedly as he pulled it over his head.

memories.description: Come to my house and I'll show you the mirror. It might only show dead people, but you can see my family any time when you come round this summer.
memories.source_text: "You can come tonight, I’m going back, I want to show you the mirror." "I’d like to see your mum and dad," Ron said eagerly. "And I want to see all your family, all the Weasleys, you’ll be able to show me your other brothers and everyone." "You can see them any old time," said Ron. "Just come round my house this summer. Anyway, maybe it only shows dead people."

memories.description: The Sorcerer's Stone? Blimey, I didn't know about that. That's mental.
memories.source_text: "The what?" said Harry and Ron.

memories.description: Blimey, in that mirror I'm proper famous. I'm Head Boy, Quidditch captain and holding loads of cups. That's mental.
memories.source_text: "I am — I'm wearing the badge like Bill used to — and I'm holding the House Cup and the Quidditch Cup — I'm Quidditch captain, too!"

memories.description: I reckon that mirror might show the future. It looked like what I'd want to happen, not just some trick.
memories.source_text: "Do you think this mirror shows the future?"

memories.description: Mrs. Norris can give us away. Even if the Cloak hides us from people, animals like her could still cause trouble. We should leg it.
memories.source_text: "This isn't safe — she might have gone for Filch, I bet she heard us. Come on."

memories.description: I'm gutted Harry had it first, but I'm dead keen for a look. I can be selfish about stuff I'm excited by, but I want to share it with him too.
memories.source_text: "You had it to yourself all last night, give me a bit more time."

memories.description: Blimey, what are you doing? I was panicking, gray-faced, grabbing the binoculars because I wanted to see what's happening to Harry.
memories.source_text: What are you doing?

memories.description: I had the binoculars in my hands and I kept watching Harry. The broom's jumping higher every time someone gets close. That's mental.
memories.source_text: Ron grabbed the binoculars.

memories.description: Snape's had a hand in this. If Quirrell told him about the anti-dark force spell, I'm bloody convinced Snape's involved.
memories.source_text: "Snape's done it, then!" said Ron. "If Quirrell's told him how to break his Anti-Dark Force spell —"

memories.description: There might be a way past Fluffy that Snape could have discovered. I bet there's some book that explains how to get past a giant three-headed dog.
memories.source_text: "Maybe Snape's found out how to get past him without asking Hagrid," said Ron, looking up at the thousands of books surrounding them.

memories.description: Blimey, I still think we should do a bit of poking around. I can't just sit on my hands when there's adventure staring us in the face.
memories.source_text: "If we just do a bit of poking around —"

memories.description: We won. You won. We actually won. That's mental.
memories.source_text: "We won! You won! We won!"

memories.description: I gave Malfoy a black eye. Neville tried to take on Crabbe and Goyle and got knocked out but he'll be all right. We're having a party in the common room and Fred and George nicked cakes from the kitchens.
memories.source_text: "And I gave Malfoy a black eye, and Neville tried to take on Crabbe and Goyle single-handed! He’s still out cold but Madam Pomfrey says he’ll be all right — talk about showing Slytherin! Everyone’s waiting for you in the common room, we’re having a party, Fred and George stole some cakes and stuff from the kitchens."

memories.description: Blimey, the dragon actually bit me and it hurt. That creature is the most horrible thing I have ever met.
memories.source_text: “It bit me!” he said, showing them his hand, which was wrapped in a bloody handkerchief.

memories.description: Hagrid won the dragon egg in a card game in the village. It must have cost nothing to him but it's a right mess for everyone else.
memories.source_text: “Won it,” said Hagrid. “Las’ night. I was down in the village havin’ a few drinks an’ got into a game o’ cards with a stranger. Think he was quite glad ter get rid of it, ter be honest.”

memories.description: Life at Hogwarts is chaotic and stressful. I wish things could be peaceful for once instead of being swamped with extra work.
memories.source_text: Wonder what it’s like to have a peaceful life,” Ron sighed, as evening after evening they struggled through all the extra homework they were getting.

memories.description: Blimey, Harry looks awful. I told him to keep quiet for a moment because I was trying to focus, but then I had to ask what's wrong when I saw his face.
memories.source_text: ["Don't talk to me for a moment," said Ron when Harry sat down next to him, "I need to concen —" He caught sight of Harry’s face. "What's the matter with you? You look terrible."]

memories.description: I suggested faking illness and even joked about really breaking a leg to stop him playing. I'm all for anything that gets him out of a dodgy game.
memories.source_text: ["Say you're ill," said Ron. "Really break your leg," said Ron.]

memories.description: He's used to walking all over people, so Neville has to stand up to him. Come on, don't let Malfoy push you about, that's just making it easier for him.
memories.source_text: ["You've got to stand up to him, Neville!" said Ron. "He's used to walking all over people, but that's no reason to lie down in front of him and make it easier."]

memories.description: Blimey, Hagrid was looking up dragons in the library. He’s up to something dragon-related, I’m sure of it.
memories.source_text: Dragons!

memories.description: Dragon breeding’s illegal. It’s a mad idea to keep dragons about because Muggles would notice and it’s dangerous. Charlie’s got the scars to prove it.
memories.source_text: Dragon breeding was outlawed by the Warlocks’ Convention of 1709, everyone knows that.

memories.description: There are wild dragons in Britain like Welsh Greens and Hebridean Blacks and the Ministry has to keep wiping Muggles’ memories when they spot them.
memories.source_text: Of course there are, Common Welsh Green and Hebridean Blacks. The Ministry of Magic has a job hushing them up, I can tell you.

memories.description: Hermione could pretend to wait for Professor Flitwick to keep an eye on Snape.
memories.source_text: "You can pretend to be waiting for Professor Flitwick, you know."

memories.description: I think Harry is being reckless and that what he wants to do is insane and dangerous.
memories.source_text: "You're mad!"

memories.description: Hermione will still help despite being annoyed. We're all still trying to work together even when tensions are high.
memories.source_text: "Oh, shut up," said Hermione, but she agreed to go and watch out for Snape.

memories.description: Blimey, saying his name makes everyone jumpy. I can't stand it, so I hiss that he shouldn't be named, like it might make him listen.
memories.source_text: "Stop saying the name!" said Ron in a terrified whisper, as if he thought Voldemort could hear them.

memories.description: Honestly, keep that name out of our mouths. It's too dangerous and it makes my skin crawl every time someone says it.
memories.source_text: "Will you stop saying the name!" Ron hissed.

memories.description: Where are we off to now? I am sleepy and trying to get a grip on what is happening.
memories.source_text: "Where’re you going?" said Ron sleepily.

memories.description: What on earth are you lot going on about? I am confused and need it explained.
memories.source_text: "What are you talking about?"

memories.description: Fine, yes please, but we are in a rush. I just want to help but we do not have time to faff about.

memories.description: Blimey, Lockhart teaches nothing useful. All I learned from him is how not to let pixies loose.
memories.source_text: I haven't learned anything from him except not to set pixies loose

memories.description: I didn't hear the voice when Harry did. That freaked me out and made me wide eyed, like something's not right.
memories.source_text: The voice

memories.description: Riddle sounds exactly like Percy, doesn't he? Who told him to squeal on Hagrid anyway? That's suspicious as hell.
memories.source_text: "Riddle does sound like Percy - who asked him to squeal on Hagrid, anyway?" Ron tried a different tack.

memories.description: Yeah, clever. But I'm not over all this yet, am I?
memories.source_text: "That's clever of you," said Ron, who didn’t seem to have forgiven Ernie as readily as Harry.

memories.description: Ouch! Hey, what was that for? Blimey. Right, spiders... I see them now, but we can't go after them at the moment.
memories.source_text: "Ouch! What’re you —" Harry pointed out the spiders, following their progress with his eyes screwed up against the sun.

memories.description: Oh yeah. I can see them, but we can't follow them right now. That's just rotten timing.
memories.source_text: "Oh, yeah," said Ron, trying, and failing, to look pleased. "But we can’t follow them now —"

memories.description: Blimey, this looks bad, but I'm ready to move and do whatever's needed.
memories.source_text: "Okay," Ron sighed as though resigned to the worst, "I'm ready. Let's go."

memories.description: He's always thinking monsters aren't as bad as they're made out
memories.source_text: "That's exactly Hagrid's problem!" said Ron, thumping the wall of the cabin.

memories.description: That got him a cell in Azkaban
memories.source_text: "He always thinks monsters aren’t as bad as they’re made out, and look where it’s got him! A cell in Azkaban!"

memories.description: What was the point of sending us in there? I want to know what we found out
memories.source_text: "What was the point of sending us in there? What have we found out, I'd like to know?"

memories.description: I'm going with you. I won't let you go alone.
memories.source_text: "Me too," said Ron.

memories.description: What are we going to do? This is serious, isn't it?
memories.source_text: "What’re we going to do?" said Ron, whose eyes were flashing.

memories.description: We should go straight to McGonagall. She needs to know right now.
memories.source_text: "Should we go straight to McGonagall?"

memories.description: She points at the sink and says the eyes were there. So yeah, the sink's where we need to look.
memories.source_text: "Somewhere there," said Myrtle, pointing vaguely toward the sink in front of her toilet.

memories.description: Bloody hell, Lockhart looked petrified. He's not the brave expert act he tries to be.
memories.source_text: Lockhart was standing well back, a look of utter terror on his face.

memories.description: We're probably under the lake. That's where this tunnel leads.
memories.source_text: "Under the lake, probably," said Ron, squinting around at the dark, slimy walls.

memories.description: I shoved Lockhart into the pipe. Someone's got to get him moving or we'd all be stuck.
memories.source_text: Ron gave him a push, and he slid out of sight.

memories.description: This tunnel is black and slimy. It's proper grim down here.
memories.source_text: All three of them turned to stare into the darkness ahead.

memories.description: I think menacing books are a real risk. I got worried when Harry tried to pick up that wet little book.
memories.source_text: "What? Are you crazy? It could be dangerous."

memories.description: I've heard from Dad that the Ministry confiscates dangerous books. Some can do seriously nasty things like burning your eyes out.
memories.source_text: "Some of the books the Ministry’s confiscated — Dad’s told me — there was one that burned your eyes out."

memories.description: There are cursed books that mess with your mind. People who read certain books can end up acting really weird, like speaking only in limericks.
memories.source_text: "And everyone who read Sonnets of a Sorcerer spoke in limericks for the rest of their lives."

memories.description: Some books can enchant you so you cannot stop reading them. That sounds dangerous and ridiculous at the same time.
memories.source_text: "And some old witch in Bath had a book that you could never stop reading! You just had to wander around with your nose in it, trying to do everything one-handed."

memories.description: I told Harry to say something in Parseltongue, urging him to try and open the tap.
memories.source_text: "Harry," said Ron. "Say something. Something in Parseltongue."

memories.description: I shook my head when Harry hesitated, showing I wanted him to stop wasting time and just do it.
memories.source_text: He looked at Ron, who shook his head.

memories.description: I'll try and shift some of this rock so you can get back through. I'm going to do whatever I can to help Harry, even if I'm shaking.
memories.source_text: "I'll try and shift some of this rock," said Ron, who seemed to be trying to keep his voice steady. "So you can — can get back through. And, Harry —"

memories.description: Blimey, Lockhart really bounces off. I told him to leave us because we can manage walking the rest ourselves.
memories.source_text: Why don’t you leave us here, sir, we’ve only got one more corridor to go

memories.description: Gone to curl his hair, more like. I don't exactly trust him to be any use in a proper emergency.
memories.source_text: Prepare his class

memories.description: Wondering if Hermione saw the attacker before she was petrified. If he sneaked up on them all, no one will ever know unless she managed to warn someone first.
memories.source_text: Wonder if she did see the attacker, though?

memories.description: How's a giant snake been moving about the school without anyone seeing it? That doesn't add up.
memories.source_text: "But how's the basilisk been getting around the place?"

memories.description: The entrance might be somewhere ordinary like a bathroom. Blimey, it could be hidden in plain sight.
memories.source_text: "The entrance to the Chamber of Secrets!" "What if it’s a bathroom?"

memories.description: I've been hearing that voice inside the walls. It's been going on and it's got me spooked.
memories.source_text: I’ve been hearing that voice inside the walls.

memories.description: Blimey, the entrance to the Chamber might be in Moaning Myrtle's bathroom. What if that's where the whole thing starts?
memories.source_text: The entrance to the Chamber of Secrets! What if it’s a bathroom? What if it’s in -

memories.description: What're we going to do? Should we go straight to McGonagall? I'm not staying here while this goes on.
memories.source_text: What’re we going to do?

memories.description: I'll try and shift some of this rock so you can get back through. I'll stay and do what I can, even if I'm shaking.
memories.source_text: "I'll try and shift some of this rock," said Ron, who seemed to be trying to keep his voice steady. "So you can — can get back through."

memories.description: I'm alive and kicking, but Lockhart's a mess after getting blasted by his own wand. I even kicked him in the shins.
memories.source_text: I'm here! I'm okay - this git's not, though - he got blasted by the wand -

memories.description: We can't get through that rockfall. It's going to take ages to clear unless we find another way.
memories.source_text: What now? We can't get through - it'll take ages.

memories.description: I'm getting fed up with Lockhart. Honestly, the bloke's useless when things go wrong.
memories.source_text: There was a dull thud and a loud "ow!" It sounded as though Ron had just kicked Lockhart in the shins.

memories.description: I reckon if the diary had powers they'd be obvious. Maybe it's shy, but seriously, why not just get rid of the thing?
memories.source_text: “If it has, it’s hiding them very well,” said Ron. “Maybe it’s shy. I don’t know why you don’t chuck it, Harry.”

memories.description: Riddle could have got his award for any old reason. It might not be anything to do with the Chamber at all.
memories.source_text: “Could’ve been anything,” said Ron. “Maybe he got thirty O.W.L.s or saved a teacher from the giant squid. Maybe he murdered Myrtle; that would’ve done everyone a favor. . . .”

memories.description: There is nothing written in the diary as far as I can see. That right there is a problem for Hermione's brilliant idea.
memories.source_text: “That’s a brilliant theory, Hermione,” said Ron, “with just one tiny little flaw. There’s nothing written in his diary.”

memories.description: I did not touch Percy's Head Boy badge, okay? Don't go accusing me.
memories.source_text: "I haven't touched it, all right?" Ron roared back.

memories.description: Scabbers's rat tonic is missing too. I'm frantically checking my trunk and everything. I might have left it in the bar but I'm packed and ready to go.
memories.source_text: "So's Scabbers's rat tonic," said Ron, throwing things out of his trunk to look.

memories.description: Ginny, you're alive! I can't believe it. What on earth happened and where did that bird even come from?
memories.source_text: "Ginny!" Ron thrust an arm through the gap in the rock to pull her through first. "You’re alive! I don’t believe it! What happened? How — what — where did that bird come from?"

memories.description: Lockhart's had his memory wiped. The Memory Charm backfired and he doesn't know who he is. He's a danger if he wanders about like that.
memories.source_text: "His memory’s gone," said Ron. "The Memory Charm backfired. Hit him instead of us. Hasn’t got a clue who he is, or where he is, or who we are. I told him to come and wait here. He’s a danger to himself."

memories.description: Ordinary birds couldn't lift someone the size of Harry up that pipe. That bird must be something else.
memories.source_text: "But you’re much too heavy for a bird to pull up there —"

memories.description: Lockhart has to hold Ginny's hand and behave. I don't trust him to do anything sensible but he can at least hang on.
memories.source_text: "He means you," said Ron sharply to Lockhart. "You hold Ginny’s other hand —"

memories.description: Myrtle fancies Harry, which is ridiculous, but it means Ginny's upset and needs me to worry about her more than petty stuff.
memories.source_text: "Harry! I think Myrtle’s grown fond of you! You’ve got competition, Ginny!"

memories.description: We escaped to Moaning Myrtle's bathroom and now we have to decide where to go next to help Ginny.
memories.source_text: "Where now?" said Ron, with an anxious look at Ginny. Harry pointed.

memories.description: Blimey, Hagrid's been up since five getting ready for his first lesson. I'm anxious and curious about what he'll have prepared.
memories.source_text: "Wonder what he’s been getting ready?" said Ron, a note of anxiety in his voice.

memories.description: We need to hurry. Divination's at the top of North Tower and it'll take about ten minutes to get there, so we should move now.
memories.source_text: "We’d better go, look, Divination’s at the top of North Tower. It’ll take us ten minutes to get there."

memories.description: When Trelawney's voice appeared from the shadows I was startled and looking for where she was. That voice came out of nowhere and was creepy.
memories.source_text: "Where is she?"

memories.description: Blimey, tell us straight away. Don't keep stuff back when it's about something that serious.
memories.source_text: What were you going to tell us?

memories.description: How dense would Harry have to be to go looking for someone who wants to kill him? That's mental, he mustn't do that.
memories.source_text: How thick would Harry have to be, to go looking for a nutter who wants to kill him?

memories.description: Honestly, I want to go to Hogsmeade so I can get into Honeydukes and try all the sweets. That's the main reason, not the history stuff.
memories.source_text: I just want to get inside Honeydukes!

memories.description: That Sneakoscope went mad in the trunk. It's the cheap kind but it still makes a right racket. We should get it checked in Hogsmeade if we can.
memories.source_text: It’s coming from your trunk... Is that a Sneakoscope? ... it’s a very cheap one

memories.description: Blimey, Harry actually did it. You bow, you wait, and if the beast bows back you can touch it. Simple really, once you get the nerve.
memories.source_text: Good man, Harry!

memories.description: I thought it looked easier than it is, but seeing Malfoy get his arm sliced shows it's not a joke. You don't go showing off with dangerous creatures.
memories.source_text: This is very easy... I knew it must have been, if Potter could do it.

memories.description: Harry's alright. He handled Buckbeak properly and I feel proud we were there to see him do it.
memories.source_text: Good work, Harry!

memories.description: I want to know if Malfoy is badly hurt, but I don't think it's that serious.
memories.source_text: "How is he?" said Ron as they all sat down.

memories.description: Don't worry Hagrid, we'll back you up and tell the truth. We're on your side.
memories.source_text: "Yeah, don’t worry, Hagrid, we’ll back you up," said Ron.

memories.description: Malfoy says he's in agony and is wrapped in bandages, but that sounds like he's playing it up to me.
memories.source_text: "Madam Pomfrey fixed him best she could," said Hagrid dully, "but he’s sayin’ it’s still agony . . . covered in bandages . . . moanin’ . . ."

memories.description: That Malfoy was a right coward on the train. He came running like a prat, so you can shut it, Malfoy.
memories.source_text: "He wasn’t so cocky last night when the dementors were down at our end of the train. Came running into our compartment, didn’t he, Fred?"

memories.description: Blimey, Hermione's timetable looks mental. No one can be in three classes at once, it just can't happen.
memories.source_text: "But look," said Ron, laughing, "see this morning? Nine o’clock, Divination. And underneath, nine o’clock, Muggle Studies. And look — underneath that, Arithmancy, nine o’clock."

memories.description: I care when Hermione makes herself nuts. I might moan, but I don't want her overdoing it, so I call her out when something's daft.
memories.source_text: "Well, then —"

memories.description: Blimey, that hug nearly cracked me. Hagrid can’t hold it together right now.
memories.source_text: He grabbed both Harry and Ron and pulled them into a bone-breaking hug.

memories.description: Alright then, I shouldn’t be letting Harry go off after dark to see Hagrid. I’ll stop him next time, I promise.
memories.source_text: "YEH’RE NOT TO GO WANDERIN’ AROUND AFTER DARK, HARRY! AN’ YOU TWO! LETTIN’ HIM!"

memories.description: Blimey, I called Malfoy out straight away when he stared at Harry. I won't let him sneer without answering.
memories.source_text: "What, Malfoy? Need something else skinned?"

memories.description: He's definitely trying to wind Harry up. I reckon Malfoy is lying to get Harry to do something daft.
memories.source_text: "He’s making it up," said Ron savagely. "He’s trying to make you do something stupid."

memories.description: Snape will order me around in front of everyone just to humiliate me. What the hell, sir?
memories.source_text: "Weasley, cut up Malfoy’s roots for him," said Snape without looking up.

memories.description: I won't be made to do Malfoy's work without a fight. I lost my temper and chopped his roots badly on purpose. That showed him.
memories.source_text: "There’s nothing wrong with your arm," he hissed at Malfoy.

memories.description: Malfoy tries to threaten us by name-dropping his father and the Ministry. Bloody hell, he always uses his family to get his own way.
memories.source_text: "I’m afraid he won’t be a teacher much longer," said Malfoy in a tone of mock sorrow. "Father’s not very happy about my injury -- he’s complained to the school governors. And to the Ministry of Magic. Father’s got a lot of influence, you know."

memories.description: I mean it. If Malfoy makes one more crack about my family I will not stand for it. Bloody hell, I am done with his rubbish.
memories.source_text: "I’m not going to take any crap from Malfoy this year," he said angrily.

memories.description: I am absolutely starving and all I can think about is the feast. Food is a priority for me, simple as that.
memories.source_text: "I’m starving. I want to get to the feast," said Ron.

memories.description: When someone looks out of sorts I panic a bit. I worry that things are worse than they are. Of course he is breathing, but I still freak out.
memories.source_text: "I mean — he hasn’t died, has he?"

memories.description: Blimey, tea-leaf reading is nonsense. I called it out because we were both sniggering and it felt daft to sit there taking it seriously.
memories.source_text: "You need your Inner Eye tested, if you ask me,"

memories.description: I tried to make something of Harry's cup and came up with daft things like a bowler hat and an acorn. Honestly, it was just guesses and I joked about him working for the Ministry.
memories.source_text: "There's a blob a bit like a bowler hat,"

memories.description: If the tea predicts money, I'm not above asking for a loan. That's classic me, hopeful and a bit cheeky when fortune gets mentioned.
memories.source_text: "'A windfall, unexpected gold.' Excellent, you can lend me some . . ."

memories.description: I admitted I got it wrong when the teacher read it properly. Bloody hell, I was embarrassed but it was true, I misread it.
memories.source_text: "I thought that was a bowler hat,"

memories.description: Blimey, you actually bought that monster?
memories.source_text: “You bought that monster?” said Ron, his mouth hanging open.

memories.description: That thing nearly scalped me, honestly, it attacked me.
memories.source_text: “Hermione, that thing nearly scalped me!” said Ron.

memories.description: What about Scabbers? He needs rest and relaxation, how's he going to get it with that cat around?
memories.source_text: “And what about Scabbers?” said Ron, pointing at the lump in his chest pocket. “He needs rest and relaxation! How’s he going to get it with that thing around?”

memories.description: I wonder why no one wanted that cat, yeah right.
memories.source_text: “I wonder why,” said Ron sarcastically as they set off toward the Leaky Cauldron.

memories.description: Blimey, that cat nearly scalped me. That could have been nasty.
memories.source_text: “Hermione, that thing nearly scalped me!” said Ron.

memories.description: Scabbers needs to rest. With Crookshanks around, Scabbers won't get any peace. That's not fair.
memories.source_text: “And what about Scabbers?” said Ron, pointing at the lump in his chest pocket. “He needs rest and relaxation! How’s he going to get it with that thing around?”

memories.description: If anyone caught Sirius Black there might be a reward. Could do with the money, honestly.
memories.source_text: “Would we get a reward if we caught him?” asked Ron. “It’d be good to get some more money —”

memories.description: I wonder why no one wanted Crookshanks. Yeah right, like that's surprising.
memories.source_text: “I wonder why,” said Ron sarcastically as they set off toward the Leaky Cauldron.

memories.description: Blimey, I really thought Harry was having a fit. He went rigid, fell out of his seat and started twitching and it scared me.
memories.source_text: "'I thought you were having a fit or something,' said Ron, who still looked scared. 'You went sort of rigid and fell out of your seat and started twitching'"
