memories.source_text: None of us could break through, and that massive Death Eater was still firing off jinxes all over the place, they were bouncing off the walls and barely missing us.

memories.description: Blimey, I thought Snape's mum wasn't much to look at. That does not help his image.
memories.source_text: "I thought she wasn’t much of a looker," said Ron.

memories.description: Why on earth didn't Snape turn me in when he knew about the book? It's proper puzzling.
memories.source_text: "But why didn’t he turn you in?"

memories.description: Right, that makes sense to me now. Snape putting on airs to impress the pure-bloods sounds exactly like something he'd do.
memories.source_text: "Yeah, that fits," said Harry. "He’d play up the pure-blood side so he could get in with Lucius Malfoy and the rest of them. . . ." "Yeah, that fits," said Harry. "He’d play up the pure-blood side so he could get in with Lucius Malfoy and the rest of them. . . . He’s just like Voldemort."

memories.description: Blimey, I'm holding Hermione and stroking her hair to try and comfort her. I'm upset too and I'm not ashamed to say it
memories.source_text: Ron ... was now holding Hermione and stroking her hair while she sobbed into his shoulder, tears dripping from the end of his own long nose.

memories.description: I'm crying along with her. This is horrible and it's getting to me
memories.source_text: tears dripping from the end of his own long nose.

memories.description: Anyone else we know been killed? I want to know if more of our lot are gone.
memories.source_text: "Anyone else we know died?" Ron asked Hermione, who was perusing the Evening Prophet.

memories.description: Blimey, that was awkward. I looked away when Ginny kissed Harry. I don\'t want to make it weird but notice taken.
memories.source_text: "I\'m going to go to bed," yawned Ginny. "I haven\'t been sleeping that well since . . . well . . . I could do with some sleep." She kissed Harry (Ron looked away pointedly) ...

memories.description: Blimey, I was sure Ginny was having me on, and now I can see she really was. That's mental.
memories.source_text: "I knew Ginny was lying about that tattoo,"

memories.description: We're taking Harry on the bike. I'll be with him. Not sure how I feel about all the attention but that's the plan.
memories.source_text: "An’ you’re with me, Harry. That all righ’?"

memories.description: He wasn't bitten at the full moon so Bill probably won't be a full werewolf, but there could still be contamination or lasting damage.
memories.source_text: "But he wasn't bitten at the full moon," said Ron, who was gazing down into his brother's face as though he could somehow force him to mend just by staring. "Greyback hadn't transformed, so surely Bill won't be a — a real — ?"

memories.description: Dumbledore sent Bill into that fight and Bill got hurt. Dumbledore owes him and he can't just leave Bill like this.
memories.source_text: "Dumbledore might know something that'd work, though," Ron said. "Where is he? Bill fought those maniacs on Dumbledore's orders, Dumbledore owes him, he can't leave him in this state —"

memories.description: They're talking about closing Hogwarts. Blimey, that would be a right mess.
memories.source_text: "They’re talking about closing the school," said Harry. "Lupin said they would," said Ron.

memories.description: I wanted to know straightaway if Harry had got the Horcrux. It mattered more than anything at that moment.
memories.source_text: "So?" said Ron in a very low voice. "Did you find one? Did you get it? A — a Horcrux?"

memories.description: Harry didn't get the real one. He has a fake locket, which means someone beat us to it.
memories.source_text: Wordlessly, Harry pulled the fake locket from his pocket, opened it, and passed it to Ron.

memories.description: The initials R.A.B. were inside the locket. Who on earth is R.A.B. and why did they take it?
memories.source_text: "R.A.B.," whispered Ron, "but who was that?"

memories.description: Blimey, I couldn't help smirking. Harry in that sidecar looked like a kid in a bumper car and I couldn't help it.
memories.source_text: "Ron smirked at the sight of him sitting there like a child in a bumper car."

memories.description: I felt awkward and guilty about grabbing Tonks in front of Lupin. I tried to play it cool but I wasn't.
memories.source_text: "Hold tight now, Ron," said Tonks, and Harry saw Ron throw a furtive, guilty look at Lupin before placing his hands on either side of her waist."

memories.description: Blimey, George's ear is gone but he is crackin' jokes. That's George for you, still daft after everything.
memories.source_text: "What’s wrong with him?" croaked Fred, looking terrified. "Is his mind affected?" "Saintlike," repeated George, opening his eyes and looking up at his brother.

memories.description: I was worried and I said so. Seeing George hurt made me sharp, I wanted to know if he was all right straight away.
memories.source_text: "How’s George?" asked Lupin. "What’s wrong with him?" piped up Ron.

memories.description: Bloody hell, Mad-Eye is dead. That makes this whole thing real and terrible. It feels like nothing will be the same.
memories.source_text: "Bill! Thank God, thank God —" Mrs. Weasley ran forward, but the hug Bill bestowed upon her was perfunctory. Looking directly at his father, he said, "Mad-Eye’s dead."

memories.description: Blimey, this is completely mental. Pretending to be Harry is a whole different kettle of fish because it's the first time for everyone and it's dangerous.
memories.source_text: "- because it’s the first time for all of us," said Ron. "This is different, pretending to be me -"

memories.description: Look, I know we are outnumbered and if things go wrong we're in serious trouble. That's why we have to be careful, not stupid.
memories.source_text: "Yeah, thirteen of us against one bloke who’s not allowed to use magic; we’ve got no chance," said Fred.

memories.description: I will push Harry to do what needs doing. I grimace and give him that look because I want him to cooperate for everyone's sake.
memories.source_text: Harry glanced at Ron, who grimaced at him in a just-do-it sort of way.

memories.description: What the hell? Why is nobody at the Ministry willing to stand up? People are just terrified and that's not good enough.
memories.source_text: Isn’t anyone at the Ministry prepared to stand up to him?” asked Ron angrily.

memories.description: Get to the point! I'm not having this dragged out, just tell us what happened.
memories.source_text: "Get to the point!" said Ron.

memories.description: Can you hear us complaining? We're not thrilled but we're not going to kick off about it either.
memories.source_text: "Can you hear us complaining?" said Ron.

memories.description: Blimey, so she actually nicked Dumbledore's books. That's mental but if Hermione says it's for the Horcrux hunt, I'm in.
memories.source_text: Ron Weasley, Hermione Granger, Harry Potter are all present in the scene where Hermione reveals she summoned books from Dumbledore's study.

memories.description: Why would he bother asking Slughorn if he could have already read how to make one in the library?
memories.source_text: "Why did he have to ask Slughorn how to make a Horcrux, then, if he’d already read that?" asked Ron.

memories.description: Is there any way to put yourself back together after splitting your soul?
memories.source_text: "Isn’t there any way of putting yourself back together?" Ron asked.

memories.description: No, I can't see Voldemort trying that. He wouldn't attempt it, simple as that.
memories.source_text: "No," said Ron, before Harry could answer.

memories.description: Bloody hell, we've actually got a lot of basilisk fangs and they'd do the job for destroying Horcruxes. Lucky us.
memories.source_text: "Oh well, lucky we've got such a large supply of basilisk fangs, then," said Ron. "I was wondering what we were going to do with them."

memories.description: Hang on, that would be a real comfort, wouldn't it? I thought the bit of soul in a Horcrux might just move on if its container was smashed.
memories.source_text: "Which would be a real comfort to me, I’m sure,"

memories.description: Hang on, the bit of soul in that diary was possessing Ginny, wasn't it? That explains why flushing it didn't get rid of it.
memories.source_text: "The bit of soul in that diary was possessing Ginny, wasn’t it?"

memories.description: I took Perkins on, like you do. Someone had to deal with the boring Ministry types.
memories.source_text: Ron took charge of Mr. Weasley's old Ministry colleague Perkins

memories.description: Yeah, I know Luna. Isn't she with you? Kind of weird question, but yeah I know her.
memories.source_text: "Yes," said Ron. "Isn't she with you?"

memories.description: Our gnomes have a cracking vocabulary. Fred and George taught them half of it. Bloody brilliant.
memories.source_text: "Ours do know a lot of excellent swear words," said Ron, "but I think Fred and George taught them those."

memories.description: Blimey, Mum's going mental about tiny things like a speck of dust and I don't see why the Delacours have to arrive so early. It's not helping her stress.
memories.source_text: Ginny’s probably left a speck of dust on a poxy napkin ring," said Ron. "I dunno why the Delacours have got to come two days before the wedding.

memories.description: This R.A.B. person might have nicked the real locket. If they destroyed it that's one less Horcrux for us to worry about and that's brilliant.
memories.source_text: This R.A.B. person," he said. "You know, the one who stole the real locket?

memories.description: Guests turning up early are only making Mum more stressed. We need to sort things that actually help, not invite more bother.
memories.source_text: "Well, guests aren’t going to help Mum’s stress levels," said Ron.

memories.description: Look, I can open a hatch and bring the ghoul down whenever I want. I’ve set it up so it lives in my attic and can be shown off.
memories.source_text: "Descendo," muttered Ron, pointing his wand at the low ceiling.

memories.description: I’m telling everyone the ghoul is me with spattergroit. It’s meant to pass for me, covered in pustules and everything, so people will think I’m too ill to be anywhere else.
memories.source_text: "He’s me, see?" said Ron.

memories.description: The plan is simple. If Hermione and I don’t show, people will assume we’re with Harry. That should send Death Eaters to our families instead of to Harry.
memories.source_text: "Look, when we three don’t turn up at Hogwarts again, everyone’s going to think Hermione and I must be with you, right?"

memories.description: Spattergroit is supposedly deadly contagious, so showing a ghoul that looks infected will keep inquisitive people away from Mum and Dad.
memories.source_text: "Spattergroit’s really contagious, so they’re not going to want to go near him."

memories.description: My dad is in on this. He, Fred and George helped transform the ghoul into the perfect sick-looking decoy.
memories.source_text: "Dad is. He helped Fred and George transform the ghoul."

memories.description: I reckon Moody might have survived. I don't want to accept he's gone without question.
memories.source_text: "I reckon he might have survived."

memories.description: The Death Eaters would cover their tracks. They'd tidy things up so nobody finds Moody's body, so not finding him doesn't prove anything.
memories.source_text: "The Death Eaters probably tidied up after themselves, that’s why no one’s found him," said Ron wisely.

memories.description: Moody would say 'constant vigilance' and I'd know what he meant. Also, I definitely won't trust that cowardly little squit Mundungus again.
memories.source_text: "He’d tell us to learn from what happened to him. And what I’ve learned is not to trust that cowardly little squit, Mundungus."

memories.description: I'm fed up of arguing about this. I'm blunt about it and want us to get on with the plan rather than keep debating.
memories.source_text: "Shut up," Ron advised him.

memories.description: What the hell? I can't believe no one at the Ministry is standing up to You-Know-Who. People are just terrified and doing nothing.
memories.source_text: "Isn’t anyone at the Ministry prepared to stand up to him?" asked Ron angrily.

memories.description: There are rumors about people disappearing. The Muggle Studies professor hasn't been seen for weeks and people are saying she resigned, but that smells wrong.
memories.source_text: "There are nasty rumors going around; I for one don’t believe the Muggle Studies professor at Hogwarts resigned. She hasn’t been seen for weeks now."

memories.description: Blimey, Luna just calmly took the mick while I snorted. I went bright red again and couldn't help it.
memories.source_text: "Ron can laugh," said Luna serenely as Harry led her and Xenophilius toward their seats... Ron, passing them in the opposite direction, let out a loud snort.

memories.description: I noticed Krum's beard and thought it looked stupid. I muttered it to Harry because I was embarrassed and jealous.
memories.source_text: "After a few moments he muttered to Harry, 'Did you see he's grown a stupid little beard?'"

memories.description: Hermione's reaction to Viktor made my ears go scarlet. Bloody hell, it was obvious I was mortified.
memories.source_text: "Viktor!" she shrieked, and dropped her small beaded bag... As she scrambled, blushing, to pick it up, she said, 'I didn't know you were — goodness — it's lovely to see — how are you?' Ron's ears had turned bright red again.

memories.description: Hang on. So the bit of soul in that diary was possessing Ginny, wasn't it? That's mental. How does that even work then?
memories.source_text: "Hang on," said Ron, frowning. "The bit of soul in that diary was possessing Ginny, wasn’t it? How does that work, then?"

memories.description: Hold on, I was surprised Dumbledore left things to all three of us. I didn't expect to be remembered in his will.
memories.source_text: "A-all of us?" said Ron. "Me and Hermione too?"

memories.description: I don't think I was that close to Dumbledore. I kept meaning to say more, but I always felt like Harry was the one he knew best.
memories.source_text: "Me? Not — not really . . . It was always Harry who . . ."

memories.description: Dumbledore left me the Deluminator. I couldn't believe it at first when Scrimgeour handed it over and I just sat there stunned.
memories.source_text: "'To Ronald Bilius Weasley, I leave my Deluminator, in the hope that he will remember me when he uses it.'"

memories.description: I figured the Deluminator is for putting out lights. That's the obvious use, isn't it? I was baffled by why he'd give me something so special.
memories.source_text: "'Why would he have left you an item so rare?' ... 'To what use did he think you would put his Deluminator, Mr. Weasley?'" and Ron's reply "Put out lights, I s'pose," mumbled Ron.

memories.description: Where are we? I need to know where we've landed so we can get our bearings.
memories.source_text: "Where are we?" said Ron’s voice.

memories.description: Blimey, the Order were at the wedding. They're still there to help, so we can't waste time going back.
memories.source_text: "Most of the Order was there, they’ll look after everyone."

memories.description: How the ruddy hell did Hermione fit all that in her bag? That's mental, she planned this properly.
memories.source_text: "How the ruddy hell — ?"

memories.description: When something's dodgy I reach for my wand and act. I jump in to protect mates, even if I don't always see the whole picture at first.
memories.source_text: The two workmen made identical movements, and Harry mirrored them without conscious thought: All three of them drew their wands.

memories.description: He can't have the Trace. Once you're seventeen the Trace breaks, that's the rule. You can't stick it on an adult.
memories.source_text: "He can’t have," said Ron. "The Trace breaks at seventeen, that’s Wizarding law, you can’t put it on an adult."

memories.description: If Harry hasn't been near any Death Eaters recently then who could've put a Trace back on him? That doesn't add up.
memories.source_text: "But Harry hasn’t been near a Death Eater in the last twenty-four hours. Who’s supposed to have put a Trace back on him?" Hermione did not reply.

memories.description: We need somewhere safe to hide and think. We can't stay here forever, we have to find a place where we're less likely to be found.
memories.source_text: "We need a safe place to hide," said Ron.

memories.description: I try to keep Hermione calm when she's scared even if I come across clumsy. I'm there for my mates when things go wrong.
memories.source_text: "It’s all r-right. . . . It’s g-gone. . . ." Ron, who was shaking from head to foot, patting her clumsily on the shoulder and saying, "It’s all r-right."

memories.description: Blimey, I heard Harry muttering Gregorovitch and I haven't a clue who he means. I suggested Gorgovitch by mistake because I thought he meant a Quidditch player.
memories.source_text: 'Who’s Gregorovitch?' 'I dunno, do I? You were the one saying it.'

memories.description: I still can't stand thinking about that Gorgovitch bloke. Seriously, I'd rather forget him.
memories.source_text: 'I try not to either,' said Ron.

memories.description: I gave Harry a joke present from Fred and George about charming witches. I thought he'd get a laugh from it and I reckon it was a good one.
memories.source_text: 'Here’s your present. Unwrap it up here, it’s not for my mother’s eyes.' 'A book?' 'This isn’t your average book... Twelve Fail-Safe Ways to Charm Witches.'

memories.description: I walked in on Harry and Ginny. I felt awkward and pointed it out. My ears went scarlet and I couldn't help being a bit blunt about it.
memories.source_text: The door banged open behind them and they jumped apart. 'Oh,' said Ron pointedly.

memories.description: I thought my mum's cake trick and the rest of the party stuff was spot on. I showed Harry the thumbs-up because I was chuffed with how it looked.
memories.source_text: He gave Harry the thumbs-up and mouthed, Good one.

memories.description: Blimey, that Snitch Harry caught when he was little is the same one. I remember him almost swallowing it.
memories.source_text: "That was the one you nearly swallowed!"

memories.description: Dumbledore was clever but dodgy. I think he was a bit cracked for doing things like leaving Harry a Snitch instead of explaining himself.
memories.source_text: "I always said he was mental. Brilliant and everything, but cracked. Leaving Harry an old Snitch — what the hell was that about?"

memories.description: I know the sword matters and I’m worried why Dumbledore wanted Harry to have it. It feels serious and confusing.
memories.source_text: "And the sword," said Ron finally, "Why did he want Harry to have the sword?"

memories.description: The Deluminator actually works. I clicked it and the lamp went out and then the light came back to us when we wanted it.
memories.source_text: "Hold ing it up in front of him, he clicked it. The solitary lamp they had lit went out at once."

memories.description: Right, I’ll handle the lights. Funny way to put it but I don’t want anything ruining the wedding, and I’m prepared to sort things out.
memories.source_text: "A brutal triple murder by the bridegroom’s mother might put a bit of a damper on the wedding. I’ll get the lights."

memories.description: Blimey, Regulus is R.A.B. and that could mean the locket is connected to him.
memories.source_text: What? That was Sirius’s brother, wasn’t it? Regulus Arcturus . . . Regulus . . . R.A.B.! The locket — you don’t reckon — ?

memories.description: It looks like the locket isn't in Regulus's room. That was a proper letdown.
memories.source_text: Is that it, then? It’s not here?

memories.description: I still need my stomach sorted before anything dangerous. I get jumpy and hungry before a scrap.
memories.source_text: If it’s massive spiders again I want breakfast before I —

memories.description: Kreacher nicked things back from us. We have to check his kitchen cupboard next.
memories.source_text: C’mon.

memories.description: Blimey, this is real. They're actually rounding up Muggle-borns and it's getting worse by the minute.
memories.source_text: 'People won’t let this happen,' said Ron. 'It is happening, Ron,' said Lupin.

memories.description: I'll do whatever it takes to protect Hermione. I'll lie through my teeth, teach her my family tree, say she's family. No one will touch her if I can help it.
memories.source_text: 'What if purebloods and half-bloods swear a Muggle-born’s part of their family? I’ll tell everyone Hermione’s my cousin —' 'You won’t have a choice,' said Ron fiercely

memories.description: I'm happy for Tonks and Remus. I want to celebrate good news even in all this mess. And I'll back Hermione against anyone who blames her.
memories.source_text: ''Congratulations,' said Harry.' 'Excellent!' said Ron enthusiastically.'

memories.description: Blimey, there are Death Eaters outside. I kept thinking they might know we're in here and we'd be in serious trouble.
memories.source_text: "Death Eaters, for sure," said Ron, as he, Harry, and Hermione watched from the drawing room windows. "Reckon they know we're in here?"

memories.description: Maybe Snape's been here and Moody's done that rotter's tongue up. I said it out loud because it's the sort of thing I'd think.
memories.source_text: "D'you reckon he's been in here and had his tongue tied by Moody's curse?" asked Ron.

memories.description: I keep fiddling with the Deluminator because I suppose I'm meant to have it. I don't know why I keep doing it, but it's mine and I'm using it.
memories.source_text: "— and he left me the Deluminator, maybe I'm supposed to use it!"

memories.description: If Harry still had the Trace they'd have known he was here, but he doesn't. Still, how they found him in Tottenham Court Road is proper worrying. Something's off.
memories.source_text: "Apart from anything else, they'd know for sure Harry was here if he still had the Trace on him, wouldn't they? But I can't see how they could have tracked you to Tottenham Court Road, that's worrying, really worrying."

memories.description: Blimey, Kreacher must've disapparated away from the Inferi using elf magic.
memories.source_text: "Well, it’s obvious, isn’t it, Harry? He Disapparated!"

memories.description: Elf magic works differently to ours; they can do things like Apparate into places we can't, even Hogwarts.
memories.source_text: "Elf magic isn’t like wizard’s magic, is it? I mean, they can Apparate and Disapparate in and out of Hogwarts when we can’t."

memories.description: When I offered the fake locket to Kreacher, it was too much for him and he reacted very badly.
memories.source_text: "Overkill, mate,"

memories.description: Blimey, I was over the moon when Harry thought Kreacher had the locket. I want something concrete to go on and that made me feel hopeful.
memories.source_text: Ron groaned as he threw himself into a kitchen chair; he looked gleeful when Harry asked about the locket

memories.description: Mundungus nicked the locket and a load of Black family stuff. That tells me who to blame and maybe who to chase.
memories.source_text: Kreacher: "Mundungus Fletcher stole it all"

memories.description: Bloody hell, if Voldemort did that to an elf it shows just how nasty his Horcrux protections are. This is serious and dangerous.
memories.source_text: Kreacher's account of being forced to a cave and made to drink potion by the Dark Lord

memories.description: Blimey, I was panicking about them back home, thinking someone was stuck. My head's all over the place.
memories.source_text: "No, he's still stuck in the bog," said Ron.

memories.description: I was terrified of Yaxley. I kept trying to play it cool but I was scared stiff.
memories.source_text: "You think it's funny, Cattermole, do you?" Yaxley said and Ron whispered, "Yes."

memories.description: If I don't get there, people I care about will be in trouble. That's on me. That's mental, I can't just ignore it.
memories.source_text: "If I don’t turn up, my wife — I mean, Cattermole’s wife —" Ron asked the other two at once; he looked stricken.

memories.description: Bloody hell, I needed instructions spelled out. I wasn't thinking straight and needed Hermione to slow down so I could remember the spells.
memories.source_text: "Say it again, slowly —" said Ron, searching his pockets desperately for a quill.

memories.description: Blimey, I do forget stuff sometimes, don't I?
memories.source_text: "Blimey, Hermione, I forget one little thing -"

memories.description: Right, she's Mafalda Hopkirk from the Improper Use of Magic Office. That's who we're copying.
memories.source_text: "She's Mafalda Hopkirk," he said, reading a small card that identified their victim as an assistant in the Improper Use of Magic Office.

memories.description: Here, I nicked the tokens and handed them over. They're stamped M.O.M. and they'll get us in.
memories.source_text: "'You'd better take this, Hermione, and here are the tokens.' He passed her several small golden coins, all embossed with the letters M.O.M., which he had taken from the witch's purse."

memories.description: Blimey, seeing Harry all big and bearded like that is proper scary.
memories.source_text: "'Blimey, that's scary,' said Ron, looking up at Harry, who now towered over him."

memories.description: So we have to flush ourselves down the toilet to reach the Ministry. That's mental but it works.
memories.source_text: "'We have to flush ourselves in?' he whispered."

memories.description: Where the hell are you heading? If we're staying here then tell me now.
memories.source_text: "Where are you going?" asked Ron.

memories.description: I thought that tent was Perkins's at the Ministry. Fancy that it ended up with us.
memories.source_text: "I thought this belonged to that bloke Perkins at the Ministry?" he asked, starting to disentangle the tent pegs.

memories.description: Blimey, that was a shock for Harry. He just went through something nasty and we need to be careful with him.
memories.source_text: Well, you’ve just had a big shock,

memories.description: What was that spell supposed to do then? I don't get all these spells, but I know when something should show up and it didn't.
memories.source_text: What was that supposed to do?

memories.description: There's no one here except us and old Dusty, the patch of carpet where that corpse thing rose. That's mental.
memories.source_text: And old Dusty,

memories.description: I checked outside. Can't see anyone. If there was a Trace on Harry they'd have followed, but they can't get in here.
memories.source_text: Can’t see anyone out there,

memories.description: When I heard the Patronus from my family I was relieved. My family are safe and that matters more than anything right now.
memories.source_text: They’re all right, they’re all right!

memories.description: Blimey, my arm's been messed up. There's a chunk gone from my upper arm and I'm out cold.
memories.source_text: He had always thought of Splinching as something comical, but this . . . His insides crawled unpleasantly as Hermione laid bare Ron’s upper arm, where a great chunk of flesh was missing, scooped cleanly away as though by a knife.

memories.description: I'm fainted. I can't even stay awake after all that blood.
memories.source_text: "He’s fainted," said Hermione, who was also rather pale; she no longer looked like Mafalda, though her hair was still gray in places.

memories.description: Bloody hell, I'm soaked from that bit of business. It was water, that's it, nothing fancy.
memories.source_text: "Why are you so wet?" "Water," muttered Ron, disengaging himself.

memories.description: They've twigged there's intruders. I reckon we've got about five minutes or less before everything goes to pot.
memories.source_text: "Harry, they know there are intruders inside the Ministry, something about a hole in Umbridge’s office door, I reckon we’ve got five minutes if that —"

memories.description: Right, when there's a chance I grab it. I pulled Mary through the fireplace when I could. Quick reactions save people, simple as that.
memories.source_text: "The balding wizard’s colleagues set up an uproar, under cover of which Ron grabbed Mrs. Cattermole, pulled her into the still-open fireplace, and disappeared."

memories.description: Reg Cattermole's a mess and people are mixed up. I had to step in and get Mary moving, even if it caused chaos with the real Reg turning up.
memories.source_text: "Reg, I don’t understand —" "Let go, I’m not your husband, you’ve got to go home!"

memories.description: Blimey, I know calling Lupin a coward was wrong, but I'm convinced he's been acting like a coward.
memories.source_text: "No, you shouldn’t," said Ron at once. "But he’s acting like one."

memories.description: Mundungus panicked and ran from danger. He'll say anything to save himself, so we need to treat him as untrustworthy and press him hard.
memories.source_text: "Right, we’ve got a few questions for you," Harry told Mundungus, who shouted at once, "I panicked, okay?..." "Well, you’re a bunch of bleedin’ ’eroes then, aren’t you..." "We’re not interested in why you ran out on Mad-Eye," said Harry.

memories.description: I tackled Mundungus to stop him fleeing and watched Kreacher rough him up. That was necessary to keep Mundungus talking. If someone's dodgy, a bit of a rugby tackle helps get answers.
memories.source_text: "Call ’im off, call ’im off, ’e should be locked up!" screamed Mundungus... "We need him conscious, Kreacher, but if he needs persuading you can do the honors," said Harry. "Thank you very much, Master," said Kreacher with a bow, and he retreated a short distance...

memories.description: I figured Mundungus was thinking about money and whether he could have asked more for the locket. He might have sold it to make a quick profit, not kept it.
memories.source_text: "No, he hasn’t," said Ron shrewdly.

memories.description: Blimey, I feel lousy. I just groaned and opened my eyes, all gray and sweating, that's how rough I am.
memories.source_text: Lousy, croaked Ron

memories.description: Blimey, I can feel something from that locket when I hold it tight in my fist.
memories.source_text: "Can you feel it, though?"

memories.description: I wasn't sure at first what Harry meant about feeling it, but I passed it to him to see.
memories.source_text: "What d’you mean?"

memories.description: I felt really sick after holding the locket and nearly couldn't sit up; that thing makes me feel awful.
memories.source_text: Ron turning a nasty shade of green and attempting to sit up

memories.description: Could you actually tell what the thief had? I couldn't see it, so it must have been hard to spot.
memories.source_text: "Couldn’t you see what the thief was holding?"

memories.description: Do you think Voldemort might be after something else to make another Horcrux? He might not even realise his soul is already hanging by a thread.
memories.source_text: "Harry, you don’t reckon You-Know-Who’s after something else to turn into a Horcrux?" "Yeah, but maybe he doesn’t know that."

memories.description: The Hogwarts Express left without us ages ago. It's weird not being on it.
memories.source_text: "I’ve been thinking about that all day. It left nearly six hours ago."

memories.description: I mess up with the Invisibility Cloak too. Also I'm watching for Hermione coming back in like always.
memories.source_text: "I do that every time. Oh, here she is,"

memories.description: Dad says most Ministry people use the Floo Network to get to work. That's why Umbridge would never walk and why we don't see her out and about.
memories.source_text: "Dad always told us most Ministry people use the Floo Network to get to work"

memories.description: Okay, a lot of details matter. I might sound casual but I know the small stuff could be useful.
memories.source_text: "Well, does it really matter?"

memories.description: Don't you dare say his name. Just call him You Know Who and show him some respect, yeah?
memories.source_text: "Don't say the name!"

memories.description: Blimey, when I'm like this I can't hear his name without feeling twisted. Call him You Know Who, alright?
memories.source_text: "I'm sorry," Ron said, moaning a little as he raised himself to look at them, "but it feels like a — a jinx or something. Can't we call him You-Know-Who — please?"

memories.description: No one tells me anything. I'm the one stuck here and I want to know what's going on. If you had the locket you could have told me.
memories.source_text: "You got it?" shouted Ron, raising himself a little higher on his pillows. "No one tells me anything! Blimey, you could have mentioned it!"

memories.description: I'm hoping someone hasn't destroyed it. If Kreacher had it and it was gone I'd be gutted, so I'm quietly relieved it's still here.
memories.source_text: "There isn't any chance someone's destroyed it since Kreacher had it?" asked Ron hopefully.

memories.description: Blimey, I was defending Hermione there, saying she gets stuck with the cooking because she's supposed to be brilliant at magic. I don't think it's fair she has to do everything.
memories.source_text: No, it’s because you’re supposed to be the best at magic!" shot back Ron.

memories.description: I was impatient and snappy earlier but when Harry warned us I shut it. I know when to keep my gob shut if he says so.
memories.source_text: Shut up!" said Harry, leaping to his feet and holding up both hands. "Shut up now!

memories.description: So they're goblins, right? Hearing those names made me realize we're eavesdropping on goblins, not just random wizards.
memories.source_text: Here, Griphook, Gornuk.

memories.description: The sword in Gringotts is a fake. That's mental. If the real sword's somewhere else, that's a lead we have to chase.
memories.source_text: It’s a fake," rasped Griphook. "The sword of Gryffindor!

memories.description: They punished Ginny and the others who tried to take the sword. Lucky they're not badly hurt, but it sounds nasty.
memories.source_text: Oh, they were punished, and cruelly," said Griphook indifferently.

memories.description: You're supposed to be able to make a Patronus, Harry. I reckon you can do it, so I was shocked when you couldn't.
memories.source_text: "But you can make a brilliant Patronus!" protested Ron, when Harry arrived back at the tent empty-handed, out of breath, and mouthing the single word, dementors.

memories.description: My arm's in a sling, and I use that as an excuse when I'm hungry or can't be bothered to help. Hunger makes me grumpy, and I complain about it.
memories.source_text: "I would, but my arm’s in a sling, in case you hadn’t noticed!" "That’s convenient."

memories.description: Blimey, my mum can somehow rustle up brilliant food from nothing. It feels like magic compared to what we're eating out here.
memories.source_text: "My mother," said Ron one night, as they sat in the tent on a riverbank in Wales, "can make good food appear out of thin air."

memories.description: I keep asking where we go next because I'm hungry and bored. I don't have the answers, I want others to come up with plans while I brood a bit.
memories.source_text: "So where next?" was his constant refrain. He did not seem to have any ideas himself, but expected Harry and Hermione to come up with plans while he sat and brooded over the low food supplies.

memories.description: I fiddle with the Horcrux chain when I'm tense. I know it annoys Harry, but being hungry and carrying that thing makes me snappy.
memories.source_text: He was tugging at the chain of the Horcrux around his neck: Harry was visited by a desire to seize it and throttle him.

memories.description: No way, do not open that thing. I mean it, I can't let it be opened.
memories.source_text: "No!" said Ron. "No, don’t open it! I’m serious!"

memories.description: That locket messes with me worse than it did with you lot. It twists what I'm already thinking into something ugly. I keep getting straight then I have to wear it again and it's impossible.
memories.source_text: "Because that thing’s bad for me!" said Ron, backing away from the locket on the rock. "I can’t handle it! I’m not making excuses, Harry, for what I was like, but it affects me worse than it affected you and Hermione, it made me think stuff — stuff I was thinking anyway, but it made everything worse, I can’t explain it, and then I’d take it off and I’d get my head on straight again, and then I’d have to put the effing thing back on — I can’t do it, Harry!"

memories.description: Hearing him call my name snaps me a bit. I can get close and do it if I have to, I just need to brace myself. Tell me when and I'll try.
memories.source_text: "You can do it," said Harry, "you can! You’ve just got the sword, I know it’s supposed to be you who uses it. Please, just get rid of it, Ron." The sound of his name seemed to act like a stimulant. Ron swallowed, then, still breathing hard through his long nose, moved back toward the rock. "Tell me when," he croaked.

memories.description: Blimey, I watched Harry go under, thought something was wrong, dived in and pulled him out, then went back for the sword.
memories.source_text: He explained how he had watched Harry jump into the pool and had waited for him to resurface; how he had realized that something was wrong, dived in, and saved Harry, then returned for the sword.

memories.description: I got the sword in and, well, I stabbed the locket. That’s what finished it off.
memories.source_text: and Ron stabbed it with the sword.

memories.description: What the hell. I came straight in and there he was. I can't believe he did that without thinking it through.
memories.source_text: "Are — you — mental?"

memories.description: I got the locket out. I plunged the sword in and pulled it off him. Job done.
memories.source_text: "Oh yeah, I got it out," he said, rather unnecessarily, holding up the sword for Harry’s inspection.

memories.description: I came back because I wanted to be with them again. I wanted Harry to want me with them.
memories.source_text: "I’ve — you know — I’ve come back. If —" He cleared his throat. "You know. You still want me."

memories.description: I tracked them for hours through that forest until I found them. It took ages and it was horrible, but I kept at it.
memories.source_text: "I've been looking for you for hours, it’s a big forest, isn’t it?"

memories.description: My Patronus is a stag. Don't get it mixed up with a doe.
memories.source_text: "My Patronus is a stag."

memories.description: Could've been worse, honestly. Remember those birds she set on me? Bloody nightmare.
memories.source_text: Yeah. Could’ve been worse. Remember those birds she set on me?

memories.description: Me? Why? Blimey, you're really asking me to do it. I'm shocked and not sure I'm ready.
memories.source_text: Me?

memories.description: I did pull the sword out of the pool, so it feels like it's supposed to be my job. That puts everything on me and it's proper scary.
memories.source_text: Because you got the sword out of the pool. I think it’s supposed to be you.

memories.description: I'm fed up. I expected us to be getting somewhere by now and we are not. That's what I meant when I said I was disappointed.
memories.source_text: "I just hoped, you know, after we'd been running round a few weeks, we'd have achieved something."

memories.description: I heard that the sword was not Snape's personal property but something goblin made linked to his school. I'm angry about the whole business.
memories.source_text: "They weren’t thieving," said Harry. "That sword isn’t Snape’s." "It belongs to Professor Snape’s school," said Phineas Nigellus."

memories.description: I left. I told Harry to go home and then I Disapparated. I needed to get away because I was furious and hurt.
memories.source_text: "Yeah, maybe I will!" shouted Ron, and he took several steps toward Harry, who did not back away.

memories.description: I am worried about Ginny and the rest of my family. I felt Harry did not seem to care enough and that made me explode.
memories.source_text: "Didn’t you hear what they said about my sister? But you don’t give a rat’s fart, do you,"

memories.description: I stayed on that hill all day hoping you'd show up. When I couldn't find you, I clicked the Deluminator, the blue light went into me, and I Disapparated to these woods.
memories.source_text: “Well, I stayed on that hill all day,” said Ron. “I kept hoping you’d appear. But when it started to get dark I knew I must have missed you, so I clicked the Deluminator again, the blue light came out and went inside me, and I Disapparated and arrived here in these woods."

memories.description: Blimey, I believed you'd appear at the end. I couldn't see you because the spells worked, but I guessed one of you would eventually show yourselves.
memories.source_text: “I still couldn’t see you, so I just had to hope one of you would show yourselves in the end — and Harry did.”

memories.description: I took the Deluminator out and clicked it. The light in my room went out and another blue pulsing light showed up outside my window.
memories.source_text: "So I took it out," Ron went on, looking at the Deluminator, "and it didn't seem different or anything, but I was sure I'd heard you. So I clicked it. And the light went out in my room, but another light appeared right outside the window."

memories.description: Blimey, it was a little bluish ball of light, pulsing, exactly like the glow around a Portkey.
memories.source_text: "It was a ball of light, kind of pulsing, and bluish, like that light you get around a Portkey, you know?"

memories.description: It floated right to my chest and went straight through me. I could feel it, hot, like it was inside me, and then I knew what to do and where it would send me.
memories.source_text: "It sort of floated toward me," said Ron, illustrating the movement with his free index finger, "right to my chest, and then — it just went straight through. It was here," he touched a point close to his heart, "I could feel it, it was hot. And once it was inside me I knew what I was supposed to do, I knew it would take me where I needed to go."

memories.description: I Disapparated and ended up on the side of a snowy hill.
memories.source_text: "So I Disapparated and came out on the side of a hill. There was snow everywhere."

memories.description: I couldn't see you lot, but I trusted one of you would turn up in the end and Harry did. That's what I was counting on.
memories.source_text: "I still couldn't see you, so I just had to hope one of you would show yourselves in the end — and Harry did."

memories.description: Blimey. For a moment I actually believed they were right and we'd have been better off without me.
memories.source_text: "Why return? We were better without you, happier without you, glad of your absence."

memories.description: I stabbed it. I smashed the locket and whatever was inside finally disappeared. I did it, even if it nearly broke me.
memories.source_text: "The monstrous versions of himself and Hermione were gone: There was only Ron, standing there with the sword held slackly in his hand, looking down at the shattered remains of the locket on the flat rock."

memories.description: I feel rotten about what I did and what I saw, but I saved Harry and Hermione from that thing. Doesn't make me feel any less rubbish though.
memories.source_text: "Ron had pierced the glass in both windows: Riddle’s eyes were gone... He had sunk to his knees, his head in his arms. He was shaking..."

memories.description: The Horcrux will use anything to wound you. It even pretended Mum preferred someone else to try to break me.
memories.source_text: "Your mother confessed," sneered Riddle-Harry, while Riddle-Hermione jeered, "that she would have preferred me as a son, would be glad to exchange . . ."

memories.description: I tried to get back to them the whole time, I called and I begged, I couldn't just leave them without trying.
memories.source_text: "I came running after you! I called you! I begged you to come back!"

memories.description: Blimey, I ran into Snatchers, proper gangs rounding up Muggle-borns and blood traitors. That's why I couldn't just go home.
memories.source_text: "I walked straight into a gang of Snatchers"

memories.description: I lied and said I was Stan Shunpike to get out of being dragged off, and, well, they were not the sharpest.
memories.source_text: "Told them I was Stan Shunpike. First person I could think of."

memories.description: I messed up a Disapparation and Splinched myself, lost bits of me, like fingernails, which is rotten, but I got away.
memories.source_text: "I didn’t do it so well, Splinched myself again"

memories.description: That Deluminator actually spoke Hermione's voice to me from my pocket. I heard 'Ron' and something about a wand and it pulled me back.
memories.source_text: "This." "The Deluminator?" "I heard you coming out of my pocket. Your voice, came out of this."

memories.description: There was this little bluish, pulsing ball of light, like a Portkey, that showed up outside my window and I followed it.
memories.source_text: "It was a ball of light, kind of pulsing, and bluish"

memories.description: The light actually went right into me, into my chest, and once it was there I just knew where to go. So I Disapparated and it dropped me near them.
memories.source_text: "it went inside me"

memories.description: I came back with the sword and I'm a mess. I'm exhausted and I didn't exactly turn up looking fine.
memories.source_text: She saw Ron, who stood there holding the sword and dripping onto the threadbare carpet.

memories.description: Blimey, Hermione's actually attacking me. Ouch ow gerroff what the hell Hermione ow I was hoping for a reaction like relief not a punch up.
memories.source_text: “Ouch — ow — gerroff! What the — ? Hermione — OW!”

memories.description: I was hopeful she'd forgive me or at least not hit me straight away. I still care about her and I wanted it to go back to normal.
memories.source_text: Ron gave a weak, hopeful smile and half raised his arms.

memories.description: Blimey, I backed off straight away because Hermione was fed up. I don't want to wind her up when she's on a mission.
memories.source_text: "If it’s annoying you, I’ll stop!" he told Hermione nervously.

memories.description: Er, why do we need to see Mr. Lovegood? I'm not convinced yet, I need convincing.
memories.source_text: "Er — why?"

memories.description: He's a cowardly old wart. Luna's got ten times his guts.
memories.source_text: "Cowardly old wart," said Ron. "Luna’s got ten times his guts."

memories.description: You don't reckon Kingsley sent the doe? I mean, I know his Patronus is a lynx from the wedding, so that doesn't add up.
memories.source_text: "You don't reckon Kingsley could have sent that doe?" "His Patronus is a lynx, we saw it at the wedding, remember?"

memories.description: Blimey, do you reckon Dumbledore could've been behind the doe? He had the sword last, didn't he? It's a daft hope, but it would be brilliant if it were true.
memories.source_text: "Harry . . . you don't reckon it could've been Dumbledore?" "Dumbledore what?" "Dumbledore . . . the doe? I mean," Ron was watching Harry out of the corners of his eyes, "he had the real sword last, didn't he?"

memories.description: Yeah, Bill said a bunch of Death Eaters cornered Kingsley but he fought his way out. He's on the run now, like we are.
memories.source_text: "Yeah, a bunch of Death Eaters cornered him, Bill said, but he fought his way out. He’s on the run now, just like us."

memories.description: So Death can sneak up on people with the Cloak. Blimey, that is creepy.
memories.source_text: "So he can sneak up on people,"

memories.description: Death isn't just dramatic and scary all the time. He might get fed up and do something subtle instead. That's mental. Sorry about the outburst.
memories.source_text: "Sometimes he gets bored of running at them, flapping his arms and shrieking . . . sorry, Hermione."

memories.description: Blimey, getting that locket destroyed feels like a proper win. I'm right back in with Harry and Hermione now.
memories.source_text: "One Horcrux down, mate!"

memories.description: No, you can't go saying his name willy nilly. It's jinxed and it lets them track you. That's why people who dare stand up to him had to be careful.
memories.source_text: "NO!" roared Ron... "but the name’s been jinxed, Harry, that’s how they track people! Using his name breaks protective enchantments, it causes some kind of magical disturbance — it’s how they found us in Tottenham Court Road!"

memories.description: You've got to give them credit, that whole Taboo idea actually makes sense. Only the really brave or reckless used his name.
memories.source_text: "Because we used his name?" "Exactly! You’ve got to give them credit, it makes sense. It was only people who were serious about standing up to him, like Dumbledore, who ever dared use it."

memories.description: I'm sorry I left. I know I was a right prat for going off like that.
memories.source_text: "I’m sorry," he said in a thick voice. "I’m sorry I left. I know I was a — a —"

memories.description: Blimey, what I did sounds better when you say it. It wasn't as heroic as it sounds.
memories.source_text: "That makes me sound a lot cooler than I was," Ron mumbled. "Stuff like that always sounds cooler than it really was," said Harry.

memories.description: I was a mess, eyes all bloodshot and sniffling, trying to act like I wasn't ruined by it all.
memories.source_text: Ron did not respond, but turned his face away from Harry and wiped his nose noisily on his sleeve.

memories.description: Yeah, I know 'The Tale of the Three Brothers.'
memories.source_text: Ron said, "Yes."

memories.description: Blimey, he looked at me straight after Hermione, like he was checking everyone out. I was just waiting to see what he'd do.
memories.source_text: "looking first at Hermione, then at Ron, and finally at Harry"

memories.description: Blimey, the Deluminator actually came in handy. It wasn't just a trinket.
memories.source_text: “The Deluminator turned out to be pretty useful,”

memories.description: The Lovegoods and The Quibbler are on Harry's side. They're backing him and urging people to help.
memories.source_text: “Lovegood’s on your side, Harry, The Quibbler’s been for you all along, it keeps telling everyone they’ve got to help you!”

memories.description: The Lovegoods live not far from my parents' place. Mum and Dad always point toward the hills when they talk about them, so finding them shouldn't be hard.
memories.source_text: “Yeah, they’re not far from my place,” said Ron. “I dunno exactly where, but Mum and Dad always point toward the hills whenever they mention them. Shouldn’t be hard to find.”

memories.description: People are talking loads about Skeeter's story. It's everywhere right now.
memories.source_text: "Oh yeah," said Ron at once, "people are talking about it quite a lot."

memories.description: Blimey, if the times were different that would be massive. As it is, it's mostly used by Dumbledore's critics to sneer, and it stings his proper supporters.
memories.source_text: "'Course, if things were different, it'd be huge news, Dumbledore being pals with Grindelwald, but now it's just something to laugh about for people who didn't like Dumbledore, and a bit of a slap in the face for everyone who thought he was such a good bloke."

memories.description: Right, there's this cracking program that tells the truth. The rest are on You-Know-Who's side. You need a password to get it and they keep moving about so they don't get nicked.
memories.source_text: "There's this one program," he told Harry in a low voice, "that tells the news like it really is. All the others are on You-Know-Who's side and are following the Ministry line, but this one . . . you wait till you hear it, it's great. Only they can't do it every night, they have to keep changing locations in case they're raided, and you need a password to tune in."

memories.description: Typical me, I missed the last broadcast. I'm hoping I can catch the next one, so I keep faffing about with the radio trying to get it.
memories.source_text: "Trouble is, I missed the last one." He drummed lightly on the top of the radio with his wand, muttering random words under his breath.

memories.description: I'm proper worried Hermione will explode if I say the wrong thing. I keep sneaking looks at her and trying not to set her off.
memories.source_text: "He threw Hermione many covert glances, plainly fearing an angry outburst"

memories.description: Patronuses can change. Tonks's did change, so they are not always fixed.
memories.source_text: "Patronuses can change, though, can't they? Tonks's changed, didn't it?"

memories.description: I used to think Dumbledore was having a laugh or being awkward on purpose, but now I reckon he knew exactly what he was doing when he left me the Deluminator.
memories.source_text: "Sometimes I've thought, when I've been a bit hacked off, he was having a laugh or he just wanted to make it more difficult. But I don't think so, not anymore. He knew what he was doing when he gave me the Deluminator,"

memories.description: I know I ran out on you, and I reckon Dumbledore must've expected that from me. I felt guilty but also like he understood me.
memories.source_text: "he must've known I'd run out on you."

memories.description: When you say 'master of Death', you mean someone who has conquered or vanquished death, right?
memories.source_text: "When you say 'master of Death' —" said Ron.

memories.description: I tease Hermione to lighten the mood. I can't help laughing at that ridiculous hat even when things are serious.
memories.source_text: "Perhaps you ought to try on the hat, Hermione," said Ron, nodding toward the ludicrous headdress. His voice shook with the strain of not laughing.

memories.description: I saw the deer and I saw Harry following it. I might have seen something move by those trees but I was heading straight for the pool because Harry went in and didn’t come up.
memories.source_text: [“And I was just thinking I’d have to kip under a tree and wait for morning when I saw that deer coming and you following.” “You didn’t see anyone else?” “No,” said Ron. “I —” But he hesitated, glancing at two trees growing close together some yards away. “I did think I saw something move over there, but I was running to the pool at the time, because you’d gone in and you hadn’t come up, so I wasn’t going to make a detour to — hey!”]

memories.description: I’m not sure if that sword is the real one, but I want to find out.
memories.source_text: [“You reckon this is the real one?” asked Ron.]

memories.description: I’m holding the locket and it’s twitching in my hand like it’s alive.
memories.source_text: [“The Horcrux was still swinging from Ron’s hand. The locket was twitching slightly.”]

memories.description: Blimey, it's in Fantastic Beasts. If it's an Erumpent horn it can blow up on you, so get rid of it now.
memories.source_text: "There’s a description in Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them! Mr Lovegood, you need to get rid of it straightaway, don’t you know it can explode at the slightest touch?"

memories.description: You're always going on about everyone helping Harry in your magazine. I called him out on that because it sounded ridiculous for him to say one thing and then act differently.
memories.source_text: "Aren’t you the one who keeps telling everyone it’s their first duty to help Harry?"

memories.description: I asked how she knew, because it seemed important and a bit alarming, and I wanted an answer right away.
memories.source_text: "How d'you know it’s an Erumpent horn?"

memories.description: Blimey, I reckon it's definitely spookier at midnight; our mum always said midnight makes a tale scarier.
memories.source_text: "Midnight, our mum always told us,"

memories.description: Look, I just think the whole thing's creepier at midnight — that's how stories work, innit?
memories.source_text: "Sorry, I just think it’s a bit spookier if it’s midnight!"

memories.description: Blimey, I was buried under that lot. I couldn't move until Hermione sorted me out.
memories.source_text: "Ron was buried deepest: Harry and Hermione climbed, as quietly as they could, over all the wreckage to where he lay, trying to prise a heavy chest of drawers off his legs."

memories.description: Bloody hell, I went straight under the Invisibility Cloak. It's like I disappeared.
memories.source_text: "Ron vanished beneath the Cloak."

memories.description: Er, I wasn't keen at first and I panicked, but then I had to trust them. Okay fine, I'll do it.
memories.source_text: "Me? But Harry —"

memories.description: Blimey, where's the Elder Wand supposed to be now then? That's what matters.
memories.source_text: So where do you think the Elder Wand is now?

memories.description: Who are these Peverells? That was the name on the grave in Godric's Hollow, wasn't it? That's proper suspicious.
memories.source_text: Who are the Peverells?

memories.description: He's a treacherous old bleeder, I can't believe he tried to sell us out like that.
memories.source_text: "That treacherous old bleeder!" Ron panted, emerging from beneath the Invisibility Cloak and throwing it to Harry.

memories.description: Serves him right that his house got blown apart. I wonder what they'll do to him now.
memories.source_text: "Serves him right," said Ron, examining his torn jeans and the cuts to his legs. "What d’you reckon they’ll do to him?"

memories.description: If Luna's been taken, she'll probably be in Azkaban and I worry she might not survive that place, because a lot of people don't.
memories.source_text: "Then she’ll be in Azkaban, I expect," said Ron. "Whether she survives the place, though . . . Loads don’t."

memories.description: They kidnapped Luna because her father supported Harry. I shouldn't be out with him because my family would be in danger if anyone knew I was with Harry.
memories.source_text: "Why hide me, though?" asked Ron. "You’re supposed to be in bed with spattergroit, Ron! They’ve kidnapped Luna because her father supported Harry! What would happen to your family if they knew you’re with him?"

memories.description: Blimey, I can fake a wheeze when I have to. I tried to bluff our way out when Wormtail came down.
memories.source_text: "'All fine!' Ron called back, in a passable imitation of Wormtail’s wheezy voice."

memories.description: I tried spells in the heat of it and sometimes they just don’t work under pressure. That was useless and terrifying.
memories.source_text: "'Relashio!' said Ron, pointing the wand at the silver hand, but nothing happened;"

memories.description: When Hermione was threatened I lost it. I am not staying back if she's in danger. Bloody hell, I will charge in.
memories.source_text: "'NOOOOOOOOOOOO!' Ron had burst into the drawing room;"

memories.description: I can pull an Expelliarmus when it counts. I will try anything to disarm them if it saves Hermione.
memories.source_text: "Expelliarmus!" he roared, pointing Wormtail’s wand at Bellatrix, and hers flew into the air and was caught by Harry,

memories.description: Blimey, I can't help it, I scream her name until I'm hoarse. When Hermione's in danger I lose my head.
memories.source_text: "HERMIONE! HERMIONE!"

memories.description: I remembered the Deluminator and used it instinctively. Sometimes I spot the simplest trick when we need light and I blurt it out.
memories.source_text: "My pocket! In my pocket, there’s a Deluminator, and it’s full of light!"

memories.description: I said to send people to Bill and Fleur's at Shell Cottage because that's where we'd go to be safe. I trust them and I say it plain and quick.
memories.source_text: "Bill and Fleur's"

memories.description: I tried to Disapparate without a wand in panic. I know I panic, but I also know I won't give up looking for any chance to save my friends.
memories.source_text: "There’s no way out, Ron," said Luna, "The cellar is completely escape-proof."

memories.description: Blimey, I reckon it's brilliant. Let's go and tell him now, come on.
memories.source_text: "Well, I think it’s genius," said Ron, standing up again. "Let’s go and tell him."

memories.description: Blimey, Lupin's living with Tonks again and she's getting big. That's mental and means they're settling back together.
memories.source_text: "Bill told me Lupin’s living with Tonks again! And apparently she’s getting pretty big too."

memories.description: At least Hagrid's alive. That's a relief even if he's on the run after that Support Harry Potter thing.
memories.source_text: "At least he’s still alive!" muttered Ron.

memories.description: Hearing Fred muck about on air reminds me to stay calm. If we can laugh at all this, maybe we're tougher than the Death Eaters expect.
memories.source_text: "I’m not being 'Rodent,' no way, I told you I wanted to be 'Rapier'!"

memories.description: Blimey, I reckon Griphook's having a laugh if he expects to walk off with our sword.
memories.source_text: "He’s having a laugh. We can’t let him have that sword."

memories.description: Goblins always have their slant on things. I reckon they're always saying we cheated them, but still, lucky it's not our wands he's after.
memories.source_text: "It’ll be one of those goblin stories," said Ron, "about how the wizards are always trying to get one over on them. I suppose we should think ourselves lucky he hasn’t asked for one of our wands."

memories.description: I thought we could nick the sword and scarper before he knows, which was a stupid idea when you think about it.
memories.source_text: "Yeah, but we could scarper before he realizes —"

memories.description: Alright, fine. If we can't pull a fast one, I was thinking we could replace it with another goblin-made sword and hope that does the job.
memories.source_text: "Brilliant. I’ll go and get one of our other ancient goblin-made swords and you can gift wrap it."

memories.description: I thought we could offer him other treasure from the Lestrange vault to make him happy. I was trying to be practical and quick about it.
memories.source_text: I’ll bet the Lestranges have got loads of stuff, you can take your pick once we get into the vault

memories.description: I assumed the sword was made for Gryffindor and belonged to us. I didn't know goblins claimed prior ownership.
memories.source_text: It was made for him, wasn't it? No one’s

memories.description: Alright, so goblins see us as arrogant for assuming the sword is ours. I can't just shrug off their claim now. That's awkward.
memories.source_text: Wizarding arrogance again! That sword was Ragnuk the First's, taken from him by Godric Gryffindor

memories.description: I got called out for suggesting we take stuff that isn't ours. I realised my offhand plan sounded wrong and it upset him.
memories.source_text: I am not a thief, boy! I am not trying to procure treasures to which I have no right!

memories.description: Blimey, there's a baby. I'm gobsmacked and proper pleased for them.
memories.source_text: ["Blimey, a baby!"]

memories.description: I keep saying blimey because I'm stunned. It's crazy but brilliant news.
memories.source_text: ["I — yeah — blimey —" (Ron said this as if he had never heard of such a thing before)]

memories.description: I can't deny that some of what Harry says lines up, but it doesn't add up completely for me.
memories.source_text: "I dunno . . . I mean . . . bits of it sort of fit together"

memories.description: We're here to destroy Horcruxes. That's the point of all this, and we shouldn't get sidetracked by Hallows talk.
memories.source_text: "I think we’re supposed to get rid of Horcruxes, Harry. That’s what Dumbledore told us to do."

memories.description: I managed to crack the Potterwatch password. It was 'Albus' and we got back on the radio. That was a proper bit of luck.
memories.source_text: "I’ve got it, I’ve got it! Password was ‘Albus’! Get in here, Harry!"

memories.description: Well, you never know where a lead might take you, so we keep poking about places Tom might've been. Keep moving, keep trying.
memories.source_text: "You never know,"

memories.description: Blimey, I know it has been done before. Gringotts has been breached in the past, so it is not impossible.
memories.source_text: "No, it isn’t," Ron contradicted him.

memories.description: Bloody hell, goblins do their own kind of magic and they think wizards hoard wandlore. That argument matters to them.
memories.source_text: "Well, goblins can do magic without wands," said Ron.

memories.description: He’s winding us up. I don’t trust Griphook to decide quickly. We need to push him, but carefully.
memories.source_text: "Little git," whispered Ron. "He’s enjoying keeping us hanging."

memories.description: Blimey, we all want You-Know-Who gone. I made that plain to try to win Griphook over and show we are on the same side.
memories.source_text: "You can’t want You-Know-Who defeated more than we do, Griphook!"

memories.description: I saw Hermione suffer and I know she was brave. I'm proud of her and I'll stick by her.
memories.source_text: How are you? You were amazing - coming up with that story when she was hurting you like that -

memories.description: Dobby mattered to us. I'm gutted he died and I want to show respect, even if I can't find the words.
memories.source_text: Yeah thanks, Dobby

memories.description: I'm ready to follow Harry. If he says it's urgent, then it is. I'll be there, even if I don't know every detail.
memories.source_text: What are we doing now, Harry?

memories.description: Great idea. I agree, let's get out of here and not hang around.
memories.source_text: "Great idea," said Ron,

memories.description: What d'you reckon it's looking for? Seriously, what's it after up here?
memories.source_text: "What do you reckon it’s looking for?" Ron yelled as they flew farther and farther north.

memories.description: I now know the wand I took from Wormtail was made for him and is brittle, but if I won it then it's more likely to work for me than a random wand.
memories.source_text: "So I should use this one?" said Ron, pulling Wormtail’s wand out of his pocket and handing it to Ollivander. "Chestnut and dragon heartstring. Nine-and-a-quarter inches. Brittle. I was forced to make this shortly after my kidnapping, for Peter Pettigrew."

memories.description: Blimey, when I find out Voldemort is going for the Elder Wand I want to go and snatch it back right now. We should stop him.
memories.source_text: "But then, let’s go!" said Ron urgently. "Harry, let’s go and get it before he does!"

memories.description: I feel torn. I want the unbeatable wand and I think it'd fix everything, but I remember Dumbledore wanted Harry to focus on the Horcruxes. I can't stop caring about both.
memories.source_text: "The unbeatable wand, Harry!" moaned Ron. "I’m not supposed to . . . I’m supposed to get the Horcruxes."

memories.description: Blimey, we're losing height, aren't we?
memories.source_text: Is it my imagination, or are we losing height?

memories.description: I spot things when I'm excited. I call them out straight away and want a plan to get them.
memories.source_text: "It’s there, it’s up there!"

memories.description: I worry about practicalities and point out obvious problems. Can't just stand there, someone needs to work out how to reach it.
memories.source_text: "And how the hell are we going to get up there without touching anything?"

memories.description: When something goes wrong I shout what's missing and try to grab it back. I react loud and fast in a crisis.
memories.source_text: "Where’s the sword? It had the cup on it!"

memories.description: I will push my mates to move even when I'm scared. I might swear and yell, but I stick with them and shove everyone into action.
memories.source_text: "Get up, climb up, come on —"

memories.description: Blimey, forget the dragon — it can look after itself. It's us I'm worried about. I don't know how to break this to you but I reckon they've noticed we broke into Gringotts.
memories.source_text: "You sound like Hagrid," said Ron. "It’s a dragon, Hermione, it can look after itself. It’s us we need to worry about." "Well, I don’t know how to break this to you," said Ron, "but I think they might have noticed we broke into Gringotts."

memories.description: Blimey, when did this tunnel appear? I didn't even know about it until now.
memories.source_text: "How long's this been here?"

memories.description: This passage isn't on the Marauder's Map and we were told there were only seven ways in and out. That's odd and worrying.
memories.source_text: "It isn't on the Marauder's Map, is it, Harry? I thought there were only seven passages in and out of school?"

memories.description: We set the dragon free. I still think Hermione was mad to want it as a pet, but fair play, freeing it was the right thing.
memories.source_text: "Released it into the wild," said Ron. "Hermione was all for keeping it as a pet —"

memories.description: We got the Horcrux, which is the upside, but on the downside we don't have the sword
memories.source_text: Well, on the upside, we got the Horcrux. On the downside -

memories.description: You sound like Hagrid, Hermione, I mean you're worrying about the dragon like he would
memories.source_text: You sound like Hagrid

memories.description: It's a dragon, Hermione, it can look after itself. Don't get too worked up about it
memories.source_text: It's a dragon, Hermione, it can look after itself

memories.description: Blimey, we were feeling our way down the wall, trying to stay quiet. I was properly terrified of those things.
memories.source_text: "He, Ron, and Hermione retreated down the side street, groping their way along the wall, trying not to make a sound."

memories.description: Blimey, the goblins obey instructions to the letter. If they think there are orders, they'll follow them.
memories.source_text: "Wait — Bogrod!" Another goblin came scurrying around the counter. "We have instructions," he said with a bow to Hermione."

memories.description: We need a goblin and those Clankers to get past that dragon. That's the only way in.
memories.source_text: "We need him," said Griphook, "we cannot enter the vault without a Gringotts goblin. And we need the Clankers!"

memories.description: Bloody hell, that thing strips every trick off you. You can't rely on disguises down there.
memories.source_text: "The Thief’s Downfall!" said Griphook..."It washes away all enchantment, all magical concealment!"

memories.description: I expect we need light and quick thinking when we get inside. We have to be ready to search fast.
memories.source_text: "Light your wands, can’t you?"

memories.description: Blimey, that silver doe was sent to us. I thought it was magical help showing the way.
memories.source_text: "The silver doe!" he said excitedly. "Was that you too?"

memories.description: Right then, Aberforth joked his Patronus looked like a goat. So not everything people say about Patronuses is straightforward.
memories.source_text: "Brains like that, you could be a Death Eater, son. Haven’t I just proved my Patronus is a goat?"

memories.description: Bloody hell, after all that I was starving. Food matters when you’re knackered and stressed, simple as that.
memories.source_text: "Oh," said Ron. "Yeah . . . well, I’m hungry!"

memories.description: Blimey, Neville's been talking back a lot. He's been cheeky enough to get punished for it, so they're making examples of people who mouth off.
memories.source_text: "Blimey, Neville," said Ron, "there’s a time and a place for getting a smart mouth."

memories.description: No kidding, what they're doing is terrifying. If Michael got that for freeing someone, I wouldn't expect anyone to keep risking that once it got that bad.
memories.source_text: "No kidding," muttered Ron, as the passage began to slope upward.

memories.description: Bloody hell, the teaching's been perverted. They actually force kids to use the Cruciatus as punishment. That's sick.
memories.source_text: "Amycus, the bloke, he teaches what used to be Defense Against the Dark Arts, except now it’s just the Dark Arts. We’re supposed to practice the Cruciatus Curse on people who’ve earned detentions —"

memories.description: They actually went for Neville's gran. Blimey, that's low even for them.
memories.source_text: "They what?" said Harry, Ron, and Hermione together.

memories.description: I was proper confused — thought we were going back into Hogwarts, but Neville's gone missing to lay low. This mess is worse than I thought.
memories.source_text: "Only thing was, once they realized they had no hold over me, they decided Hogwarts could do without me after all. I don’t know whether they were planning to kill me or send me to Azkaban; either way, I knew it was time to disappear." "But," said Ron, looking thoroughly confused, "aren’t — aren’t we heading straight back into Hogwarts?"

memories.description: Neville's gran sent him a proud letter. That's brilliant and makes me glad for him.
memories.source_text: "She sent me a letter," he clapped a hand to the breast pocket of his robes, "telling me she was proud of me, that I’m my parents’ son, and to keep it up." "Cool," said Ron.

memories.description: Well, using Bellatrix’s wand will help Hermione get into character. Blimey, that wand has a nasty history, and that makes our disguise stronger.
memories.source_text: “It’ll probably help you get in character, though,” said Ron. “Think what that wand’s done!”

memories.description: I don’t trust Griphook. His constant poking about makes me dead suspicious and fed up.
memories.source_text: “He could give my mother lessons,” growled Ron, as the goblin’s long fingers kept appearing around the edges of doors.

memories.description: I’m not sure how to double-cross Griphook either. We’ll just have to wing it, mate.
memories.source_text: Ron, on the rare occasions that they had been able to snatch a few Griphook-free moments, had come up with nothing better than “We’ll just have to wing it, mate.”

memories.description: I care about small things in disguises. Don’t make the beard too long and shorten my nose a bit. I’m practical and fussy about this stuff.
memories.source_text: “Right, but remember, I don’t like the beard too long —” “Oh, for heaven’s sake, this isn’t about looking handsome —” “It’s not that, it gets in the way! But I liked my nose a bit shorter, try and do it the way you did last time.”

memories.description: Blimey, maybe people will be too terrified to tell him anything about the Horcruxes.
memories.source_text: "Maybe they’ll be too scared to tell him?"

memories.description: Bloody hell, they might try to hide things or cover up where the Horcruxes are.
memories.source_text: "Maybe they’ll cover up —"

memories.description: What the hell did you see in his mind? How do you know where the Horcrux is?
memories.source_text: "But what did you see? How do you know?"

memories.description: Where in Hogwarts is the Horcrux? We need to know if we are going to get there in time.
memories.source_text: "Did you see where in Hogwarts it is?"

memories.description: I tried to bluff with a name, said I was Stan Shunpike. It didn't work. Bloody hell, they knew who he was.
memories.source_text: "Stan Shunpike," said Ron. "Like 'ell you are," said the man called Scabior. "We know Stan Shunpike, 'e's put a bit of work our way."

memories.description: I slurred something like Bardy Weadley with my mouth full of blood, trying to keep up the act. Not my finest moment.
memories.source_text: "I’b Bardy," said Ron, and Harry could tell that his mouth was full of blood. "Bardy Weadley."

memories.description: I felt awful and kept apologising because I said the Dark Lord's name and that may have led them straight to us. I blamed myself hard.
memories.source_text: "This is all my fault. I said the name, I’m sorry —"

memories.description: We were out camping after leaving Hogwarts and I kept trying to explain it was an accident, not some stunt. I kept sounding daft but I was desperate.
memories.source_text: "We’b lebt," said Ron. "Left, 'ave you, ginger?" said Scabior. "And you decided to go camping? And you thought, just for a laugh, you’d use the Dark Lord’s name?" "Nod a laugh," said Ron. "Aggiden." "Accident?"

memories.description: Don’t even think about it. Blimey, I’m not letting her go under the Cloak. That’s my call.
memories.source_text: “Don’t even think about it,” Ron snarled at her.

memories.description: Blimey, it's been rough for us while we've been off doing this. I'm fed up but determined.
memories.source_text: It hasn't exactly been a picnic, mate

memories.description: No, we're not leaving everyone to rot. I won't stand for that. Whatever we do has to help everyone in the end.
memories.source_text: No!

memories.description: We're doing this to get rid of You-Know-Who. I believe what we're doing will help everyone, even if they can't be told the details.
memories.source_text: What we're doing will benefit everyone in the end, it's all about trying to get rid of You-Know-Who

memories.description: They can help. I whispered it to Hermione because I think the D.A. could make a real difference if they knew enough to act.
memories.source_text: They can help.

memories.description: Blimey, what even is a diadem? I do not know that word.
memories.source_text: [Sorry, but what is a diadem?]

memories.description: Right, we need to hurry and look for this thing. If telling everyone would make it harder, we do not have to say it is a Horcrux.
memories.source_text: [We’ve got to find it fast. We don’t have to tell them it’s a Horcrux.]

memories.description: Bloody hell, the tapestry just ripped open!
memories.source_text: The tapestry at the top of the staircase on which they stood was ripped open.

memories.description: Blimey, what the hell? A whole corridor full of duelers!
memories.source_text: They ran down the next staircase and found themselves in a corridor full of duelers.

memories.description: Blimey, food's one of those things magic won't make for you, so Aberforth has actually been keeping us fed. That's proper important to know.
memories.source_text: Yeah, well, food’s one of the five exceptions to Gamp’s Law of Elemental Transfiguration

memories.description: Look, I know it's been rough for everyone hiding here, but we've stuck together. We're loyal to Dumbledore and to you, Harry.
memories.source_text: It hasn’t exactly been a picnic, mate, said Ron

memories.description: We are Dumbledore's Army. Of course we want to help. Don't shut us out when we've proven we're on your side.
memories.source_text: I never said it had, but I don’t see why you can’t trust us. Everyone in this room’s been fighting and they’ve been driven in here because the Carrows were hunting them down

memories.description: Blimey, they're having a right scrap and I'm at the back trying to keep up. I'm running too, following them off the steps.
memories.source_text: Ron bringing up the rear
